You have obtained all of the four failed souls. See if they will open the inscribed door in Nefris' chambers.
You successfully opened the door in Nefris' chambers, having reunited the four incomplete souls described by the door's inscription.
{E}Order from Chaos

A student at the Academy of Shapers and Binders named Selkhit is working on an "intellectual challenge" posed to all of the academy's students by its headmistress.
As she describes it, there are two rooms that initially contain equal numbers of ice and fire mephits. At one point, one room contained only fire mephits and one only ice mephits, but their natural tendency is to intermingle at a random end eventually even basis.
The goal of the challenge is to reverse this course, returning the rooms to a state in which one contains only ice mephits and one contains only fire mephits. The means of doing this is a lever that temporarily opens a door between the rooms, instantly switching the places of the mephit in each room closest to the door.
According to Selkhit, the pent up energy created by segregating the mephits is set up to be harnessed and transferred for use in the reconstitution of a soul that has been deliberately divided, a supposedly impossible feat, and the new soul is prize to the first student to complete the challenge.
Complete the challenge and fuse the separate pieces into one soul.
You and Nefris are now supposedly the only two people to successfully complete her mephit separation challenge, and the newly fused soul is yours for the taking.
{E}Uncanny Reflections

In the instructors' quarters section of the Academy of Shapers and Binders, you found a dais set in the ground with a network of mirrors around it. It looks as though the mirrors could be turned to direct the reflection of a person standing on the dais to some other, as-yet-undetermined endpoint.
The same person cannot both activate the device and stand on the dais, from the look of things. It remains to be seen whether it matters whose image you choose to reflect across the academy.
Attempt to project your reflection or that of one of your companions to the other end of the network of mirrors, wherever that might be.

You stood on the dais and projected your reflection around the academy to a dais in another room.
An image of yourself appeared there momentarily (although its face was obscured by a mask), and it left behind what might have been its equivalent to a soul. If this contraption was meant to replicate a person, its designer fell just short of his or her goal.

Okku stood on the dais and you projected his reflection around the academy to a dais in another room.
An image of him appeared there momentarily (although from its appearance it might rather have been Okku as he was in life - leader of a thriving clan), and it left behind what might have been its equivalent to a soul. If this contraption was meant to replicate a person, its designer fell just short of his or her goal.

Kaelyn stood on the dais and you projected her reflection around the academy to a dais in another room.
An image of her appeared there momentarily (although her wings were different - more appropriate for a fallen angel than a celestial), and it left behind what might have been its equivalent to a soul. If this contraption was meant to replicate a person, its designer fell just short of his or her goal.

Safiya stood on the dais and you projected her reflection around the academy to a dais in another room.
An image of her appeared there momentarily (although her face was older, and Safiya seemed to take the image for her late mother), and it left behind what might have been its equivalent to a soul. If this contraption was meant to replicate a person, its designer fell just short of his or her goal.

Your undead companion stood on the dais and you projected its reflection around the academy to a dais in another room.
On the other side, you were assaulted by a throng of tormented spirits, and in their wake was left behind what might have been their equivalent to a soul. If this contraption was meant to replicate a being, its designer fell just short of his or her goal.
{E}A Fitting Replacement

You came upon a room in the instructors' quarters section of the Academy of Shapers and Binders that seems to be a kind of hospice (or morgue) for experiment subjects who've had their souls removed.
One of the only live inhabitants of the room, Bebtu, has told you he is in possession of something Nefris wished for you to have - his soul, or rather, an artificial soul housed in his body.
Bebtu explained that his surrogate soul can only be removed if it's replaced with the original, which is kept in the soul depository on the classroom level. Of course, for the dark-hearted, there may be a more direct and nefarious way to obtain his artificial soul, but that would certainly mean his death.
Locate Bebtu's soul in the depository and bring it to him. He said there was a device there that would allow a user to "read" from the various souls there in order to identify nature of their owner.

You returned to Bebtu his original soul, thus displacing the surrogate he had hosted. Bebtu was grateful to be restored to his original state, but nevertheless, something about his reaction suggested that his original soul was every bit as incomplete as the false one he'd taken in its place.
Rather than replace Bebtu's original soul, you devoured the artificial soul that Bebtu had freely offered you, ending his miserable life instantly.
{E}Conflicted

Thael-ka and Oronock, twin pit fiends bound in summoning circles in the instructors' quarters level of the Academy of Shapers and Binders, have told you that they are in possession of a rare soul - one they feel you will take a keen interest in.
Naturally, there is a catch. They want a rare soul in trade. Unfortunately, they are in complete disagreement about the what the qualities of that soul should be, and many of the qualities are wholly contradictory with one another.
Thael-ka wants the soul of a virtuous, yet wretched being. Oronock, on the other hand, has requested the soul of a depraved, yet prosperous person.
See what you can dig up in the soul depository that matches the descriptions of the two devils. Hopefully the devils will be willing to accept two souls, each meeting the criteria of one of them. Otherwise, you may have to look for a way to artificially fuse them together.

You have presented Thael-ka and Oronock with souls that matched their descriptions, but they were unwilling to accept them, insisting that you bring them only a single soul that exhibits all of the qualities they mentioned.
The likelihood of actually finding such a soul naturally being just about nil, you'll need to find a means to join the souls you already have. Perhaps an academy master here might have the necessary knowledge to accomplish this.
With the help of Poruset, you are now in possession of a very unstable, but nevertheless singular soul that you can present to Thael-ka and Oronock in trade.

You brought Thael-ka and Oronock the exact soul they requested, and obtained a "hollow soul" in trade, which is evidently what remains in a living person after they have been damned.
If they weren't so grotesque, the look on the devils' faces when they got the news you'd actually obtained the soul they'd wanted would've been worth remembering for a long time.
{E}Skeleton Keys

Inarus, an instructor at the Academy of Shapers and Binders, has offered you a set of keys he claims will open many locked doors within the academy.
In return, he simply wants you to show off your ability to devour spirits in front of the class. He prefers you use your power on his worst student, but will settle for a demonstration on an elemental.

You demonstrated your ability to devour spirits in front of Inarus' class, and as promised, he gave you a set of keys to untold doors and treasures in the academy.
He mentioned, however, that there was one room - a spare room adjacent to his own quarters - that one of the keys will open, but which he expects you never to enter. What could he be hiding?

In the room Inarus specifically told you not to enter, you found a gruesome scene. The floor was splattered with gore and heaped with corpses that met grisly fates. Inarus attempted to see that you join them for violating his trust, but you overcame him.
You opted not to visit the room that Inarus forbade you to enter, which while admirable from the standpoint of your integrity, was perhaps a little foolhardy as well.
{E}The Final Test

A young academy student named Nakt has challenged you to determine which version of his friend Hasina is real, and which is a magically driven automaton he built as a class project.
Speak to each of the Hasinas, and try to find clues as to the solution. Tell Nakt when you have a final guess ready.
You failed to guess correctly which Hasina was the artificial one. Nakt was very pleased and thinks he will get high marks for his project.

You guessed correctly that neither version of Hasina is real, but this revelation agitated Nakt, who killed the real Hasina awhile ago inadvertently while working on this very project. He felt he had no other choice but to attack you.
{E}Mysterious Device

You found a device in one of the labs in the Academy of Shapers and Binders of indeterminate origin and use. The academy master whose labe it was is nowhere to be found, and is probably allied with Araman, so simply asking its creator what it does is probably not an option.
Experiment with the device and see if you can find its use.

You found that the device reacted with spirit essences, splitting them apart and releasing a wave of destructive energy - a powerful weapon and useful find.
Your discovery has provided you with new insight into the nature and properties of souls, and your skill as a crafter of items requiring spirit essences has no doubt benefited, perhaps enabling you to craft things you couldn't before.

Favored Souls
favored soul

Favored Soul The favored soul follows the path of the cleric but is able to channel divine power with surprising ease. She is able to perform the same tasks as her fellow divine spellcasters but with virtually no study. Favored souls cast their spells naturally, as much through force of personality as through study. Though this gives them extraordinary divine abilities no normal person could ever match, they see their gift as a call to action, and so in some ways may lag behind their more studious colleagues. Class Features: - Hit Die: d8 - Base Attack Bonus: Medium. - High Saves: All. - Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons and deity's favored weapon. - Armor Proficiencies: Light armor, medium armor, and shields (except tower shields). - Skill Points: 2 + Int modifier per level, x4 at first level. - Class Skills: Concentration, Craft Alchemy, Craft Armor, Craft Weapon, Diplomacy, Heal, Lore, Parry, and Spellcraft. - Spells: A favored soul casts divine spells which are drawn from the cleric spell list. She can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time the way a cleric must. To cast a spell, a favored soul must have a Charisma score of 10 + the spell's level (Cha 10 for 0-level spells, Cha 11 for 1st-level spells, and so forth). The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a favored soul's spell is 10 + the spell's level + the favored soul's Wisdom modifier. Unlike a cleric, a favored soul's selection of spells is limited, but at 4th level, and at every even-numbered favored soul level after that, the favored soul may swap a spell she already knows for another spell of the same level. In effect, the favored soul "loses" the old spell in exchange for the new one. - Deity's Weapon Proficiency: Favored souls gain a weapon proficiency feat that allows them to use their deity's favored weapon. (For example, favored souls of Kelemvor will gain the Exotic Weapon Proficiency feat, enabling them to use a bastard sword.) - Deity's Weapon Focus: At 3rd level, a favored soul gains the Weapon Focus feat with her deity's favored weapon. - Energy Resistance: At 5th level, a favored soul chooses an energy type and gains resistance 10 against that type. At 10th level and 15th level, the character gains resistance 10 against another energy type of her choosing. - Deity's Weapon Specialization: At 12th level, a favored soul gains the Weapon Specialization feat with her deity's favored weapon. - Haste: At 17th level, a favored soul gains the ability to cast haste three times per day. - Damage Reduction: At 20th level, a favored soul gains damage reduction. She may choose between damage reduction 10/silver or damage reduction 10/cold iron.

Hagspawn
hagspawn

Hagspawn Sons of malicious, predatory mothers, hagspawn are not a complete race, as there are no females of their kind. Hags continue their awful lineage by taking human males for mates, usually murdering and devouring the hapless captive later. The female children of a hag quickly grow into hags like their mothers, but the male children are hagspawn - half-human outcasts. Feared and hated by normal humans, hagspawn must make their way in the world by dint of their strength, hardiness, and sheer determination. Racial Traits: - Ability Adjustments: +2 Strength, +2 Constitution, -2 Charisma. - Darkvision: Hagspawn can see in the dark up to 60 feet. - Natural Armor: +2 natural armor bonus. - Spell Resistant: Spell resistance of 11 + character level. - Favored Class: Barbarian. A multiclass hagspawn's barbarian class does not count when determining whether he takes an experience point penalty. - Level Adjustment +2: Hagspawn are more powerful and gain levels more slowly than other races. It will take more experience for a hagspawn to reach level 2 than it would for normal races, for example.

This ancient bear spirit is massive... its body transparent, and ghostly. Somehow, its features recall that of the bear god, Okku - though this creature strikes you as far older, and somehow more detached from the mortal world.
I... know this place...
The moisture on the air... it carries the scent of my clan. And their voices, too. They are near, , can you hear them?
I remember a pool... a gathering of beasts... water rushing from above...
Do they live? I hear pain in their cries... and rage.
My kin are here... hiding among the rocks, perhaps. But why...
I hear them as well. They are lost... they are the cries of those confused, the lost - the mad. Be careful, Old King Bear, I think you may be in danger here.
[Influence Loss: Okku] Caution is for prey, not for us. Come, little friend, we should go to them!
We were scattered, little one... though I do not remember how. Come, we should go to them!
I hear my name in their calls... fleeing into the crags, like a playful wind...
[Influence Gain: Okku] Your eyes are sharp, and my nose is keen - they won't elude us, though their voices are... hard to catch...
When a cub was lost, or a clan scattered... they knew to come here. The forsaken were safe, with the eyes of Lurue upon them...
Pah! The ears of your kind are not as sharp as mine. Silence the words that clutter your mind, little friend, and hear the voices on the air...
I thought... it is like a dream, little friend... one that returns each night, and is lost with the dawn...
Mph. If they are ghosts, then I am something even less. Somehow... they remember all that I forgot...
In the long dark of my dreaming, I forgot all but my oath, little one. But they may remember...
| Not druid, ranger, or spirit-shaman |I... hear nothing.
| Druid, ranger, or spirit-shaman only |I... hear something. Whispers... echoes... but very faint.
The aged sometimes hear voices, Okku. Perhaps it is the same with bears.
Wait... you said your memories were gone, fled from your mind when you died.
| Evil |Suffer your delusions in silence, beast. You swore to follow me, not your ghosts.
Something is wrong. We'll investigate, but with caution.
Is that possible? I'd think that your relatives would be long dead.
| Good or Neutral |A change has come over you, my friend. Something is not as it seems here.
| Set Wells of Lurue quest |
Come. We'll search these gorges until we find them.
Calm yourself. We have other business, first.
| PC devoured Okku |I heard how the spirit-eater devoured Okku, my old enemy. It seems to me that spirit-eater uses the Gift wisely.
The Gift is what sets spirit-eater apart from other sentients and gives it kinship with Hill Tribe.
| PC Spared Okku. Okku not present. |Spirit-eater joins Hill Tribe for a feast. Tell me, where is the spirit-eater's ursine ally?
I have lived since another time, centuries past. A time when stories walked the lands in flesh... and blood.
| After U'juk has transformed into Uthraki. |Now spirit-eater sees the true form of Hill Tribe.
Spirit-eater is driven by the Hunger. With the Gift, spirit-eater masters the Hunger, like a whip that tames the dire wolf and makes it only attack enemies.
Hill Tribe, too, is driven by the Hunger. But Hill Tribe lacks the Gift, so the Hunger is master. This is why the Hill Tribe respects spirit-eater.
| PC devoured Okku |There is something I could teach, if spirit-eater is willing to learn.
Also, like Hill Tribe wears the skins of our prey for disguise, spirit-eater wears different shapes.
If spirit-eater does not know this, such knowledge may come, should spirit-eater survive long enough.
Okku, the bear king, once hunted and tried to eat me. I still bear the scars from Okku's teeth.
| PC devoured Okku and has the husk |Is that Okku's husk that spirit-eater carries? It has much power, even now. Spirit-eater must sense it too or it would have been discarded.
Tell me, has spirit-eater found a use for Okku's husk?
Spirits will be attracted to the husk, but each weighs too little to fill the husk of the bear king and spirits do not like to be close to each other.
Spirit-eater can use the Gift to force many spirits at once to inhabit the husk. With enough spirits, the husk will be reanimated into a new form to serve spirit-eater.
Remember my words when spirit-eater comes to a place thick with spirits.
Rashemen is plentiful in spirits, but most are free to roam wide. Find a place where many, many spirits are trapped close together.
Large cities of the sentients, and sites of great violence are where spirit-eater is likely to find such a place.
What else will spirit-eater speak of?
| PC devoured Okku |Yes, I am glad Okku is dead. Does spirit-eater understand how to use his husk?
Spirit-eater does not understand? Very well, I will explain again...
| PC Spared Okku. Okku is present. |Spirit-eater joins Hill Tribe for a feast. And spirit-eater has brought an ursine ally.
| PC spared Okku. GEORGE: Okku does not remember U'juk. |I have hunted many throughout the years. Very few have escaped my claws, and I remember them all. I do not remember you.
| PC spared Okku, but Okku is not present. |Perhaps it is best that spirit-eater did not bring the bear king here to this feast.
| PC did not devour Okku. |The spirit-eater before me betrays the Gift, by defeating one such as Okku and not feeding on it to gain the power that is the spirit-eater's right.
I have known spirit-eater in many different shapes. Some I have befriended, learned from and taught.
Others I have eaten, when they betrayed the Gift. It is a service I provide in respect to spirit-eater, so that the Gift may pass to one worthy of it.
Oh, it is not a threat, betrayer of the Gift. It is a promise.
Like spirit-eater, Hill Tribe wears different shapes. We do not feed in human form...
The food is here, spirit-eater. It just does not know it yet.
Okku does not remember me, because I conceal myself with the skin of my prey.
No, spirit-eater has come to the right place. Hill Tribe shares a long-lasting kinship with spirit-eater, and we are bound to honor it by releasing those that betray the Gift.
| PC devoured Okku |Do not be frightened. I have great respect for spirit-eater.
| GEORGE: Okku recognized U'juk |I know you now, U'juk, you chattering ape! And I remember the taste of your blood... this time, I shall have more than just a taste, I think.
Perhaps this time the Gift will pass to me when spirit-eater dies. I suspect I killed the others too quickly before. I shall make this death linger.
Ku'arra, tend to the younglings while the adults deal with spirit-eater.
Yes, grandsire. Save me a portion of the loins. I savor it so!
Before we continue, this skin I wear is fiercely uncomfortable. I feel we have reached the point where I may shed it.
Do not be alarmed. Like spirit-eater, Hill Tribe wears different shapes...
Uthraki! Clever disguises... I should have sensed them sooner. Tread carefully around these man-eating savages...
{Slight recognition}{ooth-RAK-ee }Uthraki. {now wariness, whispers a little}Shapeshifters - and not friendly.
These creatures were cloaking their true appearance... be careful, they may have other deceptions cast.
We are uthraki. Spirit-eater, this shape must be new to Rashemen, for all here know of the uthraki.
Uthraki are the dark creatures in the stories that mothers tell their children to frighten them into compliance. Some know the uthraki as the embodiments of fear.
Long have the uthraki been hunted by the Rashemi witches. Our numbers dwindle and it is more difficult for us to hunt our choice prey, sentients.
It would be most ironic if spirit-eater feared the uthraki.
Does spirit-eater insult me? The Gift demands respect, but uthraki are proud and fierce and do not tolerate belittlement.
Very well, spirit-eater.
I do not doubt spirit-eater's power, but I can sense the lack of an ability that other spirit-eaters possessed.
I meant no offense, spirit-eater. I only wish to help guide spirit-eater to fully embracing the Gift. Does spirit-eater wish to learn?
When spirit-eater looked upon Hill Tribe in our human forms, I detected no hunger. I take this to mean that spirit-eater has only learned to devour spirits.
Yes, I have known spirit-eater in many shapes, some more potent than others.
At full strength, spirit-eater alone is more powerful than six of my kind.
In that case, Hill Tribe will feast on spirit-eater this night.

Bring to us living, sentient meats, and spirit-eater shall be rewarded.
Spirit-eater wishes to leave so soon? Do we make spirit-eater uncomfortable? Perhaps our natural forms would be more appealing...
I will gladly share my knowledge with spirit-eater, but first it is customary to exchange knowledge for blood.
For a long while now, Hill Tribe has been forced to survive on a meager fare of wildlife. But with the help of spirit-eater, we can satisfy the rumblings of our bellies.
Find unsuspecting sentients, spirit-eater and lead them to Hill Tribe. For this, I will gladly share the knowledge I possess.
Spirit-eater knows the Hunger. The uthraki know Hunger too, but have less power against it.
Understand, spirit-eater, that sentient meat has already walked into our camp, and for us to let it go, we must be assured that more will soon come.
I did not wish to put it so harshly, but yes. Feed us, or we will feed on spirit-eater.
| After accepting Knowledge For Blood, before bringing food. |Hill Tribe is hungry. Tell me spirit-eater has brought us sentients to feast on.

We grow impatient and famished, spirit-eater.
I am not certain how long Hill Tribe can fight the Hunger. Please hurry and find us food.
Hill Tribe has nearly succumbed to the Hunger, spirit-eater. Do not return again without food!
Forgive me, spirit-eater, but the Hunger clears my mind of all else. Feed us and my knowledge will be shared.

Of the three bear spirits, this one seems the most similar to the bear god, Okku. You detect a similarity of demeanor, a sameness in the eyes... though this bear's fur is gray, and his eyes are clouded. You suspect that he died at a very advanced age.
Chatter at Shelvedar, if you like. I've a mug of ale to drain, and another dozen after this one.
| If player hasn't already met him with Okku |<FirstName>, join us! Gullen, Vinck, spare some room... it's our friend from the road, don't you remember?
<FirstName>! I'm afraid you find me in my cups, yet again.
You'll have to pardon my comrades - they are dour company at the best of times, but uncommonly loyal to my purse.
Nay. But we remember the mud well enough. And the ache in our shoulders from getting your cursed wagon unstuck.
<FirstName>, let me buy you a drink. They say that generosity makes one wealthy in friends, and since I am poor in all else, I will take what I can.
Happily, yes. And just before the spirits arrived. A rare stroke of luck, I assure you.
Gullen and Vinck didn't bother to argue, so here we are.
And since luck is inevitably followed by terrible misfortune, I reasoned... why not greet my misfortune in a drunken stupor?
For myself, I attribute the pleasant atmosphere to the lack of Witches. And I find the locals far more palatable when drunk.
If you can wait for the actors to sober up, I hear they're playing an especially vulgar performance of "The Fat Wizard's Wench."
Although you may be waiting for some time. Clive the Dandy has turned a disturbing shade of green, and I think I heard one of the others vomiting in a back room.
Those would be the local pirates... of course, I would never refer to them as such, if they were close enough to hear.
Their captain is Fyldrin of the Eleven Chairs... though his arse seems to require only one, and I have never inquired after the other ten.
Indeed. I know that his father is rumored to have been a great boar spirit, which would explain his considerable body hair.
Sadly, I also know that these rumors are nonsense. Fyldrin is the youngest son of Lord Thydrim, who was slain in his bed by Thayan knives.
Brave Fyldrin now spends his summers off the Thayan coast, murdering with wild abandon, and hanging his ship with bald Thayan scalps.
As I am neither Thayan nor bald, I am thankfully beneath his notice. And I have no plan to shave my locks, lest I tempt a violent end.
Scoundrels and rogues, every one. Drink enough to pass out, and they will kindly relieve you of your purse, your pants, and occasionally your hair, if the actors are in need of a wig.
None at all, I am happy to say. I whole-heartedly detest my line of work, as any reasonable person should.
His wife is Zorah - the handsome woman over yonder. Comment on her tusks, if you must, but do so at your own risk. And leave my name out of it.
And to you, my friend. My table is yours, whenever you see fit to make it so.
A colorful fellow. He calls himself Vladek, though I suspect he has traded freely in names. Almost as freely as he trades in tales.
| If Okku is present |Ah. I see that you've befriended a particularly large bear. Is he not the same creature that nearly devoured me at the gate?

Yes, we all like the bear, Gullen, thank you. Always good to be reminded that I have gristle.

Wh-what?

At times like these, I find myself wishing that I was a more diligent man, and less prone to buying drinks for everyone at the bar. I have only 3000 gold... and I swear I am telling the truth.

This tattered, blood-stained tome appears to be the journal of a former vremyonni. Most of the entries appear to ramble on about exacting revenge on his arrogant vremyonni "brothers", but a few select passages catch your eye. "15th of Mirtul - I have finally done it! I was able to animate a corpse and breathe life back into it! Well... it was the corpse of a diseased rat, which seem to be everywhere in this cave, but it was a corpse nonetheless. Unfortunately, I cannot let anyone see my creation, lest I be cast off from here or worse. I guess I will have to dispose of him." "25th of Mirtul - I think I saw Barovik going through my things this morning. I can't be sure of what he has seen. I need to be much more cautious in hiding my forbidden tomes of necromantic lore. I must go probe Barovik and see what he knows." "25th of Mirtul - Barovik dodged all of my questions regarding his activities this morning. I cannot take the chance that he has seen any of my forbidden codices. I would eliminate him, but that would only cause an investigation. Leaving is the only option. Leaving this cave means leaving all of Rasheman, abandoning all I love. No matter, it must be done." "3rd of Kythorn - Damn the Old Ones! They never taught me anything of survival in the wilderness. This morning's attempt to catch a meal went horribly. All of nature's creatures seem to recoil from me. I wonder if they can sense some sort of taint upon me. What I wouldn't give for some of Jerryn's rabbit stew. Those carrots were so tender and... I need to stop this nonsense and find a town that I can take refuge in." "11th of Kythorn - Off in the distance, I see... large walls! Even in my weakened state I think I can make it there before nightfall. I must make it there before nightfall." "7th of Flamerule - Mulsantir. That is the name of this city. I have been in my new "abode" for several weeks now. Oh, I love it here, in this dank, dark, abandoned cellar. If only there were more disease-ridden vermin, it would be just like I was back in the caves with the other vremyonni. I live like a peasant, now. I had to beg for food when I first made it to this place. Beg! I will make them pay for what they have subjected me to." "9th of Eleint - How I think about slowly snuffing out the life of everyone of those arrogant vremyonni. I think constantly about how I was ejected from my life, just because I sought to master all forms of magic. It will take many lifetimes to exact all of the revenge I have planned for them. Many lifetimes... that gives me an idea." "23rd of Uktar - I have figured out a way to cheat Kelemvor! This will take much time and lots of my resources, but it will be worth it to see the agony and hear the screams of my "brothers." I must find a suitable vessel for my soul. Also, one of my texts mentions something called "The Tome of Profane Rebirth." I must find it!" "1st of Nightal - Luck upon luck! I have found the general location of this Tome of Rebirth. It resides on the Plane of Shadow. Not only that, but from my preliminary reading, it appears that Mulsantir is the perfect place to enter the Plane of Shadow. The way to cross planes is through the temple to the Death God." "14th of Ches - Rubbish! So close to my goal, only to be stopped by a barrier that is impossible to pass. After making it to the Plane of Shadows, I have learned that the Tome I need is in the Dead God's Vault. I refuse to go in there, even for this. It matters not. I will proceed with the ritual here on this shadow plane. Now to summon some servants to watch over me..." The entries past this point are too blood-soaked to read.
Open book

This tome, which is adorned with small animal bones over its leathery surface, seems to discuss many necromantic rituals. You see three entries which appear to be marked for further use.
The first entry describes how to prepare a vessel for use as something called a phylactery. Apparently, a phylactery is used to house a soul for eternity. These phylacteries can be used in a rite to cheat death and live forever.
The second entry describes, in great detail, a ritual that was referred to in the first marked entry. This ceremony appears very complicated and it is stressed that only the most accomplished spellcasters should even consider replicating it.
Surprisingly, this third entry describes a way to free a soul trapped in a phylactery. Not surprising, this requires the destruction of the phylactery. Destroying the phylactery will allow the natural order to take its course and the soul will move beyond to its final resting place.
Unfurled scroll

"VAROVIN - He is the root of this pain I feel and I will exact my revenge on him first. I will slowly bleed him... no, I will smash his face with... no, I will yank out his..." This seems to go on for quite some time.

The problem is this. Mephits, as a species, tend to move and intermix chaotically.

If you had a room of fire mephits next to a room of ice mephits with an open door between them, in time they would distribute themselves evenly. Both rooms would have equal numbers of ice and fire mephits.
The natural flow of their movements is always from order to disorder. The problem is to do the reverse - to resegregate the two rooms such that one has only ice mephits and one has only fire mephits.

If I'm to be spared... {referring to her daughter here}perhaps it's fitting that it would be for the best of what I was...
{horrified}No! She is innocent! Blameless! I've kept her so.
{Outraged - she's feeling insulted}Is that what you think of me? Is your opinion of me so devoid of respect? {Cold, angry}I trusted you, and in return, you belittle and betray me...
{a little passion returning}Let that be Myrkul's legacy to the planes... that in the end, his cruelty broke before a mortal's resolve.

[Yet... as you direct your will, and command it to feed upon the Founder's soul... the presence balks. You close your eyes, concentrate more intensely upon it, willing the presence to do as you say...]

[...but your will is defied. You realize at once that the Founder was right. Something of Akachi remains within that empty, hungering shell. And somehow, it senses the Founder's love... and cannot betray her.]
{softly - referring to her former lover}He knows me. He remembers... doesn't he?
My magic was...always different. Tearing at forbidden boundaries, changing the nature of things. Even before his curse gave it focus.
A careless moment... concentration lost, a senseless mistake. That was all it took.
I've... never remembered it well. Though I assumed... the moment of my death would be difficult to precisely recall...
A shadow passing across my eyes, a sudden confusion... they might have been real. Myrkul's hand might have brushed my mind, cost me focus when I needed it most...
Was it a test of faith? Did Akachi love me better... or his god? Myrkul got his answer... whether he forced the point or not.
{furious}Akachi sacrificed himself... because he saw what was best in me, even if I did not. To lose Safiya... is to render his sacrifice as nothing.
{enraged, steeling for an attack at the end of this}You will not touch Safiya... even if the work of five centuries is lost. You can be replaced, stranger. My daughter cannot.
My portal will return you to the Veil. From there, the black Gate lies open to you, for as long as you bear the Sword.
[You concentrate upon the presence within you... stirring it to wakefulness. It is ravenous, as ever... wanting nothing but to fill itself up.]
[You can feel the presence recoil... balking as it senses the Founder's soul. But the strength of Myrkul lies behind your will... and you command the presence to feed.]

[Such a cry of anguish you have never known... as that which shrieks in your mind, as you force the presence - the empty shell that was once Akachi the Betrayer - to reach forth and gorge on the soul of the woman he loved...]

Rejuvenation Salve
Superior Rejuvenation Salve
Hilaiyreen

A powerful artifact of Rashemen, the Hilaiyreen is a treasured amulet passed from grandparent to grandchild, and whose power is reflected in the strength and bravery of the family of warriors who has always carried it.
Periapt of the Lost Witch

Arduelth, a young witch, had spent her life living under the shadow of Thay, and wished to study for a magical means to empower Rashemen, so she left on a dajemma - the customary Rashemi journey of self-discovery. Years later she returned, a haunted look in her eyes. Around her neck she wore an amulet that glowed with power - only the first of the artifacts she claimed to have learned how to create. She spoke long and passionately of how they could make use of such items - to not only bring peace to Rashemen, but break the back of Thay. The hathrans narrowed their eyes behind their masks as she spoke, fearing the young woman's intensity: but they listened, and gravely made her one of them. Before long, the witches began to regret their decision. The young woman seemed obsessed with the idea of creating more items of greater and more sinister properties... and her plans grew more and more elaborate, from freeing the slaves of Thay to enslaving the Red Wizards in their place, sapping them of their power for her own devices. It was suspected that Arduelth had become a durthan, eternal enemy of the hathrans - but another witch saw once that she communed with something far darker. Though the young woman still dreamed of peace and freedom for her people, she had given herself over to a dark entity - her pure intentions savaged by the lengths she would dare go to achieve them. Though it seems Arduelth's life has come to an end, the amulet still glows with a same promising light... as if it carried a fraction of its former wearer's soul, and the determination to see her plans come to fruition - whatever the cost.
Reverberating Arrow
Lost Hin's Fury
Shou Lung Wall Fragment
Dream Arrow
Touch of Death

Made in the image of Kelemvor's most favored weapon and blessed by the highest clergy of his church, this blade was created to protect the most faithful followers of the Lord of the Dead. Even as the sword is meant to protect those who guide the dead to their final rest, it is a potent weapon against those who would seek to disturb it, and is enchanted with additional powers against the vile abominations known as the undead.
Ra Bane Blade

An artifact held in high regard by the gray orc tribes, this axe was supposedly the very weapon used by the orc god Grummsh to kill the Mulhorandi deity Ra in a great battle. Though time and wear have leached some of the power from the weapon - and whether or not the legend of its use is true - the magic in this battleaxe remains strong, and imbues its user with some of Grummsh's own vicious nature.
Faraneyth's Redemption

After a cursed suit of armor drove the noble Faraneyth to frenzy and murder, he was cast from the paladinhood of Torm and forced to wander for years, preaching the worship of his deity from town to town. After stumbling upon a dark cult who had infiltrated a nearby temple, Faraneyth rallied the people to seek the truth about the impostors. Stirred by his passionate orations, a group of villagers marched with him into the temple and fought valiantly against the evil cultists, decimating their forces. Faraneyth himself was grieviously wounded by the cult leader in the battle, but before he passed from the world, a great eagle appeared by his side, healing his wounds and once again gracing him with the power of Torm. His belt - which had been removed to try and treat his wounds - was graced with a fraction of this power, and has remained an example both of Torm's forgiveness and the paladin's steadfast bravery and desire for truth.
Belt of Raumathar

This belt was uncovered in the Ring of the Gray Flames, a ruin on the edge of the Endless Wastes. Though its history is unknown, its powers (and where it was found) suggest the powerful item is of Raumathari origin.
The Raumathari were powerful evokers and enemies of Narfell and a handful of battlemages still study Raumathari arcana. As this belt bestows spells and powers an evoker might already possess, it likely belonged to a close ally of a battlemage instead of to the sorcerer who created it.
Reverberating Bolt
Dream Bolt
Longstrider's Steps

A favored soul of the god Shaundakul, Merina Longstrider was a sun elf regarded as an anomaly amongst her peers. Though it might have seemed a cruel trick that the Windrider would smile and bestow his wanderlust on someone from such an insular culture, it never seemed to bother Merina: her heart lay in the road ahead of her, and even after she left, her longing to discover new things and uncover new mysteries stayed with many of the young elves of Evermeet. The day she struck out on her own to wander the Realms, these boots appeared on the road, new and finely-crafted, and she knew at once they were meant for her. That these boots are no longer on Merina's feet does not mean her tale has ended - perhaps she merely traded them for a newer or more interesting pair.
Simbulmyn Bracers

Home to the highest concentration of half-elves, Algarond keeps the power of the Red Wizards from rapidly expanding to the western lands. The kingdom is ruled by Simbul, a powerful sorceress-queen, and the Simbulmyn are her trusted palace guard who serve as both protectors and elite spies.
Reverberating Bullet
Dream Bullet
Steadfast Chain
This chain mail is granted by Kelemvor to his most trusted defenders at the City of Judgment.
Shroud of the Elder Doom

Intimidating in size and shape both, cloaks of this nature were only worn by the highest in the Myrkulite clergy, those known by the grim honorific of 'Elder Doom.' Since Myrkul's death, few of these have managed to make it to the outside world, and slip out of the former Death God's grasp... surprising, since many Elder Dooms supposedly burned themselves alive in their own robes, unwilling to let themselves or their artifacts touch the hands of the unworthy.
Finch's Comforting Cloak

In the early days of his travels, Finch found Mayram, a monk of Torm, protecting a fellow group of travelers from a group of bandits. After helping her fight them off, he agreed to walk with her a ways farther. As they traveled together, the two became close friends, and Finch found himself falling in love with the young monk. Knowing they would part ways soon, and that their chosen lifestyles would never match, Finch gave Mayram his magical cloak, his most prized possession. The night before they were to arrive at their destination, they were attacked by a group of Malarite beast cultists, and the two fought vainly against greater strength and numbers. Finch fell before their assault, gravely wounded - but Mayram gave her last strength to save him, fighting until all of their enemies had been slain. She then gave the dying Finch back his cloak so that he could benefit from its magics - and perished immediately afterwards. Finch did his best to try and have her fellow monks resurrect her: but they only told him that her spirit had been taken into the very court of Torm, and that they could never undo so great an honor. Wracked with guilt and his unspoken feelings, Finch sold the cloak to a merchant and gave the money to the church, and again went on his travels... and sung of Mayram only once since.
Binder's Robes

At first glance, these robes look like ordinary guard worn by the Red Wizards of Thay. Closer inspection reveals that they are much more, with their origin being the Academy of Shapers and Binders in Thaymount.
Club of Submission

Once wielded by the most feared of Thayan slavemasters, the Club of Submission was used to discipline only the most dangerous of slaves. Though often other slavers warned of keeping such a powerful weapon in such close proximity to those it was meant to dominate, it was not until a young slave named Zarine managed to woo it from a careless master's hand, allowing her to slay him with it and escape. The Red Wizards themselves demanded ownership of the weapon after that, fearing what might have become had Zarine taken the weapon with her... or had attempted to free more slaves with it as well.
Myr Styah'be'eh

Scholars have long argued over the nature of this blade, claming it as a part of many ancient empires - Mulhorandi, Netherese, Imaskari - but its construction defies the conventions of any known civilization. One young wizard, promptly laughed into obscurity, once put forth an argument that the item was actually of kobold make, that its name - considered untranslatable by all others who had studied it - meant something like "master stabby" in an obscure dialect of that dimunitive people. The scholar's final argument was that as harmless as many consider kobold to be today, they do claim their lineage from dragons - and if this blade is any proof, a weapon does not have to look magnificent to be viciously effective.
Teeth of Firemane

Sacred to Nobanion, king of beasts and ally of Mielikki, hated enemy of Malar - the Roar of Shadows infused these lion's teeth with the strength of Nobanion, and these weapons remain dedicated to completing the defeat of that night and wiping out the evil brood of the Black-Blooded Pard.
Anhur's Hand

Brought over from his former world and once wielded by the Mulhorandi god Anhur's favorite captain, this blade fell from its wielder's hand when they were slain fighting the Imaskari that enslaved the people of Mulhorand. Though the Mulhorandi eventually won their freedom and the Imaskari empire fell, this blade was passed on to those who would become oppressors themselves - the Thayans.
Sey'ryu's Scales

Cut from the hide of the once powerful blue dragon, Sey'ryu, these scales function as a suit of full plate armor. Sey'ryu was the first (and currently) only dragon to ever assault the City of Judgment.

Though at first glance they hold the appearance of simple hide gloves, these gauntlets carry within them the strength and purpose of a powerful wolf telthor. When worn, the strength of the wolf fills the user, and unarmed strikes against an enemy leave tears and great wounds - the great claws of the spirit making their mark on its foes.
Sacred Hands

Only the most devoted monks of the order of the Guiding Hand are even allowed to see the power of these gloves on display - how this pair fell into the clutches of a common merchant is paradoxical. Only the most tested and devout are ever allowed to use the Sacred Hands. The deepest understanding of balance is required, the interplay of light and darkness, heat and cold... and the key function of the gloves themselves: healing and harming.
Grips of Gond

These pair of gloves once belonged to Raj Al'Lake, a masterful craftsman. Raj was so in tune with the art that it impressed Gond himself. After his death, Raj's masterful skill was then passed onto his gloves with the help of Gond's blessing.
Cat Queen's Claws

Back before Sharess subsumed the portfolio of Felidae - a deity of nomads and felines - and let her wanderlust carry her across the Realms, she was Bast, Mulhorandi goddess of cats and loyal lieutenant to Anhur. To honor their patron, her clergy made these gloves, carefully crafted to show their goddess's grace, charm, and power. However, as time has passed, the item itself has showed changes as Sharess has changed, making some enchantments more powerful... and adding a worrisome tendency to succumb to mental spells, even as Sharess herself once fell under the sway of the shadowy deity Shar.
Runescarred Greatsword

This sword bears ritual carvings all up and down its length - mimicking the marks of the runescarred berskers who have wielded it the most - and like them, marks and nicks from wear and long use have blended into the body of the blade.
Thayan Knight Halfplate
This halfplate is awarded to the finest of Thayan Knights, both to improve their combat prowess and to make them more subserviant to the Red Wizards.
Kepeturi Crest
This heavy shield was once held in the Mulhorandi prayer towers of Kepetur. After the towers fell to the archfiend Eltab and his minions, it ended up in the powerful hands of the Thayans.
Finch's Finest Hat

For a short time, the city of Mulsantir hosted Finch, a notorious half-elf bard who claimed he was on the run from a Cormyrian bounty hunter - escaping a bounty placed on his head for charming the wrong noble's daughter. While spending his time trying to woo ladies, he bemoaned the loss of his beloved hat back in Cormyr, as he was forced to leave it behind in his haste to flee (lest he stay too long and lose his head along with his hat). One young and talented ethran managed to weave her powers into a new hat for him, more glorious and powerful than the last. However, before he could wear it long, she caught him cozying up to another young witch - and once again Finch was forced to fly away in haste, leaving another excellent hat behind.
Tragedian

A master maskcrafter once joined a travelling group of actors - but much to his dismay, he and his cohorts found the road quite unsafe, and more than once were forced to fight off bandits. Unwilling to be bullied, the maskcrafter poured all of his skill and cunning into a pair of masks - elegant masterworks as well as useful weapons... and indeed, one night the company was called upon to use them when a local warlord captured the troupe, and called them to perform for his liking. The company's male lead wore the mask the crafter called the Tragedian, and used its power to lull the warlord and his men into a daze with his oratory, then unleashed on them a cripping sadness. When the female lead had used the powers of the Comedian mask, the company attacked. Later, the actors fled into the night, carrying with them the spoils of the warlord's stronghold as their 'payment' - and a battered and bruised audience wondering if they'd just seen the worst play of their lives or the best.
Ice Troll Helmet

Passed down from generation to generation of Rashemi warriors, this helm provides its user with enhanced vitality, and resistance to attacks of both physical and magical natures. However, this helm's magics favor strength over grace, and the rushing charges encouraged by its user's raging have often led to this helm changing hands perhaps more frequently than it should.
Chromatic Crown

Granted to only the most dedicated of the Dragon Queen's followers, this circlet is designed to protect its wearer with the powers of all five chromatic dragons. However, instead of focusing solely on giving one key item so much power, it could be argued that the Mother of Dragons forgot the one enchantment that could have made the most difference in its use to her: a spell to keep the disloyal from wearing it.
Deathless Diadem

Once a sacred katana from the imperial court of Shou, the poor combination of an especially canny thief and an especially drowsy guard set this powerful artifact into the wilds along the great twisting Golden Way. It was formed from a slice of an unknown substance, cut from another plane, and forged in an act that drank its creator's soul away... and that the blade seems to be growing slowly more powerful - with a sinking hunger that seems to match your own.
Sivlem

Crafted to be an intelligent weapon who inspired its wielder to acts of stunning bravery and heroism, Sivlem was to be the pinnacle of master smith Nevik's work, the finest sword in Amn. Indeed it is a handsome blade, humming quite literally with power and wickedly sharp. But when drawn forth for the first time and commanded to speak, the blade remained silent... and Nevik realized in horror what had happened. The enchantment to grant the item intelligence was added too late... and the plain but servicable blade he'd made immediately afterwards had inherited the self-awareness meant for its more magnificent sibling. Though Sivlem has still had a glorious history of participating in the doing of great deeds, its vanished twin has criss-crossed the land far more often, skipping from one adventurer to the next and attempting to keep a cheerful outlook - despite its owners' unhappy tendency to either discard it for something more powerful or be slain!
Finch's Subtle Lute

Before he saw fit to take up residence in Neverwinter, Cain Lethellon was yet another travelling bard - though doing his best to disguise the fact that he came from a family with a substantial amount of money. For a time, he even followed Finch, the notorious bard - but finally, frustrated that he could not match the half-elf's skill, Cain challenged him to a duel of lutes. Knowing full well that the other bard would not refuse a duel of honor - and moreover did not own such an instrument - Cain pretended to be generous and commissioned a fine instrument to be made for him... while promising the craftsman a large sum of gold to flaw the lute with warping spells. Finch knew full well of Cain's attempted trickery, and promised the craftsman a greater sum for a well-crafted one instead. When the duel arrived, Finch beat Cain soundly - and told a stupefied crowd that only the craftsman's creation could have ever let him play so well. As a result, Cain left the city in disgrace, the craftsman enjoyed a fine boost in business, and Finch himself sold the lute for a handy sum, preferring instead to rely on his dulcet voice. He would admit graciously later on that he'd taught Cain everything he knew - "Except how to be a pompous fathead," Finch would add. "He picked that one up on his own."
Orb of Elemental Summoning
Aromal's Truth
Ring of Seething Hatred

This band appears very plain and looks to be constructed of solid bone. A burning, prickling sensation envelops your arm when you hold this ring in your grasp and just being in the vicinity of the ring makes your neck hair stand on end.
Bone Dancer's Ring

Crafted from stone or ivory, the power of this ring belies its simple appearance. Previously a Bone Ring carved by the Myrkulite faithful, when the wearer was raised to the promising rank of Bone Dancer, their rings were taken and consecrated with additional dark blessings, bringing them closer to the nature of the undead that they saw fit to use - and often emulate.
Imaedril's Respite

After rather foolishly scorning the affections of a priestess of Umberlee, the sorcerer Imaedril shortly thereafter found himself surrounded by the priestess's wereshark minions, and unceremoniously turned into a seagull. After a year of languishing in his feathery form, the sorcerer cleverly found a way to reveal to Umberlee that her priestess had been stealing money from the church.
Umberlee, full of rage, drowned the priestess accordingly, and freed Imaedril from his avian form. Fleeing as far inland as was possible, the sorcerer swore off any dealings with the clergy, and spent countless hours crafting himself a ring that he felt would protect himself from both any transformative spells - and give him ample protection from any shapeshifting servants.
Nentyarch's Band

The ring bears the mark of three concentric circles that signifies the Circle of Leth. Led by the Nentyarch this hierarchy is an incredibly powerful group of druids that dwells in the Forest of Lethyr near Rawlinswood, to the northwest of Rashemen. The ring looks ancient and its surfaces are well worn - not through normal wear, but as if it had been exposed to the elements for decades.
Lyonsbane Ring
Said to have been a ring worn by Kelemvor as he ascended to godhood, this plain band bears almost no identifying marks - but holding it alone gives one an almost palpable sense of comfort and calm.
Astral Rodent Charm
This small charm is a wooden carving of what looks like a little fuzzy rat with a tiny snout. "For M" is scratched carefully into the bottom.
Scimitar of Mielikki
The scimitar is the favored weapon of Mielikki, the Forest Queen. She is one of "the Three."
Scythe of Chauntea
The scythe is the favored weapon of Chauntea, the Great Mother. She is one of "the Three."
Rage of the Lost Hin

This bow once belonged to Nilon Redleaf, a warrior from a small village of halflings in Shaar. While he was out hunting for a village harvest day, Moander decided to poison the community's harvest wine with a deadly plague - as a result, Nilon returned to find everyone in his village dead or dying, and could do nothing but watch as his whole family succumbed to the evil god's trick. Full of rage and grief, Nilon cursed the halfling pantheon for their inability to protect his people, and swore revenge on the greater gods for turning a blind eye to Moander's vile deed. The young halfling traveled far across the Realms, honing his skills and searching for a way to exact revenge. When he heard of Akachi's Crusade, he begged to be included, and fought with great abandon - falling at last at the very gates of the City of Judgment, next to the walls he'd sworn to bring down. His desire for vengeance persists on after death, inhabiting the nature of his favorite bow and imbuing every arrow it touches with his rage.
Fingerbone's Name

This blade once belonged to Yyev, a particularly feared specialty priest of Myrkul, who'd left her home and family. She took with her only this blade, which changed and was twisted even as Yyev grew in power and climbed the ranks of the Myrkulite priesthood. When Myrkul died, Yyev fell on her sword - hoping in vain that her death would reunite her with her god.
Shuriken of Mystra
The shuriken is the favored weapon of Mystra, the Lady of Mysteries. She is one of "the Three."
Reaper's Despair

Long ago, worshippers of Talona attacked and blighted the grove of Syrune, a young wild elven druid. She fought back and drove them away, but the damage had already been done: the creatures in the area went mad, rejecting the forest gods and dying frenzied and in pain, despite all her efforts to save them. Syrune herself became infected with the Talontar plague, and was cast out from her tribe - she went to Silvanus for aid, but he could not heal her - and even her once-despised enemy Talona would not accept her as a worshipper and remove her agony. In her rage, the young elf declared her independence from the gods, and set up her grove as a place forbidden to all, blighted or not... In the interest of keeping it that way, she fashioned a weapon that reflected her own pestilent and broken soul, and wielded it with a murderous fury, slaying anything that came near. Eventually a nearby human settlement and reclusive wild elves banded together to defeat her, and though Syrune's life was snuffed out, her pain and rage remains in this simple sickle, ready once again to destroy at a master's whim.
Dragon Pebbles

Said to be stolen from the Shou court by a courtesan thief close to the Chancellor, this valuable artifact remained in the thief's hands for little time before it was lost in the storm of people and belongings swept along to Thesk after the Horde invasion. 'Rescued' by a too-clever merchant and passed down the Golden Way, this unassuming sling - pride of the Shou Lung empire - now lies within your grasp. Whether or not it does in fact throw pieces of the great Pao Hu Jen - the petrified sea dragon that now walls off Shou Lung - likely matters little: it is its impressive damage against your foes that holds the most weight.
Frost Harpoon

Holding this weapon in your hands gives you an almost palpable sensation of loss - coupled with a feeling of deathless, unending patience. It is unknown how this weapon traveled so far from its frozen home and the tribe that once crafted it, but its magic remains potent despite the distance, chilling the very air around it. Written in small script along the haft, a small passage reads simply: "Until Ulutiu wakes, none will make me sleep."

I cannot endure this any longer - our paths must part.
I don't care if you leave, but your equipment remains here.
| Chaotic |Now that you are disarmed, prepare to die.
| Evil |There is one last thing you need to leave behind - your spirit.
If that is all, don't let me keep you. Farewell.
| Difficult Check |[Bluff/Lie] Gann, I may not always say it, but I need your skills. Without you, I will certainly fail.
| Difficult check |[Taunt] Is Gann-o-Dreams now Gann-o-Cowardice? Run, then, if you don't mind the title catching up with you.
| Easier check |[Taunt] Feel free to leave, Okku is the only ally I need.
We shall see. Let us move on.
I'm just glad you're sticking with us. Come on.
I expect you to prove it. Our journey awaits.
I expect you to prove your worth. Our journey awaits.
Trust in your pride if you must - but do so quietly.

Emerging from the chamber where you awoke, you felt an unsettling presence within you. Shortly after, this presence lashed out, unbidden, consuming a spirit wolf and healing your wounds.
You suspect that this presence continues to fester inside you... and will likely make trouble for you again. If you can discover how you came to Rashemen, and who tore the shard of Gith from your chest, you may also learn the secret of this mysterious presence.

You have defeated the bear god Okku, but your struggle has caused a dark hunger to awaken within you.
It would seem that you must feed this hunger with spirits, or it will ultimately consume you from within, and destroy you utterly.
Okku - and the native Rashemi - refer to you as a spirit-eater... apparently a curse that is not unknown in this country.
{Z}The Voice of Kelemvor

Zoab wants to strike down the Voice of Kelemvor, Kelemvor's most powerful divine servant. The Voice pronounces sentence on the doomed souls in Kelemvor's name, and silencing him would be great symbolic victory for the Third Crusade.

The Voice of Kelemvor has been silenced and the souls of the doomed have been granted a reprieve, temporary as it is. Zoab is certain this victory will shake the planes themselves, though even he is uncertain what effect it will ultimately have.

The Voice of Kelemvor has been silenced and the souls of the doomed have been granted a reprieve, temporary as it is. Zoab was slain during the fighting, but he would no doubt agree that this victory will shake the planes themselves. What effect it will ultimately have, however, remains uncertain.
{Z}Raid on Eternity's End
{Z}Holding the Gate

With the Third Crusade assaulting different sections of the city, the defenders will be spread thinner than usual. If you and Sey'ryu can defeat the forces assigned to guard the City Gate, the militia will be forced to divert even more of their numbers to watch the Gate for demonic incursions.

You defeated all three waves of attackers at the Gate, and any remaining forces have wisely chosen to remain inside the city nearby. With the gate guardians defeated, they dare not risk deploying elsewhere lest demons slip through the now-unguarded gate. Sey'ryu declared her debt to Akachi paid and left.

Although Sey'ryu was slain during the battle, you still managed to defeat all three waves of attackers at the Gate, and any remaining forces have wisely chosen to remain inside the city nearby. With the gate guardians defeated, they dare not risk deploying elsewhere lest demons slip through the now-unguarded gate.
You arrived too late to save Sey'ryu at the city gates. Fortunately, the dragon seems to have eliminated the majority of the militia there before falling.

You arrived just in time to rescue Sey'ryu at the city gates. The dragon slew the majority of the militia there, though she was badly wounded during the battle. Her debt to Akachi fulfilled, she then left the area.

The solar Zoab seeks to attack the Basilica of Lost Hope and strike down the Voice of Kelemvor, the Lord of the Dead's most powerful divine servant tasked with pronouncing sentence upon the doomed souls. Zoab must be stopped, for a victory at the Basilica could inspire further rebellion in the city or even throughout the planes.
You were able to thwart Zoab's plan to silence the Voice of Kelemvor and shattered the hopes of the rebels.

Zoab has been slain, but the damage has already been done. The death of the Voice of Kelemvor has served as a rallying cry for the Third Crusade, and a good number of the city's militia has defected and joined the rebellion.

You arrived at the Basilica of Lost Hope too late and found the Voice of Kelemvor slain. According to Zoab, a number of the False militia have joined the rebellion. You must defeat Zoab and prevent him from causing any further damage.
{Z}Demons at the Gates

Taking advantage of the chaos caused by the rebellion, demons from the Abyss have opened a portal to the Fugue Plane and are attempting to slip into the city and steal souls. You decided to stay at the city gates for the time being and help the militia repel the attack.
You crushed each wave of demons that emerged from the portal. Surprised by the fierce defense, the demons closed the portal and called an end to their ill-fated invasion.
You slew the balor lord and his minions, and the portal to the Abyss closed, preventing any additional demons from invading the city.
You've been informed that the battle with the demons at the city gates is going poorly. You should make your way there to lend aid at the earliest opportunity.

You arrived at the city gates to find the militia slain and the gates themselves in the hands of a balor lord and his minions. You must slay them them to close the portal to the Abyss and prevent any more demons from entering the city.

Safiya has confided that her mother sent her to find you in the barrow, and to bring you to a woman called Lienna. Although Safiya has never met this woman before, she believes that she is a friend. Hopefully, Lienna will be able to tell you how you came to Rashemen, and who tore the shard of Gith from your chest.
Apparently, Lienna is the proprietor of a theater called the Veil. It is located in the town of Mulsantir.

Upon entering the Veil to seek Lienna, you found the place overrun by Red Wizards and their minions.
Magda, one of the actors at the Veil, gave you an odd black stone, and told you that Lienna has retreated to the "shadowy reflection" of the theater. To find her, you need only bring the Shadow Stone to the back corner of Lienna's bedroom, near her mirror.

Lienna, proprietor of the Veil Theater, has apparently destroyed herself to avoid capture by Red Wizards.
Safiya has suggested that you find and question the Veil's actors, who escaped the theater when you arrived.
You had hoped that Lienna might tell you how you came to Rashemen, and who tore the shard from your chest. Though Lienna is dead, her actors may still have useful information...

Upon exiting the Veil Theater, you were confronted by several Rashemi Witches.
The Witches clearly do not trust outsiders, and they claim to be holding the Veil's actors in a "safe place." The Witches will not permit you to question the actors until you have confronted the army of spirits that awaits you outside the town.

Now that Okku's spirit army has lifted its siege of Mulsantir, the Witches have released Lienna's actors and returned them to the Veil Theater.
Whenever you wish, you may question them about Lienna - who she was, and what she might have known about you... and the curse that now afflicts you.
[Okku dealt with - again. Return to Magda at the Veil.]

Magda has given you the key to a "secret room" that once belonged to Lienna, former proprietor of the Veil.
From Magda's description, Lienna may have had some dealings with a Thayan wizard. Worse, Lienna may have been the one who cut the shard from your chest.
The only way to know for certain is to investigate her locked room, which lies in the Shadow Plane version of the Veil.

You encountered the creatures who brought you to Rashemen and placed you in Okku's barrow. They were a group of shadow gargoyles, apparently acting on Lienna's bidding.
The gargoyles did not know why you were chosen by Lienna and her "red twin." Nor did they know why you were left in the cavern, or what happened to you there.
But the gargoyles believed that Lienna and her ally were acting on advice from the Slumbering Coven, a collection of nine powerful hags who dwell in a sunken Imaskari ruin, to the east of Mulsantir. Since Lienna is dead, and her ally is missing, your will have to seek your answers from the hags, themselves.

You have followed Lienna into the Shadow Plane version of the Veil Theater.
Unfortunately, a group of Red Wizards has arrived here already - and they seem equally intent upon finding Lienna.

In the town of Mulsantir, you met two half-celestial siblings - Efrem and Susah. Their sister, Kaelyn the Dove, has apparently gone missing, and they suspect that she has run afoul of trouble in Shadow Mulsantir - the Shadow Plane version of the town.
If you are able to find Kaelyn and bring her back safely, Efrem and Susah have promised to reward you... and to assist you in your battle against Okku's spirit army, if you still need their aid.

Although the Witches of Mulsantir will not help you against Okku's army, they have given you access to the town prison. Any prisoner who fights by your side against the bear god will be granted freedom, and a full pardon... provided they survive the battle.
The prison is located on the northern edge of town, behind the Temple of Kelemvor.
You convinced one of the convicts in the Mulsantir Prison to join your cause. This prisoner - a roguish hagspawn shaman named Gann - has joined your party.

You managed to defeat Okku's army without recruiting any help from the prison. However, you suspect that the Witches' offer still stands... if any of the prisoners are willing to accompany you on your travels, you may freely recruit them at any time.
The prison is located on the northern edge of town, behind the Temple of Kelemvor.
[Player refused to give the Tome to Yusev. Yusev is mad and won't talk anymore.]

Upon arriving at the Wells of Lurue, Okku was seized by a powerful recollection of your surroundings. He claimed to hear the voices of his clan upon the wind, and he urged you to pursue these voices deeper into the crags...

At a sacred pool in the Wells of Lurue, you encountered the spirits of Okku's ancestors - three massive bears called Kuma, Jabar, and Wotomo.
These spirits recounted the suffering and extinction of Okku's clan, after he abandoned them. The spirits seemed intent upon vengeance, but you managed to soothe their anger, and they allowed you to leave in peace.

At a sacred pool in the Wells of Lurue, you encountered the spirits of Okku's ancestors - three massive bears called Kuma, Jabar, and Wotomo.
These spirits recounted the suffering and extinction of Okku's clan, after he abandoned them. Intent upon revenge, the three spirits attacked your party.

At a sacred pool in the Wells of Lurue, you encountered the spirits of Okku's ancestors - three massive bears called Kuma, Jabar, and Wotomo.
They have asked that you bring Okku to speak with them.

Safiya stood on the dais and you projected her reflection around the academy to a dais in another room.
An image of her appeared there momentarily (although her face was older and might as well have been her mother), and it left behind what might have been its equivalent to a soul. If this contraption was meant to replicate a person, its designer fell just short of his or her goal.

Gann stood on the dais and you projected his reflection around the academy to a dais in another room.
An image of him appeared there momentarily (although it resembled some of his less-handsome brethren), and it left behind what might have been its equivalent to a soul. If this contraption was meant to replicate a person, its designer fell just short of his or her goal.

Thael-ka and Oronock, twin pit fiends bound in summoning circles in the instructors' quarters level of the Academy of Shapers and Binders, have told you that they are in possession of a rare soul - one they feel you will take a keen interest in.
Naturally, there is a catch. They want a rare soul in trade. Unfortunately, they are in complete disagreement about the what the qualities of that soul should be, and many of the qualities are wholly contradictory with one another.
Thael-ka wants the soul of a virtuous, yet wretched being. Oronock, on the other hand, has requested the soul of a depraved, yet prosperous person.
As they have expressed that you must bring them only one soul that bears all these qualities, you may need to enlist the help of someone knowledgeable about the crafting of souls.

You spoke with Poruset, who has offered to fuse two souls together for you. He gave you a pass so that you might remove two souls from the depository to bring to him.
To accommodate the devils' wishes, you are looking for a soul that is rich but depraved, and one that is poor and selfless.
This key looks rather nondescript. You hope it will unlock the front door.

You have lost control of the hunger for spirits that has recently manifested inside of you. Your body now requires a periodic influx of energy obtained through the consumption of spirits, or it will eventually wither and die.
The vertical green bar represents your present level of spirit energy. It will drop over time (except during conversation), and as it falls, you will weaken at an accelerating rate. Each of the watermarks on the bar denotes a point at which your curse worsens to a new stage of debilitation. There are six stages of this affliction, the final of which is death. You may mouse over the watermark icons at any time to see what effects a particular stage of the affliction carries.

Several new abilities are available to you (via the feats tab of your character sheet) that will provide a means to replenish your spirit energy:
Devour Spirit can be cast on spirits (elementals, fey, and incorporeal undead). It yields a fixed amount of spirit energy, plus a bonus if it kills the target. Killing blows will also grant you a spirit essence, which can be used in crafting. Targets who are "Near Death" will die when devoured.
Suppress can be cast instead of Devour Spirit. It typically generates less spirit energy, but it does not require the consumption of a spirit. Its effectiveness increases if spirits are nearby.

The horizontal bar below the spirit energy bar is a measurement of your craving for spirits. The more you crave spirits, the faster your spirit energy is used up.
Giving in to your urge to devour spirits more than once per day will tend to make you crave them more, while actively fighting to gain control over your hunger through the Suppress ability will ease that craving. Use extreme caution when deciding whether to devour spirits if you have already done so once that day - what may seem like a safe move to keep your health high could quite quickly lead you down a slippery slope where you are in constant need of spirits to devour just to stay alive.
You may minimize your spirit-energy bar at any time by clicking the button at its upper right corner. All of the key details will still be made visible to you in this mode.

Ring of the Frozen Falls

Ages ago, a Rashemi youth camped at the Falls of Erech, the massive waterfall that marks the northwestern-most part of Rashemen. It was custom for youths leaving on the daijemma - journey of adulthood - to stay there at least one night, and the young man was eager to observe this tradition, giving his offering to the roaring waters before lying down to sleep. As the youth slumbered, however, warriors from a nearby Nar barbarian tribe moved toward him, intent on murder and theft. However, before they could harm him, a spirit possessed the youth, and allowed him to defend himself with stunning skill and savagery. As the spirit fled his body, the youth looked around at his slain attackers in wonder, and noticed a strange new ring on his finger - an additional gift from the spirits to protect him from harm.

I am {nah-KAH-tah}Nakata, a guardian of this barrow. This holy place holds the physical remains of the land's greatest spirits.
Now, you will tell us how you managed to get down here without being seen.

{noticing the player}But you were alone when you went below...
{quietly, remembering}My name... it was {nah-KAH-tah}Nakata. {a little frustrated}Memories flow together in this place... it is difficult to know which are your own.
{remembering more}My howls led an army of beasts across the groaning ice of {TEER-oo-lag}Tirulag... and there I died, struck down by an eater of souls - a monster that wore the skin of a man.

| First time meeting Efrem and Susah, outside the Veil after the witches appear. |We couldn't help but overhear. An army of angry spirits awaits you at the gates of Mulsantir. You will perhaps require more help against such a host.
My bow and my brother's sword will aid you, should you agree to first help us find our lost sister, Kaelyn the Dove.

We arrived just before the bear king laid siege. He will not let any pass until he is quelled or untill he tastes your heartsblood.
Our wings enable us to move with greater alacrity on land, but sadly they cannot carry us to the heavens like our full-blooded celestial progenitors.
Our siblings - there are five, including Kaelyn - are known as "the Menagerie." We adopt the titles of noble creatures out of respect for nature.
The Menagerie has long travelled together, led by our eldest sister. But since Kaelyn was exiled from our grandfather's court in Celestia, we have been distraught.
Will you help us find Kaelyn that we may persuade her back into the fold?
Kaelyn came here seeking the abandoned stronghold of Myrkul, the Death God's Vault, which is in Shadow Mulsantir.
Entering Myrkul's sanctum would be a violation of our faith to Kelemvor.
Kaelyn has... abandoned her faith in Kelemvor. For this she was exiled from our grandfather's court. She now follows Ilmater, the god of martyrs.
We hope to find our sister and convince her not to become a martyr herself...
Yes, it is said that Mulsantir has thin boundaries between the Prime and the Plane of Shadow, especially at night, or in dark places.
Yes, if the rumors are true there are many "weak spots" where one can cross to the Plane of Shadow at night. Perhaps a thorough search of the city would reveal some of these to you.
As you may know, Myrkul is the former God of the Dead, slain by Mystra in the Time of Troubles. Cyric took Myrkul's place, and then was deposed by Kelemvor, the present God of the Dead.
The Death God's Vault has been abandoned since Myrkul's death. It was used as a library and a prison, and a secure place to store things valuable to the Myrkulite faith.

Statue of Mystra
This statue depicts the goddess Mystra, called Mistress of Magic and Mother of Mysteries. Mystra is believed to be the embodiment of the Weave of magic that envelopes the world.
Statue of Chauntea

This statue represents the Earthmother, Chauntea, also known as the Grain Goddess and the Great Mother. Chauntea is the goddess of agriculture and summer. Some of her worshippers claim that Chauntea is the creator of all mortal races.
Statue of Mielikki
This statue bears the graceful visage of the goddess Mielikki, known as "Our Lady of the Forest." Mielikki is the patron goddess of rangers, druids, and dryads.
