This tattered, blood-stained tome appears to be the journal of a former vremyonni. Most of the entries appear to ramble on about exacting revenge on his arrogant vremyonni "brothers", but a few select passages catch your eye. "15th of Mirtul - I have finally done it! I was able to animate a corpse and breathe life back into it! Well... it was the corpse of a diseased rat, which seem to be everywhere in this cave, but it was a corpse nonetheless. Unfortunately, I cannot let anyone see my creation, lest I be cast off from here or worse. I guess I will have to dispose of him." "25th of Mirtul - I think I saw Barovik going through my things this morning. I can't be sure of what he has seen. I need to be much more cautious in hiding my forbidden tomes of necromantic lore. I must go probe Barovik and see what he knows." "25th of Mirtul - Barovik dodged all of my questions regarding his activities this morning. I cannot take the chance that he has seen any of my forbidden codices. I would eliminate him, but that would only cause an investigation. Leaving is the only option. Leaving this cave means leaving all of Rasheman, abandoning all I love. No matter, it must be done." "3rd of Kythorn - Damn the Old Ones! They never taught me anything of survival in the wilderness. This morning's attempt to catch a meal went horribly. All of nature's creatures seem to recoil from me. I wonder if they can sense some sort of taint upon me. What I wouldn't give for some of Jerryn's rabbit stew. Those carrots were so tender and... I need to stop this nonsense and find a town that I can take refuge in." "11th of Kythorn - Off in the distance, I see... large walls! Even in my weakened state I think I can make it there before nightfall. I must make it there before nightfall." "7th of Flamerule - Mulsantir. That is the name of this city. I have been in my new "abode" for several weeks now. Oh, I love it here, in this dank, dark, abandoned cellar. If only there were more disease-ridden vermin, it would be just like I was back in the caves with the other vremyonni. I live like a peasant, now. I had to beg for food when I first made it to this place. Beg! I will make them pay for what they have subjected me to." "9th of Eleint - How I think about slowly snuffing out the life of everyone of those arrogant vremyonni. I think constantly about how I was ejected from my life, just because I sought to master all forms of magic. It will take many lifetimes to exact all of the revenge I have planned for them. Many lifetimes... that gives me an idea." "23rd of Uktar - I have figured out a way to cheat Kelemvor! This will take much time and lots of my resources, but it will be worth it to see the agony and hear the screams of my "brothers." I must find a suitable vessel for my soul. Also, one of my texts mentions something called "The Tome of Profane Rebirth." I must find it!" "1st of Nightal - Luck upon luck! I have found the general location of this Tome of Profane Rebirth. It resides on the Plane of Shadow. Not only that, but from my preliminary reading, it appears that Mulsantir is the perfect place to enter the Plane of Shadow. The way to cross planes is through the temple to the Death God." "14th of Ches - Rubbish! So close to my goal, only to be stopped by an impassable barrier. After making it to the Plane of Shadows, I have learned that the Tome I need is in the Death God's Vault. I refuse to go in there, even for this. It matters not. I will proceed with the ritual here on this shadow plane. Now to summon some servants to watch over me..." The entries past this point are too blood-soaked to read.

What about that? Can you duplicate a soul?
Atsu, what do you think?
No.
And why is that?
It loses fidelity in the replication process.
The only way to keep the qualities of a soul pure is to split them off of the original, rather than duplicate them.
But then of course neither of the split pieces can ever be completely whole again.
You've kept up on your readings, Atsu, clearly. But what has he failed to do?
Moswen, what do you think?
He's assuming something can't be done just because it hasn't yet.
Precisely. What are we here for, Atsu, if not to challenge such notions?
So let's say I have a soul, and I split it. Which piece retains the memories?
Moswen, you look like you know.
I thought I did, but now I'm not sure.
Why is that?
Well, wouldn't the memories be in both?
Interesting. Explain.
Memory exists independent of a soul, but may imprint itself throughout a soul, if the memory is strong enough.
So the same memory might find its way into both parts after the split. Or it might just exist in one.
And it might be stronger in one than it is in the other.
But given its independence, unless it is erased, memory will continue to bind the two pieces together, even after the split.
Take heed, class. Erase those memories carefully, or you'll have some very disoriented homunculi when you implant the split souls in tomorrow's lab.
Mistress Zerzura - why would removing a soul make the mind deteriorate?
Hmm... think of the soul as a library, if you will. A vast store of information.
The mind is a patron of that library. In every one of its evaluations, it references a part of the soul.
A mind is a logical entity, but that logic is meaningless without a foundation - a proper means of putting it in perspective.
Take away that reference material, and the mind is without a cause for its reasoning. And so it atrophies.
It calculates, but it needs inputs from within as well as without.
The arcane triad is your greatest ally when working with souls.
No other runic symbol draws more power from its environment.
If you keep your angles precise and your dimensions within the parameters of Bastet's second formula, you will harness energy to its maximum potential.
Yes, there is a natural flow to all things, and yes, it is preordained by the gods.
But do not mistake these for the "laws" the mindless chattel take them to be.
For the gods, too, are bound by laws. Indeed, the first gods came into being because a higher law dictated a need for order in the multiverse.
If there are laws above even the greatest lawmakers, then none of their lesser laws is absolute.
We have at our disposal all the tools of the gods. Magic, reason, and will.
The structures they impose can be unmade.
Who better than their most underestimated creation to shed light on their imperfection?
Your projects last week showed no promise.
I am inclined to fail all of you. I tire of your excuses.
When I assign a project that no one yet has successfully completed, I want to see you attack it.
In this field, our greatest innovations come from our mistakes as much as our successes.
I don't care if you weren't able to get the intended result as long as the result you did get was interesting.
How is it that you think we've come as far as we have at this school?
It isn't through success, I can promise you that.

It is not entirely known from where this book from and how it was made - some propose that a wizard crafted it to draw himself closer to the elements; others suggest it came from the dangerous goddess Umberlee; and still more theorize it was crafted by a civilization beneath the waves to protect those of their kin who chose to travel on land. Whatever its origin, its power is obvious.

A favorite item of a young wizard at the Academy of Shapers and Binders at Thaymount, these subtle cloth bracers allowed their user to win more than a few dangerous magical battles, disposing of numerous powerful rivals in the process. It was not long before instructors learned of the items, but they took care not to do anything about it, certain that the problem would take care of itself. And truth be told, they did not have to wait long: the young wizard was found dead of a strange and wasting sickness not long after defeating a chief rival, the slender bracers stolen off of his wrists. Though the items were likely used again, the young wizard's death proved the folly of relying on a single magical object for victory instead of skill - and ruthlessness.

This amulet once belonged to the great warlock Alerun Ophon, who had created an institution not dissimilar from the Academy of Shapers and Binders. With their dark contacts and imbue item ability, warlocks excelled at such research and many came to study and learn from Alerun. While a skilled practitioner of the arts, Alerun had little patience for diplomacy and this ultimately led to his downfall. The Red Wizards saw his school as too great of a threat and demolished it after a fierce magical battle that lit up the skies of Thaymount for miles.

Taken from the ruins of Shandaular - now known as the City of Weeping Ghosts - this item is actually two separate rings fused together by an unbreakable magical bond. Its sad tale springs from Shandaular's final night, when the city was crushed. Two mages - both skilled in the Art, and both deeply in love with the other - swore that if one of them perished, they would bind their soul into a ring so that they could be with the other forever. Tragically, the two were killed at the same moment, and their souls were each sealed away... But the second part of the promise held, and the rings fused themselves together, holding fast to some the magical powers each had in life, and allowing each of the mages to rise as undead forms to protect the rings' user.

Shereboam Raveilwyl was a mage blessed with far more talent than common sense, and had a tendency to panic when he ran out of spells within a battle, lunging instead for a crossbow and attempting to draw on his scant combat training to aid him. Unfortunately, he was none too great a shot, and tended to fire wildly into combat. After more than a few near misses (and one direct hit to the left quadrant of a companion's rear end), his comrades insisted that he either conserve his spells more prudently or do something to improve his aim. Drawing on the deepest reserves of his power, Shereboam made himself a quiver of surpassing quality, granting him the skills of an expert archer. Alas, it came in handy only a handful of times before the mage forgot it on a journey, and caused a less understanding group of fellow adventurers to leave him to the mercy of a beholder at their soonest convenience.

Resilient Trodders

Though bearing an inelegant name, these sturdy boots carry with them a powerful magic. Crafted by a talented young smith, they were to be the masterwork that earned him a right to study under the greatest blacksmith in the city. Instead, he became smitten with a cleric of Helm - and subsequently mocked by his peers, for the cleric was half-orc and ugly to their eyes. Unlike them, the young smith saw the cleric's beauty reflected in her kindness and unwavering devotion, and dedicated himself to the church soon after giving these boots to her. Alas, the smith did not live long in his duities as a Helmite - perishing in the defense of a merchant caravan who had appealed to the church for protection from bandits - but his boots were enchanted to honor his memory and dedication, and the cleric he gifted them to wore them until the day she died.
Bracers of Artifice

Created by ancient Imaskari artificers, bracers such as these hid extraordinary powers underneath their simple copper exteriors. In addition to protecting their user from harm with all the benefits of heavy armor - and none of the drawbacks - they let them focus and collect their arcane energy more efficently.
Bracers of the Inner Planes
These bracers shield the wearer from the hostile environments found in the elemental planes as well as the Positive and Negative Material planes.
Clasps of the Devoted

Durin d'Artham, one of the most devoted paladins of Lathander, lay on his deathbed after decades of service to his god, and decided that he had not done enough to serve his god. Summoning the most accomplished spellcasters available, he begged them to bind his soul into a mighty pair of bracers for centuries to come, granting his strength and skill to those devoted to their deity. The spell worked, and Durin still serves... but unfortunately for him, he forgot to specify which deities would be acceptable to offer devotion to, and thus spent the first few years of his service in the use of a particularly vicious Blackguard of Bane.
Letter from Ivin Borsk

This letter is adorned with several half-finished runes - probably protective enchantments, which the author never had time to complete. The message reads as follows:
"To Grand Master Finlothleer, in Telflamm,
Our journey from Thesk was uneventful, and we have established ourselves in Mulsantir, as ordered.
Our spy, Shelvedar Nuum, has proved helpful, and I commend your wisdom in sending him to prepare the way for us. He enjoys his role as a local wag and drunkard overmuch... though I suppose it endears him to these savage folk.
As expected, the boundaries with the Plane of Shadow are weak in Mulsantir. We have used this fact to our advantage, setting up a refuge near the ferry landing. Several of the prominent merchants have been informed of our presence, and we have begun collecting fees as a price of doing business without incident.
Incredibly, these ignorant brutes have no existing guild of thieves or assassins, so our operations in Mulsantir should proceed unopposed. When you receive this letter, please dispatch the additional agents we discussed. Once they arrive, I will see that local officials, such as the ferry master - a brute of orcish descent - are replaced with our own people.
Your servant,
Ivin Borsk Guildmaster of Shadow, Mulsantir"

You recall the story of the beautiful Rashemi ranger Hulmarra Murnyetha, killed over two centuries ago by a Red Wizard. It is said that her husband's last gift to her, before his own demise several years before her, was a perfectly cut emerald.
According to legend, her spirit remains in the Immil Vale, kidnapping men that remind her of her husband. Hulmarra is seemingly a benevolent spirit, returning her "victims" years later, completely unscathed and looking as youthful as before. If one believes all of the stories they hear in Rashemi taverns and lodges, one would think that half of the nations men have been taken by Hulmarra at some point in their lives.

Cut from the hide of the once powerful blue dragon, Sey'ryu, these scales function as a suit of full plate armor. Sey'ryu was the first (and currently only) dragon to ever assault the City of Judgment.
Thicketfavors

In the ancient days when the Ashenwood was young, and there were those who still called them 'green elves' - gloves like these were worn by an order of wild elven druids and rangers dedicated to protecting the forest and its inhabitants. Now little is left of the order but their memory, and replicas of their gear... and the knowledge of how the Ashenwood has grown and flourished in the ages that have followed.
This strange armor seems almost alive, clicking silently to itself as if home to hundreds of tiny creatures.
Deep Guardian's Plate

In an effort to better protect their soldiers, the artificers of ancient Imaskar set about creating a kind of living symbiote, something that would bond with their user and protect them from harm. Using specimens pulled from the deepest pits of the ocean, the Imaskari spellcasters slowly began to graft these magically-enhanced creatures onto suits of plate mail, weaning them off of salt water and forcing them to rely on magic for nourishment. This technique worked well, allowing the user a far greater resistance to spells than normal... but other magewrights looked upon this creation with a growing fear, worried that a creature that fed on magic might soon grow too hungry and feed upon its masters instead. Because of this, only a few suits of this armor were ever made, and the creatures created by the Imaskari sealed away and forgotten. When Imaskar fell, it is likely they crept back into the silent darkness they'd come from... or possibly changed into something else...
This circlet was once possessed by the demilich Rammaq.

Your transformation has significantly toughened your skin, making you resistance to damage from divine sources. You also no longer feel any coldness, and electricity does not seem to affect you in any way. Furthermore, due to your spiritual focus, you are immune to any mind-affecting attacks.

This +3 mithral light shield of improved cold resistance has languished in the Imaskari Forges for centuries, never having seen use. The priests of Auril it was meant to be used against were instead slain by a particularly nasty magical plague spread by Imaskari sorcerers.

Aromal was a man far better known for his skill with words than with swords, smoothly tricking wealthy targets out of their earnings with nearly effortless tales, and the aid of several cohorts nearly as skilled with confidence games as he. He, however, was a wretched fighter, and knew that one day his luck with words might run out and force him to defend himself with steel. How fortunate, then, that he 'discovered' a blade so ideally suited to protect him?
Heart of Rashemen

Though to the untrained eye this item appears merely as a slender band of silver, those with an eye for the Art can discern it as a current of pure force, always in motion. The witches have identified it as a link to an extremely powerful telthor - Rashemi animal spirit - that imbues it with tremendous speed and regenerative capabilities.
Safiya's Robes
Safiya's robes clearly reveal that she is a Red Wizard of Thay. They appear pristine and have obviously been well taken care of.
Akachi's Scythe
This scythe was wielded by Akachi the Betrayer, former high priest of Myrkul.

The Silver Sword of Gith has been completely reforged. According to myth, this sword was originally forged by Zerthimon for Gith, before their separation into two races: the githzerai and the githyanki. Gith used this blade to free all gith-kind from their ages-long enslavement by the illithids. The sword was rumored to have been lost in the Nine Hells when Gith ventured there to seek an alliance with the red dragons and never returned. Later, the sword was possessed by Lord Akachi, a high priest of Myrkul, who wielded it in his Crusade against the City of Judgment. Eventually, the sword ended up in the hands of Ammon Jerro, who used it to smite the King of Shadows in a devastating battle that sundered the sword into dozens of shards. One shard became embedded in an infant, making them the Kalach-Cha or Shard-Bearer. The Shard-Bearer partially reforged the sword and used it to irrevocably destroy the King of Shadows in a colossal battle. In the aftermath of the struggle, the Founder of the Academy of Shapers and Binders in Thay abducted the nearly slain Shard-Bearer. She extracted the shard from the Shard-Bearer's chest, with the intent of forging the blade anew. As a result, the Shard-Bearer's special bond with the blade was lost. The Founder has since fully reforged the sword. It can now be used to unlock the Betrayer's Gate - a portal leading to the Fugue Plane, constructed by Akachi the Betrayer. The Betrayer's Gate lies on the lowest level of Myrkul's Vault, in the Plane of Shadow.

With Akachi's defeat, control of the ravenous spirit-eater hunger inside you is within your grasp. From this point on, you are once again in control of your destiny.

You destroyed the bear skeleton, infuriating the spirits and causing them to face you in direct combat. Distracted, their power over the barrier blocking your escape wavered and caused it to fall. Even though the way is now clear, you suspect your desecration won't be forgotten... or forgiven.

You inquired about the "Betrayer's Crusade" at Mulsantir's temple of Kelemvor.
The priest, Darovik, was familiar with this tale. He told you how Akachi, a powerful priest of Myrkul, led a rebellion against his god and tried to bring down the Wall of the Faithless, in the realm of the dead.
Darovik knew little more, but further details of this story may be found in an ancient scroll, the Lamentations of the Dead. If this scroll still exists, it may be found in an ancient vault, once sacred to Myrkul's faith. Though Darovik did know know its location, he suggested searching in the "shadows" of Mulsantir.
In the depths of the Death God's Vault, you discovered a scroll called the Lamentations of the Dead, which gave a detailed account of the Betrayer's Crusade.

You must gain access to the Codex of the Doomed to learn which section of the Wall of the Faithless contains your soul. To do so, you must lure the Scrivener out of the Temple of Kelemvor by holding the Supplicants' Gate, the Basilica of Lost Hope, and Eternity's End.

You must gain access to the Codex of the Doomed to learn which section of the Wall of the Faithless contains your soul. To do so, you must gain the Scrivener's trust by defending the Supplicants' Gate, the Basilica of Lost Hope, and Eternity's End.
You read the Codex of the Doomed and discovered which section of the Wall of the Faithless holds your soul. All that's left to be done is to wrest your soul from the Wall's grasp - no easy task.

With the defeat of Akachi's lieutenants, the Crusade is broken and in disarray. A messenger arrived informing you that the Scrivener, keeper of the Codex of the Doomed, has granted you entrance to the Temple of Kelemvor in Eternity's End. Read from the Codex of the Doomed and learn the location of your soul.

Because of the Third Crusade's numerous victories, the Scrivener, keeper of the Codex of the Doomed, has asked to meet with you in the Temple of Kelemvor at Eternity's End. You will need to deal with him before you can read from the Codex and learn the location of your soul.

The Voice of Kelemvor managed to escape, but at least he was driven from the Basilica. With your aid, Zoab's forces finished off the last of the devils assaulting them. The Basilica of Lost Hope is now belongs to the Third Crusade.
The Voice of Kelemvor managed to escape, and Zoab fell during the battle with the devils in the Basilica. The Basilica of Lost Hope is now belongs to the Third Crusade, but it was a costly victory.
You were able to defeat Rammaq and banish him from the Fugue Plane.
The paladin commander says that Rammaq was seen moving from vault to vault with his minions and is likely within one at the moment. Search them all and destroy him.

Your soul lies imprisoned within the Wall of the Faithless. The Wall seems to have a mind of its own, and will not give up its prize unless you take it back by force. The Wall will almost certainly defend itself somehow.

The demilich Rammaq says that certain lore stored in the vaults at Eternity's End will grant great power to whoever obtains it. He strongly advises you to seize this lore before Kelemvor's servants move it to another location.
You successfully retrieved the lore that Rammaq was after, and he used it to increase both his own power and that of his minions.
Rammaq wants you to locate a pair of tomes: the Tome of Ka'tai and the Tome of the Dolorous Sage. Both are stored somewhere in Eternity's End.

Rammaq threatened to withdraw his forces if you didn't help him retrieve the Tome of Ka'Tai and the Tome of the Dolorous Sage. Although you currently have no choice but to help him if you are to lure the Scrivener into combat, it may also be possible to thwart Rammaq's plan somehow - if you so desired.

With only one of the tomes in his possession, Rammaq was unable to achieve the divinity he had sought for so long. He surmised that he could still increase his power, however, and promised to send some of his most powerful minions to aid you when the time comes to retrieve your soul from the Wall of the Faithless.
His quest for godhood denied yet again, Rammaq abandoned you and the Crusade.
Rammaq was aware that you sabotaged his quest for godhood by preventing the tomes he required from falling into his grasp and attacked you for your betrayal.
{Z}Holding the Supplicants' Gate

With the Third Crusade assaulting different sections of the city, the defenders will be spread thinner than usual. If you and Sey'ryu can defeat the forces assigned to guard the Supplicants' Gate, the militia will be forced to divert even more of their numbers to watch the Gate for demonic incursions.

You defeated all three waves of attackers at the Supplicants' Gate, and any remaining forces have wisely chosen to remain inside the city nearby. With the gate guardians defeated, they dare not risk deploying elsewhere lest demons slip through the now-unguarded gate. Sey'ryu declared her debt to Akachi paid and left.
You arrived too late to save Sey'ryu at the Supplicants' Gate. Fortunately, the dragon seems to have eliminated the majority of the militia there before falling.

You arrived just in time to rescue Sey'ryu at the Supplicants' Gate. The dragon slew the majority of the militia there, though she was badly wounded during the battle. Her debt to Akachi fulfilled, she then left the area.

{Z}The Faceless Man

Although you were able to retrieve your soul from the Wall, it did not free you from Akachi as expected. The vision of the Red Woman explained that Akachi has begun to devour your soul from, and if he succeeds, he will fully possess your body.
Myrkul's curse is undone, and Akachi's soul has been restored. No longer will the spirit-eater plague the Realms, and at long last, both you and Akachi are free.
You defeated the forces of Akachi, the Faceless Man, at the dreamscape version of Crossroad Keep. Akachi fled deeper into your soul, and you must pursue him.

Once again, you defeated the forces of the Faceless Man, this time in the dreamscape version of your old home village of West Harbor. As before, Akachi fled, but you know this time he's cornered and has nowhere else to flee.
You imprisoned Akachi within your soul, sacrificing your freedom in the process.
You struck Akachi a final blow and cast him - and his curse - out of your soul. It has been some time in coming, but at last you are free.

With Myrkul gone, you knew that the curse of the spirit-eater was a curse no more. There were no more consequences, only power. And so, you devoured Akachi's spirit and took the power as your own, mastering the hunger and able to unleash it at will...

In the town of Mulsantir, you met two half-celestial siblings - Efrem the Stag and Susah the Crow. Their sister, Kaelyn the Dove, has apparently gone missing, and they suspect that she has gone to the Death God's Vault in Shadow Mulsantir - the Shadow Plane version of the town.
If you are able to find Kaelyn and bring her back safely, Efrem and Susah have promised to reward you... and to assist you in your battle against Okku's spirit army, if you still need their aid.

You found Kaelyn the Dove in the Death God's Vault in Shadow Mulsantir and convinced her to join you.
Return to Efrem and Susah in Mulsantir to reunite them with their sister.

You convinced Kaelyn to leave Death God's Vault with you and took her to see her brother, Efrem, and sister, Susah.
Despite Kaelyn's wishes to the contrary, you held her siblings to their promise to help you fight Okku and his spirit army.

You convinced Kaelyn to leave Death God's Vault with you and took her to see her brother, Efrem, and sister, Susah.

In the instructors' quarters section of the Academy of Shapers and Binders, you found a dais set in the ground with a network of mirrors around it, controlled by a floating orb discovered nearby. Inarus' room is just north of the staircase in the southeast section of the instructors' quarters level.

Gann is loyal to you, and through his presence, has opened your "dreamer's eye," showing you parts of your conscious and unconscious persona you didn't know you possessed. You find yourself relating with others easier, and your perceptions of the world around you have sharpened - sometimes you can catch what others say before they say them, and you instinctively know what to say to sway someone to your point of view. One side effect of this new ability, and possibly unintended, is that you can more easily see the spirits of others - and draw upon it to satiate your hunger. Whatever this effect Gann has had on you, it is permanent, and will remain, even if the two of you part ways.
Effects: +1 Charisma, +5% Bonus to Devour Spirit ability

Gann has unlocked your "dreamer's voice," immersing you in the powerful ebb and flow of your thoughts. The spirit of Rashemen itself has found a vessel in you, giving an ethereal edge to your voice and your perceptions. The skin and appearance of others around you seem secondary to what you can see of their thoughts and their nature, and often, you know how to coax the brightest ideas and behavior from those around you. What is real and what is not are easier for you to sift. Illusions and other spells and effects intended to deceive now stream off your senses like water - you see what others dream to be, and how to evoke it. It is far easier now to perceive the energy of spirit creatures, allowing you to drink deeply of spirits to quench your hunger. Whatever this effect Gann has had on you, the dreamer's voice is permanent, and will remain even if the two of you part ways.
Effects: +2 Charisma, +10% Bonus to Devour Spirit ability

You and Gann have embraced your love for each other, and with that admission, your thoughts have bled together, allowing you to share ideas and dreams without uttering a word. When attacked by the spells of enemies, your opponents will discover that they are fighting the wills of two spirits united. Whatever happens to Gann, this blending of personality is permanent, and will not fade if he dies or you part ways. He is with you forever, in body or spirit - should he die, the part that loved you will remain.
Effects: Spell Resistance 30, Immunity to Mind-affecting Spells

Okku's trust in you strengthens his resolve, and in return he has given you a measure of that determination. Even if Okku is killed or the two of you part ways, his blessing of resilience will remain.

Okku respects you first amongst all mortals and has bestowed upon you a part of his indomitable will. Okku's gift is as eternal as the bear king himself. Should he meet his final rest, or should you part company, his gift will remain.

This soul was split and then melded back together, the latter as a result of your success with the mephit experiment. This housing glistens with the light of two souls forced to occupy the same space by the skillful handiwork of Poruset. According to Thael-ka and Oronock, the visiting pit fiend dealmakers in the Academy of Shapers and Binders, this housing contains a marked soul - that is, a soul claimed for damnation by some baatezu contract-holder. There is a certain lightness and emptiness to it, as if it is not all there within the housing.

The material of this housing is bears little commonality with anything you've seen before outside of the Academy of Shapers and Binders, and was almost certainly originally developed there. It is slightly translucent and visibly porous, with a consistency not unlike that of an eggshell. Despite its near-weightlessness, its faint inner radiance would seem to indicate that it is not empty.
This housing contains the soul of your one-time travel companion Ammon Jerro. It glows with a color that reminds you of his beard.

There is something truly surreal about this casing. It looks ostensibly to be the container of a soul, but it has no weight or material component. Like a fog, it temporarily parts when you rake your fingers through it, as though it were only the image of a soul and its casing. Only by carefully positioning your hands beneath it are you able to move it about, and then only very slowly.
There is a certain heft to this soul casing, and the faintest hum of magic from its interior, but it otherwise looks unremarkable.

Accounts of a dark, hungry presence began to spread - folk whispered of a monster that feasted upon the souls of the unwary - a chorus of voices that could be heard, but never seen.

But far to the south, in the Black Jungles, tales speak of a nation of beasts and men. It is ruled - or so the stories say - by a faceless creature, who speaks with a thousand voices... whose devoted subjects beg for the honor of being devoured by their liege - so that they might live eternal as one among Many...

| Player devoured spirit-eater |You became the very monster that I had hoped you would destroy - a greater threat to order than Akachi had ever been. For you had mastered your hunger, and its power was no longer a threat to you.

I was not part of that host, but I know that the gods were fewer in number when the battle was done.

But most agreed that you had escaped their wrath, passing beyond the boundaries of their sight to worlds where the gods do not hold sway.
Whether you will remain in distant worlds and forge an empire of your own... or return to the Realms to seek a darker legacy still - that story is yet to be told...

This small bag can be used to enchant items and functions like a portable workbench. To enchant an item, simply place it in this satchel along with one or more brilliant essences, then cast the appropriate spell as indicated in the essence's description. For example, to create a frost weapon, place one brilliant water essence and any weapon into the Enchanter's Satchel, then cast ice storm on the satchel. Essences are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Such essences are typically only of volatile quality and ten must be combined using a Shaper's Alembic to create a brilliant variety. Rarer recipes and essences might be discovered throughout your adventures.

This powerful alembic allows you to convert, combine, and divide essences. Essences are used to enchant items. They are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Typically, only volatile essences are found and the alembic must be used to convert them into brilliant essences for enchanting purposes. Items are enchanted by placing them in the Enchanter's Satchel along with one or more essences, and then casting the appropriate spell. Many standard recipes are explained in the item description for any brilliant essence.
The abilities of the Shaper's Alembic include: 1. Combine Essences. Using this ability on a stack of lesser essences converts them into a more powerful one. No value is lost. 2. Divide Essence. Using this ability on a powerful essence converts it into an equivalent number of lesser essences. No value is lost. 3. Convert Essence. When used on a stack of elemental essences (fire, air, earth, water), two are converted into a single power essence of the same quality. When used on a power essence, several lesser essences are created of each elemental type.

This longsword is rumored to have been forged by Zerthimon for Gith, before their separation into two races: the githzerai and the githyanki. Gith used this blade to free all gith-kind from their ages-long enslavement by the illithids. The sword was said to have been lost in the Nine Hells when Gith ventured there to seek an alliance with Tiamat and never returned. It has since acquired several owners over the ages, and was most recently used to defeat the King of Shadows. Now fully reforged, the power of this ancient artifact has finally been restored. Designed to utilize its power intelligently, the sword adapts to its wielder, giving powers it deems appropriate for its master's abilities. With every strike, the sword has a 20% chance of dealing bonus cold damage and a 20% chance of emitting a sonic wave, similar to the spell, Sound Burst. The sword has been further enchanted with numerous abilities, each quite potent in its own right: Spell-Like Abilities: These abilities consume the sword's charges. They may be replenished by casting spells on the blade, which will absorb the energies. Alternately, the sword has been designed to recharge itself in battle, slowly restoring its power with every successful attack. Chilling Wrath: Three beams of freezing cold energy are directed at a single target as separate ranged touch attacks. If all three beams successfully converge on the target, they will conclude with a large explosion of ice and energy, dealing additional damage to enemies in the area (Fortitude save prevents knockdown on selected target). Infinite Resonance: A massive sound wave is sent radiating away from the wielder in a circular radius, dealing large amounts of damage and deafening and knocking down enemies unable to resist its power (Fortitude save prevents). Unity of Will: All creatures in view of the sword are affected by its power. Allies to the wielder, united in purpose, are granted bonuses similar to those found in the spells, Mind Blank and Heroism. Nearby enemies are given penalties similar to the spells Fear and Crushing Despair (Will save negates). Unbroken Circle: The wielder is protected from physical harm and magical attacks in a manner similar to the spells, Premonition and Spell Mantle. Perfect Rejuvenation: The wielder is restored as if affected by the spells, Greater Restoration and Regenerate. Sword Forms: The sword bearer may magically alter the edge of the blade to produce different effects, several times per day: Penetrating Edge: For a short while, all physical damage done is maximized. Anti-Magic Edge: For a short while, every time the wielder lands a blow with the sword, the target must save or be affected by Mordenkainen's Disjunction. Defensive Edge: For a short while, the sword confers a significant bonus to the wielder's armor class.

This small bag can be used to enchant items and functions like a portable workbench. To enchant an item, simply place it in this satchel along with one or more brilliant essences, then cast the appropriate spell as indicated in the essence's description. For example, to create a corrosive weapon, place one brilliant earth essence and any weapon into the Enchanter's Satchel, then cast Melf's acid arrow on the satchel. Essences are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Such essences are typically only of volatile quality and ten must be combined using a Shaper's Alembic to create a brilliant variety. Rarer recipes and essences might be discovered throughout your adventures.

This powerful alembic allows you to convert, combine, and divide essences. Essences are used to enchant items. They are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Typically, only volatile essences are found and the alembic must be used to convert them into brilliant essences for enchanting purposes. Items are enchanted by placing them in the Enchanter's Satchel along with an item, and then casting the appropriate spell. Many standard recipes are explained in the item description for any brilliant essence.
The abilities of the Shaper's Alembic include: 1. Combine Essences. Using this ability on a stack of lesser essences converts them into a more powerful one. No value is lost. 2. Divide Essence. Using this ability on a powerful essence converts it into an equivalent number of lesser essences. No value is lost. 3. Convert Essence. When used on a stack of elemental essences (fire, air, earth, water), two are converted into a single power essence of the same quality. When used on a power essence, several lesser essences are created of each elemental type.

Extract Water Elemental Transmutation [Water] Level: Druid 6, Wizard / Sorcerer 6 Components: V, S Range: Close Target: One living creature Saving Throw: Fortitude half Spell Resistance: Yes
This brutal spell causes the targeted creature to dehydrate horribly as the moisture in its body is forcibly extracted through its eyes, nostrils, mouth, and pores. This deals 1d6 points of damage per cast level (maximum 20d6), or half damage on a successful Fortitude save. If the targeted creature is slain by this spell, the extracted moisture is transformed into a water elemental of a size equal to the slain creature (up to Huge). The water elemental is under your control, as though you had summoned it, it disappears after 1 minute.

This book contains the collected sayings and stories of a revered Rashemi Witch, who seems to have died over a century ago. Most of these writings are religious in nature, some are folk tales, and a few seem to be remedies for various rashes and warts.
One page has been dogeared, however, and a brief passage is entitled "Of the Ravenous Four":
"So spoke Immith Yabog...
"In my youth, the spirit-eater curse was said to be rampant in the woodlands of the north. I was sent from Urling, with three of my hathran sisters, to seek the truth of these rumors.
"Outside the great forest, we came upon a fleeing mass of simple folk, who spoke fearfully of a foul cult - men and women who had begun to worship the spirit-eater as a god, who passed its power amongst themselves, and went into the deep forest to feed.
"Retracing the villagers' steps, we soon came upon the encampment of these wicked folk, taking them by surprise, and slaying many. Only four managed to escape us, fleeing into the deep forest. One of these bore the dark hunger of a spirit-eater, and she devoured two of my sisters before she made her escape. My remaining sister and I dared not follow.
"But we learned much from the remains of their camp. These folk were unlike others afflicted by the curse - indeed, they referred to their dark hunger as the Gift. And we discovered that many of those we had taken for Rashemi were shapeshifted uthraki. They also worshipped the one who possessed the Gift, and had learned much lore of the spirit-eater, to pass on to others who bore the hunger and reveled in it as they did..."

While my official tenure as an instructor is a new development, I have been teaching the arcane arts since I was... a child, really.

Spells are a small part of what I teach. My students are often new to the magical arts. Before they learn their first cantrip, they need to have their minds sharpened, so that they can view the world through a scholar's eye.
Our journey often has long stretches of travel and many idle hours by the campfire. I wish to use that time to teach you.
I do not mean to be condescending - I've seen you overcome bear gods and Red Wizards and all manner of challenges. But I have led a life of quiet study - a life very different from your own...
[Influence Gain: Safiya] {Hint of excitement}Excellent. It will be good to be an instructor once again. Now... shall we carry on?

Then humor me, please. While I enjoy our travels, I miss my students. I will instruct you as best as I can and if you don't learn anything... well... it will keep me sharp until I return to the classroom.
Perception, memory, focus - all of these qualities can be heightened if you open yourself to the possibility that any problem can be solved with your mind.
{Stern, but a hint of affection comes through}The more I travel with you, the more you surprise me with your... agreeable qualities.
{Stern, caught off guard}Yes, well... I grew up among tyrannical wizards... the art of the compliment is one I learned late in life.
{Neutral - could follow a flustered or happy line}I see great potential in you. Had you come to my academy as a prospective student, you would have made an excellent, if not unorthodox, pupil.
I would like to share with you arcane lore that my mother taught me when I was young.
Yes - though I'd think of it as an advanced course of study.
During our travels on foot and our idle hours setting camp, I will train you - sharpen your memory, your focus, your will.
Do not think of it as a favor - I enjoy teaching. Sharing knowledge with a worthy student is its own reward.

TIP: If you're ever unsure how to proceed, check your Journal for reminders about the various quests you are pursuing.
TIP: Save often, and in different slots.

TIP: Checking the box for Spontaneous Conversion in the Quick Cast menu will allow good and neutral clerics to convert their spells to cure wounds, evil clerics to convert their spells to inflict wounds, and druids to convert their spells to summon creatures.
The barrow guardians and spirit animals are capable of appearing out of nowhere - move cautiously.
TIP: Press "F" to display the Quickcast Panel.

TIP: The Enchanter's Satchel allows you to enchant items without needing a workbench nearby. Just place one or more essences and the item to be enchanted into the satchel, then cast the appropriate spell on it.
TIP: Disarming traps and picking locks yields a small amount of experience points.
TIP: Using the Shaper's Alembic to convert volatile essences to brilliant ones, or brilliant ones to pristine ones, costs you nothing.
TIP: Some unique creatures can provide very rare essences that can be used to create artifacts.
TIP: Your decisions have a profound effect on the world of Mask of the Betrayer. A decision you make early in the game might have repercussions much later.
TIP: Some of the optional fights in Mask of the Betrayer are extremely difficult - only the most skilled can hope to defeat everything!
TIP: Press "V" to use the Voice Menu to quickly give commands to your companions. These commands can be dragged to the hotbar.
What would a titan demilich look like?
If a thousand screaming souls gazed into a magical mirror, what would happen?
When is a club not a club?
TIP: Disarming traps and picking locks yields a small amount of experience points.

LORE: Nearly ten thousand years ago, southern Rashemen was an outlying territory of the Imaskari Empire - a nation of magical builders and artificers. The art of golem-building is thought to have originated in ancient Imaskar.

LORE: Stretching from the merchant-realm of Thesk to distant Kara-tur, the Golden Way is perhaps the most well-traveled trade route in the Realms. Caravans pass along its length at all seasons of the year, bringing eastern goods to the markets of the west.

LORE: The land of Rashemen is rich with spirits - ghostly echoes of powerful beasts, or of humans who perished while preserving or defending the wild places. Among the Rashemi, these spirits are known as telthors.

LORE: Even as far north as Rashemen, sailors whisper of distant Chult, a land of steaming jungles, deadly disease, and massive reptilian monsters. Local peoples cling to coastal regions, mounting occasional expeditions into the deep jungle... and living in fear of serpents who can take the shape of men.

LORE: West of Rashemen lies the merchant kingdom of Thesk, which has grown rich from trade along the Golden Way. Rumors suggest that its cities have fallen under the rule of the Shadowmasters - a secretive and ambitious guild of thieves.

LORE: Some Rashemi Witches have abandoned their order, believing that Rashemen should be ruled with a firm and pitiless hand. These are the durthans, who hide in remote corners of Rashemen, and plot the downfall of their more open-minded sisters.
LORE: The nation of Thay is ruled by the nine zulkirs - each of whom represents a single school of magic. Chief among these is Szass Tam, a scheming lich who is much feared by his fellow Red Wizards.

LORE: Unlike most other realms, Rashemen has no king or hereditary ruler. Instead, the people are guided and led by the Witches - a sisterhood of masked women who refer to themselves as hathrans, or 'learned sisters.'

LORE: The people of Rashemen are highly suspicious of outsiders... though perhaps with good cause. Their country has suffered countless invasions by the Red Wizards of Thay, whose domain borders Rashemen to the south.
LORE: Rashemi men are forbidden to practice arcane magic... unless they agree to join the vremyonni, an order of wizards who live in seclusion and are rarely seen by common folk.
You've encountered strange burial mounds, atop which rest the ancient skeletons of bears. The spirits in this place seem to concentrate around these mounds.
The incorporeal nature of the animal spirits makes them difficult to hit, but fortunately, they don't seem to be particularly resilient.
More spirit animals awaken with each passing moment, and you've yet to encounter the lord of this place...
Judging from the masses of tree roots protruding from the tunnel ceilings, the surface can't be far away.
The path takes you downward. Instead of more earthen tunnels, however, you are greeted with ancient stonework and the scent of oil and steel.
Like the lower barrow, the spirit animals seem to avoid this area. You should be able to rest safely here.
The path takes you downward to a place of ancient stonework and musty tomes.
Like the lower barrow, the spirit animals seem to avoid this area. You should be able to rest safely here.

Your boat rests docked at the shore of the frigid Lake Ashane. A fence of sharpened stakes marks the outline of a military outpost, but is this outpost here to protect the forest behind it, or is it there to offer protection from the forest?

The Witches of Rashemen wisely established a series of garrisoned outposts along each of their borders. Through the years, the Red Wizards of Thay have attacked from all directions, and early warning has become Rashemen's best defense.
TIP: The feat Epic Precision allows rogues to inflict some sneak attack damage against creatures such as undead and elementals.
TIP: Press "*" to switch between the different Play Modes.
TIP: Use a Shaper's Alembic to convert volatile essences into brilliant ones, which can then be used to enchant items.
TIP: If the action is going too fast, press "SPACE" to pause the game between rounds.
TIP: Base classes can reach levels 21 through 30, but prestige classes still have a maximum level of either five or ten.
TIP: Some epic feats can only be learned by characters with very high ability scores. For example, to gain an Epic Animal Companion, a druid or ranger must have a Wisdom of 25.
TIP: Epic Prowess and Epic Toughness are prerequisites for more advanced epic feats.
TIP: After level 20, characters gain a bonus feat at every odd level. Base classes gain additional bonus feats depending upon the class.
TIP: Epic characters can enchant items that already have three magical properties.
TIP: Characters continue to gain additional attacks per round as their base attack bonus (BAB) increases. So a level 26 fighter receives six attacks per round!
Keep an eye on your spirit energy bar at all times. As it drops, your character will weaken. Should the bar ever empty, you will die.
Devour Spirit is much more beneficial when used as a killing blow - whatever hit points your victim had remaining when it was devoured are absorbed as bonus spirit energy.
If you find yourself in desperate need of spirit energy with no obvious sources within reach, use your Satiate ability. It costs XP, but it can save your life.

Your current level of craving dictates how fast you lose spirit energy. Certain abilities, like Suppress, can reduce your craving and allow you to survive longer between opportunities to devour spirits.

As your spirit craving grows, you become less a being of flesh and more an embodiment of hunger. Though your spirit energy will drain faster, you'll also gain an increasingly powerful set of benefits as you begin to transcend your physical form.

Spirits include fey (such as telthors), elementals, or incorporeal undead (such as shadows or wraiths). Rashemen has them in abundance, but caution should be taken not to drive down the local population so much that you can no longer find food.

When a creature is weakened or otherwise vulnerable, you may be able to devour them without it costing a use of your devour ability. Whenever you see [Devour Spirit] in dialogue, you can expect to get that devour for free.

Never let your spirit eater power uses go to waste. If you must rest, but haven't devoured a spirit since your last rest, try to find a nearby spirit to devour, or at least use Suppress to help counteract the spirit energy cost of resting.
Stronger beings will tend to yield better spirit essences when devoured. Some especially powerful ones will have unique essences with their own special sets of benefits.

It can actually be to your benefit to wait for your spirit energy to drop before devouring a spirit. If you devour spirits when your spirit energy is high and you aren't weakened by your affliction, it will increase your level of craving.

Berserkers have been instrumental to Rashemen's continued survival, and now that you're among them, it's easy to see why. These men aren't just career soldiers, they're bred and reared for it. They live for one purpose, and all they do is preparation toward that end.

Though relatively new, the Lake of Tears outpost has clearly suffered more than its fair share of vicious battles. There's little wonder that its lifespan seems destined to be so short, given the obvious wear and tear.

It's hard to shake the feeling that you got little if anything of what you came here for in the first place. You came for a cure. You embarked on a set of tasks that would benefit the local garrison. Yet your curse remains, and the garrison is silent now, completely emptied of its defenders.

You make your way down a little-used path and find yourself in a place both ancient and mystical. It is pristine - untouched by civilization, and there is something else... an eager palpitation you've felt before. There are spirits nearby. The forest is filled with them.

Navigating the forest isn't easy. Some paths have been trodden by huge trolls or other large forest denizens, but there is little else to go by. There is one landmark, though, that has been a gift in finding your way back here. You see it in the distance, shining like a beacon...

You've been this way several times now, and there is still little sign of the berserkers missing from the garrison. Most of the predators from these parts, you'd expect, would have left behind carcasses or bones. What did they encounter here?
TIP: Epic level druids can eventually gain a dragon as their animal companion.
TIP: Only the strongest barbarians can achieve the ability to Epic Rage.
TIP: Check the manual for the prerequisites for the most powerful epic feats.
TIP: Pristine essences usually provide the same types of enchantments as brilliant ones - but the resulting item is significantly more powerful.
TIP: The difficulty class (DC) of any spellcaster's spells increases by one for every three caster levels above 20. A 29th level wizard therefore gains a +3 bonus to all of her spell DCs.
Rashemen lies many hundreds of leagues from the Sword Coast - a journey that would ordinarily take many months on foot, but can be accomplished much more quickly by magical means...

In the more remote corners of the world, some animals are said to speak the words of men, and build barrows for their dead. These creatures are survivors of a distant past, before the Age of Faith... and few are thought to remain.

Your memories of the Shadow Temple - and its collapse - are still vague. But you dimly recall the stones falling around you... and the shouts of your companions. Some of them survived the collapse - of that, you are certain.

The shard of Gith has been torn from your chest, the wound raggedly closed and stitched. You are somewhat astonished that you survived the procedure... though you strongly suspect that magic was employed to keep you alive.
A presence... a hunger... still lingers inside you, ever since you awoke in the lower barrow. It is quiet now, barely noticeable, but you feel strangely hollow and empty, nonetheless.
Okku's army of spirits is encamped outside the gates of Mulsantir. According to Sheva Whitefeather, they will not leave until you face them...

Magda's shadow stone is a key, of sorts. If you approach a location where the boundary between the Prime Plane and the Plane of Shadow is weak, a rift will open, allowing you to pass between the two planes.

Sheva Whitefeather is the ranking Witch of Mulsantir - an authority in matters of law and faith. She can be found at the outdoor temple to the Three, which overlooks the river in the northern part of town.

Ever since the arrival of the spirit army at the gate, the sense of an emptiness inside you - a feeling of hunger that cannot be quenched - has become more intense. Your eyes appear sunken, your cheeks hollow, and you suspect that simple exhaustion is not the cause...
Amongst the Rashemi, powerful spirits of the land - such as Okku the bear - are revered as minor gods. No Rashemi would dare raise a hand against them.
Wizards of the Coast, Atari, and Obsidian Entertainment welcome you to Neverwinter Nights 2, the ultimate D&D computer role-playing experience.
Use the Neverwinter Nights 2 toolset to create your own adventures for friends to enjoy.
You awaken to the sound of falling water...
The lower barrow apparently served as some sort of prison, and the spirit animals avoid the area. Whatever was imprisoned there seems to be gone, and you should be able to rest safely.
The spirits are aware of your intrusion now, and it's probable that any encounter with them will be less than friendly.
Amongst the Rashemi, powerful spirits of the land - such as Okku the bear - are revered as minor gods. No Rashemi would dare raise a hand against them.

The Ashenwood is mostly an evergreen forest, but the snow is so thick in some places you'd hardly know it. More so than in Mulsantir, the onset of winter here must be swift and unrelenting, year in and year out.

There is a strict protocol set up for anyone who wishes to hunt in the Ashenwood, where it is said many ideal specimens of creatures reside. They must burn offerings before ever entering the forest, and thank the spirits for every kill. Failure to do so brings untold, but supposedly dire, consequences.

The Witches keep a careful eye on the Ashenwood, wary of losing it to foreign invaders. In times past, they have received valuable counsel from its eldest treants, as well as its greatest source of wisdom, the Wood Man. Would they have sent you here knowing that he had disappeared?

There is a new quiet to the forest. The hostility you felt from it as you ventured through these parts earlier is gone now, the threats that awoke its feral survival instinct pacified for the time being.

The blaze was easy to locate, once you were pointed in the right direction. The scent of wood burning, the sight of smoke on the horizon leading you onward. Now at last the flames are in sight, and it occurs to you how remarkable their presence is amongst all this snow.

The strangest sense of having been here before - long ago - crosses your mind, which, having grown up in a swamp on the Sword Coast, seems relatively unlikely and most likely some bizarre by-product of your spirit-eater malady.

You descend from the slopes of the Running Rocks and arrive in the place Nadaj described - Immil Vale. It is unseasonably warm here, making you wonder briefly whether your journey took much longer than you'd expected.

The Vale is alive with the growls of animals that should be hibernating and the calls of birds that should have migrated. It's surreal, but a welcome respite from the harsh winter that enshrouds the rest of the surrounding land.

The Immil Vale, like Neverwinter, experiences a temperate climate year-round. And just as Neverwinter's is rumored to be, the Vale's secret is a geological one - it's nestled between the foothills of an active volcano.

This dwelling provides a respite from the freezing gusts off of Lake Ashane, but little else has been done to make it hospitable. It's little wonder the Rashemi are such a surly bunch, if they insist on living in such barren accommodations.

It hardly feels like a military garrison in this small abode - more like a study. There are many books lining Dalenka's shelves, and a sizeable portion of them seem to be non-magic related. Is this how time is passed in a tiny outpost so far from civilization?
You entered a cave, but as you've advanced, the walls have smoothed out, and you realize you are in a mineshaft. It gets colder with every step forward.

Sometimes an animal is born - often of ancient lineage - that exhibits absolute perfection of its species. These remarkable paragon beasts are to their kind what heroes are to normal men, and for that they are greatly sought after by hunters, although few hunters who come in search of them ever emerge from the woods again.

Your mind is active with thoughts of your plight, and your sleep is light. A gentle, glassy hum stirs you - an invitation to partake in something important. You open your eyes and are aware of your surroundings, but you are also aware that you are dreaming.

The air is filled with the strong stench of sulfur, leaving little doubt that the mountain whose paths you walk is an active volcano. A tall, multi-tiered structure looms above, its main tower so high it seems almost disconnected from the rest.
You come upon a grisly scene just inside the academy's main doors. A large and bitter struggle took place here, and no one has yet bothered to remove the dead from the hallways.

The halls echo with chatter from adjacent classrooms where lessons are being taught. The reality of living in Thay must truly be grim if they are so quickly able to return to their habits and ways of life as though nothing had happened at all.

Despite the recent coup, there is a single-mindedness about this place unusual for a country that blames most of its failings on internal strife and competing ambitions. The school's coat of arms hangs from banners in every hall and classroom, and its motto, "Nothing is immutable," is posted everywhere.

At every turn, you half expect to be discovered by Araman, and for a decisive battle to ensue. Yet you have seen no sign of him - only of his overthrow of the headmistress. His prolonged absence is becoming an increasing cause for concern.

There is an unsettling way in which the students and teachers look at you here. Even the youngest students stare calculatingly, a look of pure defiance on their faces. It's as if it's something they teach here.

It is quiet as you descend into the area where the academy's instructors sleep - partially because class seems to be in session, and partially due to the many recent vacancies brought about by Araman's coup.

The academy masters seem to live relatively close together. Still, you'd expect Red Wizards to take pains to keep as many secrets from their colleagues as possible. There is probably much that is hidden on this level...

The main hallway seems to hold a large collection of stocks and torture equipment. It seems like a detention facility, but there are also tables and chairs and house plants. It must be more of a lounge area.

A winding staircase seems to take you up for an eternity. At last, at the very top, you come upon Nefris' room, which has been ransacked. You can only hope that the pillagers didn't destroy or remove everything you might have found useful.

This room, disconnected as it is, must have been a lonely place for Nefris to sequester herself. You notice a loom in one of the far corners, facing toward a window. Did Nefris ever get out of this place, or was that her only view of the world below?

It occurs to you that a portal system would have been much better for ascending this tower than all those stairs. Unless of course the Headmistress wanted to discourage visitors, in which case the stairs are ideal.

You feel suddenly light, as if a deep breath would make you float away, but some force still binds you to the rocky terrain at your feet. Before you is an endless sky, and you feel briefly as though it provides you with insight into the perspective of deities.

Rot and mold swell up in the moist air that pours thickly into your nostrils. You are in a place that is wholly unkempt, seemingly centuries removed from the time it was steadily maintained. Or perhaps it never was...
The Fugue Plane is where all souls go after death. The Faithful are eventually transported to their deity's home plane - everyone else faces sentencing in the City of Judgment.

Newly arrived False and Faithless souls are brought to the Basilica for judgment and sentencing. For the False, the punishment varies, but for the Faithless, there is only one sentence - entombment within the Wall.

Baatezu are permitted within the halls of the Basilica, extending bargains with the doomed souls awaiting sentencing. Souls likely to be judged Faithless often prefer to join the devils as an enslaved minion rather than face oblivion on the Wall.
The Throne of Judgment in the Basilica is almost always empty. Only in the most severe cases does Kelemvor himself appear to personally sentence a doomed soul.

Jergal, a former god of the dead, created Eternity's End with the explicit purpose of storing the names of every creature who has ever died. The district is now used to store lore and artifacts deemed too dangerous to be loose in the planes.
Though the paladins of Kelemvor are few in number, Kelemvor bestows a measure of his divine power upon each of them, greatly increasing their power.
The Codex of the Doomed, the giant tome in which all the names of the False and Faithless are inscribed, can be found in a Temple of Kelemvor in Eternity's End.

Your soul now lies in the Wall of the Faithless, occupying the place that Myrkul reserved for Akachi. The souls of past spirit-eater have also been imprisoned here... and been dissolved when they succumbed to the curse.
Most of the vaults simply contain tomes with endless lists of names of people long-dead, but a few have been adapted to store magical lore and artifacts.
Descent. Ahead of you is a warm, idyllic place, a place of compassion and mercy. It is your true self, uncloaked by words and deeds, and it is there that Akachi awaits you for one final battle.
There are many temples in the City of Judgment, but this particular temple holds the Codex of the Dead. Within the Codex lies the location of your soul.
Regardless of how you feel about it, your childhood village of West Harbor *is* important to you. It is part of you, a part which the Faceless Man is attempting to destroy.
Descent. Ahead of you is a cool, twilit place, a place of pragmatism and balance. It is your true self, uncloaked by words and deeds, and it is there that Akachi awaits you for one final battle.
Descent. Ahead of you is a bleak, hellish place, a place of hatred and ruthlessness. It is your true self, uncloaked by words and deeds, and it is there that Akachi awaits you for one final battle.
You cannot attempt to devour the same creature twice.
The dark presence within you has been revealed as a symptom of a curse - a supernatural hunger that will devour you from within, unless it is fed with spirits... or suppressed by your will.

Among the Rashemi, a bearer of your curse is called a "spirit-eater" - a monster from ancient tales. Many Rashemi, especially simple folk, may react to you with even more fear and suspicion than before.

Even if you continue to feed - or suppress - the empty presence within you, it is likely that your supernatural hunger will grow, and eventually consume you... unless a more permanent "cure" can be found.

You suspect that your hunger can be traced to the strange presence within you... which you have felt since you awoke in Okku's barrow. You can sense little about this presence, but it seems an empty, hollow thing - a void that seeks always to fill itself up.

You may discover additional insights about your curse by talking to residents of Mulsantir and the surrounding lands. Spirit-eaters have not been seen in Rashemen for many years, but fragments of their lore have been preserved by the Witches, and by others as well...
According to the Wood Man, your curse is a punishment, bestowed by a dead god. But he could not say which god was to blame... nor why a dead god should bear you any grudge.

Gods do not die as mortals do... their curses and blessings live on, and their corpses float in the endless sky of the Astral Plane. And as long as mortals remember them - with love or with fear - a spark of their consciousness may persist beyond death.

The creature that possessed Nadaj was called a genius loci - a powerful and malevolent spirit that can sometimes arise in ancient, untouched places. It arose after a spirit-eater nearly drained the forest of life - as a result, this genius loci was especially vengeful...
Your curse has been revealed as the work of Myrkul, former god of the dead. If you have any chance of defeating your supernatural hunger, you will need to find a way to speak with a dead god...

It seems clear now that Safiya's mother, Nefris, was seeking a way to contact the dead god Myrkul... presumably to end your curse. Nefris is - or was - headmistress at the Academy of Shapers and Binders, in Thay.

Myrkul ruled as god of the dead until he was slain, during the Time of Troubles. After his death, his throne briefly passed to the insane god, Cyric... but Cyric was soon overthrown, and Kelemvor took his place.

If you wish to learn more about the fallen god Myrkul, you might inquire at the temple of Kelemvor, in Mulsantir... or seek the ancient Myrkulite vault in Shadow Mulsantir, where Myrkul's servants once celebrated his faith.
According to the Slumbering Coven, Lienna and Nefris were "twins" of a sort. In your dream, their faces appeared almost identical, though they were dressed quite differently...

When Myrkul ruled the City of Judgment, it was a place of horrors and torments - the Wall of the Faithless was only one of these. Kelemvor has ended most of Myrkul's cruel punishments... but the Wall remains.

With the proper magic, a mortal soul can be broken into fragments, and each fragment can be given a body of its own. If the fragments are kept apart for long enough, they may become increasingly distinct from one another... like identical twins who go their separate ways.

In ancient days, it was customary for Rashemi towns to offer up a small number of their infant children as "sacrifices" to the church of Myrkul - these children would be raised as wards of the church and trained as priests. Akachi, and his brother Araman, were two such children.
Kelemvor, current god of the dead, was born a mortal man, and lived during the Time of Troubles. He is, by all accounts, a fair but passionless god.

The City of Judgment is inhabited by countless souls of the False - those who betrayed their gods - and by Faithful who once worshipped the god of the dead. Those who were heroes in life often serve as guardians of the City, protecting its walls from demons... and from others who might seek to assault its gates.

It has been nearly a thousand years since Akachi led his Crusade against the Wall, freed the Founder's soul... and was terribly punished by Myrkul. In all the years since, the Founder labored to end his suffering.
Total Influence

As Safiya mentioned, the golem's power was tied to the Imaskari ruins located under Okku's barrow. At this distance from the barrow, the life force sustaining the golem has failed, and the golem has collapsed into an inert pile of stone, never to rise again.

I'm getting rather cross with you...
Yes.
You'll regret crossing me!
You'll have to do better than that!
Farewell!
Heal me!
Somebody help me out here!
Well met!
No!
You there, come talk to me!
Don't cross me... You won't like me when I'm angry...
Yes.
You'll pay for this!
You think you hear screams and evil laughter coming from across the waves, but you are unsure if it is just your imagination.
Stepping into the Shadow Plane once again, you feel a sudden uncertainty, as if perhaps you are not prepared for the dangers here.
You feel a brief apprehension upon arriving in this dark place. But reminding yourself of the dangers you overcame in Ashenwood, you steel yourself for the challenges ahead.
Hearing the ominous sounds of the creatures that lurk in the depths below, you wonder how any of the floating corpses manage to drift ashore uneaten.
Once again the numbing darkness closes over you and all color drains away. You wonder how many more times you must return to the Shadow Plane.

Through a window ahead you can see the Slumbering Coven, suspended in repose in the Chamber of Dreamers. Your feelings of uncertainty persist. You are risking much for the hope that the Coven will give you answers.
Through a window ahead you can see the Slumbering Coven, suspended in repose in the Chamber of Dreamers. You are eager to face them and get answers.
You are struck again by how badly it smells here. You would think the hags would make their hagspawn servants keep the seat of their power tidy.
You don't stand a chance!
Have you had enough?
Come back soon.
Somebody... Please heal me!
I need assistance!
Hello there.
No.
When you have a moment, we should speak.
Yes!
You're testing my patience...
Yes.
You realize you are trapped in this place. This is where the hags send those who they never want to see again.
You find yourself back in the Chamber of Dreamers...
The ability to walk in dreams is not unique to the hags of Rashemen, but they would like it to be, so they seek out other "dreamers" and slay them, or worse... trap them within a nightmare.
You are shocked to find yourself in a familiar place. Did the Coven somehow return you to Mulsantir?
You have seen this gate often in your dreams, and sometimes you even see it when you are awake...

Those who die without committing themselves to any god are judged Faithless and imprisoned in a living wall that surrounds the City of Judgment - the Wall of the Faithless. These doomed souls are slowly dissolved into the very substance of the Wall.
You hear music, and the sounds of people talking and laughing, but this tavern is empty except for one tired-looking soul who is playing cards with himself.
Had enough?
Long ago the githyanki were a slave race to the illithids, or mind flayers. They revolted under the leadership of Gith, and swore vengeance on their former slavemasters.
There are many fables about the foolishness of making deals with devils. Some people just don't listen.
You leave me no choice!
Is that the best you've got?
Bye now.
So much blood... Heal me... Please!
Help me!
Heya.
No.
Hey there - come over here and talk to me!
Yes!
You're realing getting on me nerves!
Yes.
You fight like a child...
Prepare to meet your end...
You'll have to do better than that...
Go now, and be at peace with the land.
Heal me... My time is running short...
Someone help me!
Greetings, child.
No.
Come close, child! I must speak to you.
Leave me be!
Yes.
Die and be judged, then... I care not.
To judgment with you.
May your soul fly screaming to the Wall!
My will is stronger than yours... and I have no mercy to give.
This body fails me...
Allies... I need your help.
Yes?
Yes.
No.
We part ways, then. Farewell.
Very good...
Wait... I would speak to you.
I warn you... trouble me any further, and I will not stay my hand.
