Before you face the might of the bear god, Okku, and the spirit army he commands, make sure you are well prepared, and have found allies in Mulsantir to stand with you.
Foreigners typically gather at the Sloop - a seedy tavern near Mulsantir's ferry landing. By unspoken agreement, the Witches leave the Sloop and its patrons in peace.

In the center of Mulsantir, near the thriving bazaar, is one of Mulsantir's oldest landmarks: the Veil Theater. With its distinctive, circular architecture and brightly colored banners, it is difficult to miss.

Mulsantir's ferry landing provides transit across River Mulsantir for travelers along the Golden Way. It is also a staging point for the witchboat patrols that help keep Rashemen safe from Thayan incursions across Lake Mulsantir.

It may be difficult to find allies to stand with you against the spirit army, but if you thoroughly explore shady places like the Mulsantir Prison, and speak with people around town, you may find the help you need.

With the spirit army outside the gates, the only way out of Mulsantir is via the ferry landing on the western side of the city. Unfortunately, the spirits of the river are allied with the bear god - and no ship would survive a crossing if you were aboard.
Many of the residents of Mulsantir are fearful of the spirit army and have locked themselves away in their homes.

Now that the spirit army has been driven away, the residents of Mulsantir should be more at ease. Try speaking with them again, and revisit places that were previously locked. Sheva Whitefeather will also want to speak with you.

In Mulsantir, the boundaries between the Plane of Shadow and the Material Plane are especially thin, particularly at night. It is rumored that occasionally an unfortunate resident will stumble into the city's shadowy reflection.

To honor the spirits of the land, many residents of Mulsantir bury valuables in the ground around the city. It is said that anyone who loots these caches will be cursed. But you are already cursed, so...

Though it seems like Sheva Whitefeather has given you free run of her city, you feel like she is watching you always, anticipating - perhaps hoping for - the moment when fate takes you away from Mulsantir permanently.
Rashemen is home to many famed heroes. One such is the ranger Minsc who, with his pet hamster Boo, served as the loyal companion to the witch Dynaheir.
In Shadow Mulsantir lies the Death God's Vault, which contains much of the collected knowledge and treasures of Myrkul, the former God of the Dead.
Though the Plane of Shadow is not itself evil, it is populated by a number of foul creatures who hate the light and the living.
Some outlaws use the Shadow Mulsantir as a place to hide from and subvert the witches' authority. Sheva Whitefeather would surely be grateful to anyone who roots out such criminals.

The Plane of Shadow is highly morphic, so buildings and geographical features are often different from their Material Plane counterparts. Thorough exploration of Shadow Mulsantir may reveal paths that are blocked in Mulsantir itself.
Other places in Rashemen - besides Mulsantir - may have "weak spots" through which one can enter the Plane of Shadows.
The Plane of Shadows is called a Transitive Plane. Transitive Planes are the "glue" that holds the universe together. Other Transitive Planes include the Astral Plane and the Ethereal Plane.
There is a lot of superstition surrounding the Veil Theater. Some claim that backstage is a "gateway to darkness" and that the masks created by Lienna, the theater's owner, have a life of their own.
The famous bard Grobnar of Neverwinter once said "There is nothing so sad as an empty theater... except maybe one full of people crying."
The Veil actors are working on a new play called "The Sorcerer's Concubine" which is to be a dramatic romance about a powerful enchanter and his pure-hearted mistress.
Magda and the the Veil actors are probably deeply disturbed at what happened to Lienna, but the show must go on...
The Veil actors look down their noses at Vladek's Sloop Troupe, and their "artless, inane attempts at theater."
The Plane of Shadow is a dimension that coexists with, and overlaps, the Material Plane. It is a world of black and white, as if color itself has been bleached from the environment.
Lienna sealed several of the doors and chests in this Shadow Plane version of the Veil theater with a special lock. Perhaps Magda would know how to access them.
Lienna left much behind. Perhaps a thorough search would reveal some answers that may have otherwise died with her.
You are haunted by vague, but terrifying memories of your first visit to this place, when you were bound to a crude operating table.
This place smells of death, but not in a sinister way. This temple is where many come to die in peace.

Some appreciate Kelemvor's unbending lawfulness, compared to past Gods of the Dead. But there are a few who believe that the laws of universe are flawed and Kelemvor is wrong to follow them so closely.
Darovik is one of Kelemvor's Chosen - the god's most powerful agent in this part of the Realms. He may seem peaceful and even-tempered, but it would be folly to anger him.
This vault was built by Myrkul, the old God of the Dead who was killed by Mystra in the Time of Troubles.
Myrkul was replaced by Cyric as God of the Dead. Shortly following Myrkul's death, Cyric's faithful stormed Death God's Vault slaying all of Myrkul's followers.
Though Myrkul is long-dead, it feels like vestiges of him remain here in his vault. You almost feel like he yet lives, and is watching you from somewhere far away.
You feel pulled to descend to the lower depths. Images of a massive, twisted gateway flash in your mind.

You feel a great sense of dread upon reaching the bottom of the stairs. The icy chill running down your spine betrays that you are mortal and this is a place in which you will die if you are not well-prepared.
You feel compelled toward the open door to the north.
The images in your mind coalesce and you see the gate before you, though you know it is somewhere to the northwest. The urge to approach the gate is unbearable.
This prison reeks of the desperation of doomed men. Perhaps here you will find someone desperate enough to stand with you against the spirit army.
Tirzah "the Old" is a moniker that the witch adopted for herself, shortly after taking on the duty of being the warden for Mulsantir's prison.
The air here is crisp and fresh, but it carries with it sounds of mournful howls... seeming to come from beasts who are lost, confused, or mad.
It is a mystery how the farmer Janiik manages to maintain and protect his farm in such a dangerous territory.
Outlying areas filled with great spirit energy often attract durthans, and other evil beings, that seek to corrupt and draw power from the darker spirits that inhabit Rashemen.
The hathran witches have done their best to exterminate the uthraki, terrifying ape-like beasts who prey on the sentient. Uthraki are wily, however, and know how to disguise themselves.

The Sloop was constructed from the salvaged wreckage of a galleon called the Mystic, the flagship of a Rashemi armada that repelled Thayan invaders led by Zulkir Szass Tam in the Year of Tattered Banners.

To compete with the Veil Theater as the main venue for entertainment, Vladek recently formed a band of actors called the Sloop Troupe. Vladek intends to draw in an audience with low-brow comedies and parodies.
Since the Sloop was taken over by Vladek, it has become seedy and ramshackle, and most of the locals stay away. Despite this, the inn continues to prosper due to foreign visitors and seamen.

There is a rumor that the ghost-sailors of the flagship Mystic haunt the Sloop, and have become more restless of late. Perhaps they are distressed over the poor conditions in which Vladek keeps the Inn.
Berserkers are often itching for a fight, and eager to prove themselves superior in strength and combat. It is usually wise to not give them excuses.
The berserkers of Rashemen are organized into lodges named after local creatures. The lodges are like extended families, and a berserker is always welcome at the lodge-house of another village.

Berserker lodges are usually guarded by a telthor animal that represents the ideals of that lodge's fighting style. With the fortitude to endure freezing weather, the badger is a typical guardian of Ice Troll lodges.
Janiik's farm house is well-constructed, but humble and utilitarian. The lack of creature comforts suggest that Janiik spends more time in the fields than in his home.
Anya's mind has constructed a place so serene... You can see why the girl would prefer to be here than in her father's dismal dwelling in the Wells of Lurue.
Most half-drow are outcasts, with the exception of those who dwell in far off Dambrath. Mulsantir is one of the few towns in the East tolerant enough to allow half-drow to take up residence.
Not all liches are created equal. In fact, many who try to become liches fail miserably, and their fate is not always so kind as a hideously painful death.
Rashemi children are tested for magical talents at an early age. Those who show aptitude are taken to study with the Old Ones, hermit-like male wizards of great power.
Any Rashemi males who wish to practice the arcane arts must do so in service to the wychlaran, the female witches that rule Rashemen. Refusal is grounds for exile... or execution.

One of Many is compromised of many malevolent spirits battling for control of the Many. The current dominant spirit is the Boy, who favors the rogue class, but if another spirit within the Many were to become dominant, it's likely that One of Many's personality and favored class would change...
One of Many will automatically level up in its current favored class when appropriate, gaining more powerful natural weapons and becoming more resilient. Because of its incorporeal nature, One of Many is unable to equip any items.

Okku is a powerful fey creature who favors the fighter class. While he can't use weapons or armor, his claws and hide will become stronger as he gains levels. Okku is also capable of wearing amulets and rings.
Okku automatically levels up when he gains enough experience, not so much learning new abilities as he is remembering long-forgotten ones.

Kaelyn is a cleric and is capable of casting powerful healing spells. Her cleric abilities also make her very useful when battling undead, and her half-celestial heritage grants her a number of unique racial feats such as immunity to disease and damage reduction versus non-magical weapons.

New spirit-eater feat acquired:
Spirit-eater

You have lost control of the hunger for spirits that has recently manifested inside of you. Your body now requires a periodic influx of energy obtained through the consumption of spirits, or it will eventually wither and die.
The vertical green bar represents your present level of spirit energy. It will drop over time (except during conversation), and as it falls, you will weaken at an accelerating rate. Each of the watermarks on the bar denotes a point at which your curse worsens to a new stage of debilitation. There are six stages of this affliction, the final of which is death. You may mouse over the watermark icons at any time to see what effects a particular stage of the affliction carries.
Several new abilities are available to you that will provide a means to replenish your spirit energy. They are available on the feats tab under "history."
The horizontal bar below the spirit energy bar is a measurement of your craving for spirits. The more you crave spirits, the faster your spirit energy is used up. Giving in to your urge to devour spirits more than once per day will tend to make you crave them more, while actively fighting to gain control over your hunger through the Suppress ability will ease that craving. Use extreme caution when deciding whether to devour spirits if you have already done so once that day - what may seem like a safe move to keep your health high could quite quickly lead you down a slippery slope where you are in constant need of spirits to devour just to stay alive.
Further details about spirit-eater abilities are available in their feat descriptions.

Bark Trigger: Entering The Sloop
Well, one man's dump is another man's pile of dung.
Oh, yes, my rude patron. Now listen and learn...
They hate it! As soon as they make it, they try to bury it, flush it into the Lake, fling it at passersby, or even just get away from it, so that others accidentally step in it!
Dung is produced by every living creature, and all of them - every last one - hates their dung.
Hello again, patron. Are you enjoying yourself in my proud Inn?
Gladly! I acquired the Sloop a few years ago, with my wife Zorah. When we took it over, it was an unprofitable, glorified museum of some sort.
I turned the Sloop into an Inn, a fabulous place where the common man - or woman - can come to relax, enjoy and be entertained!
And here we have none of that elitist "high drama" nonsense like you'll find at the Veil Theatre. We cater to the masses, and I've great pride that my Inn will succeed.
It's not that I dislike the Veil. Magda is a fine lady dwarf who could even drink my wife Zorah under the table. The problem is that they are stuck in the past.
You see... the people, by and large, no longer want to see grand epic stories filled with big words they can barely comprehend. And that is all the Veil does.
So there is a need here, unfilled, and Vladek hears that need and is acting to fill it! That is why I'm forming a new theater, right here in the Sloop, called the "Sloop Troupe."
Catchy name, isn't it? Yes, the Sloop Troupe. They will put on plays that will appeal to the common man. Lighthearted plays of comedy and farce.
Currently we are working on "The Fat Wizard's Wench" which is to be a parody of the Veil's next ghastly, epic drama.
Ah, but you didn't let me finish. Come back if you wish to hear more of Vladek's theory of dung!
Well, a wise farmer - or a businessman like me - knows full well the value of dung.
Simply put, you can enjoy great success if you are able to take something that people don't want and turn it into something they do want. Like this place!
Proud? This place is a dump.
And a "pile of dung" is better than a dump?
They hate their dung?
I am completely missing your point.
Yes, nobody likes dung. So?
Farewell.
Tell me about your Inn.
It sounds like you dislike the Veil Theater.
The Sloop Troupe?
I was being kind when I said it was a dump. Pile of dung is more like it.
What does dung have to do with anything?
I've heard enough to lose my appetite. You will drive your kitchen out of business.
Never mind. I'm leaving now.
Tell me again about your theory of dung.

This tattered, blood-stained tome appears to be the journal of a former vremyonni. Most of the entries appear to ramble on about exacting revenge on his arrogant vremyonni "brothers," but a few select passages catch your eye. "15th of Mirtul - I have finally done it! I was able to animate a corpse and breathe life back into it! Well... it was the corpse of a diseased rat - which seem to be everywhere in this cave - but it was a corpse nonetheless. Unfortunately, I cannot let anyone see my creation, lest I be cast off from here or worse. I guess I will have to dispose of him." "25th of Mirtul - I think I saw Varovin going through my things this morning. I can't be sure of what he has seen. I need to be much more cautious in hiding my forbidden tomes of necromantic lore. I must go speak with Varovin and see what he knows." "25th of Mirtul - Varovin dodged all of my questions regarding his activities this morning. I cannot take the chance that he has seen any of my forbidden codices. I would eliminate him, but that would only cause an investigation. Leaving is the only option. Leaving this cave means leaving all of Rasheman - abandoning all I love. No matter, it must be done." "3rd of Kythorn - Damn the Old Ones! They never taught me anything of survival in the wilderness. This morning's attempt to catch a meal went horribly. All of nature's creatures seem to recoil from me. I wonder if they can sense some sort of taint upon me. What I wouldn't give for some of Jerryn's rabbit stew. Those carrots were so tender and... I need to stop this nonsense and find a town that I can take refuge in." "11th of Kythorn - Off in the distance, I see... large walls! Even in my weakened state, I think I can make it there before nightfall. I must make it there before nightfall." "7th of Flamerule - Mulsantir. I had no idea I had walked that far. I have been in my new "abode" for several weeks now. Oh, I love it here, in this dank, dark, abandoned cellar. If only there were more disease-ridden vermin, it would be just like I was back in the caves with the other vremyonni. I live like a peasant, now. I had to beg for food when I first made it to this place. Beg! I will make them pay for what they have subjected me to." "9th of Eleint - How I think about slowly snuffing out the life of everyone of those arrogant vremyonni. I think constantly about how I was ejected from my life, just because I sought to master all forms of magic. It will take many lifetimes to exact all of the revenge I have planned for them. Many lifetimes... that gives me an idea." "23rd of Uktar - I have figured out a way to cheat Kelemvor! This will take much time and lots of my resources, but it will be worth it to see the agony and hear the screams of my "brothers." I must find a suitable vessel for my soul. Also, one of my texts mentions "The Tome of Profane Rebirth." I must find it!" "1st of Nightal - Luck upon luck! I have found the general location of this Tome of Profane Rebirth. It resides on the Plane of Shadow. Not only that, but from my preliminary reading, it appears that Mulsantir is the perfect place to enter the Plane of Shadow. The way to cross planes is through the temple to the Death God." "14th of Ches - Rubbish! So close to my goal, only to be stopped by an impassable barrier. After making it to the Plane of Shadows, I have learned that the Tome I need is in the Death God's Vault. I refuse to go in there - even for this. It matters not. I will proceed with the ritual here on this shadow plane. Now to summon some servants to watch over me..." The entries past this point are too blood-soaked to read.

This essence swirls and glows with a bright blue light. Eight Brilliant Water Essences can be combined into one Pristine Water Essence by using the Shaper's Alembic on them. Two Brilliant Water Essences can be converted into a single Brilliant Power Essence. Brilliant Water Essences are also suitable for enchanting. To enchant an item, place it in the Enchanter's Satchel along with one or more Brilliant Water Essences, then cast the appropriate spell on the item. These scrolls appear to have been written by Myrkulite priests, centuries ago. They record the fates of many who opposed the former god of the dead, and they were probably read aloud to encourage fear of Myrkul and his faithful. At one time, there must have been many of these scrolls, but this one has decayed considerably, and much of it is missing. A prominent passage records the fate of a traitorous high priest:
"Know that all who follow the Lord of Bones shall face tests of faith. Not even his most favored are spared, as we are taught by the tale of Akachi the Betrayer.
"As a child, Akachi was offered as a Sacrifice to the church. Along with his brother, he was left unnamed upon our temple threshold, as was the custom in that time. Akachi was thus favored by our god, and named in the tradition of the eastern church, as are all those who come as babes into the faith of the dead. Indeed, he showed an uncanny faith as a boy - no poison or disease would touch him, and when the Black Whisper ravaged Mulsantir, he alone walked amongst the sick, hauled their corpses, and dug their graves unharmed. He offered salvation to those who would embrace the Lord of Bones, and it is said that those who converted to Myrkul's faith were healed.
"Each night, Akachi would return to the temple and entreat his fellow priests to join him in ministering to the dying, but all refused, except for Akachi's brother, Ereshi. They remained hiding in the temple, fearful of the plague. So Myrkul permitted the Whisper to enter his church, carried upon the robes of the two young brothers, and all his cowering priests died coughing and rasping in their beds. Only Akachi and Ereshi survived, and the boy Akachi was annointed high priest of the Mulsantir temple.
"When the plague had passed, hundreds converted to Myrkul's faith, inspired by Akachi's courage and divine favor. While Ereshi ministered to the faithful, Akachi walked the surrounding lands and converted hundreds more souls to the Lord of Bones. Myrkul's eye was upon him, and our god would visit Akachi in his dreams, instructing him in the highest mysteries of the faith, and entrusting him with missions to destroy his enemies.
"Akachi became the hand of Myrkul's justice, hunting the foes of our god across the planes. No slight against the Lord of Bones went unpunished, no betrayal went unavenged... and no honor was denied Akachi, in return. In his hand he bore a silver blade, taken from the depths of the Hells at Myrkul's bidding, and granted to him as reward. Akachi was Chosen of Myrkul, favored above all.
"But with such favor come the greatest tests. Akachi's lover was a wizardess who cared little for the gods. One day, her enchantments went awry, and she was killed in a magical conflagration. Then was Akachi distraught, for he knew what awaited his beloved. All those who died without faith were bound into the Wall of the Faithless, and finally dissolved into the substance of the Wall.
"Akachi entreated Myrkul to spare his lover. For this, he would pay any price, perform any service Myrkul might desire. But Myrkul's judgment is swift and sure, and it does not waver for those who deny the gods. Akachi's lover would remain in the Wall.
"In that moment, Akachi's pride outshone his faith. His anger turned to wrath, and he swore that he would tear down the Wall itself to take his lover back. And by this sinful vow, he was doomed, and he became the Betrayer.
"Akachi spoke wicked lies to his brother Ereshi, and turned him against Myrkul. By his devotion to his brother, Ereshi was also doomed. Ereshi set aside his name, and he took a new name that was given to him by his brother, as a token of his own betrayal.
"And Akachi spoke lies to others as well, turning many faithful against the Lord of Bones. He opened the prison of Myrkul's vault and called forth the demilich Rammaq, who had thrice attempted to become a god, and had been thwarted by Akachi himself. The Betrayer made pacts with many others, as well, promising them great rewards when the Wall of the Faithless was overthrown. Among these were Zoab, a prince of Celestia, and Sey'ryu, a queen of dragonkind. When he had assembled a mighty host, Akachi carved a doorway between the Plane of Shadow and the realm of the dead, and he led his army into Myrkul's realm.
"In that hour, Myrkul appeared in his glory, at the head of an even greater host - all the heroes of the ancient dead marched at his back, with all the masses of the False, and many baatezu who had been summoned from the Hells. Akachi's army crumbled before the Lord of Bones, and his generals fled to the darkest corners of the planes. Not even the Betrayer could stand against Myrkul, in the realm of the dead. Akachi was dragged in chains to the Basilica of Lost Hope, and Myrkul pronounced Judgment upon him.
"Be watchful, oh faithful of the Lord of Bones. For it is said that Akachi's generals still live, and that they promised to return, should the Betrayer ever stand before death's gates again. And it is also whispered that Akachi tore the soul of his lover from the Wall, before Myrkul struck him down. If this sacrilege is true, then she shall be hunted, and find no rest in this world... for the Faithless must be held to account, and none may challenge the judgment of the Lord of Bones."

This is the most thorough book of its kind - a step-by-step handbook for appeasing spirits and gods of the wilderness, something no hunter should be without, particularly within the borders of Rashemen.
Ashenwood is mentioned specifically - a ritual for burning offerings before entering the forest is here.
The book has a tendency to open to one particular page, which must've been frequently consulted by the hunters. It describes how to anoint oneself to gain the favor of Malar, beastlord and god of the hunt. It submits that one mixture that has proven empirically successful is made up of two significant elements of the forest in which hunting favor is desired, which are to be placed into a container filled with the blood of an animal that Malar would favor, which is to say, an incredibly vicious one.
This mandolin is exceptionally light.
The Silent Mandolin

This mandolin has an otherworldly feel to it. It is unfathomably light and the music it creates when strummed is barely perceptible. Any tune played upon it transforms into a haunting dirge that fills one's soul with untold sorrows.

This band was once a broken ring, found in Nefris' chambers, that must have once been an artifact of incredible strength. After absorbing your most powerful essences like a rag soaking up water, it seems to have completely mended itself in a matter of seconds and looks like it was made to fit your finger. Even now, the ring seems to be absorbing nearby energy.

Ages ago, a Rashemi youth camped at the Falls of Erech, the massive waterfall that marks the northwestern-most part of Rashemen. It was custom for youths leaving on the dajemma - journey of adulthood - to stay there at least one night, and the young man was eager to observe this tradition, giving his offering to the roaring waters before lying down to sleep. As the youth slumbered, warriors from a nearby Nar barbarian tribe moved toward him, intent on murder and theft. Before they could harm him, however, a spirit possessed the youth, and allowed him to defend himself with stunning skill and savagery. As the spirit fled his body, the youth looked around at his slain attackers in wonder, and noticed a strange new ring on his finger - an additional gift from the spirits to protect him from harm.

Let's continue on.

Emerging from the chamber where you awoke, you felt an unsettling presence within you. Shortly after, this presence lashed out, unbidden, consuming a wolf spirit and healing your wounds.
You suspect that this presence continues to fester inside you... and will likely make trouble for you again. If you can discover how you came to Rashemen, and who tore the shard of Gith from your chest, you may also learn the secret of this mysterious presence.

You have defeated the bear god Okku, but your struggle has caused a dark hunger to awaken within you.
It would seem that you must feed this hunger with spirits, or it will ultimately consume you from within, and destroy you utterly.
The Rashemi refer to you as a spirit-eater... apparently a curse that is not unknown in this country.

The Wood Man revealed that your "hunger" is the work of a dead god. He was unable to tell you which dead god was responsible, but he was certain that no god of the forest was to blame.
Further, it seems that there have been many spirit-eaters before you. All of them have ended the same - consumed from within and destroyed, victims of their own supernatural hunger.

You have discovered that your curse is the work of Myrkul, who once reigned as god of the dead. Unfortunately, Myrkul himself is now dead... slain during the Time of Troubles. Since your curse originated with Myrkul, he may have known how to remove it. But you will need to discover a way of speaking to a dead god. Safiya's mother, Nefris, may already have attempted this... so the hags suggested that you find her - or evidence of her work - at the Academy of Shapers and Binders. What is still not clear is why Myrkul devised such a terrible curse... and why the curse has now fallen to you.

In the endless sky of the Astral Plane, you found the "corpse" of the god Myrkul... whose consciousness had not entirely faded with death. Myrkul told you the truth about your curse. It seems that the empty presence within you was once a mortal man - Akachi the Betrayer - a former servant of Myrkul who turned against his god and led a rebellion to tear down the Wall of the Faithless. In punishment, Myrkul placed Akachi into the Wall of the Faithless, and watched as his mind and soul were drained away... then tore him free before his soul was completely dissolved, so that his torment would linger eternally. Akachi now exists as an empty, hollow soul - a "spirit-eater." The creature is a mindless embodiment of hunger, seeking always to fill itself up. It steals mortal bodies - such as yours - and gradually devours its victims' minds and souls. It seems that the spirit-eater had been trapped, for a time, in Okku's barrow... but someone bypassed the wards and intentionally gave you to the spirit-eater. The spirit-eater now inhabits your body... and your soul has gone to fill Akachi's place the Wall of the Faithless. Myrkul referred to the person who left you in the barrow as your "ally"... whose hidden sanctum can be accessed from the Astral Plane.

In the endless sky of the Astral Plane, you found the "corpse" of the god Myrkul... whose consciousness had not entirely faded with death. Myrkul told you the truth about your curse. It seems that the empty presence within you was once a mortal man - Akachi the Betrayer - a former servant of Myrkul who turned against his god and led a rebellion to tear down the Wall of the Faithless. All this was an effort to save the soul of his lover - the Red Wizardess who you know as the Founder. In punishment, Myrkul placed Akachi into the Wall of the Faithless, and watched as his mind and soul were drained away... then tore him free before his soul was completely dissolved, so that his torment would linger eternally. Akachi now exists as an empty, hollow soul - a "spirit-eater." The creature is a mindless embodiment of hunger, seeking always to fill itself up. It steals mortal bodies - such as yours - and gradually devours its victims' minds and souls. It seems that the spirit-eater had been trapped, for a time, in Okku's barrow... but the Founder bypassed the wards and intentionally gave you to the spirit-eater. The spirit-eater now inhabits your body... and your soul has gone to fill Akachi's place the Wall of the Faithless. The Founder had intended to use you as a means to end the curse... and her lover's suffering. According to Myrkul and the Founder, the only way to defeat the curse is to assault the City of Judgment and free your soul from the Wall...

It seems that Myrkul lied to the Founder... and to you. Freeing your soul from the Wall of the Faithless did not end the curse or free you from the spirit-eater. Instead, the monster that was once Akachi has begun to devour your soul... and you must fight him, if you hope to survive.

You imprisoned Akachi within your soul, sacrificing your freedom to ensure an end to the curse. No longer will innocent mortals suffer the spirit-eater's hunger... and Akachi will know silence and peace.
In making this sacrifice, you have accepted the fate that should have been Akachi's - you will remain in the Fugue Plane as an honored guardian of the City of Judgment.
You struck Akachi a final blow and cast him - and his hunger - out of your soul. It has been some time in coming, but at last you are free.

With Akachi's defeat, you knew that the curse of the spirit-eater was a curse no more. There were no more consequences, only power. And so, you devoured Akachi's empty spirit and took his power as your own, mastering his hunger... and becoming a creature that even the gods will learn to fear...

You inquired about the "Betrayer's Crusade" at Mulsantir's temple of Kelemvor.
The priest, Darovik, was familiar with this tale. He told you how Akachi, a powerful priest of Myrkul, led a rebellion against his god and tried to bring down the Wall of the Faithless, in the realm of the dead.
Darovik knew little more, but further details of this story may be found in an ancient scroll, the Lamentations of the Dead. If this scroll still exists, it may be found in an ancient vault, once sacred to Myrkul's faith. Though Darovik did not know its location, he suggested searching in the "shadows" of Mulsantir.

In the Death God's Vault, you encountered a ghostly scribe - a former servant of Myrkul. He told you that the Lamentations of the Dead scroll could be found in the archives, on the lower level of the Vault.

You arrived at the Rashemi garrison on Lake Ashane to find it under assault. You fought off the attackers with the aid of Nadaj, a young hathran, who expressed her gratitude.
She told you that before you enter the forest, you'll need to speak with Dalenka, the ranking Witch at the outpost.
Dalenka can be found in her house in the northwest portion of the garrison.
You restored the blighted portion of Ashenwood to its natural state, fulfilling what was to be the last request of Gnarlthorn, who seemed to prefer death after having suffered for so long.

You prayed at the Red Tree to Malar, the Beastlord, and received from him a toxic solution that will kill plant life.
Gnarlthorn unwittingly advised you that you can easily unleash it on the entire grove by dropping the item in the middle of the pond there, from which all nearby trees feed, or by pouring it on one of the trees.

You prayed at the Red Tree to Chauntea, the Earthmother, and received from her a blessed salve.
Gnarlthorn advised you that you can easily distribute it to the entire grove by setting down the salve in the middle of the pond there, from which all nearby trees feed, or by pouring it on one of the trees.
{Z}The Wall of the Faithless
Now that you've discovered which portion of the Wall contains your imprisoned soul, you must travel to that section of the city.

Although you were able to retrieve your soul from the Wall, it did not free you from Akachi as expected. The vision of the Red Woman explained that Akachi has begun to devour your soul from within, and if he succeeds, he will fully possess your body.
With Akachi's defeat, control of your ravenous hunger is within your grasp. His fate... and your own... are yours to decide.

With Myrkul gone, you knew that the curse of the spirit-eater was a curse no more. There were no more consequences, only power. And so, you devoured Akachi's empty spirit and took his power as your own, mastering his hunger... and becoming a creature that even the gods will learn to fear...

Upon entering the Veil to seek Lienna, you found the place overrun by Red Wizards and their minions.
Magda, one of the actors at the Veil, gave you an odd black stone, and told you that Lienna has retreated to the "shadowy reflection" of the theater. To find her, you need only bring the Shadow Stone to the back corner of Lienna's bedroom, near her mirror.

Lienna, proprietor of the Veil Theater, has apparently destroyed herself to avoid capture by Red Wizards.
Safiya has suggested that you find and question the Veil's actors, who escaped the theater when you arrived.
You had hoped that Lienna might tell you how you came to Rashemen, and who tore the shard from your chest. Though Lienna is dead, her actors may still have useful information...

Now that Okku's spirit army has lifted its siege of Mulsantir, the Witches have released Lienna's actors and returned them to the Veil Theater.
Whenever you wish, you may question them about Lienna - who she was, and what she might have known about you... and the curse that now afflicts you.

Magda has given you the key to a "secret room" that once belonged to Lienna, former proprietor of the Veil.
From Magda's description, Lienna may have had some dealings with a Thayan wizard. Worse, Lienna may have been the one who cut the shard from your chest.
The only way to know for certain is to investigate her locked room, which lies in the Shadow Plane version of the Veil.

You encountered the creatures who brought you to Rashemen and placed you in Okku's barrow. They were a group of shadow gargoyles, apparently acting on Lienna's bidding.
The gargoyles did not know why you were chosen by Lienna and her "red twin." Nor did they know why you were left in the cavern, or what happened to you there.
But the gargoyles believed that Lienna and her ally were acting on advice from the Slumbering Coven, a collection of nine powerful hags who dwell in a sunken Imaskari ruin, to the east of Mulsantir. Since Lienna is dead, and her ally is missing, you will have to seek your answers from the hags, themselves.

The shadow gargoyles who brought you to Rashemen did not know Lienna's purpose in abducting you. However, the gargoyles revealed that Lienna got the idea from a collection of hag oracles called the Slumbering Coven. This Coven dwells in the ruins of an Imaskari city that long ago sunk beneath Lake Mulsantir.
To learn more about why you were brought here, you must find the sunken city and the Slumbering Coven.

You spoke with Fentomy, who claimed to be a fisherman. He spoke cryptically, but seemed to imply that the Sunken City can only be entered at nightfall.
Perhaps you should camp here until night to see if a passage into the city reveals itself.

U'juk and his tribe of uthraki were not very satisfied with the two scrawny berserkers you sent to them. But you were rewarded nonetheless.
In exchange for feeding his tribe, U'juk taught you how to use your spirit-eater abilities to devour souls.
You did not feed U'juk and his tribe of uthraki, and your relationship with the Hill Tribe ended with violence. Whatever knowledge U'juk may have had is lost to you now.
You met U'juk, the leader of the uthraki Hill Tribe. He spoke of a kinship that he felt uthraki have with you, mentioning that the spirit-eater wears many shapes, like the uthraki.

The two half-celestial siblings, Efrem and Susah, mentioned someone called Akachi, who led the "Betrayer's Crusade."
You have never heard of this Crusade before... perhaps others in Mulsantir may know more.

In the Ice Troll Lodge, you asked Nak'kai the shaman about your curse. He evidently believes that the curse was inflicted upon the country of Rashemen by the gods... as punishment for the actions of a Rashemi priest, who lived centuries ago.
According to Nak'kai, the priest was a follower of Myrkul, former god of the dead, and he led a rebellion against the gods.
It is possible that the priests of Kelemvor - current god of the dead - would know more about this rebellious priest.

In an ancient vault, hidden in Shadow Mulsantir, you encountered a ghostly scribe.
He spoke of someone called Akachi the Betrayer - a former high priest of Myrkul who turned against his god and led an army to assault the City of Judgment, in the realm of the dead.
It is possible that the priests of Kelemvor - current god of the dead - would know more about the Betrayer.

You spoke to Darovik at the Temple of Kelemvor and learned about Akachi's assault on the City of Judgment during Myrkul's reign.
Darovik told you that the Lamentations of the Dead, a scroll with more information about the Betrayer, might be found within a shadowy vault that contains ancient Myrkulite treasures.
You tricked Anya into running off to find her imaginary lover Gannayev in the crags where the uthraki dwell.

You survived the Skein and reached the Slumbering Coven in Coveya Kurg'annis. You used your new Dream Haunting ability to enter the Hag's Dreamscape.
Now you must find the Coven and speak with them.

Your conversation with the Slumbering Coven was enlightening - the hags told you that your curse originated with the dead god, Myrkul... and if you wish to end your hunger, you will need to find a way to speak to him.
Some of the exiles in the Skein banded together for protection. Their leader in spirit is a blind half-drow woman they call "The Sleeper." You are not quite sure what to make of her.

You spoke with Djafi, one of the masters of the Academy of Shapers and Binders, who told you that Araman has killed Nefris - Safiya's mother and the school's headmistress - and taken control of the academy, confirming your worst suspicions.
While you can no longer ask Nefris directly, you still need to determine how she planned to contact Myrkul if you are to remove the curse he created.
Make your way to Nefris' tower and look for evidence of how she intended to commune with Myrkul.

You spoke with Myrkul and learned the full history and nature of your curse.
He also suggested that your "ally" - the person who placed you in Okku's barrow and who now possesses the Sword of Gith - is waiting for you in a hidden sanctum. This sanctum can be accessed from a nearby portal, which has just opened.
Determine whether Myrkul spoke the truth - find this new portal, and see what lies on the other side.

Passing through a newly-opened portal near Myrkul's corpse, you have found yourself in a hidden sanctum, far beneath the earth.
According to Myrkul, you will find your "ally" - and the reforged Sword of Gith - somewhere in this ancient place.
And it seems that you are not alone. Myrkul's servants have entered the portal before you, and they are also hunting for your mysterious "ally"... though their intent may be more violent than your own.

You confronted Araman before he was able to breach the sanctum's entrance and defeated him.
The way is now open for you to speak with your "ally," whose knowledge should provide answers to all the remaining questions about your spirit-eater curse.

A student at the Academy of Shapers and Binders named Selkhit is working on an "intellectual challenge" posed to all of the academy's students by its headmistress.
As she describes it, there are two rooms that initially contain equal numbers of ice and fire mephits. At one point, one room contained only fire mephits and one only ice mephits, but their natural tendency is to intermingle at a random end eventually even basis.
The goal of the challenge is to reverse this course, returning the rooms to a state in which one contains only ice mephits and one contains only fire mephits. The means of doing this is a lever that temporarily opens a door between the rooms, instantly switching the places of the mephit in each room closest to the door.
According to Selkhit, the pent up energy created by segregating the mephits is set up to be harnessed and transferred for use in the reconstitution of a soul that has been deliberately divided, a supposedly impossible feat, and the new soul is prize to the first student to complete the challenge.
Complete the challenge and fuse the separate pieces into one soul. Then retrieve the soul from its stand in the room where Selkhit is working.

You and Nefris are now supposedly the only two people to successfully complete her mephit separation challenge, and the newly fused soul is yours for the taking. It can be found on the soul housing stand in the room where you met Selkhit.

In the Death God's Vault you came across a crematorium with a furnace that is haunted by the spirits of those who were cremated there.
The spirit of a former High Priest of Myrkul seems to be the leader of the furnace spirits, but he refuses to speak with you. Return later when you've found some way to influence him.

In the Death God's Vault you came across a crematorium with a furnace that is haunted by the spirits of those who were cremated there.
The spirit of a former High Priest of Myrkul seems to be the leader of the furnace spirits, but he refuses to speak with you.
Perhaps your new spirit-eater abilities can be used to make the spirit more cooperative.

In the Death God's Vault you came across a crematorium with a furnace that is haunted by the spirits of those who were cremated there.
Using your spirit-eater abilities, you convinced the leader of the spirits, a former High Priest of Myrkul, to speak with you. Even though he is speaking now, he is still ellusive.

In the Death God's Vault you came across a crematorium with a furnace that was haunted by the spirits of those who were cremated there.
You used your spirit-eater powers to combine all of the furnace spirits into the husk of the bear god Okku. This created a powerful undead minion that calls itself One of Many.

In the Death God's Vault you came across a crematorium with a furnace that was haunted by the spirits of those who were cremated there.
You used your spirit-eater powers to exorcise all the spirits in the furnace, and gained the ability to grant eternal rest to spirits as an alternative to devouring them.

In the Death God's Vault you came across a crematorium with a furnace that was haunted by the spirits of those who were cremated there.
You used your spirit eater powers to devour all of the spirits in the furnace.

In the Death God's Vault you came across a crematorium with a furnace that was haunted by the spirits of those who were cremated there.
You used your spirit-eater powers to free all of the spirits from the furnace. You have the uneasy feeling that his might cause repercussions later, as most of the spirits released were powerful, evil, and angry.
{B}Shadow Mulsantir

The Shadow Stone that Magda gave you opened a portal in the Veil Theater in Mulsantir. The portal took you to a version of the Veil Theater in the Plane of Shadows.
Perhaps the Shadow Stone can be used to find other portals to the Plane of Shadows in Mulsantir.

Efrem and Susah told you about Shadow Mulsantir. They said that, according to rumor, there are several "weak spots" in Mulsantir that reveal themselves at night, or in dark places. These places can be used to cross into the Shadow Plane.
They suggested that the witches of Mulsantir may know more.

You asked Sheva Whitefeather about Shadow Mulsantir. She told you little so that you would not spread even more fear among the populace of Mulsantir. However, she marked a location on your map and told you to go there at night with the Shadow Stone that Magda gave you.

You discovered a portal in Mulsantir that led to the Shadow Plane version of Mulsantir.
Mulsantir is rumored to have several such "weak spots" which the Shadow Stone you were given by Magda will reveal at night.
{D}Passage to Thay

According to the Coven, the dead god Myrkul is the architect of your curse... and the only being who might know how it can be ended.
Safiya's mother, Nefris, may have discovered a way of speaking to the dead god - but she has returned to the Academy of Shapers and Binders, in Thay.
To reach the Academy, you will need to use one of Lienna's portals. Return to the Shadow Veil, and speak to the Keeper of Doors. He will be able to open a portal to the Academy.

You have passed through Lienna's portal and arrived at the Thaymount... a series of volcanic peaks where the Red Wizards maintain many of their academies and private fortresses.
Now you must gain entrance to the Academy of Shapers and Binders... by whatever means necessary.

Near the Academy entrance, you were met by Master Djafi, a former friend and ally of Nefris. It seems that Nefris has been slain, and the wizard Araman has taken her place as headmaster.
This complicates matters considerably...
{Z}Beyond the Black Gate

With the Sword of Gith in hand, you can now open the Betrayer's Gate - a passage between the realm of the living and the kingdom of the dead. On the other side, you will find the Wall of the Faithless... where your soul now lies.
The Gate was once used by Akachi to lead his army against the City of Judgment. It is located on the lower level of the Death God's Vault, in Shadow Mulsantir.
Once you pass through the Gate, it is unlikely that you will be able to return. You also suspect that the Gate is being watched from afar... and that Akachi's former captains, who you glimpsed in the Coven's dream, have been waiting for this moment to resume their Crusade...

You have left the mortal world behind you and passed through the Betrayer's Gate to the realm of the dead.
As expected, Akachi's captains have been awaiting the reopening of the Gate for many centuries, and they are already assembling their armies outside the City of Judgment, hoping to resume Akachi's Crusade.
They await you at the gates of the City, along with a delegation of the City's defenders.

You decided to support Akachi's captains in their assault upon the City of Judgment. Your choice is not likely to win you many friends amongst the gods... but that will matter little if you don't retrieve your soul from the Wall.
You decided to assist the defenders of the City against the Third Crusade... and to trust that they will permit you to retrieve your soul when the battle is won.
The Story So Far

You were raised in the marsh village of West Harbor, on the Sword Coast. Your early years were uneventful - raised by your foster father, Daeghun, you grew to adulthood with little knowledge of your past.
That changed just a few months ago, on the night of the High Harvest Festival. West Harbor was attacked by a force of githyanki - interplanar warriors who were seeking the lost shards of an ancient blade. You helped to repel their attack and save your village... only to be sent away by your foster father, bearing one of the mysterious shards to the city of Neverwinter. Along the way, you assembled a band of companions - some more loyal than others - that included Khelgar Ironfist, a hotheaded dwarf, Neeshka, a tiefling rogue, Casavir the paladin, Bishop the traitorous ranger, and others.
In Neverwinter, you discovered that the githyanki were only a small part of a much greater tale. The shards they sought were once a part of the legendary Sword of Gith, which had been shattered years ago, when the warlock Ammon Jerro wielded it against the monstrous King of Shadows. Their battle was fought in your village of West Harbor, when you were a mere infant... and as the Sword burst into dozens of shards, one of them struck you, and embedded itself near your heart.
You defeated the githyanki who pursued you, only to become embroiled in a new struggle against the King of Shadows, whose gathering armies now threatened Neverwinter and the Sword Coast. Over the course of your adventures, you earned a knighthood and were granted command of a castle, becoming Knight-Captain of Crossroad Keep. You also witnessed the destruction of your home village, which was razed by a servant of the King of Shadows... only your foster father and a few others survived.
In the end, you allied with the warlock Ammon Jerro and commanded the defenses of Crossroad Keep against an army of undead. Then you fought your way into the fortress of the King of Shadows and struck him down. But with the King's death, his fortress began to collapse... and you were unable to escape. You remember great blocks of stone tumbling around you... the cries of your surviving companions... then darkness, and nothing more.
Fragments of a Mask

In a dream, you were given a single fragment of a shattered mask. Incredibly, the fragment was still in your hand when you woke - somehow, it can exist outside the dream.
You sense that this object is important, though you don't yet know why.

You have acquired a second fragment of a shattered mask. Both were given to you in dreams, but somehow, they also exist in the waking world.
It is clear that they are important and are somehow related to your curse.

You have acquired three fragments of a shattered mask. Together, they would form a whole... but you cannot reassemble them by any ordinary means.
Two of the masks were given to you by mysterious figures who you encountered in dreams - the Red Woman and the Boy. Both suggested that the fragments somehow contain their essences. You found the third fragment embedded in the Wall of the Faithless - or at least, a dream-version of the Wall. Incredibly, all three fragments are able to exist in the waking world.
You suspect that you may see the Red Woman and the Boy again... and they may provide you with a means to join the fragments together.

Before your final battle against the Faceless Man, the Red Woman and the Boy appeared to you once again. They explained that the three mask fragments contain all that remains of Akachi the Betrayer - those aspects of his soul that survived his imprisonment in the Wall of the Faithless.
The Red Woman joined the three fragments together and gave you the completed mask. If you wear this mask in your battle against the Faceless Man, it will help shield you against his hunger.
What is more, if you defeat the Faceless Man - the empty shell that was once Akachi - you can call forth the Red Woman and the Boy and restore Akachi to what he was... and the curse of the spirit-eater will end.
Shocking Golem Arms

These gauntlets appear relatively ordinary, but when stricken with enough force, an electrical impulse is discharged, shocking anything they make contact with. A golem using these as its arms would be incredibly dangerous, and should in no way be considered a bathtub toy.
Properties: Enhancement Bonus: +3 Damage Bonus: +3d6 Electrical
Scorching Gaze Golem Head

The eyes of this golem head glow red, even though it is inert. Placed atop a golem, a single look could be deadly to its foes.
Properties: Bonus Ability: Scorching Gaze
Swift Golem Legs

These legs were clearly built for speed. They are lean, aerodynamic, and highly flexible. A golem using these would likely find it easier to both float like a will-o-wisp and sting like a manticore.
Properties: Improved AC: +4 dodge bonus Haste
Galvanized Golem Torso

This golem torso appears to have been treated using a specialized forging technique whereby the piece is heated to extraordinary temperatures and then quickly cooled. The process is repeated over and over, and with each repetition the outer shell hardens until only the rarest and most refined of metals can even scratch it.
Properties: Damage Reduction 10/Adamantine
Weather-resistant Golem Torso

Magical wards carved directly into this golem torso carry enchantments to prevent weathering, and consequently, this golem is well preserved despite its age.
Properties: Damage Immunity: Acid Damage Immunity: Cold Damage Immunity: Electricity Damage Immunity: Fire
Ashenwood

The vast Ashenwood reaches all the way from the ice-encrusted shores of Lake Ashane in the west to the foothills of the mystical mountains known as the Running Rocks in the east. The Rashemi refuse to inhabit it, as it is densely populated with spirits, but accomplished hunters occasionally enter its borders in search of the magnificent animal specimens said to dwell within.
Burning Grove
Despite the frigid weather, there are rumors of a fire in this region of the Ashenwood that rages endlessly.

Rumored to be an ancient place, rich in spirits, the Wells of Lurue were once sacred to the beasts and wild creatures of the land. The great beasts have not been seen in years, but the air still echoes with mournful howls...

Shrouded in a cold mist, Mulsantir clings to the bluffs that overlook the river. A prominent ferry landing serves the travelers who ply the Golden Way, and the city is encircled by numerous fortifications - it has survived at least five Thayan sieges.
The gates of Mulsantir rise above a marshy lowland. A prominent east-west trade route - the Golden Way - passes into the city at this location.
These caves are the burial ground for a clan of paragon bears and the beasts who once served them. They are dug into a great earthen mound, which rises above the ruins of an ancient Imaskari outpost.

Immil Vale is an oasis in the High Country - a secluded valley situated along the northern face of the Running Rocks that continually defies the harsh winter that surrounds it on all sides. Some regard it as a spiritual nexus, and journey tremendous distances to see it.

This was once the site of a grand Imaskari city, whose name has been lost to time. Though the ruins are all but swallowed beneath the turbulent waves of Lake Mulsantir, it is rumored that they are home to the Slumbering Coven, and the seat of power for all the hags of Rashemen.
Black Dragon
{Workbench}Chemist's Workbench
{Workbench}Craftsman's Workbench

Tall and ruggedly handsome, Gann wears a sarcastic half-smile and affects an air of casual indifference. His skin has a faintly blue or violet cast... a legacy of the night hag who was his mother. Unlike other hagspawn - men born of a human father and a hag mother - Gann's face is neither brutish nor ill-favored... but the Rashemi still treat him with a good deal of suspicion.

In life, Okku was a paragon bear - one of an ancient race of intelligent beasts who ruled the wild places. In death, he has become a creature of spirit, regarded by the Rashemi people as a deity of the land. But his teeth and claws are no less sharp than they once were... and his strength no longer depends upon bone and sinew, arising instead from the multitude of spirits and beasts who revere his name.

One of Many is many evils in one - its consciousness composed of a multitude of murderers, lunatics, and other human detritus, all driven to insanity by imprisonment in Death God's Vault in life and then decades of disembodied misery in the Vault's crematorium. As such, One of Many is malice personified and wishes to either feed on or do violence to all sentient beings - all except for you. You are the creator of this undead aberration so, for better or worse, it is bound to you, and you to it.
Black Dragon{shape}
Blue Dragon{shape}

Kaji is a homunculus - an artificial creation, shaped and given life by Safiya's magic. He is about 18 inches tall, with rough, warty skin. Though he seems generally harmless, his teeth are quite sharp, and his fingers are long and quick... the mark of a formidable thief.
This creature is an absolute, pure embodiment of hunger - all it touches is drained of life.

These scrolls appear to have been written by Myrkulite priests, centuries ago. They record the fates of many who opposed the former god of the dead, and they were probably read aloud to encourage fear of Myrkul and his faithful. At one time, there must have been many of these scrolls, but this one has decayed considerably, and much of it is missing. A prominent passage records the fate of a traitorous high priest:
"Know that all who follow the Lord of Bones shall face tests of faith. Not even his most favored are spared, as we are taught by the tale of Akachi the Betrayer.
"As a child, Akachi was offered as a Sacrifice to the church. Along with his brother, he was left unnamed upon our temple threshold, as was the custom in that time. Akachi was thus favored by our god, and named in the tradition of the eastern church, as are all those who come as babes into the faith of the dead. Indeed, he showed an uncanny faith as a boy - no poison or disease would touch him, and when the Black Whisper ravaged Mulsantir, he alone walked amongst the sick, hauled their corpses, and dug their graves unharmed. He offered salvation to those who would embrace the Lord of Bones, and it is said that those who converted to Myrkul's faith were healed.
"Each night, Akachi would return to the temple and entreat his fellow priests to join him in ministering to the dying, but all refused, except for Akachi's brother, Eveshi. They remained hiding in the temple, fearful of the plague. So Myrkul permitted the Whisper to enter his church, carried upon the robes of the two young brothers, and all his cowering priests died coughing and rasping in their beds. Only Akachi and Eveshi survived, and the boy Akachi was annointed high priest of the Mulsantir temple.
"When the plague had passed, hundreds converted to Myrkul's faith, inspired by Akachi's courage and divine favor. While Eveshi ministered to the faithful, Akachi walked the surrounding lands and converted hundreds more souls to the Lord of Bones. Myrkul's eye was upon him, and our god would visit Akachi in his dreams, instructing him in the highest mysteries of the faith, and entrusting him with missions to destroy his enemies.
"Akachi became the hand of Myrkul's justice, hunting the foes of our god across the planes. No slight against the Lord of Bones went unpunished, no betrayal went unavenged... and no honor was denied Akachi, in return. In his hand he bore a silver blade, taken from the depths of the Hells at Myrkul's bidding, and granted to him as reward. Akachi was Chosen of Myrkul, favored above all.
"But with such favor come the greatest tests. Akachi's lover was a wizardess who cared little for the gods. One day, her enchantments went awry, and she was killed in a magical conflagration. Then was Akachi distraught, for he knew what awaited his beloved. All those who died without faith were bound into the Wall of the Faithless, and finally dissolved into the substance of the Wall.
"Akachi entreated Myrkul to spare his lover. For this, he would pay any price, perform any service Myrkul might desire. But Myrkul's judgment is swift and sure, and it does not waver for those who deny the gods. Akachi's lover would remain in the Wall.
"In that moment, Akachi's pride outshone his faith. His anger turned to wrath, and he swore that he would tear down the Wall itself to take his lover back. And by this sinful vow, he was doomed, and he became the Betrayer.
"Akachi spoke wicked lies to his brother Eveshi, and turned him against Myrkul. By his devotion to his brother, Eveshi was also doomed. Eveshi set aside his name, and he took a new name that was given to him by his brother, as a token of his own betrayal.
"And Akachi spoke lies to others as well, turning many faithful against the Lord of Bones. He opened the prison of Myrkul's vault and called forth the demilich Rammaq, who had thrice attempted to become a god, and had been thwarted by Akachi himself. The Betrayer made pacts with many others, as well, promising them great rewards when the Wall of the Faithless was overthrown. Among these were Zoab, a prince of Celestia, and Sey'ryu, a queen of dragonkind. When he had assembled a mighty host, Akachi carved a doorway between the Plane of Shadow and the realm of the dead, and he led his army into Myrkul's realm.
"In that hour, Myrkul appeared in his glory, at the head of an even greater host - all the heroes of the ancient dead marched at his back, with all the masses of the False, and many baatezu who had been summoned from the Hells. Akachi's army crumbled before the Lord of Bones, and his generals fled to the darkest corners of the planes. Not even the Betrayer could stand against Myrkul, in the realm of the dead. Akachi was dragged in chains to the Basilica of Lost Hope, and Myrkul pronounced Judgment upon him.
"Be watchful, oh faithful of the Lord of Bones. For it is said that Akachi's generals still live, and that they promised to return, should the Betrayer ever stand before death's gates again. And it is also whispered that Akachi tore the soul of his lover from the Wall, before Myrkul struck him down. If this sacrilege is true, then she shall be hunted, and find no rest in this world... for the Faithless must be held to account, and none may challenge the judgment of the Lord of Bones."

Prostrate on this cot lies a shell of a man, his eyes deeply sunken into a face so thin it might be in the early stages of decay. His skin is grayish-white and bloodless, and were it not for the labored rattle of his unsteady breathing, he would be easily mistakable for a corpse. Certainly he cannot be far off from becoming one himself. Flies swarm around him, settling variously on his cheeks, nose, beard, and mouth. He makes no move to brush them away.
What horrific ordeal he has been through, you can only imagine.

This book contains the collected sayings and stories of a revered Rashemi Witch, who seems to have died over a century ago. Most of these writings are religious in nature, some are folk tales, and a few seem to be remedies for various rashes and warts.
One page has been dogeared, however, and a brief passage is entitled "Of the Ravenous Four":
"So spoke Immith Yabog...
"In my youth, the spirit-eater curse was said to be rampant in the woodlands of the north. I was sent from Urling, with three of my hathran sisters, to seek the truth of these rumors.
"Outside the great forest, we came upon a fleeing mass of simple folk, who spoke fearfully of a foul cult - men and women who had begun to worship the spirit-eater as a god, who passed its power amongst themselves, and went into the deep forest to feed.
"Retracing the villagers' steps, we soon came upon the encampment of these wicked folk, taking them by surprise, and slaying many. Only four managed to escape us, fleeing into the deep forest. One of these bore the dark hunger of a spirit-eater, and she devoured two of my sisters before she made her escape. My remaining sister and I dared not follow.
"But we learned much from the remains of their camp. These folk were unlike others afflicted by the curse - indeed, they referred to their dark hunger as the Gift. And we discovered that many of those we had taken for Rashemi were shapeshifted uthraki. The uthraki worshipped the one who possessed the Gift, and had learned much lore of the spirit-eater, to pass on to others who bore the hunger and reveled in it as they did..."

This essence swirls and glows with a bright white light. Eight Brilliant Air Essences can be combined into one Pristine Air Essence by using the Shaper's Alembic on them. Two Brilliant Air Essences can be converted into a single Brilliant Power Essence. Brilliant Air Essences are also suitable for enchanting. To enchant an item, place it in the Enchanter's Satchel along with one or more Brilliant Air Essences, then cast the appropriate spell on the item. Use up to four Brilliant Air Essences for more powerful enchantments. Any item can be enchanted to hold up to three item properties total, or four if the enchanter is of epic level. Enchanting an item with a property it already has will replace the item's existing property, whether or not the new property is better than the existing one. The required caster level depends upon the number of essences you are using: 1 Brilliant Essence -- Caster Level 12 2 Brilliant Essences -- Caster Level 15 3 Brilliant Essences -- Caster Level 18 4 Brilliant Essences -- Caster Level 21 Standard recipes are: Craft Magic Arms and Armor Weapons: Shock Weapon. Spell: Call Lightning or Lightning Bolt Armor: Weight Reduction. Spell: Protection from Energy Craft Wondrous Item Cloak: Energy Resistance (electricity) and Save Bonus versus electrical attacks. Spell: Endure Elements Gloves: Unarmed Damage Bonus (electricity). Spell: Shocking Grasp Amulet: Energy Resistance (electricity). Spell: Resist Energy Rings: Save Bonus versus electricity attacks. Spell: Resistance *Note that while the Cloak provides two benefits, the amulet and ring bonuses are greater for a given number of essences.

This essence glows brightly, yet erratically, with either the fragments of a powerful spirit or those of many weaker ones. This small bag can be used to enchant items and functions like a portable workbench. To enchant an item, simply place it in this satchel along with one or more brilliant essences, then cast the appropriate spell as indicated in the essence's description. For example, to create a frost weapon, place one brilliant water essence and any weapon into the Enchanter's Satchel, then cast ice storm on the satchel. Essences are automatically distilled from the remains of many creatures, such as elementals and most beasts. Such essences are typically only of volatile quality and then must be combined using a Shaper's Alembic to create a brilliant variety. Rarer recipes and essences might be discovered throughout your adventures.

You acquired this object in a dream... and when you awoke, it was still clutched in your hand. The object appears to be a piece of a shattered mask.
In the dream, this fragment was given to you by a gold-skinned woman, garbed in red. She looked nearly identical to your companion, Safiya. The fragment's colors shift and blur as you look at it, though it most often has a reddish tinge.

You acquired this object in a dream... and when you awoke, it was still clutched in your hand. The object appears to be a piece of a shattered mask.
In the dream, you pried this mask from the fingers of Bishop, your onetime companion, who had been absorbed into a wall of screaming souls. The fragment's colors shift and blur as you look at it, though it most often appears pale and maggot-gray, drinking in the light but reflecting none.
This outfit is used to disguise Safiya as a Rashemi peasant. It is prudent for Safiya to wear these clothes within Mulsantir, where many fear and revile the Red Wizards of Thay.
You discussed your faith with Yusev. This has convinced him to be a more devout Kelemvorite.

You convinced Anya that the Gannayev of her dreams was not real. She left her dream with some insight into her latent dream-walking powers.
Janiik should be pleased that you cured his daughter. Return to him for a reward.

You managed to significantly thin out the numbers of petitioners in Nightshore. The hagspawn guards agreed to let you enter Coveya Kurg'annis at the last place in line to see the Slumbering Coven.
Make your way to the front of the line in Coveya Kurg'annis.

You discovered an ancient vault in Shadow Mulsantir, which stands on the site of the temple of the dead.
Within, you found a great, black door that may lead to the lower level of the Vault. Unfortunately, it is locked.
You spoke to the ghost of a temple scribe, who believed that the key was in the possession of the last high priest who presided over Myrkul's church in Mulsantir.
Darovik, a priest of Kelemvor, told you that this high priest was hurled alive into a crematorium furnace. He is probably referring to the furnace in the Death God's Vault.
Hey, get out of the way!
You begin reading the infernal contract.
What have you done?! He was my last hope!

Caster Level(s): Cleric 8, Sorcerer / Wizard 8 Innate Level: 8 School: Necromancy Descriptor(s): Death Component(s): Verbal, Somatic Range: See text Area of Effect / Target: See text Duration: See text Save: Fortitude negates Spell Resistance: Yes
This spell allows you to scribe a potent rune of power upon a surface. When triggered, a symbol of death slays one or more creatures within 60 feet of the symbol (treat as a burst) whose combined total current hit points do not exceed 150. The symbol of death affects the closest creatures first, skipping creatures with too many hit points to affect. The symbol lasts for 1 minute per caster level or until it has affected 150 hit points' worth of creatures, whichever comes first. Any creature that enters the area while the symbol of death is active is subject to its effect, whether or not that creature was in the area when it was triggered. A symbol of death is triggered whenever a creature touches the rune or passes over the rune. You and all creatures within your party are automatically attuned to the rune and as such cannot trigger it and are immune to its effects, even if within its radius when triggered.
Note: Magic traps such as symbol of death are hard to detect and disable. A rogue (only) can use the Search skill to find a symbol of death and Disable Device to thwart it. The DC in each case is 25 + spell level, or 33 for symbol of death. Also, a symbol of death can be removed by a successful dispel magic targeted on the rune.

Swashbuckler The swashbuckler embodies the concepts of daring and panache. Favoring agility and wit over brute force, the swashbuckler excels both in combat situations and social interactions, making her a versatile character indeed. Class Features: - Hit Die: d10 - Base Attack Bonus: High. - High Saves: Fortitude. - Weapon Proficiencies: Simple and martial weapons. - Armor Proficiencies: Light armor. - Skill Points: 4 + Int modifier per level, x4 at first level. - Class Skills: Bluff, Craft Armor, Craft Weapon, Diplomacy, Lore, Parry, Taunt, and Tumble. - Weapon Finesse: A swashbuckler gains Weapon Finesse as a bonus feat at 1st level even if she does not qualify for the feat. - Grace: A swashbuckler gains a +1 bonus on Reflex saves at 2nd level. This bonus increases to +2 at 11th level, to +3 at 20th level, and to +4 at 29th level. A swashbuckler loses this bonus when wearing medium or heavy armor or when encumbered. - Insightful Strike: At 3rd level, a swashbuckler becomes able to place her finesse attacks where they deal greater damage. She applies her Intelligence bonus (if any) as a bonus on damage rolls (in addition to any Strength bonus she may have) with any light weapon, as well as any other weapon that can be used with Weapon Finesse, such as a rapier. Targets immune to sneak attacks or critical hits are immune to the swashbuckler's insightful strike. A swashbuckler cannot use this ability when wearing medium or heavy armor or when encumbered. - Swashbuckler Dodge: A swashbuckler is trained at focusing her defense on a single opponent in melee. She gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC against melee attacks from her current target or last attacker. This bonus increases by +1 at every five levels after 5th (+2 at 10th level, +3 at 15th, +4 at 20th, +5 at 25th, and +6 at 30th). A swashbuckler loses this bonus when wearing medium or heavy armor or when encumbered. - Mobility: At 7th level, a swashbuckler gains Mobility as a bonus feat even if she does not qualify for it. - Improved Flanking: A swashbuckler of 8th level or higher who is flanking an opponent gains a +4 bonus on attacks instead of a +2 bonus on attacks. - Lucky: At 11th level, a swashbuckler gains Luck of Heroes as a bonus feat. - Acrobatic Skill Mastery: At 13th level, a swashbuckler becomes so certain in the use of her acrobatic skills that she can use them reliably even under adverse conditions. When making a Tumble check, a swashbuckler cannot roll less than 5, even if in combat. - Weakening Critical: A swashbuckler of 14th level or higher who scores a critical hit against a creature also deals 2 points of Strength damage to the creature. Creatures immune to critical hits are immune to this effect. - Slippery Mind: When a swashbuckler reaches 17th level, her mind becomes more difficult to control. If the swashbuckler fails her save against an enchantment spell or effect, she automatically gets one reroll. She gets only this one extra chance to succeed at a certain saving throw. -Wounding Critical: A swashbuckler of 19th level or higher who scores a critical hit against a creature also deals 2 points of Constitution damage to the creature. (This damage is in addition to the Strength damage dealt by the swashbuckler's weakening critical class feature.) Creatures immune to critical hits are immune to this effect.

Doomguide (PRESTIGE CLASS: This class is not available at character creation and must be unlocked by meeting special requirements, listed below.) Those who worry about life after death turn to the doomguides of Kelemvor, an elite order of spellcasting warriors in service to the Judge of the Damned, to answer their fears with promises of a painless transition and a fair judgement in the afterlife. When not administering to the needs of those about to die, doomguides halt the spread of necromancy by cleansing the taint of unlife through careful application of faith, spells, and bladecraft. As both compassionate undertakers and vigorous foes of undead, doomguides represent the inherent dualism that defines death in the Realms. Doomguides come exclusively from the ranks of Kelemvor's clergy. Requirements: Alignment: Any Lawful. Skills: Diplomacy 5 ranks Feats: Extra Turning, Great Fortitude Spells: Level 3 divine spellcaster Deity: Kelemvor Class Features: - Hit Die: d6 - Base Attack Bonus: High. - High Saves: Will. - Weapon Proficiencies: Doomguides gain no weapon proficiencies. - Armor Proficiencies: Doomguides gain no armor proficiencies. - Skill Points: 2 + Int Modifier. - Class Skills: Concentration, Craft Alchemy, Craft Armor, Craft Weapon, Diplomacy, Heal, Lore, and Spellcraft - Spells Per Day: At each doomguide level, the character gains new spells per day as if he had also gained a level in a divine spellcasting class to which he belonged before adding the prestige class level. He does not, however, gain any other benefit a character of that class would have gained. - Kelemvor's Boon: By the grace of the Lord of the Dead, doomguides add their doomguide class levels to their cleric levels for purposes turning or destroying undead, both for the initial turning check and the turning damage roll. - Bonus Feats: Bonus Feats: At Level 2, the Doomguide gains Improved Turning. At level 3, they gain Extra Turning II. At level 6, they gain Divine Vengeance. At level 10, they gain Empower Turning and Extra Turning III. - Save Bonus: At 4th level, doomguides get a +4 bonus on saving throws against death effects and to saving throws to overcome a negative level. Upon reaching 8th level, a doomguide always makes his saving throw to overcome a negative level. - Bond of Fatal Touch : The doomguide's devotion to Kelemvor and dedication to the teachings of the Lord of the Crystal Spire has helped him to establish certain supernatural links to Fatal Touch, Kelemvor's powerful bastard sword. These links manifest in the form of a pale green nimbus around the weapon, representing the ability of a doomguide to increase the power of the weapons he wields. The ability lasts for 1 round each time it is used, and can be invoked a number of times per day equal to the doomguide's Charisma bonus (minimum one). A doomguide must decide to use the ability before attacking, and if the attack misses that use is wasted. At 5th level, the bond grants wielded weapons the ghost touch property. At 7th level, weapons wielded by the doomguide gain both ghost touch and the undead bane properties. At 9th level, wielded weapons gain the ghost touch, undead bane, and disruption properties even if they are not bludgeoning weapons. The weapon's normal abilities still apply. - Ethereal Purge: At 8th level, once per day the doomguide may surround himself with a sphere of power with a radius of 5 feet per class level that forces all concealed creatures in the area to manifest on or shift themselves to the Material Plane, as appropriate. Such creatures may attempt a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 doomguide's class level + doomguide's Wisdom bonus) to resist this effect. Those who fail suffer the above effects and are prevented from returning to concealment for 1 minute per class level. - Kelemvor's Grace: At 10th level, a doomguide gains complete immunity to death effects. Furthermore, allies within 10 feet of him gain a +4 bonus on saving throws against death effects and to saving throws to overcome a negative level.
