Oh, hello! You look like the intrepid adventurer type. Want to help a businessman out?
You see, until just a few months ago the old cold iron mine to the southeast - in the Sword Mountains - was overrun by orcs, goblins, and other unpleasant creatures.
I'd planned to gather together some people - probably some veterans from the Shadow War - to clear out the orcs and seize the mine for Phandalin. Maybe finally put out some good ore for once...
When suddenly, low and behold, these two representatives of some Mining Company mysteriously show up, say they've cleared out the orcs and won the rights to operate the mine.

It just doesn't seem right. Maybe they have connections to the Black Network. Maybe they're representatives of Luskan, or Amn, or... I don't know. But how did they know the mine was there? How did they raise an army so quickly? Something's not right.

What's worse, they haven't been selling to any outside buyers and they brought in all of their own miners - so the people of Phandalin haven't seen a copper from the mine. We're happy the orcs are gone, but we deserve better.
If you'll investigate and prove they are up to something, I'll reward you... and if you help us establish control of the mine, we'll sell you Cold Iron - at a reduced price, of course.
The mine is to the southeast - please let me know as soon as you've found anything.
Well, let me explain the situation first.
Thank you, thank you. The mine is to the southeast - please let me know as soon as you've found anything.
If you change your mind, come back. I'll be waiting.
Have you found anything yet?
Oh dear! And the heads of the company?
Very well. I'll be waiting here for when you do.
Oh, goodness! Did you deal with the monsters in the mine?
All right. Well, in order to reopen the mine, I'll need you to clear out the monsters. Sorry, but it's what must be done.
Thank heavens! We'll begin work on opening the mine immediately. In the meantime, here's your reward.
You're most certainly welcome. Farewell, friend.
Farewell, friend.
Oh, I will. I thank you and Phandalin thanks you. Farewell.
Have you dealt with the monsters in the mine?
All right. Well, in order to reopen the mine, I'll need you to clear out the monsters. Sorry, but it's what must be done.
Yes.

[CONTINUE]

I'll do it.

They were Ogre Magi.

I'll be back - and I expect you to have some cold iron for me.

My father died in the collapse. He didn't make much, but ever since he's been gone I've had to work in this tavern.

My father was a great man. He gave our family all that he worked for - I was tutored with a cleric of Waukeen and could have been a great businessman. But, now that he's gone, I'm forced to work here to support mother.
Well, I mean, I know what they told us. Father was leading a group of workers expanding a tunnel, and the tunnel collapsed, flooding the mine.

Well met, stranger. What can I and my humble inn do for you?
Someone told me worgs have showed up near the High Road? Strange to hear they've come that far...
Some folks from Neverwinter stopped by - if ye believe 'em, there's been a suspicious ship anchored near the coastline to the north o' the city.
Someone came by talking about Netherilixer or Nethlicks or something like that. I wonder what they could mean?
You ever hear of West Harbor? Little town down in the Mere, Knight-Captain's hometown... well, supposedly they're asking for help from adventurers. If you've got the time, it might be worth a look.

Some crazy fella came in here once - said that the mechanical men that worked for the King of Shadows are still around... hiding in plain sight! Said they dressed up like normal people... can you believe that?

Things're tough in Neverwinter these days. Nasher's been tryin' to keep it under control, but what with the Luskans to the North and rumors 'bout the Black Network in the city... Understand why the man declared martial law. I'da done the same!
So I hear Port Llast is under Luskan control... can you believe it? First the massacre at Ember, and now this - those folks never get a break, eh?
As if things weren't bad enough these days, I've heard people whispering about Bane returning. I hope, for all our sakes, that it isn't true.
Recently, the Neverwinter River has been behaving strangely - I've even heard that it's begun to cool. I wonder if something is happening at Mt. Hotenow.
I envy those Harbormen down south... they got the worst of the King of Shadows, but they built themselves right back up. Up here, we struggle - and the Luskans swoop right in to prey on us.

I heard that some bizarre and eccentric gentleman scholar has taken up residence somewhere in the Sword Mountains. He probably just wants to be left alone. But it seems like a bit of a dangerous place for that, don't you think?
I hear Crossroad Keep got itself a new merchant company... it's a shame. I like trade plenty, mind, but what we need right now are troops, not traders.

Bandits been more common on the High Road of late. Always been some here and there, mind, but since the War... too many desperate folk. And worse - for some, seems like someone big's behind the attacks. Hells take 'em for kickin' us when we're down!

I once heard a story about a type of zombie - kind of undead, really - dies in water, right? They rise up, and come after you... and make you feel like your lungs are filling up. If I drown, I want it to be at sea... or in ale! Ha!
While back I heard about some gnome bard, what's his name - ah yeah - Grobnar Gnomehands? Bet he was awful! How's one gonna play a lute with tiny li'l gnome hands?

Some woman came by the other day - elf, real pretty, think she was a druid. Asked about the animals in the area, said Malar was riling up the creatures around. And then she spent a half-hour talking to a cow. Heh... more like she was crazy, I think.

Y'know, I even had a Luskan drop by here once... didn't stay long, shifty rascal. You know that place's run by pirates and the Arcane Brotherhood - that seedy group o' mages? I'm surprised they don't go killin' each other within a week!
So those worgs attacking the High Road? Someone killed them! They must've been brave... or crazy...

Hello. You seem to be the enterprising sort.
Are you interested in doing some work for me? I can pay you handsomely for your efforts.
That is a shame. I'll be here if you change your mind.
I had been managing my uncle's mine for years, until a recent disaster collapsed and flooded it.
Unfortunately, the miners who were working at the time perished in the accident. And they appear... to have risen as undead.
To make matters worse, my uncle passed away earlier in the year - and he did not bequeath his mine to anyone! He has no other family here, and my father has long been estranged from him.
As a result, the town has decided to simply award the property to whomever can first clear it out, and recover the deed from the mine itself.
In short, I need you to recover the deed to my mine, and kill the undead who now roam it.
The mine, Parrum's Rock, is to the west in the Neverwinter Wood, by the river.
Should you bring me the dead and proof that you've cleared the mine, I will pay you a hefty sum of both gold and goods that my company has acquired in recent trading.
Have you cleared the mine out and recovered my deed yet?
Well, get to it. I, and the people of Conyberry, are relying on you.
Thank you, thank you.
As for your reward, here it is: One thousand gold coins and an assortment of goods. I will have my men deliver them directly to your headquarters. You needn't worry about carrying it.
No, thank you. And farewell.

But who, in truth, are the strong?

Protect the weak? From what? From their own weakness?
I thought as you did, once. Unfortunately, I can no longer ignore those weaker than I.
We are all frail. We live, acting out of petty greed, hatred, or fear. We overcome obstacles that to the strong are trivial but become gargantuan due to the limits placed on the strong.

The King of Shadows should have been less than even a nuisance. Ammon Jerro knew he was a threat, and attempted to move against him. But he was restrained - not by the King of Shadows, but by those too weak or stupid to see the real threat.
And how many more died as a result of such rigid thinking? How much damage done to the very fabric of existence?

Signed Contract

This appears to be some sort of contract to produce a book of collective research for a mind flayer named Zhiir: We, the undersigned, do hereby pledge to research the manipulation and enhancement of extraplanar beings and compile our knowledge into a single book for the sum of no less than 10,000 gold pieces, deliverable on a date no later than six months from the signing of this contract. An addendum adds: The contractees are each assigned one third of the key required to access the completed tome from its vault as a preventative measure against theft, greed, or other mishap.
Empty Ring of Djinni Summoning
This ring has been especially tuned to imprison a specific djinni. It is useless against anything else, but it's still a well-crafted and valuable ring as it is.

Most of the previous pages have been torn out, leaving only the last few entries. The second to last entry reads: Our research for Zhiir is nearly complete, and not a moment too soon. The djinni is unusually powerful, to put it mildly. He even nearly broke free the binding circle the other night. Foseth claims it was simply a flaw in the circle, but I have my doubts. As a contigency, I've crafted a ring which will bind the djinni into it should he actually manage to get free. Our experiments have made the djinni quite insane, but it was necessary to complete the research. The latest entry reads: Foseth is screaming. This can't be good, but the wards around my laboratory should be strong enough to keep the djinni out. A hasty postscript follows: I was wrong about the wards.

Long ago, two Narfellan wizards who were overly proud of their skill challenged each other to a duel by proxy: one invention against another. The first wizard created a monstrous snakelike creature, with a hide like iron and needle-like claws. The second wizard took up a piece of rare magical stone and used his powers to shape it into a sword, infusing it with the power of an earthquake and having it grant the user the strength of stone itself. The battle that followed showed the second wizard's invention as the clear victor: his champion slashed away merrily at the snake-monster, its slashing claws and snapping teeth hardly scratching their intended opponent. The wizard's glee at winning was short-lived, though, as the fighter forgot to account for the snake-monster's tendency to collapse when dead - and got himself well and truly crushed. In frustration the wizard sold the sword, but its powers (and weaknesses) have remained to this day.
War Cord

In the most dangerous battles of the Rashemi, male and female spellcasters of great power - vremyonni and hathrans - march together to battle, joined by a silken cord such as this one. Their power has sunk deeply into this cord, imbuing it with the magic and the potent determination of the Rashemi people.
Boots of Forceful Entry

Found in a remote forest, these were once worn by the mighty warrior Kuron. Not to be bothered with searching for keys, Kuron relied upon his feet to trailblaze his way to gems, gold and glory. Alas, only the boots remain of this forgotten soul.
A well-crafted chain shirt.
Spellsealed Hauberk

A seldom-spoken story among the Rashemi of tells of a strange foreign warrior who came to Mulsantir seeking her fortune. The witches and the berserkers were both suspicious of this stranger, who wielded magic with as great a skill as she did a blade. Though most shunned her, a young vremyonni met the woman by chance, and the two fell deeply in love. To protect his lover, the vremyonni crafted her a majestic chain shirt that would allow her to use her magical abilities while still being protected by its steel, in which he'd wound additional spells to keep her safe from harm. One night, both the young man and the warrior woman vanished, leaving nothing but a note saying he was joining her to seek her destiny in new and foreign lands. And although the armor itself returned - with new dents and wear, remnants of battles fought against magic and blades - the merchant carrying it claimed he knew nothing of its former owner's fate... but tales drifting on the Golden Way of a fierce warrior woman and the mage at her side have given the Mulsantiri cause to believe that the pair are still continuing their adventures across Faerun.
Heaven's Tears

A celestial being once shepherded a mortal warrior along his journey to paladinhood, and slowly grew more and more attached to the virtuous man as he distinguished himself time and again with his valor in combat and his virtue in protecting the poor and needy. The celestial began creating a suit of armor for the paladin to wear proudly into battle, pouring its admiration into every element of the making. It gifted this first piece of the eventual suit to the warrior, and the paladin was well-pleased with the extrodinary and glimmering chain shirt. However, the man's pride at the gift grew greater and greater, until one day he turned away from paladinhood to seek glory for himself. In shock and grief the celestial abandoned construction of the rest of the armor, retreating from dealings with the mortal world entirely when the once-noble paladin was killed in a bar fight, his armor stolen. Though its powers now reflect the attitude shift of its former master - and seem to bespeak the sorrowful countenance of the original maker - the armor is nonetheless powerful.
Red Wizard's Raiment

"Now this... this could get me thrown out of Mulsantir if they knew I had it - maybe even run out of all of Rashemen, or taken before the Iron Lord. That color there - it's what you think it is, that's certain. Did they really belong to a Thayan? Who's to say, my friend, who knows? But you know how powerful these are - I can smell it. Not everyone knows how much the robes make the wizard, but these... wear 'em carelessly and they'll get you killed, but wear 'em smartly and they'll save your life time and again. What do you say - think you can appreciate these?"
Baleful Anlace

This blade was once held by a master assassin, whose actual name died with him. He was only known as the Wraith. He kept a ledger on his person, which detailed every person he was hired to kill. There were over five thousand names in the book, a feat few (if any) have proven to match since. It is thought that he would drain the life of his victims in order to prolong his own, evidenced by the power in this dagger. He would always carry two of such blades. This one was found still buried deep in his chest, the other probably taken as a trophy. Why this dagger was not taken as well can only be known by the person who drove it into the Wraithâ€™s chest, and nobody has ever claimed responsibility.
Wasp Stingers

Looking at these darts, you'd swear you had too much to drink. You sometimes see 3 tips, other times only 1. You hope it's just the darts and not your eyes playing tricks on you.
It's as if the power of Nature itself is held in these darts. They are made from the stingers of giant wasps, with the poison still help inside. When thrown, the magic in the dart sometimes forces it to split into multiple darts, pelting your target with up to four stingers.
Brobdingnagian Chopper

Rothar Stonehands, as a small boy, was the most famous dwarf of his clan. His fame, however, was not born from his deeds. He was known for being nearly twice the size of a normal dwarf, something for which his father was always suspicious of his mother. Being picked on most of his young life, he decided to train rigorously, in order to become the strongest of his clan. His training paid off, becoming undefeated in every fight he ever fought. As gratitude for his heroic efforts, the elders of his clan commissioned a weapon, one so massive only Rothar would be able to wield it. For years he would fight with the impressive axe by his side.
Many years later, when it came time to decide which of his sons would be willed the weapon, he decided to give it to whichever son could wield it without looking foolish. His plan backfired, however, as none of his sons were able to meet the requirement. In fact, as stout as they were, his sons were barely able to lift it off the ground, let alone use it with any skill. They were some of the best warriors of their generation, but none had a stature that would even come close to their father's.
Some weeks later, his eldest son - Rogin - had an idea. Late one night, he took the axe from his father and dragged it to a craftsman. Rogin tasked him to shrink the weapon enough so that he would be able to wield it. The plan worked but it also had some side effects. The result was what you see before you now, a dwarven waraxe still powerful in its own right, but with enchantments having only a fraction of the power they once held.
Arcane Archer Haubergon

Those berserkers, they rush right up and swat things, but precise strikes, that I can appreciate. Maybe this'll match well with those skills of yours, eh?"

This piece here, handed down to me from a paladin of Tyr - true story, sincerely - too old for battle, wanted to live out the rest of his days at a chapel, doin' the bidding of Tyr among the people. Great fellow, gave me a fantastic price for this. Well... truth be told, he paid me to take it to his home church for him, but curse me if I didn't make it all the way back to Waterdeep and couldn't find the place to save my life! A single church of Tyr in a city that size? What if I'd gotten the wrong one! So I thought I'd hold onto it, maybe see if someone came along who could use this armor just as well as he did. You think you might want to give it a try, friend?"
Dwarven Defender Uniform

You're not the only person who knows how to recognize Harper gear, and many won't be as friendly as I."
Blade's Gear

The merchant gave you a suspicious look when showing this outfit to you, as if afraid you might aim to rob him. "Now this here... looks like normal clothes, mostly, right? But it'll protect you better than plate - you see if it doesn't! Fits close, doesn't hinder you, but good for concealing, ah, certain valuable implements of the trade, if you catch my meaning. All looks very innocent, witches hardly bat an eye at it, but you and I, we - we know better, isn't that so?"
Neverwinter Nine Armor

The merchant looked at you excitedly while unwrapping this armor, missing your expression of surprise when he unveiled it at last. "Something else, isn't it? This is from Neverwinter - small city up north, on the Sword Coast, nice little place, I'd call it cold but then again we're in Rashemen now, aren't we - the elite guard of the Lord wear this -Nisha, Nathur or something, I forget. But there was an order, years and years ago, before all those rumors about a plague up there and a war with Luskan - an order from one of the city elders for ten suits of armor like this, with the last finer than all the rest. Nine were finished on time and sent - but the last one never made it, swiped instead by some lad who said he worked for the blacksmith who crafted it in the first place. Fellow was in a panic, needed money fast, practically begged me to take if off his hands - couldn't have the thing anywhere folks could recognize this eye symbol here and knew what it meant. The thing of it is... he just grabbed the first one he had a mind to take, you know? But it seems this was the one meant for the Neverwinter lord - how about that! Wear this and you'll be tweaking the nose of Lord Naftur, wouldn't you think?"
Garments of the Pale Master

The merchant kept looking at you warily while showing you these robes, sniffing as if he was trying to catch a smell of grave dust about you. "Nasty things, undead - if you don't mind me sayin.' Tend to smell, hard to control, though I s'pose they're no so much aware that they're dead. And these spirits around here are technically dead too... and likely know they are. Wonder which is worse - knowin' you're dead and walkin' around or not? Er - not that I'm in a hurry to find out! I'll leave those mysteries to the mages..."
Red Wizard's Prize
Sacred Fist Habit

The merchant nods offhandedly as he displayed the garb. "Monks, eh... pious types, usually donâ€™t have much truck with 'em, but now and then, even a monastery has a lean month for donations and has to sell a few things to feed themselves, and you find stuff on the cheap. Some poor novice probably let this go without knowing what it was worth, which is a shame, sure - but the more shame for it to be locked away in a closet to gather dust and not see good, honest use, wouldn't you say?"
Shadowdancer Skin

The merchant looked at you a litlte suspiciously when showing you this gear, as if at any moment you might melt away into thin air. "Thought orders that'd use this typically stayed more in big cities... but you're a tricky bunch, I make no mistake - and no disrespect, mind, just speakin' my thoughts. But this here - had it around for a long time. Don't get much call to have folks look at it - but maybe it'll suit your fancy."
Shadow Thief Garb

The merchant eyed you carefully when showing you this armor, as if trying to recognize all possible ways in which you could have changed your appearance. "You know what this is, eh? Interesting little organization there in Amn, really... promising amount of expansion. Hasn't gotten out here yet, I'd thought - but then again, you never know about these things, do you? I suppose if you're with them they wouldn't mind me selling this to you - or if you're not, it'll be their business to take care of and not mine - so you're aware."
Stormlord's Array

The merchant cocked his head at you a little curiously when showing you this piece, as if reevaluating your look. "Work with nature, eh? Sure, being a merchant, as part of the job you're out in it quite a bit - well, so far as the roads go - but a fellow like me keeps more company with Shaundakul than Mielikki, know what I mean? ...No offense meant, of course - best to keep as many gods on your side as you can these days, that's what I say. But the outdoors... won't begrudge you for bein' fond of it, can be quite nice in small doses. Give me a city square and a nice tent, though, and that's all the outdoors I need. ...You buyin'?"
Arcane Trickster's Leathers

The merchant eyed you a little warily when showing you this armor, surreptitiously watching your hands. "Magic and steath - good kin, eh? Seems like they'd match well together... but I bet the witches here'd disagree, the vremyonni, too. Guilds likely worry about the magic bit, mages probably worry about the sneaky bit, huh? So long as you don't try either magic or sneaking on me, we'll be good friends, eh?"
Warpriest's Guard
Weapon Master Jazerant

The merchant gave you a slow, measured nod when showing you this armor. "Can't say I relate to you so much - only thing I was ever able to dedicate myself to was the coin, praise Waukeen and Tymora for that - but I can appreciate dedication, that I can. Takes all kinds of make the Realms interesting, you know? And, heh, the only downside of this armor is that it'll make combat less interesting - 'cause your enemies won't be able to hit you as well, you get me? Ah, bad joke - but the armor's top notch."
This weapon seems ancient and well-worn, although excellently weighted.
Flail of the Risen Deity

Once slain by Set, a fellow Mulhorandi deity, in a power struggle over the leadership of the gods, Osiris was brought back to life and mummified - the act granted him eternal life, and made him the deity of death. Though technically somewhat of an undead being himself, Osiris loathes the undead, believing in the balance and harmony of death, and the right of the universe to judge the deceased for their deeds during life. As slave and king will be judged on the same level when they come before the Judge of the Dead, so does Osiris bring down his vengeance on those who would attempt to escape such a day of judgement - creating weapons like this one, and placing them in the hands of those ready to do his bidding (whether knowingly or not).
Orrtak's Flail of Torment

This flail once belonged to an orc chief named Orrtak. Orrtak had many nicknames, none of them very flattering, and many tales have been spun about the origin of his flail. They all vary wildly except for one fact: Orrtak was extremely sadistic. Preferring to torture any who opposed him, even slightly, he would use the flail to inflict great pains upon his victims. It wouldnâ€™t be long until he rose to power, leaving a wake of tortured corpses behind him. As with most leaders mad with power, he fell victim to his oppressed followers, who had finally had enough. His body was put on display - replete with over twenty daggers still imbedded in his back - forever a reminder to future leaders of the tribe that there is only so much despotism that they will tolerate.
Thrymbreath
This axe seems unusually heavy for its size, its blade stained with long streaks of blood.
Executioner's Arm

A young man in Thay once dreamed of success, of helping to raise his family to prominence and power. He was of non-Mulan blood, which put him and his kin at a disadvantange within the Thayan populace - the only way he could hope to gain authority was to put himself into the service of someone in power, and the only way he was likely to gain a position was to appeal for one nobody else wanted. He committed himself to serve a local zulkir as a headsman, and found out altogether too soon that the noble was cruel and bloodthirsty, and that his services would be too much needed. Over many years, the man served the zulkir, and his heart grew heavier as the list of people he had been forced to kill grew longer... but always he thought of his family, and the prosperity he hoped his sacrifice would bring them.
Strident Edge

Even with the greatsword in its scabbard, you hear a low hum - not pleasant, but not entirely annoying either. However, when unsheathed, the sound emanating from the blade is both shrill and extraordinarily loud, especially when striking your enemies. Not having a hilt to protect it, when an opponent is struck the sonic effluence very often stuns it for a short time.
This weapon seems sturdy, well-honed, and oddly... mischevous. Just holding it compels you to want to trip someone.
Nightmare Shard

A small cult of Beshaba once existed who believed that the Maid of Misfortune spoke most clearly and tellingly through dreams. A man could lose something in his physical life and then take steps to mitigate the loss, and combat the ill-fortune: but in dreams, when one is without control of their environment, one is entirely subservient to the will of the dream. This belief soon took hold of a young Cormyrian nobleman who was haunted by hideous nightmares, and in desperation he submitted his will entirely to Beshaba, doing everything he could to shelter and fund the small cult of Lady Doom. For its leader, he comissioned this weapon, to trap the cult's enemies into a wasting, nightmarish sleep.
However, one morning found the young nobleman slain, the cultists either dead or writhing in the grips of nightmares, and the powerful weapon missing. It is suspected by some that the cult tried to make a victim of someone whose dreams were never undefended... and who was quick to turn their own abilities against them.
This weapon seems to vibrate slightly in your hands, as if on the lookout for foes anywhere.
Worldrender

Created to keep the wilder elementals of the world somewhat more in check, this weapon bears enchantments not only to do serious damage against its chosen foes, but to make them feel their wounds like any other living creature might.
Crossbow of the Hideous Shriek
This weapon is cursed with the angry soul of a banshee - eager to inflict the vicious power of her voice on all who endanger this crossbow's wielder.
Xvimlyth

This crossbow, constructed by the faithful of Bane, celebrates the dark god's return to life by bursting forth from the body of his demonic son, Iyachtu Xvim. Said to be profaned with some of the smouldering remains of the demigod's corpse, this crossbow fires bolts that bear the burning hatred and malevolence of the Black Hand, and push his agenda of domination.

This crossbow seems particularly difficult to handle - its mechanism seems to give more than the necessary recoil when fired, as if it was also designed to inflict a slight amount of damage to its user as well.
The Lash

Sisters who worship the Maiden of Pain, Loviatar, usually utilize their goddess's favorite weapon, the whip - but often they appreciate the simple and deadly beauty of that ancient technique, the ambush. To that end, crossbows such as this one were carefully crafted, giving their users access to frightening power. The Lovitarians could play with a mark as long as they chose: then, when the moment was right, use this crossbow to pin them down in agony... where the Lovitarian could approach casually and mete out whatever fate to their victim they thought was fitting.
This sturdy shield has an almost glassy sheen to its surface, and seems to glow softly with power.
Defiant Bulwark

A prime example of the skill of ancient Imaskari artificers, this shield is invested with tremendous magical power - devoted both to protecting its user from harm and healing them when the shield is unable to do its job. You can't help but be a little awed at the thought of a legion of Imaskari warriors wielding such equipment... and shudder a little at the thought that even such a powerful empire eventually fell.
A well-constructed heavy shield.
Zulkiri Defender

Though this shield seems to have held up well for a very long time, its inherent properties cannot help but make you wonder if its previous users put far too much stock in its ability to protect them, and the shield's penchant for removing fear drove its users to deeds that were more foolhardy than valiant.
Comedian

A master maskcrafter once joined a travelling group of actors - but much to his dismay, he and his cohorts found the road quite unsafe, and more than once were forced to fight off bandits. Unwilling to be bullied, the maskcrafter poured all of his skill and cunning into a pair of masks - elegant masterworks as well as useful weapons... and indeed, one night the company was called upon to use them when a local warlord captured the troupe, and called them to perform for his liking.
The lead actor first unleashed the powers of the Tragedian mask, and the company's female lead immediately came onstage wearing the Comedian mask. As the audience cringed and wept in sadness from the actor's performance, she told a ribald joke - and used the powers of her own mask to send the audience into uncontrollable fits of laughter, unable to defend themselves... which is when the rest of the troupe arrived onstage, clubs and saps in hand. Later, the actors fled into the night, carrying with them the spoils of the warlord's stronghold as their 'payment' - and a battered and bruised audience wondering if they'd just seen the worst play of their lives or the best.
Berserker's Helmet

Passed down from generation to generation of Rashemi warriors, this helm provides its user with enhanced vitality, and resistance to attacks of both physical and magical natures. However, this helm's magics favor strength over grace, and the rushing charges encouraged by its user's raging have often led to this helm changing hands perhaps more frequently than it should.
This armor has the look of hide, but feels as if you hold leaves in your hands.
Dryad's Embrace

A group of wild elves once declared themselves champions of a particular grove of trees, in which dwelt a young dryad who was hardly more than a sapling. As the dryad grew, she saw the wild elves' true dedication, and slowly crafted this set of armor to protect them. As the elves used the best years of their lives to protect the dryad, so did she use the best parts of herself: the suppleness of young bark, the softness of new leaves, and the willowy strength of sturdy limbs. It is said that as the elves wore this armor, they grew more and more attached to the grove they protected that eventually, one day their feet sank into the earth, their humanoid forms melted away, and they melded into the floor of the forest, strengthening the roots of the grove and keeping it safe. The armor they wore for so long remained behind, waiting for someone with the dedication to carry on their legacy.
Potent Jhuild

Although jhuild - Rashemi firewine - is commonly shared amongst wealthier individuals in Rashemen, this particular batch seems to have had some... particuarly vicious tampering done to it. Though you suspect that drinking it wouldn't be precisely fatal - and would in fact likely fill you with a strength that the mighiest of the berserkers would envy - the thought of the hangover alone is enough to give you pause.

The idea that the unity of mind, body and spirit bestows power and wisdom is a staple philosophy of monestaries across the land, and the Soulfire Kama is the tangible incarnation of that philosophy. This weapon is capable of manipulating and concentrating the subtle energies that flow within the wielder, granting an inner sense of perfect calm that fluidly translates into physical, mental and spiritual potency.
Soulfire Kama
Galvanic Blade

You're almost afraid to remove the katana from its scabbard, due to the sheer amount of electricity dancing around the blade. In fact, there's so much energy contained in the weapon that enemies in the vicinity of your victims are struck by bolts of lightning arcing out from the blade.
The origin of the Galvanic Blade is unknown, though some folks say that it was forged by beings from another plane. Not believing in such wild tales, you know one thing for certain - from its appearance, you suspect that it has seen quite its fair share of difficult battles.
This kukri seems almost hot to the touch.
Zealot's Blade

Wielded by the Black Flame Zealots - a Thayan cult feared even by the powerful Red Wizards - this weapon served as a mark of high status among the most faithful of Kossuth, and bears the touch of the Lord of Flames along with its fearsome bite.
Deadeye Crossbow

After having to kill a friend who had been slain by a ghast - and then rose as one after death - the undead hunter Nerilous "Deadeye" Draheim resolved to try and find a wiser way to fight the unliving than hand-to-hand. His solution was to craft this elegant crossbow, enchanted to be particularly vicious to the undead. Before going on his final mission - cleaning out a massive camp of vampires - he gave this weapon to his apprentice, who claimed (before a bad encounter with an ogre zombie terrified him out of the practice) that it took the entire vampire camp to end Nerilous's crusade for good.
This crossbow is compact and well-designed - its spring mechanism looks as if can hurl bolts with surprising force.
Darkhunter's Ambush

Those who tackle the risky proposition of hunting enemies within the treacherous maze that is the Underdark must be forever careful what tools they choose to bring with them: whatever weapon gives them the most advantages within the often-cramped space is best. This crossbow was shaped to put the advantage solely in the hunter's hands - a spell to blind and damage their light-sensitive foes, and a powerful punch in their bolts.
Gavel of Righteous Indignation

Dugen Steelhammer, one of the most skilled Dwarven artificers of the last century, died at an unusually early age while in the process of forging this holy instrument. Rumor has it that just weeks prior to his death, Dugen began hearing a voice that expounded to him the need for a hero to rise up and judge the wicked. Accepting this voice as that of his god, Moradin, he began to toil endlessly on a tool that would allow him to fulfill his destiny. Sadly, his dedication turned into obsession, and his fervor alone was not enough to sustain his body nor to stave off the delirium of exhaustion. After days without food, water or sleep, Dugen was found dead in his home, his hands bloodied, clutching the fruit of his labor and life.
A simple but solidly-constructed hammer.
Builder

Though not Ilmater's favored weapon, this hammer nonetheless bears his blessing: the tale connected to it tells of a noble craftsman who neglected his own business to help build houses for those who were homeless, or who had lost their belongings in a fire or flood. Soon the craftsman took on the vocation of an Ilmatari priest full-time, and began to organize others to help build and repair houses for those in need, making sure all those who needed it were given the comfort of a place to live. Though not originally intended as a weapon, this hammer was meant to protect what was sacred, and punish those who would take comfort and safety away from others - though the Crying God is forgiving and merciful, his servants have nontheless been given the tools they need to protect the innocent... to both build and to break down.

In the hands of a noble and pure-hearted archer, this bow knows no rivals. It is immediately apparent to the wielder of this weapon that there are strong divine energies at work, as if the bow is acting as a conduit to the Higher Planes. Any soul righteous enough to possess the Bow of Celestial Radiance is truly blessed by the Angels.
Bow of Celestial Radiance
Precision

Created to complement the existing skills of expert archers (and cover the flaws of the less-expert), this bow seems to possess a near-sentience, guiding the hand of its user and granting them keenness of thought and vision. Though the bow possesses no real sentience that you can tell, it seems to "care" well enough about how its handled that it tends to verge almost on the controlling, often leaving you a bit off your guard while it searches for the ideal shot.
Incisive Bow of Portent

At first glance, this bow does not appear to be a bow at all. It simply looks like a smattering of jagged pieces of metal, bound together in the general shape of a bow. Touching any part of the bow other than its handle or string is ill advised, as evidenced by the myriad of cuts you've already suffered on your hands. Pulling back the bow's string causes the jagged metal to reshape itself, creating an arrow in the process. These arrows are themselves extremely sharp, slicing their targets with every hit.
The sharpness of the bow is not merely relegated to the damage it causes. It also seems to give you an insight into the nature of your surroundings, allowing you to better judge your opponents' moves during combat. This allows you to avoid attacks more gracefully and also provides immunity to many death effects.
This sword glitters with a righteous light.
Virtueclaw

Crafted by the paladin organization known as the Talons of Justice, this blade is said to exemplify the courage, strength, and dedication to doing good that is exemplified in their deific patron, Xymor. While the members of the order are actually silver dragons who have usually have no need for such weapons, their occasional foray into undercover operations - neccessitating a temporary adoption of humanoid form - makes such blades tremendously useful in protecting the lives of their wielders, and the sacred cause of the King of Justice. That this weapon is outside of the control of the secretive Talons could mean it was stolen - or gifted to a loyal ally. No matter its user, it remains a formidable weapon.
This mace manages to look somewhat regal - as well as deadly.
Scepter of the Sun God

Within the church of Lathander, there are those who believe that the god himself is actually the rebirth of Amaunator, a god of fallen Netheril - and who will one day ascend as the prime deity to bring order to the world. To this end, they have crafted weapons not only to serve their deity's purposes, but refect their belief in his status as the chosen leader-to-be of all the gods of Abeir-Toril. Though there is much debate within the church of the Morninglord about the accuracy of any of these beliefs, the utility and usefulness of the sect's weapons are obvious.
Plucky

Once belonging to a travelling bard, this mandolin found its way into the hands of an infant fell troll after it was spoon-fed the bard's remains. Gifting the instrument the name Plucky, the left head had delusions of becoming a world-famous performer while it wailed away on its strings. As one might expect, the original strings did not last very long and had to be replaced several times before being just sturdy enough. Once Plucky had its strings fully repaired to withstand a fell troll's might, the little giant played and played. Soon after, the right head - growning rather irritated with the lackluster performances and insistent participation - bashed the left head with its dominant arm and flung the instrument far from reach. It would later be found by a band of travelers who inevitably sold the mandolin for funds to purchase ale. The repairs made to the mandolin while in the fell troll's possession reinforced its sturdiness, such would be required to withstand a fell troll's brute strength for extended periods of play. While the infant owner no doubt loved his Plucky, he was unaware of the abilities that the travelling bard had enchanted within it. Only a true - and possibly only single-headed - bard would be able to unlock its power.

Also known as Venomous Stars, Spider Bite morningstars are powerful artifacts possessed only by the highest ranking Drow High Priestesses of Lolth. It has been said that the Spider Queen herself rewards her most brutal and vile servants with these weapons, not for the protection of the wielder, but in order to further spread the destruction, chaos and terror of the Dark Mother.
Spider Bite
Shifterbane

Rashemen is known far more for its spirits, but the land and its vast forests have been troubled by malevolent lycanthropes more than once. Though the vremyonni who crafted this weapon intended for it to be used primarily against evil were-creatures, you have no doubt that its utility extends to shapechangers of all kinds.
Numbing Epee

This rapier was the preferred weapon of a brigand who became very rich after starting to use it. Nuwebin Geslan began his career as a street thug, barely making ends meet. It wasn't until he happened upon this blade that he became famous. Nuwebin would use the rapier's chilling effects to freeze his victims and rob them blind. But it wasn't the robberies that made him famous. As if pilfering his victims' posessions wasn't enough, he would use their frozen state to arrange them into embarrassing positions, either by partially disrobing them or by moving their limbs into rude or humiliating poses. How ironic it was then, when one day his body was found naked, bent in half, with the rapier run through the corpse and planted into the ground.
Sea Goddess's Spite

After rather foolishly scorning the affections of a priestess of Umberlee, the sorcerer Imaedril shortly thereafter found himself surrounded by the priestess's wereshark minions, and unceremoniously turned into a seagull. After a year of languishing in his feathery form, the sorcerer cleverly found a way to reveal to Umberlee that her priestess had been stealing money from the church. The Sea Goddess, full of rage, drowned the priestess accordingly, and freed Imaedril from his avian form. Fleeing as far inland as was possible, the sorcerer swore off any dealings with the clergy, and spent countless hours crafting himself a ring that he felt would protect himself from both any transformative spells - and give him ample protection from any shapeshifting servants.
This scale mail is oddly hot to the touch, seeming to sear the skin but leaving no trace of injury.
Motes of Flame

Sacred to Kossuth, this armor is given only to the most dedicated of the Firelord's Thayan worshippers. Once the devotee has reached one of the top terraces of Kossuth's religious hierarchy, they show their dedication by immolating themselves, stepping wholly into raging flames with the firm belief that either their god will protect them - or that they will become his sacred warriors in the afterlife. Those warriors who step in the fires and are not consumed sometimes emerge with their armor glowing forever red-hot: a blessing from the Lord of Flames. Rare as these suits of armor are, however, it is not entirely unimaginable to find one outside of the church: Kossuth's highest clergy is occasionally known to send inferiors on suicide missions purely to increase their weath and standing within the church.
This scimitar looks ancient, but still sharp and deadly.
Bent Nail

This ancient Imaskar blade was once common in use, enchanted by powerful spellcasters to provide effective strikes against the foes of the Imaskari. Many now lie discarded, sapped of their power, like old bent nails - but in this weapon, you can still feel the enchantments holding strong, ready to do battle once again.
The Bountiful Harvest
Sacred to Chauntea (whom the Rashemi call Bhalla), this scythe displays the goddess's nuturing nature - as well as her resolve towards protecting her people and defeating her enemies.
This well-made bow seems to hum slightly, and plucking its string seems to give a slight but pleasant tune.
Finch's Singing Shortbow

Finch - the half-elven bard of some renown (and more infamous than famous) - would often claim that he chose most often to wield a bow in combat because plucking its string reminded him of playing of the lute. Knowing Finch, it should be no surprise that the truth is Finch was a rather poor swordsman and preferred to stay as far away from a fight as he could. Failing that, he found it wise to invest in a weapon that would give him every advantage to delay and disconcert his foes. This weapon would obviously be serving him excellently now, were it not yet another item lost to Finch's own forced hasty departure from the city he had been in - the result of yet another ill-advised tryst with a gullible young noblewoman.
This bow seems to seep a dark and dangerous radiance, a malevolence that commands worship and rejoyces in chaos.
Dark Sun's Gift

Empowered by the dark god Cyric, this shortbow is a fitting manifestation of his evil, underhanded nature, allowing its user to cloak themselves in trickery and burn their enemies with the acidic unholy will of the Prince of Lies. However, this is not without cost - the weapon itself was created during Cyric's period of madness, and the user's struggle against the chaos of the weapon makes its mark on their soul, unnerving all nearby.
Eldenserimm

Legends tell of a unique amethyst dragon known as Eldenser, a curious wyrm who seemed to believe the best way to see the entirety of what Toril has to offer is not on his own two wings, but by forming himself into a sword... thus the epithet, "The Worm Who Hides in Blades." Though this weapon doesn't seem to exude any kind of spectacular intelligence, its abilities are nonetheless impressive. Likely it is a sword crafted to honor the legend... that, or Eldenser himself is quite good at staying quiet.
Eyes of the Hidden One
Enchanted by followers of the goddess Mystra for her more secretive servants, these shuriken not only bear a vicious dose of electricty, but the ability to deny others Mystra's own magical blessings.
This sickle has a stylized daisy carved into the base of the hilt... and seems to smell faintly of fresh-cut grass.
Green Sister's Gathering

Sheela Peryroyl - halfling goddess of nature and beauty - is said to have bestowed sickles like this on her most trusted followers, especially the order of clerics and druids known as the Green Children. Though the Green Sister treasures life and the balance between the wild and the domesticated, she knows well that striking a balance between the two can be difficult. Only in dire times is this sickle used as a weapon, and only if its soothing enchantments fail - then her followers are permitted to deal with threats of plant and beast alike as they see fit.
Aurilsbreath

The leather of this sling is constantly rimed with frost, and crackles and snaps at every motion, making a horrible grinding, tearing sound when spun. Said to hold all the cold and selfish ire of the icy goddess, any enemies unfortunate enough to face the wielder of the sling are said to hear Auril's spiteful laugh in their ears just before they perish.
This sling seems oddly fragile to the touch, as if it were made from paper.
Definer

A particularly eccentric wizard once caught onto a certain phrase about the ability of sticks and stones to do more damage than words, thought it foolish at first, then dedicated himself to a bizarre personal quest to twist it to his own ends. Drawing from a creation story told by followers of Oghma - that in the beginning, that which the Lord of Knowledge named was automatically brought into being - the wizard created a sling that could bring ammunition into being with a single utterance, insuring that the user would never be out of ammo. The usefulness of the item had to be somewhat refined after the first test run was brought to a screeching halt from the application of a Silence spell, but this particular sling seems like a later iteration, as that issue appears to have been fixed... somewhat.
Torrid Spear of Rejuvenation

This spear once belonged to Turoc, the spirit shaman of an ogre clan whose name has long since been forgotten. Every year, the spirit shaman would go on a pilgrimage deep into the mountains, always coming back looking years younger. His spear - battle hardened by the myriad of conflicts Turoc had been involved in defending the clan's territory - would also look renewed, as if a new spear had been fashioned. It wasn't until the shaman's apprentice followed his master into the mountains that someone found out what the truth really was.
The young ogre's name was Kithrak, and he had been Turoc's apprentice for several years before he finally found the courage to follow his master's footsteps into the mountains. Once the old shaman arrived at his destination, for three days and nights he was enveloped in a divine light. A voice, booming presumably from the Heavens themselves, would speak to the ogre, but in a language Kithrak did not comprehend. Fearing that Turoc would no longer have him as his apprentice, the young ogre stayed his tongue, never telling anyone of what he had witnessed.
Many years later, the old shaman, weary of the endless fights his clan would wage, asked his apprentice to join him in his pilgrimage. It is thought that Turoc wanted to pass his knowledge and power to Kithrak, that he was no longer willing to carry the burden. No one knows for sure, as the two never returned. Shortly thereafter, the clan itself disappeared... not a trace of any of them remained. Tales told among the ogre clans say that the apprentice was not ready to wield the divine power held by his master. Others say that the apprentice tried to murder his master, and he and his clan were destroyed by the gods as punishment. Whatever the truth may be, all that remains as proof of the clan's existence is this spear.
Nestrai's Sheltering Spear

This spear's origin was actually the walking stick of an old Rashemi spirit shaman. A vremyonni - indebted to the shaman for saving his life during a battle against Thay - used the stick as a base to fashion a spear. This spear, the wizard thought, would protect the shaman from the many hardships he would have to endure. Unfortunately for the both of them, the spear proved not to be enough as they both perished in another Thayan conflict soon thereafter.
Treant's Finger

In order to help druidic devotees help protect the Ashenwood from outsiders (and those who might perpetuate the blight within its borders), the treants of the forest crafted a number of these staves, enriching them with magical power and the blessings of the woods. Though some of the staff's intense power seems to wane somewhat when taken too far from its home, its strength remains impressive.
Sturdily-crafted leather armor, strengthened with studs and heavy with magic.
Great Stag Garb

Crafted by talented vremyonni, this armor is meant for inheritance by the greatest warriors of the Great Stag lodge, fearless berserkers who charge unhesitatingly into battle. How this armor ended up outside their care is uncertain, but knowing the habits of Rashemi berzerkers, it's reasonable to bet it was lost in a test of some kind of strength - and is likely sorely missed. Though quite a prize, it might make one an appealing target for possible challengers keen to win it for themselves...
Bleeding Hatchet
Cynteron's Perdurable Tomahawk

As a half-orc child, Cynteron loved to throw things around: his toys, chairs, essentially anything he was strong enough to pick up. He was so determined in his passion that his parents were forced to fasten everything in their house to the floor, lest the items find their way through a window, a wall or even a guest. When he came of age, his parents - tired of Cynteron's hobby - commissioned a craftsman to create these throwing axes and then banished him from the village. For many years he wandered the countryside, leaving a trail of axes wherever he went. No target was safe - trees, fences, walls, animals - anything he saw would become a scintillating target. The trail of axes eventually ended. Cynteron was never seen or heard from again. It is unclear what fate befell the half-orc, though any that knew him suspect one of his axes probably struck something or someone that it should not have.
A solid tower shield.
Implacable Wall

Meant only for the most elite of the Thayan Knights - sworn protectors of the Red Wizards - this shield carries with it an impressive array of abilities to thwart the attacks of even the most dedicated foes.
A sturdy tower shield made from rough bark.
Greatbark
Made from bark shed from the eldest tree in the Ashenwood and blessed by the telthors inhabiting its depths, this shield is designed to protect the forest's wisest and most implacable champions.
Wand of Automata

Left unused and unwanted in the Academy of Shapers and Binders in Thay, this wand remains a magical oddity. Though very useful - summoning forth one of three golems to do the bidding of the wand's master - both the item's tendency to occasionally summon a weak homonculous (and at rather inopportune times for its former wielders) and the fact that none at the academy no longer could divine precisely how the item worked caused it to be cast aside in favor of items more reliable and easier to divine.
Golemdoom
This vicious-looking warhammer was most likely built by an unknown enemy of the Imaskari, and designed in particular to crush their enemy's troublesome and persistent constructs.
Grog'thar's Walloper

Nobody knows where the mighty orc champion Grog'thar found - or stole - this weapon. What is known is the fact that he was practically invincible while wielding it. So paranoid was he that he would keep it chained to his person at all times, even while sleeping. After its chain was cut during a particularly bloody battle, Grog'thar raided a gnome village, enslaving three of their artisans. Tirelessly working for weeks, the gnomes managed to graft the warmace to Grog'thar's hand, so that he would never lose his grip on it. After having finally died of old age, it would seem that his hand would forever be unable to be removed from the handle. It wasn't until very recently that a frost giant hermit, whose name remains unknown to this day, was able to separate the hand from the weapon. Why the giant didn't keep the weapon for himself remains a mystery.

Yes? You had something to bother me with?
To make sure you are aware of this fact - I am not employed by Sa'Sani. I represent the interests of this company's investors, and act as Sa'Sani's advisor against her more... ill-advised ventures.

Are you aware of where we're standing right now? Are you also aware that this is not Samargol? Hm? That alone gives them more than enough reason to mistrust her. I am attempting to restore that trust, and remind her of her priorities.
Must I explain? You should know them as well as I do. Expand the business, and gather wealth and power. Easy enough.
It was folly to come here - time shall prove me right.

First and foremost - to leave Samargol without even an attempt to speak with the council is madness. We might as well have admitted wrongdoing outright! And to leave the business in the hands of that simpering majordomo... the operation, all our hard work - as good as lost.

And let us not forget this Keep's storied history - ruined not once, but twice! I disliked the idea of founding an operation here to begin with - but to have actually moved here... To abandon Samargol for this pitiful "keep" is insanity.
Their absence is unusual, yes, but did we receive any urgent missives? Any cries for help? No, we did not.
They will most likely return - no doubt having been distracted by a lucrative opportunity - and wonder why we are here while our rivals are picking apart our operation in Samargol.

It might as well be. Do you really imagine Osi's presence will be enough to keep our operation running? It was Sa'Sani's influence that kept her rivals from behaving foolishly, but with her away, it will not be long at all for them to undo all our hard work.
Oh? I wasn't aware that ruined walls and yards full of weeds were a sign of prosperity here in the North. My mistake!

Capable enough as a bookkeeper and manager of ledgers, certainly - I shall give him that. But as a leader of Samargol's largest merchant organization? It is blood in the water - and the sharks will reach him soon enough. I might feel sorry for him, if the situation did not infuriate me so.

If another massive undead army arrives, I might be happy of their presence, because it means something about this Keep might serve as designed. In terms of serving as a thriving mercantile hub, this wreck's ability to keep out writhing hordes of zombies is the least of my concerns, thank you.

It's as chilly as Samargol was hot, and a great deal less pleasant - if that is even possible. At least there you had the luxury of proffering a single respectable bribe to the right official - now you have to use force or a fortune to get your cargo anywhere.
The majordomo is irritatingly chirpy, the dwarf is a headache, the citizenry are stubborn and unwashed, and you are irritating me. Is there anything else, or can I go back to my work?

Profit? Ha! It was panic that drove her up here, not the chance to make some gold. If we can cobble together an operation capable of rubbing two silver pieces together in the long term, I'll be amazed.
Must I? It might be difficult for you to imagine the true size of our operation in Samargol, but this company doesn't yet come close to matching it.
Hm. It's not unimpressive - but forgive me if I imagine how much better things would be if this success was in addition to our Samargol hub and not instead of it.

I show her the respect that she has earned. Leaving Samargol caused enough problems with our investors that I've had to work twice as hard to keep them from rising up and pulling our funding. Now - if you're finished making hamfisted accusations, I'd like to get back to work.
Hmpf. Nothing like being greeted and asked to be silent in the same breath. Did you want to waste my time with idle chatter, or did you actually want to ask me something?

Oh, you're so certain? Running off without even an attempt to appeal to the council? And leaving the business in the hands of that simpering majordomo when Sa'Sani's presence was the only thing keeping her competitors at bay?
Farewell.

You make it sound like they don't trust Sa'Sani.

It seems my "allies" have done little to create a positive reputation for the company, so unlike in Samarach, we have no real power here - none yet, at least. So it remains to seek out allies amongst the mercantile powers of this region.

I wish you to travel north to Neverwinter City and meet with representatives of the Circle of Friends, The Forgotten Lords, and the Fated Winds at the temple of Waukeen in the Blacklake district. Make an alliance with one of those factions - the choice of which, I will leave to you - and return to me when you are done.

If we are successful here on the Sword Coast, then yes, I believe so. I find that wealth tends to gloss over any perceived shortcomings - and the Samargol officials remain pleasantly susceptible to bribes.
Let us hope their more charitable activities don't cut too much into our profits. Still... their positive reputation could open markets to us that might be otherwise reluctant to trade. Well done.

An excellent choice. While the acquisition of coin is their primary pursuit - as is ours - they are well-known for distancing themselves from activities which may be too unprofitable or disreputable. I quite approve.
An interesting selection. Their more... ruthless reputation may help to secure trade deals in more reluctant markets - hopefully without involving us in anything too disreputable. Excellent work.

Continue to build a relationship with them in whatever way you can - as your standing improves, so do our company's opportunities. In addition to this, you still have free rein to conduct other business opportunities in the Sword Coast.
What would you like to know?
Trade bars are primarily for transactions between merchant houses, a form of standardized currency. As you can see, this is advantageous when dealing with numerous foreign lands.
To the average person, they carry little worth, correct. However, many civilized governments accept trade bars as an alternate currency - but only from reputable merchants.
Simply visit one of the other towns or cities in this region, and speak with the local government. There will most likely be a fee involved.
Since you are more capable than most, any assistance would be greatly appreciated - but not required. You have proved yourself valuable - and my coin is still good.
Currently, any business with the town is handled through an intermediary - we trade with the local merchants, who in turn trade with the town's inhabitants.
A trading post will allow us to distribute goods directly to the citizenry. It reduces the cost of dealing with the middle-men, and increases our influence in the region.
Of course, but this is business. Competition is to be expected.

Despite the... setbacks in Samarach, there is a great deal of opportunity here on the Sword Coast. The economy here wavers on the verge of ruin, and it will take an enterprising merchant to repair it.

Perhaps it is different here in the north, but a stable economy is in the best interests of everyone. Short-sighted profiteering will only cause it to crumble further - and I have my eyes set upon longer-term goals.
As an employee of this company, you are entitled to a monthly stipend of trade bars. The size of this stipend, however, will depend on how well the company is doing.
In addition to using them to buy and sell goods, you may also turn in trade bars in exchange for gold. The ratio is not one to one, but it's more than fair.
In addition to this, the trade bars you turn in will be used to fund projects outside the scope of the business - such as... upgrading our operation here in the Keep.
Let your weapons talk, and naught else - there is little speechifying will do to change the minds of ignorant trolls.

Likely because of the associated costs, but most of all, because the region itself is unstable - the post relies on the ability of the company to get its goods to and from the town with a reasonable degree of efficiency. Others have failed to do so - we shall not.
These trade bars will be of use to you. After this, your share of any profits will be paid monthly - simply speak to Variel.
Farewell.

It's a long story - or, well, it's a short story that went on for a long time. A while back, I was hired by the two merchants that bought this place - Il'foss and Kizu - to act as the majordomo for their trading company. Said they were going to "change the Sword Coast."

Well - we have a large warehouse which currently empty, a cleric of Waukeen with no shrine, a portal which only goes to Samarach, and a spare room in the headquarters itself. So I'd say there are plenty of good places to start!

Well, since you're an adventurer, I thought it might be a place to display all the trophies you've acquired from your travels. It would bring in the locals, give them something to gawk at - maybe charge them a coin or two?

It's quite a large area - there's plenty of room to build a smelter, lumbermill, and tannery in there. All small scale operations, of course, but considering that it would be the only operation for miles around... well, you can see how advantageous that would be!

Her name is Daija and we - er, I - sort of promised to fund the construction of a shrine for her if she bestowed us with Waukeen's blessing. We've had... a few difficulties holding up our end of the bargain.

It would be nice if it could be used to go to other places in this region of the Sword Coast, but Orias - he's the gnome who maintains it - assured me that it would be quite expensive to alter the portal's magic. Right now, sadly, and we don't have the resources to spare.

I don't understand it, either. Maybe they were just arguing about her decision to leave it? I don't really know... but I don't think I heard anything about the guards seeing her leave, so... I don't know.
I think that might be the case, but Orias would know better than I - if she used the portal, that is. I don't think any guards saw her leave.

| 4-5 trading posts |With trading posts in numerous towns... I'd say we're moderate-sized.

Certainly - how can I help?
You can use them to buy and sell goods, of course, but you can also turn them in to me in exchange for gold. The rate isn't perfect, but I think it's more than fair.
Any trade bars you turn in to me will be used to fund projects outside our usual business scope, like upgrading the Keep. Lady Sa'Sani has granted you the final say in those matters.

For one, they're easier to cart around - and for another, they're primarily for dealings between merchant houses. It's basically our own form of standardized currency - which comes in handy when dealing with multiple foreign countries.
Oh, no, they're worth quite a lot! Just not to the average person, you see. Some governments do actually accept them as an alternate currency - but only from merchants with good reputations.
Well, you work for Sa'Sani, and with the profit-sharing that goes on in the company, you'll get a monthly stipend of trade bars. The bigger the company gets, the bigger your stipend gets - see?
Right now, trade with towns involves us selling to local merchants, and in turn they're the ones who sell our goods to the townsfolk.
If we build a trading post in a town, it'll let us trade directly with the townspeople. The cost will go down, and the profits will help our company to grow.
Well... maybe a little, but it's business, you know? Many of them could sign on with us, if they wanted...
If you talk to the local government in whatever city you're in, there's a chance they'll let you set one up - for a small fee, most likely.

Soon after I got here, I handled a few shipments, but we received word that a pair of huge shipments were on their way. Kizu and Il'foss both seemed very excited - I think they were disappointed at how slow things were going, too.

The shipments arrived on time, and Il'foss insisted on taking one of them to Neverwinter City himself. A few days later, Kizu vanished with the other shipment - but I've heard nothing from them since. I've been doing my best to keep this place in order, but that's really all I've had to do.

Well - no! I admit... when they offered the position, I did sort of jump at the chance. These days it doesn't matter if you graduate at the top of your class from a prestigious scribe's college, no... they just care if you can use magic to set things on fire. Hmpf. ...Anyway - sorry about that.

Tantam and well met, traveller! Welcome to the headquarters of the Circle of Friends.

Good! To join, we must first collect a small donation of two hundred and fifty trade bars. Not only will this prove your dedication to the Circle of Friends, but - more practically - will buy you a permanent business pass into Neverwinter City.
Of course. What are your questions?
Certainly! What do you wish to speak of?

A merchant cartel we may be - but we firmly believe it is also our responsibility to aid the citizens of the Sword Coast who have suffered in the recent war. How can we fill our coffers when the needy suffer so?
I am glad to hear you say that. Perhaps you would be a good fit for the Circle of Friends.

But you see - why must those roles conflict? We may make lesser profits than the other cartels in the short term, yes, but our efforts improve the lot of all those around us. When Neverwinter finally lifts her head again, will we not all benefit from such renewal?
However... regrettable though it is, if you don't agree with our philosophy, you may find one of the other cartels more to your liking.
Yes? My ears are open, friend!
We encourage our members to be professional in their dealings, and kind in their demeanor - to act in ways that benefit both the Circle of Friends and the Sword Coast as a whole.

Though I must say - we do have one absolute rule. Members of the Circle must always offer a fair price to towns suffering from a shortage of goods - nothing but grief lasts from extorting gold from those most in need.
We are not naive, nor fools - we know well the desire to turn a profit, and Waukeen's own smile is gold! But such a profit should not be at the cost of our customers - not at the expense of the poor.

Because of our reputation, our kindness is well-repaid. In times of surplus, those who sell to us will always present us with the best price - a gift in return for our persistent efforts to aid this struggling nation!
So you see - being good is sometimes more than its own reward, eh? Heh!
Quite all right. If you're still interested in joining later, the Circle is always accepting new members. Once you have the bars, come by again, and we'll speak further!
Certainly.

We believe that a strong economy is the best reward. Though anyone with two apples to sell is welcomed in a starving city, even the most satisfied towns are glad to see the Circle of Friends. Surpluses may deny profits for some - but never us!

In addition to this, our members are granted access to our private collection of arms, armor, and provisions. Because we support the well-being of the Sword Coast, many of our items are donated by the devotees of the House of the Triad - Tyr, Torm, and kind Ilmater - and their allies.
Happy to hear it! But alas - before you join, there's something I should tell you.

While we have done our best to keep a cooperative spirit with the other cartels, I fear there still remains a suspicious air between us. Should you join our ranks - and I hope this is so! - I know the other cartels will turn your membership away.
And - I should say - of course you'll have to abide by our rules.

Understood! The Circle is always accepting new members - should you wish to join us, we'll be here.

Finally, each of our member organizations receive a distribution of profits, dependent on their rank... though some of these profits will be donated to charity. The Sword Coast cannot recover by mercantile means alone, you know - we must show kindness to help it flourish!
Here is your pass to the city. You can present this to the city guards, who will then waive your entry fee.

Those lower in the ranks had no idea 'bout the connection, but when we did, we rose up and kicked out the Zhent loyalists. Now we're free and on our own - and doin' far better than those Zhents ever did.
I talked to Jordan Wright about Mikul - says he's got some kind of explanation that'll clear everything up. I'm not so sure, but I don't got much of a choice.

Had a chat with the leaders of the Circle of Friends and the Forgotten Lords - we've set up a meeting at the tavern in Conyberry so Wright can explain everything. If we can get them on our side, we've got a chance to clear all this up.

We've gotta keep this quiet for now - but I want you t'come along. You saw the New Leaf situation firsthand... and if it comes that Wright's spinnin' falsehoods, it's best you be there to say otherwise.
I'll set things in order, then - you sure you're ready to leave?

There's a town called New Leaf, over in Neverwinter Wood - suddenly has a massive shortage of all their trade goods. Might be wise for you to find how that happened... and see if town'd consider looking to us for protection.
And, of course, while you're there - take full advantage of that shortage. Others in the Fated Winds'd kill for this kind of chance for a huge profit, so I s'pect you'd leap at the opportunity.
Aye, but not a great one, so keep your expectations low, mind.
Some crazy fire genasi callin' himself "Phineas the Sensate" wandered in today, askin' for some rare resources - not even shipments, hardly even more'n samples.

He might have good reason for it, or he could be more confused than an orc in the court at Evermeet - either way, his money seems good. If you care to try your luck with him, he's wanderin' outside the Temple.
Somethin' big - so keep your ears open. There's a town up the coast called Port Llast - small place, but important. And not long ago, the Luskans just walked in and conquered it.

Since then, trade's completely stopped - which is bad in particular, 'cause Port Llast is the only importer of Knucklehead Ivory from up in Icewind Dale. But down in Waterdeep, they're wild for ivory... if we secured that source, our profits would soar.

Now, I don't care what you think of Luskans - but they're best in charge of Port Llast, far as I can tell. Neverwinter's desperate for every penny... but Luskan, they're of more a mind to let us have our profits. Get them to open up the land and sea routes, and there's five hundred trade bars for each waitin' for you.

However, we do try to keep the economy of the region stable. We neither gouge nor undercharge during shortages - it's hardly beneficial to our long-term business strategy.

My name is Akila - and in case you could not discern it from my appearance, I am a Red Wizard, and the Khazark of this enclave.
It is the title granted to the head of enclaves such as these. The title is not as important to me as it might be to other Thayans.
Honestly, I enjoy the autonomy that it grants more than the power it supposedly brings.

I am not certain. It could be related to energies released during the recent Shadow War, or it could be due to an extraplanar event.

Here I am safe from the scheming of the zulkirs back home. And I research out of desire for enlightenment, not as a fumbling attempt to gain power. I am... not cut of the same cloth as most Thayans.
I have created a magical device that assists me in studying these oddities. It acts as a kind of... "magical scribe," I suppose, and retains residual energy from the nexus.
I have used this device to study the nexus here, but it contains energies from many places - places of this plane and of others.
I need you to take this uncharged device and direct it at any arcane nexus you come across in your travels. That will charge it with arcane energies.
Should you return to me with a charged device, I shall grant you a reward for your work. I will also recharge the device so that you can gather more data.
I am reasonably certain that there are more of these oddities elsewhere. if I gather data from many such nexuses, I may be able to isolate their origin.

{businesslike but welcoming}Welcome to the new face of Port Llast. Are you merchant, traveller or adventurer?
Ah, well then. I must apologize that our inn is temporarily closed. Be warned if you make camp near Port Llast - the undead are running rampant of late.
Recently, we have been plagued with waves of walking corpses. What first began as a nuisance has grown into a significant obstacle to overland trade and town security.
Don't take this in a threatening manner, but since we liberated Port Llast, everything and everyone in this town is now my business.
Port Llast has long been tied to Neverwinter, an association that has provided little benefit, and cost dearly.
One need not travel much in these lands to see the profound effect Neverwinter's troubles have had to the Sword Coast. Their recent war has impacted everything between Luskan and Waterdeep.
The Arcane Brotherhood thoroughly investigated that matter. From careful review of the facts, and eye-witness accounts, they determined Garius and his followers acted independent of Luskan authority.

I was not involved in the investigation, so I wouldn't expect you to take my word for it. If my associate Khralver were here, he could enlighted you, as he lived through the events of the war that we can only muse on.
Khralver Irlingstar is a diplomatic aide the Brotherhood sent with my expeditionary force. I sent him on an errand of some importance, but he is long past due.
There were two that I am aware of. One was actually Khralver, my missing associate. The other was some paladin our agents found left for dead in the ruins of Merdelain.
The reports of undead attacks started coming in roughly a tenday after we liberated Port Llast. About a fortnight later, small groups of undead began attacking the town by night.
I tend to agree. I suspect they are being controlled by some powerful being who wishes to harm Port Llast. We have been unable to find either the source or put a stop to it.

I beg your understanding here, stranger. At first I did send patrols out to find the source of the undead scourge - but after the third patrol failed to return alive, I refocused my efforts on the security of the town.
Apologies for that. We had enough soldiers to liberate Port Llast, but we need still more to solve the problems that are limiting commerce. Reinforcements from Luskan are slow to come...
I can't recall his name. Neverwinter considered him some sort of hero, but now he answers for his crimes against Luskan as our prisoner.
There were many charges against the poor sot. The main one was his involvement in the murder of Sydney Natale, a high profile figure in Luskan.

I agree. However, it is not exactly a well-kept secret. After all, I am telling you strangers who just wandered into my town. I suspect Nasher has too many of his own problems to be concerned with negotiating extradition of a criminal.
