{calm, measuring but not unfriendly}New faces in West Harbor - that's uncommon. Well, if you'll be needing supplies or healing, I'll help you best I can. Also, if it's not too much trouble, I had a small request for you...

Goodwife Aruna, strangers - call me Aruna should it please you. Came here from Wanderfen - place to the south that got taken back by the swamp. This place takes care of me now, so I do my best to take care of it in return.
Heh, now that sounds sinister... nothing special about me, traveller. Earthmother just favors my sickle come the harvest, is all.
Not a lot of villages out here to begin with - but yes, some. Those that weren't... the wasting shadows took many, and the undead... they did for the rest.

Not so much anymore - still a few here and there, but they don't harry us like they used to. Occasionally some poor corpse stumbles up out of the swamp, but the militia knocks it over and sets it aflame before it can be much of a bother.
|PC is good or neutral|That you may be, child... it makes sense there are more like us, after the Time of Troubles... but I'm rambling. Forgive me - was there something else you wanted?

I hear you're going to seek out the missing mage, and whether you might take on a second task.

You might run into some lizardfolk in the swamps here... it sounds strange to say, but if you find my shawl with them, may I have it back? Small, handwoven, well-worn - you'll know it should you come across it.

A determined and hardworking woman, Ginni has managed to keep with her much of her good humor, despite the ravages of the King of Shadows nearly destroying her family. She spends whatever spare time she has training with the West Harbor militia, and has become one of their most talented fighters.

Lazlo Buckman is tall and red-faced, the mayor of West Harbor and the leader of its militia. Having lost most of his family in the King of Shadows' attack on the village, he is very protective on his son Jan and determined to see West Harbor prosper again with his aid.
Buckman

Though the attack on West Harbor robbed him of a little of his carefree nature, Pitney Lannon remains a genial man - one of the few left in the village. He and his family were lucky to survive the ravages of the Shadow War, and he serves as the second-in-command of the West Harbor militia.

This young man holds a worn spellbook in his hands, and seems to be half-reading it, idly watching the world around him with a small expression of worry pinching his features. He smiles shyly at you when he notices your gaze, an awkward gesture of welcome.
Jan

Eldest of the Lannon children, the Shadow War had a profound effect on Pitney Junior. He holds himself responsible for taking care of his younger siblings should anything happen to his parents, and takes this role very seriously. Though not old enough to train with the militia just yet, Junior does his best to practice on his own.

Kaye and her twin Kiri are the middle children of the Lannon family, precocious and curious. The horrors of the war have made them wary of the rest of the world, and like their older brother Pitney Junior, they want to protect their family more than anything.

Kiri and her twin Kaye are the middle children of the Lannon family, precocious and curious. The horrors of the war have made them wary of the rest of the world, and like their older brother Pitney Junior, they want to protect their family more than anything.

Kyl is a sweet young child of maybe five years, curious and eager to learn. He doesn't remember the Shadow War as clearly as his elders do, and like a normal child (and a strong contrast from his siblings), doesn't usually think before he acts.
{even-tempered but not particularly welcoming}|First time visit|New faces, eh? Name's Lazlo Buckman - I'm the mayor here. If Caryl let you in, you probably came to help us out, correct?
Well, if you want to know about giving us a hand, just let me know - I'll be here.

I can't offer much in the way of pure coin, but I've got something better - Harvest Mead. Old family recipe - used to be shipped all over the Sword Coast before West Harbor got burnt the first time. If you're selling, guaranteed folks will buy.
{frowning}Trade, eh? Not much of that can happen right now, with the troubles we're having. If you can help us, though, that's surely something we can negotiate.
Couple of old black dragons out in the swamp - seem to have their eyes set on West Harbor, want to conquer the town.

As for the job - pair of old black dragons are aiming to take over West Harbor. We're doing the best we can to be ready for their attack, and it's a damn good thing their wings are too gnarled to fly. Doesn't mean we're safe, though.
This village has been through a lot, and we're preparing to fight them off as best we can. Good thing their wings are all gnarled - they can't fly over the walls that way.

I can't offer you much in the way of pure coin, but I've got something better - Harvest Mead. Old family recipe - used to be shipped all over the Sword Coast before West Harbor got burnt the first time. If you're selling, guaranteed folks will buy.
{frowns}Fair enough. I'll be here if you change your mind.
{Trying to avoid the subject, uncomfortable}I'm sure I don't know - the minds of dragons are odd things... unpredictable. But they're after this village, that's certain.

I've got something to make it worth your while, though - Harvest Mead. Old family recipe - used to be shipped all over the Sword Coast before West Harbor got burnt the first time. If you're selling, guaranteed folks will buy.
Well - the situation's gotten a little more complicated recently.
Our wizard, Tarmas - his spells help keep this wall solid. But he went off to scout the dragons' cave, and hasn't come back for days. Two of my best fighters went to find him, but so far - nothing.
Good, glad to hear it. The lair is somewhere in the Mere - I expect it's pretty well hidden, so it might take some searching. Best be prepared for that.
|party is level 8 or higher|In the meantime, you're welcome to take a look around - just don't get too cozy. I'll help how I can.
|party is below level 8|I don't mean to be rude, but your crew looks a bit green for this job. I'd toughen up a bit first, mayhaps. But in the meantime - feel free to take a look around.
|Have talked to Buckman about job, haven't taken quest|Back again, are you? Changed your mind?
|Have taken quest|Welcome back. Any progress yet?
|Haven't talked to Buckman about job|Changed your mind about helping us out, have you?
{little stiffly}I can't chat all day, but I'll answer what I can.

I can't offer much in the way of pure coin, but I've got something better - Harvest Mead. Old family recipe - used to be shipped all over the Sword Coast before West Harbor got burnt the first time. If you're selling, guaranteed folks will buy.
Trade? Sure - just need to get this dragon problem taken care of first. {sarcastic}Takes up a bit of one's attention, wondering if one's village is about to be overrun.
Somewhere in the Mere - probably pretty well covered-up, I'd say. Watch yourself out there - hear those dragons got dealings with lizardfolk.
Anything else?
Honey makes mead, friend. Once we get our Harvest Mead out to buyers, West Harbor will prosper again - mark my words.
Every bit worth it. Trust me on that one.
Half-drow - says his name's Quarrel. Came around a few days ago looking for something... hasn't exactly been chatty. Or friendly.
Something about Ammon Jerro - don't know why. Wasn't him directly that burned this village - either time - but he wasn't exactly a good influence on West Harbor. The less he's spoken of, the better.
Not so - got something against him, though. If you haven't talked to him yet, try to catch his ear and you'll see what I mean.

Because we're survivors, and we aim to stay that way. Something in the Mere shook us all out of our homes, and we're damn lucky to be alive. We don't prepare for whatever's next, it's same as if we gave them the knife to stab us.
{Trying to avoid the subject, uncomfortable}I'm sure I don't know - the minds of dragons are odd things... unpredictable. But they're after this village, that's certain.
Well, our Caryl's a good judge of character - and we're a bit off the beaten path, so I assume you didn't come out here for the sights. But - as for the help...

{wary}Easy, stranger, I don't mean to insult. We don't have much else here, but I promise you, that mead is more than worth its weight in silver. A barrel will have buyers as far away as Baldur's Gate begging for a good price, I promise you.
Well then - come back when you decide to lend a hand, yeah?
The bees are only a part of it - the rest is the determinination of the people in this village - and I'd stake my life on that.
{grateful}Thanks again for your help - Pitney's working on keeping us well-stocked with Mead.
Jan said that? It's - it's nothing. I should tell that boy to stop exaggerating... he'd tell you I killed the King of Shadows myself if it'd get you to help us.
Now, if there's nothing else...
{very grateful}|CULT DEAD|You did us another kindness, traveller - thank you.
{furious - PC was responsible for his son's death}|CULT AND JAN DEAD|Don't talk to me - you lost me my son!
That depends. What's the job, and more importantly, what's the reward?
We're a merchant company out of Crossroad Keep, looking to trade.
What is it you need help with?
Just taking a look around for now.
So you need us to kill a couple of dragons? This'll cost you.
|Int 14+|That's odd... usually dragons would just grab wanderers through the swamp. Any idea why they seem to set on West Harbor?
From what I can see, it seems like you're well-prepared for a fight.
Did you want us help you here if they attack, or go and hunt them ourselves?
Not fond of the idea of killing dragons just for booze. Think we'll pass for now.
Farewell, then.
Not fond of the idea. Think we'll find something more worth our time.
|Int 14+|I get the feeling you're not telling us everything.

Sounds too risky. We'll pass.
|PC Nonevil|If people need rescuing, we'll help.
Fine, we'll give you a hand - but you better not skimp on the reward.
|party knows about Tarmas|Right - we'll find your wizard.
|party doesn't know about Tarmas|Right, two dragons. You need them dead, we can handle it.

We'll speak with you later.

You seem to have an awful lot of beehives.
Who's that odd elf wandering around?
What's with all the militia training?
|Harvest Mead wasn't mentioned before|Before I find this Tarmas... is there anything in the deal about a reward?
Can't say we're happy about getting drink instead of coin, but maybe after results... we can renegotiate.
That'll do - might come in handy.
Any chance you might think of making the Harvest Mead trade a more - permanent arrangement?
Farewell.
Can I ask you something else?
Bit of high expectations to put on insects.
Looking? For what?
|party member is drow or half-drow|[Drow] You got something against the drow, then?

|Int 14+|That's odd... usually dragons would just grab wanderers through the swamp. Any idea why they seem to set on West Harbor?
|Evil|I doubt it - why would we want to bother?

|Dragon Disciple|You're certain they can't be reasoned with? Why would they want the town?
|+6|[Intimidate] You think mead is enough for us to risk our lives?! If you're insulting us, you'll pay for it.

This tall humanoid looks like a cross between a powerfully built human and a lizard. It has clawed hands, a long tail, and toothy jaws. This one seems to be the strongest and most savage of its kind - likely magically enhanced by its masters, the dragons.

Lizardfolk Elite {2}
Militia Club

Fascinating... yes... I think I see...
No... gods damn it, it's just not... damn!
Do you mind leaving me alone? I'm busy.
There is an infernal aura here I'm trying to track - you're messing me up!
Do you know what the phrase "go away" means?
There's so much here, but it's - indistinct... faded... but how?
Come to see the failed warlock, then, have you?
{cheerful and ingratiating}Hello, traveller. How can I be of service?

Sheydann Zinn is my name, and I'm afraid the clothes are an affectation that I am unable to rid myself of. I am a merchant formerly of Neverwinter - but I lost everything after the Shadow War. I moved here for a life that is - simpler, finer.
As for my services, I can offer a small selection of goods - and perhaps a few other baubles that might catch your eye.
Hello again, friend. How can I help you?
Greetings, adventurers. Quite a thing you did for the village, indeed - very impressive.
Shame about Lazlo and the others, though... suppose it couldn't be helped.
And you managed to rescue Lazlo! Quite brave of you... and remarkable how quickly these villagers seem to have forgiven him for his transgression.
Oh, I should add - I was keeping some... items in reserve, for fear Lazlo would frown on me selling them. Though I grieve at his passing, I feel I can trust you to offer them up for sale.

I assure you, traveller, it was nothing of the sort. They saw my richer clothes and imagined I might divulge the location of my wealth to them - and I admit, I did my best to play to their expectations.
And what on Toril should I tell them? I can only prevaricate so much - my hope was to come up with a plan to save the lot of us. I am glad you managed to beat me to this!
Now, if you'll excuse me - there are some things I must attend to. Good day.
It was nothing, good sir. I only wish I could have done more!
Now - is there anything else I may help you with?
Yes, but what was the cost? The entire village could have been lost! ...But, I shall admit, I digress.
Welcome back, adventurers! How may I help?
It was nothing, good madam. I only wish I could have done more!
|Wis 10+|You seem a little well-dressed for the swamp, mister...
|Ranger, Druid, Spirit Shaman|Those fine clothes are a foolish choice for this climate, stranger.
What kind of services do you offer, mister?
Just passing by.
Show me what you have for sale.
Farewell for now.
|talked to Aruna|Some villagers think how you got through the dragon's occupation was a little - suspicious.
|Good|And you didn't think to try and shield your fellow captives with a similiar lie?
|6+|[Bluff] I can appreciate cunning - well done.
We'll see.
Fine, then - farewell.
|Good|He was only trying to help his village.
|8+|[Appraise] You look to have gotten through the dragon occupation well enough... did you bribe them to leave you alone?
|Rogue|Items Lazlo would frown on? Must be interesting. Let's take a look.
Show me what you've got.

This man favors you with a winning smile and a slight nod of the head, and you find yourself wondering what such a charming personality is doing in such a backwater village.
Zinn
Sheydann
Good to be out of that hideous cage... and out in the smelly swamp air.

{gruff and sarcastic}Glad all that's over... what a bother. I suppose I have to thank you for your part - without your help I'd be a mouldering corpse in that cage... centipedes probably feasting on my eyeballs.
What, Jan? Nonsense - how could I punish him for something even I overlooked? Hmph. Boy needs to pull himself out of his doldrums... although I suppose he could use a word of encouragement.
Well - while I admit rattling you was not my aim, I do seem to have a mind for the macabre. Comes from being close to death recently, I'd suppose.
What a... considerate offer. I'll have to turn you down on that one, though... regrettably.

All that aside, I wanted to see if you might be interested in some old magical items I picked up in my travels. As my recent experience has taught me, they seem less than able to keep me from harm - but you might enjoy them. For a price, of course.
I've got some shiny things to trade. Sound good?
Oh, you again. What can I do for you?
Please - I am a wizard, not a common cutpurse. I wouldn't bother you with it if I didn't think it'd be something you could use... I'm not above a little bit of gratitude, at least.
I told him not to go - said it was a stupid idea. He insisted they'd teach him, he'd get more powerful - ugh. The young fool...

Idiot - I tried to stop him! Lazlo won't even let me find him - doesn't want to stand in his son's way. He's lost faith in himself too - damn the Buckman family! Jan's inheriting a curse of a personality....

I find your veiled extortion despicable - but you still have a point. Here - this may be of use to you. I have little else I can offer for your personal use... not when I'm uncertain if you'll actually do what you say.
I can't go find him - but if you do, take these with you... and make sure you give Sheydann the punishment he deserves for preying on the naive.

I tried - Lazlo is convinced he should let the boy do what he wants, find his own way in the world. Fool's hardly a shell of a man now - so afraid to make another mistake from meddling that he'll let his own son wander off. Madness.
Here - if you go find Jan, take this with you. Hopefully, your own skills will be such that you won't need this - but just in case.
{grieving}|CULT & JAN DEAD|You did what you had to... I know. Naive fool though he was, Jan... will be missed. I don't think I can take another apprentice - not anymore.
That aside... what can I do for you?

{gruffness covers gratefulness}|CULT DEAD|It's good to have Jan back in town - if you haven't spoken to him yet, I advise you to do so. Do not worry about berating him for his naivete - I'll take care of that.
Yuck, Tarmas.
|Con 12+|I just killed dragons - that image is not going to make me ill.
|PC Pale master or evil cleric|I could have raised you as quite a capable zombie, I'm sure.
|Good|I hope you haven't punished your apprentice - he did do his best to protect West Harbor.
Nice... I'll be going now.
|Int 8 or lower|Er - what?
Show me what you have for sale.
No thanks - maybe later.
|+6|[Spellcraft] I hope you don't try to sell me something whose worth has been exhausted - don't imagine something like that can get slipped past my notice.
Aruna told me about Jan's connection to the cult.
Why didn't you stop him?
|+8|[Intimidate] You didn't bother to stop him? Some guardian you are.
|+10|[Bluff] Maybe if you gave me something to help find him, I could be of more use...
Nothing right now.
Farewell.

Tarmas has seen more than his share of West Harbor's difficulties - he arrived at the village years ago, after the first battle that nearly destroyed it, and managed to flee by magical means before the village was assaulted once more. In in the interveining years, the gruff wizard seems to have grown fond of the strange swamp town, and now works hard to keep it safe. He has taken on Jan Buckman as his new apprentice, and daily renews the wards that empower West Harbor's palisade walls.
{Lazlo dead - pleased and amused}So you've taken care of our problem! Not bad work - I can appreciate that level of savagery.
Oh, we'll honor it - assuredly. Here's the gold I mentioned - for your trouble... heh.
{laugh}Oh, I like your style, <Race>! You might well have scales under that rubbery flesh of yours, similar to us as you are. Waervaer might even deign to talk to you one day.

We shall make certain there is a handy supply of Dragon Mead around for you to trade - anything you need aside from that, you talk to me. No sneaking in the town, now... there's no need for that. Don't need the workers to be distracted.
{after deal - bored}You return. Was there something vital you needed that you see fit to bother me directly?

{scoffing}What? Our Dragon Mead is an improvement! Why go back to the original when our changes have made the taste so much sweeter and stronger? Never! Now did you want something else, or just to waste my time?

{angry hiss}Such a duplicitous little rodent! I can't say this is unexpected. My brother shall want to see this... it will certainly be a show. I would advise you to try and enjoy the time you have left.

{initial conversation - amused}Hello again, little snack. Didn't expect to see you up and around here. Well - mostly because I expected you to die in the lair, but oh well. Guess you smoothskins are more resilient than I took you for.
Leave? Ha! That's rich. Much as I'm sure it's useless to bargain with you, little mouse, I'll echo your cordiality and give it a shot.
Can't say I'm acquainted with many... but let's see if your common sense matches your sturdiness, wide one.
Not so much the traps on their own, but the monsters behind them, really. No matter - I can see you're a clever customer. Allow me to propose a more beneficial solution.
Trying to make a dragon mad, meatling? Well - you certainly aren't heavy on common sense, but perhaps you can recognize the reasonable nature of my offer.
Hm - how to reason with a hunk of stinking meat? Perhaps a better bargain than the one it's getting... so listen to this proposal.
{amused}Oh, really? And you suppose the only reason I haven't decided to melt you into a fairly gooey pile of bubbling meat is just because I'm feeling generous?
And some bluster to the mix. Not particularly charming, but I'm looking for a blunt instrument, not a consort - and I have an offer you might well find intriguing.
Hm. And a brain in that round little skull, too - how surprising. A positive development, believe it or not.

I suspect Buckman has figured out now that he can't keep his little scheme hidden any longer - he did approach my brother and I about taking care of the Mere's small undead problem. Typical for him - having someone else do his dirty work.

He's guaranteed you our hoard, I bet - but why take orders from someone who only offers what isn't his? And we held up our end of the bargain and kept the undead away from the village... Why not take our mead - Dragon Mead - and some gold on the side - and kill Buckman instead?
|Pitney|No! You traitor!
|Ginni|Don't do this - I beg you!
{savage laugh}Well, I tried to make you see reason. Stand back, my servants - I'll give you a show, shall I? ...Oh, I shall enjoy this, fleshling.
{about to fight PC}|start of fight|Enjoy the show, brother! I'll make this entertaining...
|%80 health|Is that the best you can do, rodents?
{getting angry}|65% health|This has ceased to amuse me!
{frustrated and angry}|50% health|Hurry up and die!
{enraged and desperate}|25% health|Waevaer! Help me!
{irritated}So you're back, then, foolish fleshbag. What do you say to this deal of mine - kill Lazlo, or die?
Well, look who it is!
My my my... you are resilient, aren't you just?
I bet your fleshy friends just missed you like crazy.
Are they just cowering in the shrubbery? How sad. Bring them out to say hello.
How disappointing. Oh, well - guess I'll have to do all the work then. Stay out of this one, my loyal defenders - we'll see if these wretches can put up a decent fight.
|Buckman|Then I suppose we'll resist you as best we can - for the people of West Harbor!
|Voarag|Oh, this will be interesting. Do try to make them suffer, won't you, meatling?

And our deal?
Did you require anything else?
Agreed.
Would you consider switching back to making the classic Harvest Mead?
Just stopping by.
I believe I changed my mind - I think I'd like you and your brother dead after all.
I could say the same.
Save your flattery, beast. I'm here to see you and your brother dead.

Greetings, friends! I'm glad to see you here.
What... you mean, go? Never! Don't you understand? This group, this way - has given me such purpose, such strength! I can't go back until I have more...
I... may be able to visit, though... talk to Master Sheydann. He's the word of the new lord - he'll be able to tell you.
That you've come to share the word, of course! 'Tis a wonderful thing.
Evil? No, no - you must be mistaken. The tests of the master are strict, but... but fair. He would never - no, never mind. I can't go back home - not yet!
It's not... the happiest place, I admit - but even West Harbor is still in the swamp, and that's nice, isn't it?
I... I can't. I failed them once - I can't again. Not until I have the power to protect the village!
I told you - I can't leave! Talk to Master Sheydann - he'll know what to do.
What... what have I done?! They were my friends...
I... I don't... I... don't remember much of anything, really. I just - followed Sheydann here, and people arrived, but I didn't - I listened to him instead.
He told us of what the new way was, and all that he was saying sounded so - promising. Change for the Sword Coast, the power to protect my village... I believed in it, in all of it.
My friends - I - why can't I remember their names? It's a blur now... I just remember coming here, and listening to Sheydann...
And he gave me this - strange, it was glowing before... I think whatever sustained him, gave this life, too. Here - I don't want it anymore. I just want to go home.
R... right. It's a blur... I'm leaving. I can't stand this place anymore...!
Why are you glad?

Though it may not be so dire as a broken leg, I promise you, friend - my injuries prevent me from doing what I wish the most - exploring this most verdant and mysterious country!

A shame! Well, should you be available to assist me with any, ahem, "research" into various elements of Samarach, feel free to stop by!

I cannot help but wonder what a creature like that must taste like! If you were to... acquire me some meat from one of those "dino-saurs," I would be most grateful! It would be a helpful thing for a traveller to know, if such beasts were succulent fare - wouldn't you say?

Master Osi has told me that one of the reasons the populace is so scared of snake-men is that once, a group of yuan-ti inflitrators was unmasked in their midst, and panic was widespread. However, they've been nearly exterminated since, which makes me wonder...

Few beings have seen the temples of the snake-folk and lived, but since few remain here... I'd imagine there's got to be an empty one somewhere! A single artifact from such a place - even just a little bit of stone - would be thrilling to possess!

I have heard that here in the south, there are things called... "pair-rots" - talking birds that repeat what you say! Is that not wondrous? I should dearly like such a creature for a pet. What a companion it would be!

However, due to an - ahem - misunderstanding betwixt myself and a merchant... selling what he claimed was "powdered beard of Elminster" - I'm not allowed to venture out into the market stalls anymore. If you should be so kind as to pick up a talking bird for me, I should be most grateful!

Gond's titanium tongs, how did I know that woman would send someone to bother us one of these days? It was just a matter of time...
Creative! But hardly frightening, considering the amount of golems I have to defend me. Huh - only person who knows where we are and would risk sending thugs like you is Sa'Sani.
As charming as it would be to reacquaint myself with an old friend, I'm also someone who isn't easily fooled. Sa'Sani sent you here, didn't she?

No need to ask what Sa'Sani wants from us, though - but I'm afraid she's fresh out of luck. Even if she does pay the normal fee, our portal's broken right now - we can't even go home to Lantan at night.

Yes, broken - is there a parrot nearby or did you repeat me? A part's missing, and we have more problems atop that. And living in tents has made me less than my usual charming self, so you get cranky Dall Nickleplate instead of the pleasant one.
"Things." That's the quick reply. The longer one is that a part's missing, and we have more problems than I'm happy with, and thus the cranky Dall Nickleplate is the one you get to meet.
Little more complicated than that - don't really want to go into detail right now. Got plenty more problems on top of that, you see, and problems make Dall Nickleplate a very unhappy gnome.

Not bad... yes and no. The magic is fine, it's just - look, it's complex, and I've got enough problems bothering me that I don't have the time to explain. These issues are making Dall Nickleplate into the crankiest gnome on Toril right now, sorry.

Gee, what was I thinking? I'll just snap my fingers and send it to - oh wait, I can't, the portal is broken. Maybe if you volunteered to give us a hand, we could help. Otherwise, there's nothing I can do for you.

It'd help us a great deal if you thinned out some of the dinos - and bring me three claws as proof. And also find out what's damaging our equipment.

Gond's gears... I never thought... We'll give them a burial - send their remains home to Lantan. Make sure that happens.

My apologies... and thanks for bringing that matter to light. I'll need a moment to - gather my thoughts, but talk to me again soon, please.
Either I'm mistaken, or those are dinosaur claws... I assume their numbers are thinned, then?
That's a relief - too much of our time has been spent looking over our shoulders, worried we're going to be their next meal. Thanks for your help.

I'll study these claws to see if I can't create the base for some kind of... anti-dinosaur device - maybe some kind of sonic emitter - but let me jot down some notes. Come back and talk to me again and we'll see about the portal...
You've helped us out, travellers, and I thank you for that. I've been hoping to put off telling you the details of this, but since you've helped us, you deserve to know.

The portal being broken isn't the least of our worries - our chief artificer died a very short while ago, and the missing part is so critical, only he'd really know how to fix it. So you see the position we're in.

It seems like a simple jungle disease - that he just stopped breathing. But it came too close to the portal breaking, and I cast a number of divination spells... plus I happen to have - ahem - a little training in the ways of the wild... but it was poison.
The Interface Widget - an absolutely critical piece of machinery that allows for the funneling of stored magical energy into a concentrated... you know, it's complicated. It would likely bore you.
...Gond himself would be proud of this part. Excellent work - it seems to do the trick!
|Assistant|Excuse me, I um. We did... I was tinkering with it at lunch one day, but a dinosaur attacked, and I threw my lunch basket at it when I was fleeing, and I... well, it... er...

Right, right - something that heavy isn't going to get out of its gut easily - and the part's designed to tick when it gets too far away from the camp... if it's not dead, you should be able to track it without a problem.
...I hardly believe it - but this should work perfectly! Excellent!
...It's not gnomish design, but - I think that would function... yeah... It'll take some work to enchant this, but I definitely think it'll work!
I've managed to keep it under wraps, but with the portal broken, the workers are getting more and more on edge. If we could only do something about that part...

This should fix everything. I'll send a messenger to Crossroad Keep - that was it, correct? - for you. We'll need to run some tests first - don't know if the portal is really safe for living things first... maybe do some trial runs with lizards - but we'll get the message through soon as we can.
Will you be able to help us with the missing part for the portal?
Ah - I see you have the part! A bit... worse for wear, perhaps, but it was designed to work under high-stress environments anyway, so a Megaraptor's gut... anyway.
Back again? What's the news?
A ghost, huh? Not what I expected - but appreciated all the same.

Salutations! I don't believe I've seen any newcomers to the camp in quite a while! Have you come to take a look at my marvelous friends?
My wonderful golems, of course! Don't tell me you didn't notice them!
Oh, no! ...Which isn't to say they're not terribly interesting, in their own way, but no - I mean my golems!
Yes, yes! Good eye - you know what I mean!
Only about my golems, my friend - and about mushrooms. Ha! I'm kidding, I'm allergic to them. Mostly! But no - golems!
They're the backbone of the lumber camp here, you know. Too dangerous? Send in a golem! Too heavy? Have a golem lift it! Where Lantanese man - oh, and woman - power fails, a golem steps in!

Buy? Oh, goodness, no! I could never part with one - plus I think Dall would feed me into a wood chipping device if I let some of our most precious technological secrets up and walk away! But I am flattered you'd be interested!
Usually, very much yes! But I've developed a special formula of oil that helps fortify against water intrusion - that, along with constant love - er, maintenance - keeps them running.

What? ...Oh, you must be joking! Ha! No, no, never. My friends are loyal as they can be made - not that they really have a brain, so much, but if they did, they'd know how much I care about them. Or maybe they'd need a heart for that? On a theoretical level, I mean... hm.
Come by anytime - I'll be happy to talk to you!
Sure do - don't have much, but if you've got coin, I don't see any harm in taking it. Ha!
Come and see us again!
You're back! Welcome again! Can't stay away, can you? Hee!
Yes! And now you're done! Ha! ...Just kidding, of course. What can I tell you?
Oh, so flattered! But the cost - and, well, Dall's anger - er. He's not nice when he's angry, not nice at all, and letting even a single golem go would make him very, very angry... so no, sorry.
Every time! Reliable as clockwork, because they're clockwork themselves - on their mother's side, that is. Ha! Small joke! ...But yes, they're loyal, wonderful things.

Well, I - er - can't really, Lantan secret, and um... well, I can tell you I myself have made more than a few "modifications" here and there - they're my special guys, nothing like 'em in the Realms! That plating? You won't see that come out of any factory, no way - er - if there were factories, that is. Um.

Oh! I... well... gee. That's awful nice. Sometimes I think it's him doing the crafting, not me, y'know? But that's probably way too unimportant for the Lord of All Smiths, huh... oh gosh, I hope he didn't take offense at me saying he was doing my work! I'll have to work harder today to make up for it...
Okay! Come back and see me again soon!
Can I help with anything else?
What else can I do for you?
So, um. Anything else I can answer?
What else can I do for you, fellow crafter?
They're... I... sniffle... gone!
My golems! Lately they've just been... so... difficult, I don't know any other way to put it - and my clockroaches all ran away!
If someone doesn't do something, they're - programmed to clean, and with their acid, they might... oh, why did they run away?!
Yes! All of a sudden, they just - started acting weird, and my clockroaches all ran away!
Oh, thank you! If you brought me the pieces to at least four of them, I'm sure I could find out what went wrong... maybe make you something special.
What can I help you with?
You do! Oh, thank you... I was so worried. This isn't the way I wished to have them back, but I'll take what I can get.
Here... it isn't much, but I hope this will come in handy. It's a little one, not as powerful as the others, but it oughta help you. I hope you like it.

I hear tell as far away as Rashemen that the spirits are stirring... something has woken, something is hungry. That is all I have heard, all the voices here can teach me. It is mysterious.
The manticores of Zhentil Keep are gnashing their teeth at the dark shapes on the sands - the shadow they cast is dimming their glorious fires.
Ubtao's children seem restless lately - packs of them roam beyond the borders of the Samarlogh, feasting on human and livestock alike. Some say they scent a greater danger on the wind...
The Mines of Selgol seethe with flame - and the hisses of a deeper danger. They hold more than salt, now, this is so.

Some who touch magic claim visions - that when a grief befell the Coast of Swords, something grasped their minds as well. And even as the North struggles to recover, so too do they... yet their fear lingers.

I have heard a druid sing of separation - two piles of grain, and a hand that parts them. He gave me a handful of dates and said to plant the seeds... that soon another sea would draw nearer, before the palms would be much more than saplings. Druids are so odd...

[The bizarre stone has a slight warmth to it. As you touch it, you feel a slight tingling at the back of your neck, like a hand about to brush against your skin.]
[As you imply intense pressure to the stone, it seems to crack and immediately reseal, repairing the damage done.]
[As you focus, the tingling at the back of your head cascades through your being, turning your vision a brilliant white. And, as quickly as it came, it is gone.]

[You open your eyes, knowing they are yours - but the memories that unfold before you are not yours. Bizarre images coagulate at the edge of your vision, but fade to mist the moment you attempt to focus on them.]

[The images come sporadically - a spire that stretches forever; a city with no gates, but countless doors. Streets teeming with creatures both familiar and bizarre, and a dangerous lady who silently rules...]

[A man approaches you, searching; his dessicated face twists into a scarred grin as he draws near. He brings with him flashes of his life, of his search - and in the end, what he has found - only death.]
[Suddenly, a blinking of your mind's eye. As it reopens, you find yourself as you were before, the stone gone. You feel somewhat shaken... but a bit wiser for the experience.]

[As you force apart the stone, a great thunderclap tears through the air. You cannot place its location - it seems to surround you and originate within you all at once. Reflexively, you close your eyes...]

[...and they open again to bewildering images, flashes of a strange place. A city with no gates but countless doors; with pale ruddy skies and myriad bizarre creatures that walk the twisting streets.]
[A man, scarred and weak, lies huddled before you, but your vision will not focus on him. You cannot resolve who - or what - he is.]
[He is surrounded by others - perhaps fellows, perhaps foes, perhaps servants. Perhaps equal parts each.]
[Each shoulders a portion of a shared burden; each is leashed by the rope that lashes them.]

[As you relax and will yourself to learn from the experience, the feeling at the back of your neck wraps around you, suddenly washing your vision with dazziling brilliance. As quickly as this feeling is upon you, it vanishes.]

{M, Simple, L01}Crossroad Keep - The Next Step
Sa'Sani has asked you to meet her in your new Merchant Headquarters to discuss the next steps needed to advance her interests on the Sword Coast.

You met with Sa'Sani and discussed setting an alliance with one of the other merchant factions in the Sword Coast. She also introduced you to Variel, her majordomo in the Sword Coast branch. With Sa'Sani occupied with other matters, you'll be dealing with Variel most of the time.
{M, Complex, L10}Crossroad Keep - Protection Money

Sa'Sani has informed you that Tuka-Akut, leader of a band of trolls and ogres, has offered to stop attacking her caravans in exchange for an unspecified amount of tribute. She would like you to visit Tuka-Akut, "negotiate" with him, and then inform Variel of the results. He can be found in a cave of crystal, east of Crossroad Keep.

Your intimidating presence has made Tuka-Akut look weak in front of his minions, and they have begun to fight amongst themselves. Tuka-Akut naturally blames you for this, but killing him in the chaos should be easier.

A well-told lie has caused dissention within the ranks of Tuka-Akut's band, and they have begun to fight among themselves. Tuka-Akut naturally blames you for this, but killing him in the chaos should be easier.

You provided tribute as Tuka-Akut demanded, and your caravans will be safe in Tuka-Akut's territory - so long as he decides to keep his word. Return to Crossroad Keep and inform Variel about the deal.
Tuka-Akut is dead, and without his leadership his band will split up and scatter. Return to Crossroad Keep and inform Variel that the caravans will be safe.
You told Variel that Tuka-Akut won't be troubling the caravans ever again.
You told Variel that you paid tribute to Tuka-Akut. She wasn't entirely convinced that it was the right thing to do, but she will stand by your decision.
Although you already paid Tuka-Akut his tribute, you ended up killing him after all.
{M, Simple, L10}Crossroad Keep - Murder at Crossroad Keep

Nas'sirin has been murdered, apparently by Kuwara, and Kuwara herself is missing. Variel is convinced that Kuwara is innocent, and in great danger. She wants you to investigate the matter. Searching Kuwara's room seems like a good place to start.
You found the remnants of some type of powder in Kuwara's room, but were unable to determine its origin. Orias may know more about it.

The spell components you recovered from Kuwara's room are commonly used in teleporation magic. While Kuwara could have gone anywhere in the Realms, a return to her mercantile house in Samargol is the most likely destination.

A group of men were busy ransacking Sa'Sani's mercantile house when you arrived. They were in no mood to talk, but you managed to recover a map from them detailing a secret route through the Narubel Pass in northeast Samarach. It would seem your next destination is the Jungles of Chult.

Kuwara, or Sa'sani, as she calls herself now, did in fact murder Nas'sirin. Nas'sirin was an agent of Sa'sani's brothers, and she eliminated him before he had a chance to warn the brothers that Sa'sani had become aware of their treachery.

You have encountered a group of enraged worgs. Perhaps further investigation will reveal their origin.
You have discovered a cave in southwest Neverwinter Wood. The worgs here seem unusually crazed and vicious.

You have killed the enraged worg Den Mother and ended the immediate threat to the Sword Coast. It seemed that some force - either magical or divine - enhanced these Worgs and drove them to attack Human settlements.

{N, Complex, L10}Port Llast - Under New Management

The Fated Winds have heard word that trade has been interrupted to the occupied town of Port Llast, to the north. Because the Winds cannot secure as favorable trade agreements with Neverwinter, they would like you to resolve the problems halting trade without removing the Luskans from power.

Aster Merris sees an opportunity in the town of Port Llast. Travel from the town, both by land and by sea, has completely stopped. As a result, demand for their prized Knucklehead Ivory has gone unfulfilled. Aster will reward you for restoring trade to Port Llast - and thus trade in Knucklehead Ivory.

Jon Archen has informed you that Luskan has occupied the town of Port Llast - and as a result all trade to and from Port Llast has been interrupted. The Circle of Friends is willing to pay you one thousand trade bars to restore at least one trade route to and from Port Llast and to free the town from its Luskan occupants.

You've spoken to Rynn Shepherde of Luskan, the new leader of Port Llast. He told you about two major problems crippling trade in the area. Note

This book contains the mad scrawlings of what appears to be a fervent - and quite insane - worshipper of Malar. "THE THIRD MONTH - THE FOURTEENTH DAY - THE seventh HOUR: the children speak to me they call to me I hear them breathing! my lord you lord of hunt you bloodied tooth bloodied fang face butcher of men and beasts - i call to you! show me what your children need here in their home they are home they are home with me and i must be their shepherd - their friend - their teacher. the "woodsy" one he thinks he knows what he does - my father says "find the woodsy one" and i say "the children know - they shall find!" the children come, my hands shake with glee, i speak and they lick their lips for my words. the mother comes to defend her children but we are all friends we are all friends wild ones..." Another entry, further along in the journal, stands out: THE THIRD MONTH - THE SEVENTEENTH DAY - DARKENING: it grows dim and the children bring such delicious morsels to me, the mother she has coupled with my lord and my lord has granted her great things, the little ones drink of her, his and her children we drink of her and we are fulfilled. father HAS his way now! i have given him the woodsy one - deer and bear and beast slayer and the murderer SHALL be avenged he SHALL pay he SHALL and our lord will be appeased. FATHER TELLS ME wait here, I HAVE MORE FOR YOU. i will wait. the children and mother will feed me. I HAVE heard a rumbling i know not what it be" And then a final entry: "they came and spoke with my lords voice, we bring them meats and our lord is pleased i am theirs and they are OUR FATHER." On the last page of the journal, a small map is scrawled with a note, written by a saner hand: "Son, Our children make their bed here. We must not allow the woodsy two-leg to cull their mother - she bears child. Teach them, and bring him to me so I may devour his heart in praise of our lord."
Tyburn the Mad's Journal

Type of Feat: Class. Prerequisite: Doomguide Level 5. Specifics: The doomguide's devotion to Kelemvor and dedication to the teachings of the Lord of the Crystal Spire has helped him to establish a certain supernatural links to Fatal Touch, Kelemvor's powerful scythe. These links manifest in the form of a pale green nimbus around a weapon, representing the ability of the doomguide to increase the power of the weapon he wields. The ability lasts for 1 attack each time it is used and can be invoked a number of times per day equal to the doomguide's charisma bonus (minimum 1). A doomguide must decide to use the ability before attacking and if the attack misses that use is wasted. At 5th level the bond grants wielded weapons a damage bonus against undead. At 7th level weapons gain both the damage bonus and undead bane properties. At 9th level wielded weapons gain the damage bonus, undead bane and disruption properties even if they are not bludgeoning weapons. The weapons normal abilities still applies. Weapon Traits: - Damage Bonus: The Doomguide's devotion to Kelemvor grants wielded weapons a damage bonus of 1d6 against undead foes. - Undead Bane: A bane weapon excels at attacking one type or subtype of creature. Against its designated foe, its effective enhancement bonus is +2 better than its normal enhancement bonus. It deals an extra 2d6 points of damage against the foe. - Disruption: A weapon of disruption is the bane of all undead. Any undead creature struck in combat must succeed on a DC 14 Will save or be destroyed. Use: Selected.

Hellfire Warlock (PRESTIGE CLASS: This class is not available at character creation and must be unlocked by meeting special requirements, listed below.) The hellfire warlocks are a secretive group of specialist warlocks who have mastered hellfire, a dangerous energy found only in the Nine Hells. By tapping into this infernal power, these characters learn to infuse their eldritch blasts with the dark power of hellfire. Requirements: Skills: Intimidate 6 ranks, Spellcraft 6 ranks, Lore 12 ranks. Spells: Brimstone Blast or Hellrime Blast Class Features: - Hit Die: d6 - Base Attack Bonus: Medium. - High Saves: Will. - Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons. - Armor Proficiencies: Light armor. A warlock can use any of his invocations while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. A warlock wearing medium or heavy armor or using a shield incurs a chance of arcane spell failure. - Skill Points: 2 + Int Modifier. - Class Skills: Concentration, Intimidate, Lore, Spellcraft, Use Magic Device. - Hellfire Blast: Whenever you use your eldritch blast ability, you can change your eldritch blast into a hellfire blast. A hellfire blast deals your normal eldritch blast damage plus an extra 2d6 points of damage per class level. If your blast hits multiple targets (for example, the eldritch chain or eldritch cone blast shape invocations), each target takes the extra damage. This damage is not fire damage. The Hellfire Warlock takes 1 point of Constitution damage each target hit in this manner. - Invoking: At each level, you gain new invocations known, increased damage with eldritch blast, and an increase in invoker level as if you had also gained a level in the warlock class. You do not, however, gain any other benefit a character of that class would have gained. - Resistance to Fire 10: At 2nd level, you gain resistance to fire 10. This resistance stacks with any resistance to fire you have gained from warlock class levels. - Summon Baatezu: At 2nd level, once per day, the Hellfire Warlock can randomly summon a powerful devil from the Nine Hells to fight for the party. Control of the Baatezu lasts for a number of rounds equal to 1D8 + the Hellfire Warlock's class level + their Charisma bonus. When the ability expires, the caster loses dominance over the Baatezu - which can have disastrous consequences, as devils typically despise being bothered by lesser beings. The caster is advised not to leave this up to chance, and dispel this summons before this time is up, sending the Baatezu back to the Nine Hells - though the devil might not attack, this method is the only certain way of avoiding a violent confrontation with the angry creature. - Hellfire Shield: Starting at 3rd level, you can call up hellfire to surround yourself with a protective barrier. This barrier deals damage equal to your eldritch blast (including bonus damage from the hellfire blast ability). This barrier automatically strikes the target every round, which can attempt a Reflex saving throw for half damage (DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Cha modifier). Each time this ability hits an enemy creature, you take 1 point of Constitution damage. Because the diabolical forces behind the power of hellfire demand part of your essence in exchange for this granted power, if you do not have a Constitution score or are somehow immune to Constitution damage, you cannot use this ability.

Yuan-ti Pureblood The yuan-ti are descended from humans whose bloodlines have been mingled with those of snakes. Their evilness, cunning, and ruthlessness are legendary. Yuan-ti constantly scheme to advance their own dark agendas. They are calculating and suave enough to form alliances with other evil creatures when necessary, but they always put their own interests first. Yuan-ti that can pass for humans with suitable clothing, cosmetics, and magic are known as Purebloods. These creatures are usually charged with infiltrating humanoid societies and managing covert operations that require direct contact with humanoids. Hunting. Tashalar's wilds are expansive and beautiful, but the jungles of Samarach have a certain... additional appeal. The Samarachans shrink in fear from them... and let the creatures roam free and unchallenged. But instead I sit here, idle...

Wise and well-spoken - from Tashalar is where my sister and I hail. From Tashluta we traveled by ship to hidden Samargol - here we will train until we are skilled enough to brave the mountain journey back. She is injured at the moment, so now... we must wait.

My sister, Kwesi, and I were hunting the great boar Bal-alak. We peppered his hide with bolts, but to no avail - he fled, and gave her a wound in her leg to remember him by. Now she works handling the bounties of the land, and I... I wait.

This young man carries himself as if he is much older than he looks. His seemingly calm, calculated composure is betrayed only by his eyes, which appear perpetually haunted, as if he has seen too much, too young.
Septimund
You - it is you. I have seen you in my dreams.
I do not seek passion - I am here on a sacred mission!
|PC Male|She came in here lookin' for you, lad. I tried to shoo her, but she didn't move a muscle 'til you showed.
|PC Female|She came in here lookin' for you, lass. I tried to shoo her, but she didn't move a muscle 'til you showed.
I came here - all the way from Evermeet - because my goddess - bless the name of Angharradh! - sent me. A dire fate awaits the elven race if I did not find you, she said - indeed, all the races!

I... admit I am not as young as I was. But the Triune Goddess has always shown me great favor, and in my dreams she spoke to me. No one but I was to travel here - none else was told the way. None else could have survived - my strength has not failed me!
I gotta admit - we tried to stop her comin' in, and she knocked some of our Greycloaks silly with the haft o' that spear without breakin' a sweat. It weren't too shabby of work.
I thank you, master dwarf. I will admit... I had not expected such kindness as what you displayed to me earlier. I am in your debt.
I... er... weren't nothin, I uh - travelled with elves before. Ahem.
Mock me not - my quest is sacred!
Do not think I was glad to see the face of a kinslayer, and oath-breaker in my dreams, drow - but my goddess gives orders, and I obey. Do you not do the same?
You do not need force to make me depart! I shall leave. But remember well - a darkness is descending on the face of Toril. We each will play a part in it... be wary of yours!
I did not come here for you, youngster - but you, too, have a role in this, no matter what deity you pay homage to.
Ease your thoughts, young one. Long have I been her devotee - and now I come to join my strength to yours.
No - it does not seem so. It was not fate that brought you here, that I can divine...
But nonetheless, the Triune Goddess tells me you are positioned such that your deeds affect factors beyond your ken... and I must be here to aid you.
This I do not know - but I know I am here to aid you, in whatever way you require.

Allow me to travel with you - my spear is yours, to aid you as you see fit. That you live, that you do what you feel you must whenever it is that the time comes - if the time does come - that is all I ask.
I... thank you for your forebearance. The Triune Goddess has instructed me to find you - and after that, to offer you my help.
No matter how you find it - I have my orders from the goddess. Find you - and offer my help.
|PARTY FULL|I fear you have too many followers at present - I shall retire to a suitable location and wait for your convenience.

|HERE|I shall remain here and wait for you, then.
|LOGGING|I shall keep company with the gnomes, then.
|CK|I will make my way to the Keep, as I did before.

Gray Orc
Gray Orcs
gray orc
gray orcs

Gray Orc The orcs of the eastern lands are concentrated in the Moonsea and Endless Wastes today, with a much smaller number scattered through the various lands that lie between. A gray orc looks less bestial than their more savage northern kin, but is still obviously nonhuman. Grey orcs are more apt to wear "civilized" clothing than mountain orcs, though they typically follow a nomadic existence - dwelling in remote, desolate places and eking out a meager existence as best they can. The true power behind a tribe of gray orcs is not the chieftain, but the tribe's high priest, typically an adept or a cleric (often female), who has held the position for many years. The gray orcs are zealots, and the word of their tribal clerics is law. Gray orcs are just as mean, savage, and barbaric as their northern cousins, but they lack the mountain orc's drive to conquer and enslave. Gray orcs are quite likely to react suddenly and irrationally to events, trusting their heart and instincts more readily than logic. When presented with an opportunity to attack a hated rival, a gray orc doesn't hesitate to attack even having been brutally defeated dozens of times before by the same enemy. Racial Traits: - Ability Adjustments: +2 Strength, -2 Intelligence, +2 Wisdom, -2 Charisma - Long Gait: Gray orc base land speed is 40 feet. Their gait is long and loping and they can cover great distances quickly. - Light Sensitivity: Gray orcs suffer a -1 penalty on attack rolls in sunlight or within the radius of a daylight spell. - Scent: Can detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell. This allows the user to track hidden and invisible targets when using the Track ability. - Favored Class: Cleric. Although gray orcs are comfortable with the savage life of the barbarian, they tend to be more calm and collected than northern orcs, focusing their rage and hatred inward. This allows them to excel as clerics of the warlike orc deities. - Level Adjustment +1: Gray orcs are slightly more powerful and gain levels more slowly than other, more common races. It will take more experience for a gray orc to reach level 2 than it would for normal races, for example.
GRAY ORC BIOGRAPHY
Weapon Proficiency (Gray Orc)

Type of Feat: Race Prerequisites: Gray Orc Specifics: Gray orcs are proficent with the greataxe and the longbow, having trained with such weapons from childhood. Gray orcs are marginally cleaner than mountain orcs, and their equipment is kept in better shape as a result - axes in particular are viewed as holy, and gray orcs take fastidious care of their greataxe. Use: Automatic.
Scent

Type of Feat: Race Prerequisites: Gray Orc Specifics: Scent allows one to detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell. This allows the user to track hidden and invisible targets when using the Track ability. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Heritage Prerequisite: Fey Heritage. Nonlawful Alignment. Specifics: Your fey heritage guards you against all weapons except those crafted from the dreaded cold iron. You gain damage reduction (overcome by cold iron) equal to 1 + the number of feats you have that list Fey Heritage as a prerequisite (including such feats that you take after gaining this one). For example, if you have Fey Skin and Fey Presence, you would have damage reduction 3/cold iron. This value stacks with any similar damage reduction you might have from your type, subtype, race, or class, but not from other sources, such as spells or magic items. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Heritage Prerequisite: Can only take this feat at 1st level. Non-good alignment. Specifics: You are descended from creatures native to the Lower Planes. You share some of your ancestors' natural resistance to poison, and you are resistant to the magic of good foes. You gain a +4 bonus on Fortitude saving throws against poison. You also gain a +1 bonus on saving throws against spells or other effects produced by good creatures. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Heritage Prerequisite: Fiendish Heritage, Non-good alignment, Character Level 9. Specifics: You are descended from creatures native to the Lower Planes. This appears to be some kind of prayerbook, ancient and well-worn. You're not able to make sense of much of the text - a great deal of it has simply been worn away with age - but you're able to find the following passage, written in an archaic dialect of the Common tongue: "Praise ye be to the Great Serpent, the Slitherer Supreme! To Sseth let our prayers rise - let the great one hear as we offer our sacrifices to him, as they give their lives willingly to his glory, and we slither through their blood. Let subtlety be our ways, and manipulation guide us - in the Sacred Way of Sseth, the whisper is mightier than the fang, manipulation greater than force. Let the tsaa olo not know we guide them, let them not know our motions until we have won. May Sseth bless the vrael olo, that one day, as it should be, we hold the reins of the world - that we order and guide it according to His favor!" "Yea, let praise be to Sseth. Let honor be given to the Slitherer Supreme. May he bless his faithful children, and may we ever honor his name."

Sorlyn's Ditty

The original template of this flute was created as a Midsummer gift to Sorlyn Sheerla, cleric of Milil, and teacher at a bardic college in Amn. So charmed was she with the design that Sheerla ordered dozens of copies made, with the aim of giving one to each of her most promising students. However, since making so many with such powerful magic would have bankrupted herm, Sheerla thought it was all right to reduce the potency of their enchantments a bit... reasoning that any prize student of hers would know well enough to stay out of trouble!

You've managed to reach the third level of the Temple without setting off the alarm. It's likely you'll be attacked on sight since no one but House Se'Sehen's elite is permitted to be here.
You triggered the alarm, and the entire Temple of the World Serpent is now on the alert for intruders.
Against all odds, you reached the Throne of the World Serpent without triggering the alarm or being discovered by sentries. The gods themselves are probably impressed with your feat.
{O, Complex, L15}Chult - The Fall of House Se'Sehen

The leaders of House Se'Sehen have all gathered at a yuan-ti holy sanctuary known as the Temple of the World Serpent. Finding them and wiping them all out in a single blow will prevent House Se'Sehen from uniting all yuan-ti into a murderous force bent on sacrificing all other beings for the glory of Zehir.

With the loss of their leaders and the embarrassing defeat of the Herald of Zehir, House Se'Sehen no longer has the power or the credibility to unite all yuan-ti under their banner. The yuan-ti clans who have turned to the worship of Zehir will remain a threat elsewhere in the Realms, but Samarach and the Sword Coast are safe for now.
Return to Sa'Sani at the Viper Temple and let her know that the threat of House Se'Sehen is ended.
With both House Se'Sehen and House Sauringar defeated, both Samarach and the Sword Coast should be free of yuan-ti influence for some time to come.
{O, Simple, L15}Crossroad Keep - Trailing Sa'Sani

Sa'Sani has returned to Samarach, but her ultimate destination remains mystery. Dall said that Sa'Sani was last seen heading east from the lumber camp, but he has no other information. Making inquiries in Taruin or Torich may yield further clues as to Sa'Sani's whereabouts.
You learned that Sa'Sani was reported heading up the Narubel Pass, towards Chult, and that she was not alone.
You've located Sa'Sani within the ruins known as the Viper Temple.
{N, Simple, L08}Neverwinter City - The Trading Post

Your merchant faction has tasked you with acquiring the right to purchase the recently constructed trading post in the Blacklake District. Speak with Sir Nevalle to find out what you must to do secure the right to the property.
Nevalle has set the price of purchase for the Neverwinter Trading post at eight hundred trade bars.
You've purchased the Neverwinter Trading Post in the Blacklake District.

Rogue's Harness

This harness may hold a dagger in plain view, but its most helpful features are the ones others don't see - an assortment of tools concealed in the interior of the bandolier that help even the most hamfisted of thieves pick locks more efficently.

Though these wasp stingers look terrifying, they aren't terribly successful at fully striking a telling blow on their target. However, when they do manage to hit their target solidly, their barbs manage to work their way deep within their victim's skin, causing a capable amount of pain and agony.
Ferrous Clogs
These strange boots seem to exert and almost magnetic pull against the earth, preventing their user from being knocked over.
Marvelous Galoshes

Originally crafted by the gnomish explorer Emil "Swamptread" Stuttervalve in 1273, these strangely-named shoes allowed the eccentric young scientist to venture into the most entangling swamps without fear of getting caught or frozen in its murky, sucking waters. Though his papers about the viability of will o' wisps as a distillable fuel source were largely disregarded, his plans for these particular brand of footwear persisted far beyond his academic career.
Barkplate
This odd armor resembles a standard breastplate, but crafted from a strange, thick wood. Though it doesn't offer optimal protection, it carries with it some interesting abilities.
Superior Barkplate

This odd armor is an improvement from an old design, created from the bark of a tree strengthened by a strange magic. Though it doesn't offer optimal protection, it carries with it some interesting abilities.
Kudeu Nuts

These strange nuts are plucked from the kudeu tree - quite carefully, in fact, because the seeds often house dangerous, stinging beetles. Adult bugs burrow into the seeds when they are young and soft, and lay their eggs inside - as the nut ages and hardens, the young eat the nut meat as they hatch, and grow strong. However, if the nut is cracked open before its time - say, in a well-placed hit on an enemy when fired from a sling - the angry bugs within will swarm the victim, causing them to react with panic and fright until the hateful little creatures are shaken off or squished.
This suit of chainmail is icy-cold to the touch, nearly frost-burning your fingers with its frigid bite.
Auril's Icy Accoutrements

This chainmail was once the property of a cleric of Auril under the employ of the Luskans who controlled Port Llast. With the city freed, this armor seems to have relucantly accepted your use... though having its constant chill nearby is often a far cry from comfortable.

Appearing at a single glance to be an elegant silvery cloak, further study shows that the fabric seems to swallow light, preventing proper illumination. Once a day, the wearer can command the cloak to activate, investing its user with a wraithlike appearance.
These clothes are silky to the touch, and seem to crackle with energy.
Enduring Vestments

However, they still left her subject to harm by other means, and she met her end when her carelessness with a summoned elemental filled her lungs with water.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: The regular routine your group has established for resting has been honed to perfection, allowing you to set up, watch, and break down camp with the utmost speed and efficiency. The party is 50% less likely to have a hostile encounter when resting. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: The members of your team can combine their attacks to slice through the defenses of a foe they have surrounded. All party members get +2 bonus on damage rolls when attacking a flanked opponent. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: Your party projects an air of menace, that causes some would be foes to flee when your team approaches them on the overland map. Hostiles on the Overland Map will run from the party if their CR is 3 levels or more below the party level (without this benefit, enemies will run away if they are 4 levels or more below the party). Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: Your team has become even more menacing, causing many would-be foes to flee when you approach them on the overland map. Hostiles on the Overland Map will run from the party if their CR is 2 levels or more below the party level (without this benefit, enemies will run away if they are 3 levels or more below the party). Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: Your team is especially good at tracking down and destroying specific types of creatures. All party members gain a +2 bonus to damage when attacking the favored enemies of their fellow party members. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: You and your teammates have reduced your need for sleep by learning the ways of the elves. You are fully rested after only 4 hours, as opposed to the usual 8. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: Your team excels at firing as a group, unleashing a saturated wave of arrows and bolts. Party members get a +1 to their attack with missile weapons when a previous party member attacks with a missile weapon. The buff lasts for one round. If no one else shoots a ranged weapon that round, the buff disappears. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: Your team members can use their camaraderie and shared experience to shrug off the effect of fear. All party members get a +2 saving throw vs. fear. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: Your team is good at harrying foes by taking maximum advantage of their divided attention. All party members get a +2 bonus to hit when attacking a flanked opponent. Use: Automatic.

Type of Feat: Teamwork Benefit Specifics: Your team travels faster than normal as a group. The efforts and assistance of the faster characters allow the slower ones to keep up. All party members move at the same rate as the fastest member. Use: Automatic.

The childhood home of the illustrious Knight-Captain, this small swamp village was rebuilt by many of the Mere-dwelling survivors of the Shadow War.
A small mining town near the Mere of Dead Men, Leilon does business up and down the High Road.

But you love your own life well enough, aasimar - for as much as you pretend to loathe living. And you crave coin without even using it, as a dragon does - so I will line your palm with it if you assist me.

What, and turn down the chance to use your powers against an entire house of yuan-ti? Surely you wouldn't mind giving House Se'Sehen a headache in return for all the misfortune they've caused you... share and share alike.
Unexpected solemnity from you, bard. But I sense your meaning - and your understanding that what we face is bigger than you or I.
Brave words, one-tusk. Valiant to the last, I see - a fine show, and I would applaud if sarcasm did not bounce off of you like arrows on a brick wall. Just like that, you go to face danger.

Indeed. I had never thought it a valuable thing to have one of the family of Tashalar around - but as your people drove the Se'Sehen clan from your nation ages ago, so it may be your valor will aid you in hunting them down now.

How... thoughtful of you. I do not suppose it matters that I never intended for you or your ship to come to any harm... but that it mixed you up in this - and that you have stayed for so long - your aid here and now is... is welcome.

Because that would avail you not at all? You wish power, half-drow - that desire eminates from you like an odor. Do you not wish to take by force the secrets that a clan as ancient as the Se'Sehen might hold, and use them as you see fit?
Heh... it is odd, human. All this time I remained certain you either lay in the grip of madness or suffered from the most aggressive of stupidity... but now you speak the most sense of all.

Such a pretty speech, Doomguide - I commend you on it. I know the thing you love the most is service... that any mortal being could win such love from you would be a thing to see... but I digress. You say you will aid me, and that is appreciated.

{quiet, speaks of a hurt she's carried for a long time}I... appreciate your devotion. My lord Sseth once spoke to me so clearly - and his silence has caused grave pain. {switching tracks}But Zehir's threat is greater than any silence - and the Se'Sehen courting him must be stopped.
This is good to know, druid of the jungle. I cannot promise any outcome - but you can expect no aggression from me. Zehir is our enemy - and we shall together bring him low.
{dryly}Once again, gnoll, your modesty is a shining example to us all. But that aside - we have our target, and it is one that cannot be ignored.
{wryly}If you were, I'd have been dead long before now... not to mention you'd be long exiled from their ssrath - 'disowned,' so to speak. You're in just as much danger as I. So, then...
Is your own life not enough incentive? ...Fine. I'll owe you a favor - and with my influence, you should know the boundaries on that are not unimpressive. Now - to business.
This is good to know - it saves me useless words in attempting to convince you of what is obvious.

In a word, yes. The resulting power struggle within the House will leave them too disoriented to exert control over the other yuan-ti clans... and significantly reduce Zehir's power and influence as well.
{dry, sarcastic}Hardly. He did not work his way up to be the leader of the largest clan of yuan-ti by acting on things directly. Zehir enjoys aggression and deceit - not brute force and stupidity.
Still your ire - I have tasks that I alone can accomplish. My clan is wounded - but we are far from defeated.
You - you followed me, even here? I am impressed... and not wholly unsurprised.
Nas'Sirin? Shed no tears for him. What he would have done to you and your kind - that earned him a worse fate than even what I gave him.
It is... not in my nature, but the time for honesty has arrived, and I will not turn from it.
It was not a lie I told you - just not the entirety of the truth. But this I shall remedy.
You know me as Sa'Sani - that name will suffice for now. But a merchant I am not - or not only. I am princess of the Sauringar clan of yuan-ti - this temple is our home and our stronghold.

My clan's mission was to revitalize the economy of the Sword Coast, as I had stated - but to place our people in power, to assure that the mistakes of the past were not repeated. The Se'Sehen clan created this plan, claimed to be its shepherds... but their words, I came to discover, were lies.
An ending is owed? Then I shall give you the truth of the matter, to open your eyes.
So it is. You have come all this way... and I owe you the truth.
Escape? You misunderstand - this was always my destination. And I know the time for deception is past.

Unknown to me, the Se'Sehen clan had turned from the worship of our god - Sseth, the Slitherer Supreme - to the worship of Zehir... whose foulness I am certain you know by now. Where we had sought to create a foothold to sow stability and peace, the Se'Sehen clan used to sow chaos and pain. They even turned my friend, Il'Foss, against me, and against his own people.

With enough confusion distracting the peoples of the Sword Coast, the cults of Zehir grow in power... and those desperate for protection and hungry for change were to flock to him... and the Se'Sehen that promoted his cause.

I - my clan - we were unwitting assistants in this scheme. When I had enough evidence, I confronted Nas'Sirin - and with enough torture, he told me everything. I knew the Se'Sehen would strike against my people, so I fled - and came here to tell them the truth... and try to protect them.

The Se'Sehen lied to my clan - said they wanted to bring stability to the Sword Coast. As we gave them the means to do so, they instead lied to us and used it to empower the servants of their foul god Zehir.

Yes - no longer do they worship our god Sseth, but have turned their prayers to the interloper god Zehir. In his name, they lied to us... claiming that they wanted to bring stability to the Sword Coast - but using my clan's hard work to spread chaos and sow deceit.

Correct. They no longer worship Sseth, god of the yuan-ti - but have turned to Zehir. The Sauringar's efforts to bring stability only gave the Se'Sehen bases of operations to work from... creating the Forktongue cults to sow fear and chaos, and gain fanatical new servants.
I... thank you. I had not anticipated assistance from such an - unexpected source.
But we must not delay. First we... wait - what was - !
An interesting ideal... not without its own unique merit, however.
Your focus is admirable. First, we must... wait - what was - !
It is well you conceive the scale of the danger we face. It is not to be taken lightly.
...Interesting evaluation. We shall see.
I shall accept that - and forgiveness is not a thing I will trouble you with asking for.
Stay your hand. I simply need time to-
First, we must... wait - what was - !
