Not entirely... but it matches too well the stories I managed to gather from sources independent of her, people she had no contact with after the wreck. It seems solid enough...
Luaire must be found and brought here. There are number of questions he must answer - to my complete satisfaction - before I absolve him of blame.

Scrying is practically a Samarachan pastime - and my customers enjoy knowing that I can offer them a modicum of security. Many of the company's more senior members wear items that shield them from this surveillance... people such as myself, Nas'Sirin, and unfortunately, Luaire as well.

He was bound to the northeast - there is a lumber camp staffed by gnomes from Lantan, and they have a working portal system. However, they are not supposed to be there - they owe me a favor for not informing the Samarachan authorities of their presence.

Luaire was supposed to use the portal to deliver a message to my colleagues at Crossroad Keep - an old fortress in the Sword Coast that acts as the northern hub of this trading company. However... if Luaire is the saboteur, I have put the warning I wished to send them in the worst hands possible.

Travel to the lumber camp - find Luaire, and bring him to me to answer these accusations in person. And if my message has not been sent - kindly send that as well... perhaps it will not be too late for Crossroad Keep.
|PORTAL NOT FIXED|It has been a time - and you are without Luaire. This is unfortunate - I hope you will explain.
Hrammar! Gods damn it... I should have known.

Do not be too hasty, my lady - it may be that the saboteur overtook Luaire and slew him, or he was forced to flee to save his life. Would you truly take the word of some unknown ship captain over our own experience?
I would like to believe that, Nas'Sirin, but these events speak poorly for his innocence. But the message was not delivered - this must be changed.
Return to the Lantanese Lumber Camp and aid them with fixing their portal in whatever way you can - a warning must be sent to Crossroad Keep!
That is an incorrect assumption - but Luaire gone... gods damn it, I should have known!
You speak the truth - and wisely. I cannot believe I was so foolish as to trust him with the missive!
|RETURNED, PORTAL FIXED|I just received a coded message from Dall - it seems the portal is working once more, thanks to you... but not to the saboteur.
I cannot stand this - if it was planned for me to be fooled in such a fashion! But whoever the saboteur is - I will set them straight.
Agreed. And we shall use that fact against them now.
Dall told me as well that he gave you a toxin sample from the blood of the poisoned artificer. It is regrettable that is our only lead, but we must follow it.
Indeed you do - and such is fortunate.

His full name is Luaire Farwander, and he is a fairly capable wizard under my employ. He is well-travelled, and often makes trips to other ports to make sure my cargo is loaded securely and no one is attempting to short me on our deals.
|AFTER LASTRI SAVED|He is our prime suspect for the sabotage of the Vigilant - at least according to Captain Lastri. We shall see about such.
|HAS LASTRI QUEST, NOT RESCUED|Yes - what do you want of me?
|PORTAL NOT FIXED, HAS TALKED TO|You were best on your way to fix that portal... but what can I do for you in the meantime?
|RETURNED, SABOTEUR NOT DEAD|Time is of the essence - we cannot sit idly by while this saboteur threatens us!
But quickly - what is it I can do for you?
|AFTER PORTAL FIX|He is a clever wizard - and it would not be far off to suspect he possesses other skills as well. He is certainly intelligent and likely deadly - do not underestimate him.
Of course, my Lady Sa'Sani. I am at your disposal!
|+2|[Intimidate] Is that a threat?
|+2|[Diplomacy] So what must we do to gain your protection?
|Chaotic|I'm not afraid of any guards.
So what now?
I just want to get out of here.
|+2|[Intimidate] I'm not working for anyone without pay.
|+2|[Diplomacy] I'll assist you, but I'm afraid I'm not very well-equipped at the moment. If you could offer some gold to help with this, I'd be grateful.
Very well.
Forget it - I'm not working for you.
Fine - I'll work for you.
Not yet.
|Evil|I'm not taking orders from the likes of you.
|Good|How can we help?
|+14 Int|Let me guess - you're interested in the lost cargo?
What's the first task?
Go on.
|Nongood|I don't mind killing more batiri. What is it?
|+2|[Appraise] It's unlikely the goods would survive for very long under the current conditions... and the batiri probably stole some... but I'll see what we can do. What's next?
|+10 Int|I would assume the second task has something to do with the first, correct?
And the second task?
Hurry up.
Here's some of the cargo I was able to recover.
Not yet.
Here's the evidence you requested.
Yes - here's the evidence you requested.
Not yet.
Yes - here's what I was able to locate.
|RECOVERED SECOND MATE|I've located a survivor from the Vigilant - the second mate was captured by batiri, but we've freed him.
|+4|[Lore] Batiri are often cannibalistic... I hope bones will suffice as evidence, if it comes to that.
|+2|[Survival] After this long, her odds are slim - but maybe if they moved her further from the beach, she has a chance of living.
We'll see.
It's unlikely she's still alive, but we'll look around.
|Nongood|Killing batiri? I can do that.
Can you tell me anything about the area?
I have a question about someone.
Tell me about yourself.
Who's Nas'Sirin?
Who's Osi?
What can you tell me about Vadin'ya?
Let me ask you something else.
Tell me about Captain Lastri.
Nothing right now.
Do you have any other tasks for me?
Who?
|+4|[Intimidate] If you're going to accuse me of something, come out and say it.
|Int +14|She's certain it was only one person?
So I take it this person - they're still alive?
That stammering idiot?
|Int +10|How do you know she wasn't trying to divert blame onto someone you knew?
|Nongood|So - how quickly do you want him dead?
Are you sure?
|+4|[Diplomacy] And you believe her story?
So where is he?
|Nonlawful|I suppose it's too much to hope he's in the area...
|+4|[Spellcraft] Why can't you just scry his location?
|+3|[Survival] I should be able to track him. Where was he headed?
Great - another wild will-o'-wisp chase.
I went to the camp - the portal is broken, and Luaire is missing.
|+5|[Diplomacy] I made my way to the lumber camp - but the portal is broken, and there was no evidence of Luaire. It does not seem the message was ever sent.
|+4|[Intimidate] Take the threat out of your voice, merchant - the portal's broken and Luaire's gone. Nothing I could do about either.
Maybe later.
|Track feat|It seems like Luaire's trail did lead to the camp... but vanished shortly after I got there. What's more, the portal is broken... doesn't seem like a conincidence.
|+15 Int|I'd say he realized once I rescued Lastri that we'd be on to him - the wards on Leira's Trick made her unreachable. So he went north to the camp, broke the portal, and disappeared.
|Rogue|The work they did was rough - in a hurry. Maybe we could trace it.
|+14 Int|This saboteur is imperfect - they have left plenty of clues.
So what now?
I might have something that can help.
That stlarning Luaire did it. He's dead now, but he revealed he was a yuan-ti.
I could see it as I killed him.
|Good|How can I be of help?
|Pureblood yuan-ti|If they suspect anyone associated with you... it is wise for me to head north, as well.
Tell me about Luaire.
I'm very busy - stay out of my way.
No other visitors - from Sa'Sani or anyone else. But plenty of problems, that's for certain.
Ha! That'd be a feat for sure - but take a breath, stranger. You've been the only visitor for ages - from that woman or not.
Until someone showed up wanting a favor from her, that's what. It's been a while since anyone bothered us - especially from that blasted merchant woman - but I knew she wouldn't wait for long.
No, I told you, nobody like that - no vistors, but plenty of problems.
I know Sa'Sani will be waiting for you, so I'll send an animal messenger on ahead to her, letting her know we still need to make some portal adjustments. But you - you should be careful.

Take this. It's a sample of the artificer's blood - complete with the toxin that killed him. The missing part, his death... knowing Sa'Sani, she's probably aware of this already, but someone's out to get her - and they seem to know exactly where and how to strike. So... watch yourself out there.
She didn't send anyone else?
|+12 Int|Wait - "one of these days"? Nobody recently?
|+3|[Intimidate] You better tell me if anyone else came here - or even those golems won't be able to protect you.
Matter of time until what?
Nothing right now.
I'm sorry.
So what do you want?

Sa'who? Oh - the merchant, right? Hired the ship... s'pose she wants to know who caused the wreck...
Watch yer mouth! Ya don't know what I've been through, out here... watchin' them goblins come at night... not knowin' if anyone else made it...
I - it's my fault, is all - the crash. I thought I could handle the ship, an' it wasn't budgin'... and when the Captain got knocked out, an' I couldn't stop it... I shoulda done better!
S-sabotage? Y'don't say... would explain why that wheel was so damned hard to move... huh. Guess I should head out, then...
Here - I know it probably don't smell so great by now, but this necklace always done me good... hope it'll do you the same.
Guess since ya saved my life, I can't get around it... fine, I'll go talk t' her. Hope she don't have me thrown in jail, though - I heard stories about Samargol jails before, and none of em are good.
Sa'Sani sent us to look for survivors.
Not her - Sa'Sani.
|+2|[Taunt] Oh, so the tough guy is gonna start crying now?
|Chaotic|What, did you have a hand in the shipwreck or something?

Start explaining.

|Chaotic|[Lie] She knows - you need to be brought to justice.
|Lawful|Then you should go and answer her questions. She's your employer, you owe her an explanation.

Just go talk to her.

Youve returned to West Harbor to find it conquered by dragons - the Tarmas that Pitney rescued was an impostor.
Volo is going to attempt to parlay with the batiri, and has suggested you check the piles of debris and plants in the area for any items that could be of use.
You've managed to fight off the batiri... only to get yourself into a graver situation.
The Samarachan patrol that you encountered on the beach doesn't seem inclined to be friendly - you'll have to find a way to keep them from throwing you in jail... or worse.
Sa'Sani has agreed to hire you as a temporary member of her merchant company so you can travel freely throughout Samarach.

With Sa'Sani's assistance, you've managed to free yourself from the guards of Samargol - but you can't leave the city. Sa'Sani has suggested you rest at the inn - Leira's Trick - and then return to speak with her.
Sa'Sani was satisfied with your report on the shipwreck.
Sa'Sani was very pleased with your attention to detail, and rewarded you for the through nature of your report.
{U, Simple, L05}Samargol - Seeking the Truth
Sa'Sani wants you to track down Luaire at the Lantanese Lumber Camp, and to see if her message to Crossroad Keep was sent.
You've discovered Luaire missing, and the Lantanese portal broken. You must fix it before you are able to send the message.
Sa'Sani has asked you to return to the Lantanese Lumber Camp and aid them in fixing the portal. Once the portal is fixed, you will be able to send her warning to Crossroad Keep.

The Deinonychus in the area seem to have developed a taste for gnomes, and are slinking around the area looking for victims. Dall would like it if you thinned their numbers a bit - 3 Deinonychus claws should prove suitable for shooing the dangerous creatures away.

The portal machinery has been sabotaged - a critical part of the machinery is missing, and the artificers are having little success in creating a replacement. You might be able to suggest a solution - or, if all else fails, track down the dinosaur that ate the previous replacement part.

You've managed to hunt down and slay the dinosaur that ate the part, recovering it for the gnome camp. Though it may need a bit of cleaning, you're confident that this will get the portal back into working order before long.
Sa'Sani has asked you to track down Luaire, the saboteur, and deal with him. Finding someone who can identify the toxin sample from the lumber camp is probably your best bet to tracking him down.

Vadin'ya is certain that the poison came from a rare plant called a Chokemist, which only grows in a particular area within Samarach. She suggests that you investigate the caves between the shipwreck and the Lumber Camp - that the saboteur is likely hiding out near there.
You tracked down Luaire the saboteur and dealt with him.

The mechanic at the Lantanese Lumber Camp is distressed - her clockroaches have all escaped, and she's worried about the damage they might do to the area. She'd like you to track down and destroy at least 4 of them, and bring back their parts.
You've managed to destroy - and collect the parts to - 4 clockroaches. The mechanic back at the Lantanese Lumber Camp would probably be relieved to see your progress.
The mechanic accepted the ruins of her 4 clockroaches, and rewarded you for your time.
Volo would like a fragment from a ruin in the Samarlogh, the lands north of Samargol. There might be something you could acquire from one of the denizens of the jungle.
The leaders of the merchant cartels have left for the Conyberry tavern, where the meeting is to occur. Meet them there when you are prepared.
You triggered the alarm, and the entire Temple of the World Serpent is now on the alert for intruders. New arrivals - such as yourself - are likely to be killed on sight.
{M, Simple, L13}Crossroad Keep - Steadfast Resolve

Maxil has tasked you with defeating the the young red dragon, Sintalpandax, whose lair is somewhere to the north near Mount Hotenow. Performing this deed will complete your Steadfast Resolve training.
With the defeat of Sintalpandax, you've completed your Steadfast Resolve teamwork benefit training.
{M, Simple, L11}Crossroad Keep - Foe Hunting

To complete your Foe Hunting training, Candril has tasked you with eliminating some of her hated enemies - umber hulks. A group can be found in a cave in the foothills near Leilon, to the southwest of Crossroad Keep.
You defeated all the umber hulks and completed your Foe Hunting training.
{M, Simple, L8}Crossroad Keep - Group Trance

To complete your Group Trance training, Candril has sent you on a pilgrimage to meditate near the ruins of an elven holy place. The ancient tower can be found to the northeast of Crossroad Keep, in the woods south of Conyberry.
You meditated at the ancient elven tower as Candril requested and have completed your Group Trance training.
{M, Simple, L8}Crossroad Keep - Missile Volley

To complete your training in Missile Volley, Candril asks you to put her lessons to the test by destroying a golem in a ruined keep east of Thundertree. Battling the golem with ranged weapony is recommended.
You defeated the strange golem and completed your training in Missile Volley.
{M, Simple, L8}Crossroad Keep - Circle of Blades

To complete your training in Circle of Blades, Juen has requested that you defeat an evil Necromancer who, among his many misdeeds, shamed Juen in a duel. Juen has tracked him down to an ancient Illefarn outpost in the Sword Mountains. She's also warned you that the Necromancer likes to keep his foes at a distance - and recommends that you not allow him to do so.
You have defeated the Necromancer and have completed your training in Circle of Blades.
{M, Simple, L09}Crossroad Keep - Awareness

You've been invited to play a game of hide-and-seek with three of Juen's friends to complete your Awareness training at a house south of Highcliff. You are the seeker, and you must locate all of Juen's friends to win the game.
You won the game of hide-and-seek and completed your Awareness training.
{M, Simple, L10}Crossroad Keep - Improved Camp Routine
To complete your training in Improved Camp Routine, Maxil has tasked you with setting up camp in the haunted Circle of the Mere, located in the Mere of Dead Men south of Crossroad Keep.
You completed your training in Improved Camp Routine, and the ghosts who attacked your camp were foiled in their attempt to drag you to a watery grave while you slept.
{M, Simple, L5}Crossroad Keep - Camp Routine
Maxil has sent you to inspect the remains of a destroyed camp located southwest of Neverwinter to complete your Camp Routine training.
You've completed your Camp Routine training, having witnessed the price for complacent or incompetent camp practices in the unforgiving wilderness.
{M, Simple, L11}Crossroad Keep - Team Rush

To complete your Team Rush training, Daerred has asked you to eliminate a very old, very deadly goblin near Mt. Hotenow, who despite his decrepit state has managed to prey upon slow-moving or slow-witted adventurers.
You have defeated the slow-moving goblin and completed your Team Rush training.
{M, Simple, L9}Crossroad Keep - Superior Flank

To complete your training in Superior Flank, Juen has asked you to deal with some of her old enemies who have also mastered the tactic. These assassins are located in an old graveyard just north of Neverwinter.
You dealt with the assassins and completed your training in Superior Flank.
{U, Simple, L05}Samarach - The Lady's Apprentice

Sa'Sani, pleased with your progress, has decided to give you the opportunity to participate within her company as a merchant. Any of her ore that you recover can be sold to the towns within Samarach, and the trade bars earned from these sales can be returned to Osi in Samargol. Osi will reward you with a dividend in gold whenever you return trade bars to him.
In addition, she is allowing you to use any of her ore that you recover to craft whatever weapons or armor you need to continue in your work for her.

You have completed your first assignment as a merchant, being paid for the trade bars you delivered to Osi. Should you wish to earn more, you can continue selling any Ore you find to the towns of Samarach, and then turning in the trade bars from those sales to Osi to earn gold. You may also use any Ore you recover to craft weapons or armor.

One of the most useful items in an adventurer's arsenal, the Bag of Holding is said to actually open into a pocket dimension in which the user can freely deposit a large amount of items without fear of weighing themselves down overmuch. It has been the dream of more than one larcenous spellcaster to find a way into a proposed plane to raid all of these pocket dimensions at once - but as your belongings are still safe, it's safe to assume such a plane has not yet been discovered.

However, he seemed to constantly forget he'd created a set, and continued crafting more. He was hardly happy when he figured out his error, but reasoned it was always nice to have spares.

Riftcleaver

Whether the gold dwarves that created this axe meant to imply that this weapon was strong enough to have created the Great Rift or simply that it was crafted there is unknown. What is certain is that this axe provides power where it is needed, and is useful to anyone who wields it.
Trollblood Axe

Once a simple stone axe, this weapon has been magically enhanced with the blood of trolls. Although the dark rites bind the trolls' regenerative properties into the weapon, they also include a dose of their weaknesses as well.

This mask is carefully crafted by greenish clay, stuck through with feathers and fronds.
Jungle Headdress
Enchanted by a batiri shaman for the younger and more daring members of the tribe, this mask is said to whisper the ways of the wild in its user's ears, aiding in their treks through the wilderness.

Shederran trees are only known to grow in Neverwinter Wood. Among the largest in FaerÃ»n, their wood is supple but strong, and is used in the crafting of high-quality items by Neverwintan craftsmen. The strength of the wood in this crossbow causes its bolts to fly faster and truer - making them trickier for their intended target to dodge.
This kama seems to make you feel stronger - and more impulsive - as you clutch it.
Brutal Bite

The son of an accomplished blacksmith, Noshu Kellarn turned his back on his family's business to try and become a monk of Tempus. Though he insisted to his relatives that he was doing well in his pursuit, slender Noshu was actually failing in his training. To help him save face, his older sister crafted him this weapon, designed to make him appear stronger, more ruthless. It had the unfortunate side effect of lowering his ability to concentrate somewhat, but earned him the grudging respect of his peers as they saw the results of his fighting prowess.
This weapon seems to sharpen your senses - making you aware of anything sinster around you.
Snakeblood Slayer

Forged long ago by a devoted servant of Lathander, this weapon is purely meant to hunt yuan-ti "and eradicate their darkness with pure, holy light." Any time its powers have been used contrary to the Morninglord's aim, it is not long until the weapon mysteriously disappears. But because the motives of those who go in for the large-scale killing of any particular species are hardly pure - no matter how cruel or underhanded they may be - it is rare that this kama remains in any one person's hands for long.
A powerfully-shaped kama, unusually light.
Ubtao's Tooth
Said to be shaped from the fang of a megaraptor sacred to Ubtao, King of the Dinosaurs, this kama grants its user additional swiftness and strength.
Healthful Edge

Though it isn't the best for those intending to inflict great amounts of damage in battle, the invigorating enchantments on this kukri make them an excellent choice for those planning to hang back from the thick of the fray.
Serrated Fang

Often used by thugs and devotees in the cults of Cyric and Loviatar, this weapon's ability doesn't guarantee the victim a swift death, but shreds wounds, making it difficult for them to heal. The agonizing pain often makes captives all the more willing to confess to any number of crimes.
Skinning Blade

Some blame this kukri's creation on devotees of Malar, as evidence of his rapacious bloodlust - others on clerics of Silvanus, saying it is only meant to kill those creatures corrupted by vile forces. Whoever is responsible for this weapon, it bears powers to deal great harm to magic and normal beasts alike.

Harvested only from Neverwinter Wood, the pale, greenish wood of Shederran is prized by craftsmen seeking to make the highest quality of bows and crossbows. The tensile properties of shederran allows the user to exert their full power on the bow, adding their own strength to it.
This strange shield seems crafted from a large shell.
Batiri Buckler

Created from the overlapped shells of giant jungle beetles and slashed with the warpaint of the batiri, this shield is lightweight, easy to carry, and allows for easy casting while using it. However, the downside of this shield is that the bug's organic components make it vulnerable to flame, and thus endanger the wearer slightly as well.
Nondushiran Amulet
Passed down in the Nondushir family for generations, this amulet is said to grant extra health and well-being to its wearers.
This is a slender, gleaming wand used in connection with finding and recording arcane nexuses.
Quilt of Silence

Though it doesn't offer the most optimal protection, this padded armor seems designed with the thief-about-town in mind - with it, one's footfalls sound more silently, one's hands are more deft, and even when caught - a handy spell aids in one's getaway. Which after gifted spellcaster created this armor, one imagines they asked to be paid in advance... and warded themselves well against the user arriving to steal their money back.

Samarachan Patrol Gear

Worn by the guards of Samarach, this armor is mostly composed of stiff leather plates with a thin - mostly cosmetic - veneer of brass. Extensive magic use in the nation has resulted in this armor being granted the ability for mages to wear it and cast spells without ill effects.
Spidersilk Jerkin

This mysterious armor is crafted from drider silk - and though harvesting such a substance is a dangerous prospect, the results seem well worth it. Though this jerkin protects the wearer like a suit of masterwork studded leather armor, it is light and airy, allowing the user to move and cast almost as if they were wearing only normal clothing.
Flameblessed

Only a few swords of this type were made - a gift from a high-ranking (and very corrupt) Calimshite official to his most loyal guards. These blades made short work of all the official's foes... until he crossed a sorceress with an extensive knowledge of cold spells, and discovered to his horror the downside of relying on a single line of defense.
Tohn-Beh-Ri's Dagger
Lute of Charming
The haunting melodies of this instrument can cause the most rapacious enemy to pause in their tracks a moment, their actions arrested by the irresistable allure of the music.

This is a distilled form of the toxin drawn from the dead artificer at the Lantanese Lumber Camp... you don't know how it was distilled, or from where, and you believe you're very likely better off never asking.

Yes, thank you, Master Volo. ...Captain Dajos {DAH-johs} - we meet again. What brings you to this Mercantile House today?
An order from the Council - it seems you've had rather troubling luck with your employees of late. I hear reports that one of them sabotaged your ship... and might have had dealings with the yuan-ti.

That employee was summarily dismissed shortly after the shipwreck - I filed the paperwork with the Mercantile Affairs Committee. And if you should insinuate that I and my company have anything to do with the snake-folk -

Your authority over me is no longer recognized, Sa'Sani. In fact, by order of the Council, you are to leave Samargol immediately while this matter is investigated, and care of your merchant company is to be remanded to your highest-ranking inferior - in this case, the resident Osi Tchaluka.
No - Lady Sa'Sani, I -
Osi - be at ease. I should be glad to have you run the company in my - temporary absence.

Silence, foreigner - you are not the law here. I have that privilege.

Goodbye, my little pigeon...
Mostly I'd just like to get your observations on a few areas - the lay of the land, you see - but occasionally I might have a particular task in mind for you, if you're up for it.
Should you wish to acquire any tasks to aid me, just stop by. As I learn more of this place, I shall assuredly wish to investigate more of its wonders!
Most excellent! I look forward to our collaboration.
Most excellent! Tell me all about it, and I shall take notes!
Gods above - how chilling! And how marvelous - an excellent travel destination for those looking to visit the more unconventional markets of the Shining South. Well done!

Incredible! Not only does the danger lie in the yuan-ti, but in any patrols that might have seen you exiting such an area... surely they would attack on the mere suspicion that you were allied with the snake-folk!

Remarkable! The batiri are savage creatures, yes - I know that firsthand - but they possess a matriarchal culture that is nothing short of fascinating. I hear the Shattered Spear have dealt with humans before... perhaps they will tolerate tourists, if they behave themselves...
Tyr's Beard! Although... perhaps that might draw a different crowd into the area, eager for action instead of a quiet tour of the salt mines. I'll make another note of it...

Magic gone wild! Exceedingly dangerous... but not the first time I've seen it, sadly. Although it does seem to draw its own peculiar crowd of admirers and gawkers. Swamp is a downside, but I'll call it... a "fen," yes. Sounds nicer.
Ah - the tribe from the beach, is that not so? Well - I think I can speak with authority regarding their downfall. A tragic tale of hubris, and the cave as the spot where it all ended? Excellent...
Interesting! Not so much with the spiders... but perhaps it will hold a particular interest with druids... indeed!
Dangerous... but with proper warning, potentially a great draw to the curious. A tale of evil brought to its end, tracked to a corner and defeated in combat - that always draws a crowd!

Most fortunate! Believe it or not, crypts and mausoleums and the like have their own sort of audience - Kelemvorites looking to make sure no undead are there, historians wishing to study them, and, of course... the perpetually moody looking for a handy place to lurk.

Kobolds? Most peculiar! I wonder if they are a native species to the area, or a lost tribe that somehow found its way there from the northern reaches of Toril! It shall be noted - mayhaps a cunning scholar might be able to divine an answer... or a grant from their educational institution claiming they are searching for one. Ha!
Lizardfolk on the coast? Not their usual habitat, I don't think. Perhaps they can be negotiated with... maybe even act as guides to see these strange lobster-men or sea monsters I've heard of!
Most curious... like this very city, Samarach seems to keep much of its history shrouded in secrecy. It may be some enterprising adventurers might be eager to get to the bottom of such mysteries!

Ancient towers are dangerous things... and quite a draw for the curious! On their own they are enough to marvel at, but for those wishing to see what may be hidden beyond the occasional creature infestation... it is a worthwhile note indeed!

Excellent! If he's still alive, he's an excellent mark for enterprising adventurers or bored young nobles to hunt... and if he's taken care of, the cave can be listed as a charming place for a romantic tryst. Well done!
Ugh, foul things... but if the mine isn't spoken for, rest assured there will be someone keen on acquiring it! As it stands - it's definitely a worthy footnote for my book!

Nas'Sirin is dead, apparently at Sa'Sani's hands. Sa'Sani herself has fled - or escaped - through the portal back to Samarach. Speak with Orias to arrange for teleportation back to Samarach.
You've returned to Samarach, ready to pursue Sa'Sani, wherever she may have gone.
You convinced Nall and his mercenaries to change their minds. They've decided to help train the Greycloaks after all. Khelgar will be pleased to hear about this new development.
{M, Simple, L10}Crossroad Keep - Missing Associates

Sa'Sani wants you to travel north to Neverwinter and meet with representatives of the Circle of Friends, the Forgotten Lords, or the Fated Winds to seek out information on her missing associates. These associates were responsible for the trading company that was supposed to operate out of Crossroad Keep, but they disappeared, leaving the work incomplete.

You joined the Circle of Friends, and Jon Archen told you that the last time Sa'Sani's associates were seen, they were meeting with Jordan Wright, head of the Fated Winds company. Speak with Wright and find out what he knows.

You joined the Forgotten Lords, and Aster Meriss told you that the last time Sa'Sani's associates were seen, they were meeting with Jordan Wright, head of the Fated Winds company. Speak with Wright and find out what he knows.

You joined the Fated Winds, and Martin Keller told you that the last time Sa'Sani's associates were seen, they were meeting with Jordan Wright, head of the Fated Winds company. Speak with Wright and find out what he knows.
When asked about Sa'Sani's associates, Jordan Wright was evasive and refused to give you any direct answers. Return to Sa'Sani in Crossroad Keep to find out what she wants to do next.
Sa'Sani wants to continue to build up your status within your allied merchant faction in the hopes of eventually uncovering the truth of Wright's involvement with the disappearance of her associates.
Jordan Wright is dead by his own hand, but his involvement with the yuan-ti and the Snaketongue cultists is clear. Return to Sa'Sani and inform her of these new developments.

Sa'Sani has finally received word from her long-lost associates, and given recent events, suspects that it is no coicidence and a trap. You are to go in her stead to the Night's Rest inn, located to the east along the road to Phandalin.
You've located Sa'Sani's missing associates at long last, but as she suspected, the meeting was a trap - her associates were also Zehir worshippers eager to add you to their list of victims.
You have turned in enough Trade Bars to Osi that Sa'Sani has given you a special reward. You can still collect Ore to earn more gold or to craft weapons and armor.
{M, Simple, L06}Crossroad Keep - Sword Coast Trader
Sa'Sani wants you to establish a trading post at one of the towns adjacent to Crossroad Keep - Highcliff, Thundertree, Leilon, Phandalin, or Neverwinter itself.
You've established a trading post as Sa'Sani requested. Return to her to get instructions for the next step.
Now that you've got a trading post established, Sa'Sani wants you to set up a caravan between Crossroad Keep and the trading post.

You set up a caravan route between Crossroad Keep and your trading post. You've done what Sa'Sani asked, but you're free to continue expanding her operation by building additional trading posts and caravan routes in the other towns in the region.

You met with the bandit leader and discovered that the bandits are being organized by an association known only as the Snaketongues. Return to Volo at Crossroad Keep with this information.

One of Many is many evils in one - its consciousness composed of a multitude of murderers, lunatics, and other human detritus, all driven to insanity by imprisonment in Death God's Vault in life and then decades of disembodied misery in the Vault's crematorium. As such, One of Many is malice personified and wishes to either feed on or do violence to all sentient beings.

:: It is a weak morsel. Of these souls would take exactly eleven to satisfy our hunger. ::
[Before you is a being that radiates incredible power, and malice. It regards you balefully, but does not move.]
[The strange being extends what you believe to be its arms toward you, as if attempting to grasp onto you.]
:: So the morsel returns. Come close, morsel. Closer... ::
:: A thousand tortured souls are bound up in this shell. I am their voice. I am One of Many. ::
:: The morsel smacks its meat flaps together and speaks to us of hunger. Yes, we are starving! ::
:: Useless morsel. Had we met in spirit-rich Rashemen we would slay you and leave your corpse to rot, undevoured! ::
:: We sought new feeding grounds. Rashemen grew too wary of us. No longer able to hunt in shadows, no longer under the Master's protection. ::
:: Hau, hau, hau! A morsel wishes to know the Master, but the less it knows, the better for it. The Master is the only being on FaerÃ»n more terrible than us! ::
:: Sho'nuff! ::
:: There is much life here, but weak morsels all! And the morsels all stay far enough away that we cannot feed. ::
:: Would the morsel help feed us? Then it may throw itself into our maw, or give us its cohort morsels. ::
:: The morsel would help feed us? Then it may throw itself into our maw. Or bring other morsels, by trickery or force to sacrifice to us! ::
:: Feed us, and we can give great, dark power! ::
| One cohort devoured |:: Ah, small morsel. It whets our appetite for more! ::
:: Our strength is not yet restored enough to leave this place. Give us more! ::
:: If only this insolent morsel, would come closer. It, too, could wet our maw with its gamey lifeblood, however briefly... ::
| 2 cohorts devoured |:: We must choke it down. However poor tasting, it will sustain us! ::
| 3 cohorts devoured |:: A beggars feast, but we will take it. ::
| 4 cohorts devoured |:: Blech! Foul morsel, its dirty feet feebly kick at us! ::
| 5 cohorts devoured |:: What we would not give to sink our teeth into an Uthraki, or a Night Hag... ::
| 6 cohorts devoured |:: Little by little by little, our strength returns. ::
| 7 cohorts devoured |:: Though at first revolting, we begin to savor these morsels ::
| 8 cohorts devoured |:: Juicy sweet morsel! It gets in our belly! ::
| 9 cohorts devoured |:: Were we not starving, we'd never have acquired such a taste for these lesser morsels. ::
| 10 cohorts devoured |:: Nearly enough, nearly enough. One more morsel should replenish us! ::
| 11 cohorts devoured |:: Yes. Yes! That does it. One last bite and then... ::
:: Our strength is restored! And we must thank this morsel for bringing so much sustenance. ::
:: Is it certain? We would bestow our greatest gift. Eternal and everlasting power can be had if it wishes! ::
:: Then it prepares to receive our gift. It will join the Many, and become one of us! ::
:: So be it. We leave this place in search of meatier prey. ::
[One of Many regards you expectantly.]
:: Has it brought more morsels to sustain us? ::
[Parley.]
[Leave.]

Second Entry: Jerrod's gone - something from the water took him down in a flash before he could scream. Nothing but blood and bubbles came up. Third Entry: I saw Jerrod tonight. He was standing on the water, looking pale and bloated like a drowned man. He called out to me, begging to me to join him. I made the signs against evil, but he refused to go away. Fourth Entry: I tried to return to Rassatan today, but Jerrod's always there, on the water. Why won't he leave me alone? Final Entry: I'm going to make a run for it. I won't let him catch me. And so, dear readers, here ends my tale - of sinister plots, heroism, and sacrifice!

Fear not, my good readers - as my name is Volothamp Geddarm, I would not leave you in the lurch. Though I am not an historian by occupation, I am a tireless investigator, and I here present what I was able to uncover...
|SAMARACH LOW|Though it played host to us for a time, by all accounts, Samarach remains unchanged... however, my sources whisper that certain high-ranking officials have fallen under yuan-ti control.
More troubling still is the uncertainty of whether the yuan-ti in question still bear fealty to their ancient god, Sseth... or worship the vile interloper Zehir.

|SAMARACH HIGH|From what I've heard, it seems Samarach is experiencing a renewal of sorts - relaxing some of their more stringent requirements for entry and becoming slightly less offensive to foreigners.

Though I would love to claim credit for this, I must admit that it should go to the adventuring party, who went out of their way to aid the nation... and thus perhaps won some grudging thanks from them.
| PL VISITED |Now, as for the fate of the beleaguered Port Llast...
| WH VISITED |But what of the tiny village of West Harbor, the childhood home of the great Knight-Captain?

| WH - DRAGONS |The humble village of West Harbor remained under the control of the dragon brothers for a time, producing Dragon Mead. Eventually, a number of the villagers rose up in defiance, sacrificing themselves to allow others to escape.

After this, the dragons had no one to make them mead - and thus returned to the swamp. Sadly, without anyone to inhabit it, West Harbor fell into disrepair... and was swallowed up by the Mere of Dead Men.

| WH - CULT + LAZLO |Though West Harbor was saved from the dragon twins, it sadly fell under the influence of a nearby cult. Though Chauntean clerics acted quickly to destroy it, the cult claimed the lives of Jan Buckman and other Harbormen.
Consumed with grief, Jan's father Lazlo vanished into the swamp... and the poor village of West Harbor eventually followed him, reclaimed by the wilds of the Mere of Dead Men.

| WH - CULT |Though saved from the dragons, West Harbor struggled over the deaths of its key citizens - and soon fell under the sway of a dark cult. Eventually, the cult was destroyed... wiping out West Harbor in the process.
Emptied of life, the hamlet of West Harbor vanished into the Mere of Dead Men... for a final time.
| WH - ARUNA DEAD |Though saved from the vile dragon twins, West Harbor soon fell under the influence of a dark cult. With no voice of reason to speak against it, the whole village joined.
Soon, Chauntean clerics came to stop the cult... and in the battle, all Harbormen were slain. Emptied of life, the hamlet of West Harbor vanished into the Mere of Dead Men... for a final time.

| WH - NO CULT OR JAN |Suffering from the loss of two of its prominent citizens, West Harbor looked to new leadership. It found it within the wise, calm hands of Goodwife Aruna, who took on the mantle of mayor of the small hamlet.
Under her leadership, West Harbor has managed to prosper, and advance its reputation as a crafter of the choiciest mead in northern Faerun.

| WH - NO CULT + JAN |Safe at last, West Harbor began to grow and prosper. Jan continued to study magic, and with the combined efforts of Lazlo Buckman and Goodwife Aruna, the village became an excellent trading stop for merchants.
Today, West Harbor is known as the hidden jewel in the Mere of Dead Men, and its Harvest Mead is known as the highest-quality mead in all of northern Faerun.

| STORMS |Without any divine forces to still their wrath, the unnatural storms that raged around Port Llast grew steadily worse... until an unnamed pirate slew a nearby priestess of Umberlee, ceasing the raging malestroms.

Grateful at the the pirate's contribution, the folk of Port Llast took a break from their rebuilding efforts to grant the man a trim sailing vessel... which he of course used to plunder the Sea of Swords - much to Lord Nasher's vexation.

| NO STORMS, NO PRIORESS |Though the brave adventurers stopped the storms ravaging Port Llast, such action was not without cost. The goddess Umberlee must know of the death of her priestess... and will one day likely take her revenge.

| NO STORMS |With the raging storms in the area put to rest, Port Llast was able to repair itself and resume sea trade, slowly growing in size as it capitalized on the import of Knucklehead Ivory from Icewind Dale.

| ARMY OF THE DEAD |Though it has been some time past now, the folk of Port Llast still talk about the army of undead that liberated their town, and tales and songs of the incident have become popular throughout the Sword Coast.
...Except, of course, in Luskan - but that's to be expected.
| LUSKANS DEAD |With Port Llast free of Luskan invaders, Neverwintan forces acted quickly to re-secure the town, and Lord Nasher himself called the liberation of the town "a hero's deed."

| LUSKANS ALIVE |With Port Llast solidly under their control, the Luskans soon fortified their position in the town, building additional garrisons... and causing rumors to spawn about their eventual attack on Neverwinter City itself.

| NYA ALIVE |Her days of necromancy behind her, Nya returned to Port Llast, reopening her magic store. Before long, she became known as one of the best resources for magical items in the northern Sword Coast.
| NYA DEAD |Though she succumbed to madness, the news of what Nya had attempted to do reached the ears of many in Port Llast, and there are those who still honor her memory because of it.
| MERCHANT MAX |And what of the merchant factions of Neverwinter City? Fear not - their progress is marked as well.

| FW |Thanks to the diligent aid of the adventurers, the Fated Winds were able to spread their power and influence throughout the Sword Coast region... eventually growing to control all trade in and out of Neverwinter.

| FL |With the assistance of the brave adventurers, the power of the Forgotten Lords expanded tremendously, making the Sword Coast branch one of the most successful in the Realms. For her capable service, Aster Merris was promoted to be the new leader of the organization.

| CoF |Due to the hard work of the adventurers, the Circle of Friends prospered, swiftly becoming the largest trading organization within Neverwinter. Thanks to their charitable efforts, the city began to renew itself, and battle against poverty.
| COHORTS |As for those souls who lent their aid - they, too, have not been forgotten.

| BELUETH - FW |Belueth the Calm returned to Neverwinter, and eventually relinquished her status as a freelance blade-for-hire to become a permanent member of the Fated Winds... and eventually, Martin Keller's personal bodyguard.

Though the peace that has settled on the region has made it so her more deadly skills are less needed, it doesn't seem Belueth is unhappy at this - there are those who claim to have caught her in a moment of ease, a soft smile on her face.

| BELUETH - NO FW |After the events at the Temple of the World Serpent, Belueth's rage at the cults of Zehir seemed to intensify ever greater - as if she piled all the hate and anger in her heart at the feet of the god and his minions.

Eventually the young woman disappeared from Neverwinter... though cultists tell tales of a yellow-haired woman who appears out of nowhere, slaughters their people by the dozens, and vanishes into the night like a ghost.

| CHIR |Chir Darkflame decided not to return to the Underdark, and instead wander the world in search of magical knowledge. Though she stayed for a time in the Thayan Enclave in Neverwinter, she was soon thrown out because of some unforgivable act.

My sources say she then wandered north to Luskan - and rumors speak of a sweet but terrifying little svirfneblin wizard who is teaching the Hosttower mages new and horrifying things to do to their enemies...
| FINCH |Finch the bard used his experiences in the employ of the merchant company to create a few promotional songs for the Church of Waukeen, for which he was paid handsomely.
With his earnings, the handsome bard bid a farewell to the Sword Coast once more, and claimed there was far more of the world he needed to see before he was ready to cede his soul to Sune.
The last anyone saw of him, Finch was boarding a ship bound for the distant land of Calimshan... and already wooing a lovely young noblewoman on board.
| GRYKK |Grykk Bannersworn returned to his order with tales of the deeds he performed and the things he had seen - and was honored with a full title of Divine Champion by his superiors.

Though he was offered the command of a dozen soldiers, Grykk politely declined, voicing his intent to see more of the world and learn of its ways... and personally hunt down the worshippers of dread Zehir, and bring them to justice.

| INSHULA |Though almost endlessly impressed with the powerful creatures available to hunt on the Sword Coast, Inshula sar Mashewe eventually began to miss her older sister Kwesi, and became homesick for her distant home of Tashalar.

Carrying many impressive trophies of their hunts, Inshula and her sister returned home to Tashalar. In the chaos that followed the fall of House Se'Sehen, they worked tirelessly to keep their home city safe, and remain as its guardians still.

| LASTRI - PRIORESS DEAD |Worried that the goddess Umberlee might take revenge on her for travelling with a group that killed one of her priestesses, Lastri Kassireh reluctantly gave up on her career as a sailor, and decided to become a wandering sellsword.

However, a chance encounter with another wandering swordswoman on the road led to a recommendation of her selling her services to Neverwinter, and before long, Lastri climbed the ranks to become a Captain of the Neverwinter City Watch.
Though it is not the ship on which she always dreamed she'd live out her days, Lastri nonetheless seems happy in her new job, and bears numerous decorations for bravery and skill.
| LASTRI |With her revenge on the party responsible for wrecking her beloved ship, the Vigilant, Lastri Kassireh quickly returned to her true love - the sea.

Borrowing a sum from the merchant company (as an investment, of course) Lastri purchased a trim little galleon she named the Serpent's Bane - and once more sailed the waters of Toril, an excellent captain with a capable crew.
| QUARREL |Though he stayed at Crossroad Keep for quite some time - "learning patience" and growing in power - Quarrel was unable to cool his heels in one location for long.

When a story reached his ears hinting that his hero, Ammon Jerro, was rumored to be somewhere in the far east of the Realms, the young half-drow packed his things at a moment's notice, and set off eastward - in his wild eyes an unwavering determination to reach the far-distant realm of Thay.

| RIBSMASHER |Regrettably, the fate of the mad monk known only as "Ribsmasher" remains somewhat of a mystery. Shortly after the events at the Temple of the World Serpent, he vanished from Crossroad Keep during the night, bound for parts unknown.
The Greycloaks who saw him run out of the entrance of the Keep claim they only heard his jubilant bellow of "finding new ribs to smash" before he vanished into the night.

| SEPTIMUND - DIDN'T JOIN |With the situation at Port Llast resolved to the satisfaction of his superiors, solemn young Septimund returned to the safety of his brotherhood, resolutely following the decree of Kelemvor to the end.

| SEPTIMUND - NYA DEAD |Though Septimund shortly thereafter returned to his fellows at the temple, the death of Nya - and the thought that his inaction might lead to some additional disaster - harassed his thoughts constantly.

Though the few sightings I could gather thereafter described the young man as haggard, Septimund earned himself a reputation as one of Kelemvor's most dedicated Doomguides - relentlessly eliminating any undead he could find.

| SEPTIMUND - NYA LIVES |With the death of the Herald of Zehir, Septimund bid his companions farewell to return to the temple of Kelemvor. On his way, he was moved to stop by Port Llast, where a confident, changed Nya greeted him.

Slowly, the two began to reconnect, and once more, a friendship bloomed between them. Though Septimund returned to the temple, he and Nya still write one another... and he returns to Port Llast - often - to be by her side.

| SORAEVORA |The loyal servant of Angarradh, Soraevora Aeravand, remained with the adventuring party until shortly after their return to Crossroad Keep, stating that it did not seem a complete journey to her until she walked within the Keep's walls once more.

Her mission accomplished, the ancient elf reported shortly that her goddess had given her leave to return home, and so she set off alone into the wilderness - as she began - on the long journey back to Evermeet.

| UMOJA |Though greatly pleased with the unexpected directions his journey through the Maze had taken him, Umoja bore a great concern within him about how the appearance of the god Zehir might affect his people back in the Chultan city of Mezro.
Bidding their friends at Crossroad Keep farewell, the druid and his dinosaur companion returned to their home, eager to protect the people of Chult from the subtle evil of the yuan-ti.
|ZARL |Never entirely certain that he wasn't secretly being tracked by agents of the Red Wizards, Zarl nonetheless grew attached to the Sword Coast, and became fond of the mercenary life.

And though many were at first wary of the idea of hiring a massive Thayan gnoll, word of his skill soon surpassed warnings about his annoying nature, and the loud "supergnoll" was able to make a comfortable living doing what he did best - killing things.
| ECONOMY & SA'SANI |But most importantly... what of the fate of the Sword Coast, and the beautiful merchant leader, Sa'Sani?
| SA'SANI DEAD |After the fall of clan Se'Sehen and the tragic death of the Sauringar princess, yuan-ti throughout the Realms were thrown into confusion.
Dozens of long-slumbering yuan-ti plots were sprung throughout Toril, causing countries such as Thindol to fly into a panic and start massive, catastrophic purges within their populace.

At Crossroad Keep, the ownership of the merchant company Sa'Sani once led became a hotly disputed topic, and the matter was eventually settled by placing ownership in the hands of the adventurers who had nobly defeated the Herald and stopped the dire plot of Zehir.

| ECONOMY WEAK, S DEAD |Despite the valiant efforts of the adventurers, the merchant company found itself adrift after Sa'Sani's tragic death, and the organization soon fell apart, leaving Crossroad Keep an abandoned husk.
Unable to recover economically, Neverwinter lost much of its territory to larger powers in the area, like Luskan and Waterdeep.

| ECONOMY MOD, S DEAD |After Sa'Sani's death, the merchant company did its valiant best to aid Neverwinter in its economic struggle, assisting it through a long recovery that left the city stable, but not at the heights of power and influence it had previously possessed.
Though Neverwinter remained politically strong, much of its power was unfortunately ceded to neighboring powers, such as Luskan and Waterdeep.

| ECONOMY GOOD, S DEAD |Thanks to the tireless work and great strides made by the merchant company, Neverwinter used their economic momentum to aid in recovering from the War of Shadows - even without Sa'Sani's powerful business savvy.

Regaining much of the power and influence it had lost, Neverwinter was once more able to stand on its own in the political arena, tempering both outside influences and the ambitious aggression of Luskan.
| ECONOMY WEAK, S ALIVE |Previous to the epic battle with the Herald of Zehir, the merchant company had made slow strides in improving the economic status of the Sword Coast.
After the conflict, Sa'Sani contracted with the adventuring group as enforcers for a time, protecting her caravans and aiding the company in other ways before their eventual parting of the ways.

| ECONOMY MOD, S ALIVE |Greatly pleased with the progress they had made with growing her company and restoring economic prosperity to the Sword Coast, Sa'Sani invited the adventuring group to stay on as valued investors.
With their assistance, operations ran smoother than they ever had before, speeding along Neverwinter's economic recovery.

| ECONOMY STRONG, S ALIVE |Because of the adventuring group's dedicated work into improving the economy of the Sword Coast and the massive economic strides made by Neverwinter thanks to their efforts, Sa'Sani promoted the members of the group to be the company's co-owners.

Together, they utilized the merchant company's powers to restore Neverwinter's splendor, growing it into an economic powerhouse - with its heart located in the now-massive structure of Crossroad Keep.

| NO PROMISE |After the vanquishment of the Se'Sehen, Sa'Sani abdicated leadership within the Sauringar clan to return to Crossroad Keep, resuming her work restoring the economic prosperity of the Sword Coast.

| PROMISE |After the vanquishment of the Se'Sehen, Sa'Sani abdicated leadership within the Sauringar clan to return to Crossroad Keep, resuming her noble work restoring the economic prosperity of the Sword Coast.

Though her policies delivered consistently positive results and her company prospered, many of Sa'Sani's decisions were regarded as harsh or unforgiving... and those unfortunate enough to get in the way of her plans had a tragic habit of disappearing.

All the same, she aided Neverwinter in regaining great amounts of power and influence... and none suspected that the yuan-ti of House Sauringar had effectively become the new rulers of the Sword Coast.
True to her word, the elegant Sa'Sani introduced many innovative initiatives to bring wealth and prosperity to the region - but never at the cost of lives or livelihood.

She became known as an intelligent and fair businesswoman - and after a time, even her enforced promise of harming no-one ceased to chafe her, and she appeared to be almost comfortable within human society.
| END |This concludes my tale, dear readers. Though I know not when or how it may be read, one persistent concern still remains in my mind that I must share with you.

These events - though seeming separate - have appeared to me to be more closely intertwined than I had previously imagined each time that I think on them, and a grave chill freezes my bones when I do so.
I hope here to report to the world the bravery of the heroes who faced down and defeated the Herald of Zehir, and enter such into legend... that such legends exist to inspire us in the days ahead.
So reader - I stand by my fear that something dreadful is coming... perhaps something that shall change the face of the Realms forever.
I can only hope that brave heroes - like the ones that I was privileged to journey with - can step from obscurity and face the darkness when it arises.
(And to my friend, the esteemed Elminster - if this book sells well, I'm going to publish my work about nymphs in Samarach. I have an interested buyer!)
With flourish, Volothamp Geddarm, Historian and traveller of Faerun.
THE END
For those who aided the heroes along the way - their tales lie within these pages, never to be undone. Let us not forget the power of their deeds and words!
But what, you may ask, happened after the fall of Zehir's dread Herald? What was the future of all the lives that were touched - or undone - by such events?

|PRE SWORD COAST|Though they came from auspicious beginnings and survived one of the most chaotic battles which I have ever been a part of, regrettably, the adventurers I met aboard the Vigilant did not venture much further with their careers.

What became of them is a mystery - but luckily, a new group stepped to the fore... {emphasize this, as if implying the player's party is LAME}a powerful, heroic band who came from the most unlikely beginnings... and soon became legend.

|AT SWORD COAST|Soon after the journey to the Sword Coast, the brave adventurers that I had met aboard the Vigilant disappeared from note - probably pleased to be free from the restrictions of Samarach and able to wander at last.
None know what became of them, and it is with disappointment I close their chapter within this book.
|JOINED MERCHANT FACTION|Much to the perturbation of their merchant faction, the adventurers from the lovely Sa'Sani's company disappeared, slipping off to unknown locations.
Though this also angered the beautiful merchant leader, Sa'Sani was soon able to recruit the impressive abilities of a nearby merchant group.
|END STATE|Following Sa'Sani's disappearance from Crossroad Keep, a great shadow began to fall on the Sword Coast.
People spoke in hushed tones - the price of necessities rose to unaffordable heights - and cults and bandits began to ravage the countryside, growing in number with each day that passed.
Then the yuan-ti revealed themselves - and descended upon us.

There was no one left to fight back by then - the resources of Neverwinter had been depleted, the Knight-Captain was missing, and even the band that had braved the journey from Samarach to the Sword Coast was not there.
Carrying the banner of their new god Zehir, they swept over the Sword Coast in a wave, eliminating all who stood against them.

Now, dear reader, you likely know all this. Perhaps you know more than I do what happened to the band of adventurers at Crossroad Keep - all I know is that they vanished, and were never heard from again.
What I have left to tell you now - as I wait here in my cell, writing by the light of a stub candle and waiting my turn to be the next sacrifice to Zehir - is how it began...
P.S: Also, if you happen to find yourself in a yuan-ti prison, don't even bother to sample the food. It's terrible.
THE END
Once again, the brave band of Daerred, Candril, Juen and Maxil stepped forward to carry the torch of the Knight-Captain and come to the Sword Coast's aid.
Fatalists preached that the end of the world was nigh, and although most realists dismissed such a notion, they were forced to admit that something seemed wrong.

Tattered Journal

This is the journal of one Harrows Blastingway - a Luskan wizard heading back to the Hosttower. Most of the journal talks about his mundane travels through the Sword Coast, doing research concerning the King of Shadows and the battle that occurred outside of Crossroad Keep. One of his journal entries is bookmarked with a dog-eared page. "Here are two fine blade golem specimens. A find in this condition is quite rare in the field. I am truly lucky to come across these golems. I've heard tell that many golems used during the siege of Crossroad Keep required special wards to be used while handling them. Normally, a Protection from Evil spell would ward against a demon or powerful undead creature. Something similar to that, but different, might work in allowing me to interact with the golems."
Take this - your protection, as a stranger who need not have aided us, means more than my own devotion. May the All-Father smile on you today, friend - and days after.
Friends - let us return home - and celebrate another day of life with mead and song!
Kossuth burn their souls to ash! This is going to take some explaining to my superiors...
Ah - yes. I - I assure you, I have not forgotten the part you played in bringing them - ah - "under control." Yes.
Now is hardly the time for idiot jokes and frippery... but you did manage to save my hide, yes...
Ah - an accident! Could happen to anyone - please, can we not forget about this? I can compensate you!

Very well, then. ...As a merchant, you must be as good as your word - but be careful how you use it. There was a trade agreement I remember, some years ago...
...and he learned never to swear by his eye again - the one he had left, that is. May you remember that one - for the sake of your vision.
Tell me about being a merchant.
Can you tell me about being a merchant?
Sure - take this.
Never mind.
This slender woman regards you with a professional, businesslike nod.
This man seems strange... regarding everything around him with a kind of detached wonder.
This older man seems cross and preoccupied, his thoughts far elsewhere.
Well... I suppose I do not consider myself one as such, but as an enclave's focus is as a magical respository, I suppose that is much of what I do.

There is... a fair amount of distrust about my people - not that it isn't justified, but it can be hard to bear, particularly when my goal is purely to advance knowledge on the mysteries of the Art. Why, just the other day...

...you should have seen the look on his face when he was freed from the trap by Mugen - er, that's the gnoll outside - it was such shock and amazement I feared he would topple over on the spot! But... I do hope he had no hard feelings.
Tell me about being a merchant.
This older gentleman seems to be a high-ranking Red Wizard of Thay... making his kind expression all the more odd.
One of the leaders of the assault, this abomination is taller even than its hideous brethren.
Though you clearly recognize the woman before you as the one you knew from Samarach and Crossroad Keep, seeing her in her "true form" is still somewhat of a shock.
Sa'Sani Exit
The older adventurer looks both more excited and more solemn than you've ever seen him... the effect is somewhat unnerving.
This duergar spares you a single side glance, then harumphs and looks away.
This tall, gaunt humanoid has rough, yellow skin and russet hair pulled into a pair of topknots. Her eyes have a sinister gleam, and her ears are pointed and serrated in back.
This duergar regards you with cold cunning, ready to tear you apart.

This is the corpse of the yuan-ti that led the attack on the Viper Temple previously... he appears to have been sacrificed.

Well... it can be trying. Long hours out in the sun, deciding whether or not to stay open when it's raining... and then there are the customers. Why, I...
...but I suppose it's nice to know I've helped people who need it. I do enjoy that.
Unfortunately, I will lose control of the lesser undead throughout the cemetery. It is imperative you dispose of them before we begin.

Dressed in fearsome spiked mail, this woman's cold gaze seems to chill you.
One of the elites of the occupying Luskan force, this man exudes a supreme confidence.
This soldier sneers at you, obviously feeling himself superior.
This soldier regards the town around him with a smug sneer.
Something in this soldier's demeanor speaks of a man overworked on a regular basis.
This soldier's eyes keep darting around nervously.
This soldier seems to be uneasy, shifting his weight as though waiting for something to happen.
This soldier looks the most relaxed of the lot, regarding the area around him casually.

Location, my friend, it's all about location! ...And I suppose opportunity. And clever marketing. And...

...and you can imagine, after all that, that the Duchess was quite pleased! Ah, those were good times. Busy, yes, but good.
Tell me about being a merchant.

Az'zurix Everflame
Axe of Sacrifice

Once wielded by Sunna Crimsonhair, a battlemaiden of a clan of gold dwarves, this axe saw the young woman defend her clan to her last breath, slaying scores of invading firenewts even as she bled from dozens of wounds. In her last moments, her soul invested itself in her weapon - granting it great power, but also burdening its user with the same fatigue and pain she felt in her last glorious struggle.
Belt of Growth
This belt causes the user to grow in size, enchancing their strength and durability.
Girdle of Might
This belt grants the user an enhancement to their strength, and spreads a magical sheen across their skin, granting them additional natural armor.
A powerful pair of metal boots - glowing with a strange enchantment.
Boots of the Mountain King
Sturdy and imposing, the magics within these boots allow the user to move freely over difficult terrain, and grant them the ability to harden their skin to a stonelike consistency once a day.
A harmless set of ragged clothing.
Deceptive Rags

Though it looks like little more than beggars' rags, these simple clothes bear powerful enchantments, protecting the user better than the finest set of plate mail.
Said to be made by a crafty spellcaster who wanted his enemies to think him penniless and unprotected, he wore these and stood out in the street, begging for alms. When his foes were lured out of hiding, he allowed them to attack - so he could savor the stunned look on their faces when his rags shrugged aside his blows. Then, bystanders said, a cloud of darkness descended... and when it finally faded, the attackers were dead - and the caster was gone.

Vampire Fang

Forestguard Chain

Crafted from mithral blessed by Silvanus, god of nature, these shirts of chain are meant for the protectors of wooded areas to wear. Designed to guard against fell beasts - driven mad by the magics of dread Talona and Malar - this armor has powerful protective magics woven into it.
This pale-skinned construct resembles an idealized human female warrior with a serene expression.
Ivory Shieldmaiden
Chaos Sliver

Said to have been formed by the swirling mess of various planes mingling, the magic powers of this falchion may not do much damage separately... but together, they are assuredly a force worth noticing!
Flail of Panic

Although it is unknown who crafted this fell weapon, one thing is certain - whoever is unfortunate enough to endure a strike from it is subjected to a flood of terror that puts the most intense of nightmares to shame.
Greataxe of Flame
Gloves of Slowing

Shaped after the teachings of Liin Paleleaf, a hin fist, these gloves are designed to mimic Liin's ability to hit her targets in such a way that the impact numbed their muscles, making them stumble in shock until their nerves recovered.
Hands of the True Strike

Once the property of "One-Shot" Hennar, a brawler famous for bragging that he could take down any opponent in a single hit, these gloves allow the user to put all of their focus into a single attack once per day. The reason these gloves are in your possession right now instead of Hennar's is the simple reminder - when you pick a fight, always be wary of how many friends they have around!
These finely crafted metal gauntlets are etched with a coppery alloy.
Blazing Gauntlets
Created to bring both a blazingly-painful addition to unarmed strikes and call down a fearsome flaming burst from the skies, these gauntlets utilize the power of fire to an impressive degree.

This cold iron blade was crafted with high attention to detail. Its extensive engravings are intricate and ornate, though some of the designs have been blemished by heavy use in battle. One side of the blade contains an illustration of a family history that begins with a weaver's loom and culiminates with a battle against a menacing dragon. The blade's other face contains a family tree for the Cadorna line. A more recent engraving can be found on the hilt, "To Skullcrusher, For All Your Service - P. Cadorna, 1351 DR".
Cadorna Family Sword

Created to commemorate the fiftieth anniversary of Magnus Cadorna's unlikely victory against a young red dragon, the Cadorna Family Sword was passed down through four generations until it left the family's possession.
Originally a small family of weavers from the Dragon Reach, the Cadorna family fell on hard times when a dragon began plaguing the region near their village. The oldest son of the family, Magnus, joined a local militia in a weak attempt to control the dragon's ransacking.
When adventurers finally arrived to deal with the dragon, the militia waited in reserve in case the adventurers failed. The adventurers did fail, and the wounded dragon set out to take vengeance against the villagers who had helped his would-be killers.
In a short but bloody battle, most of the militiamen were killed. Desperate and half dead, Magnus Cadorna dove at the wounded creature and struck a fatal blow. The hero of the village, Magnus received treasure and honors that elevated the family to a prominent position. They soon spread out across the Dragon Reach as a powerful textile trading company.
When Magnus was eighty two years old, the Cadorna Family Sword was created to commemorate the event that catapulted the family to prosperity. Magnus appreciated the gesture, but also found it a bit "silly". The sword was passed down for a few generations in the self-styled "dragon killer" family until it came into the possession of junior councilman Porphyrys Cadorna in the ill-fated city of Phlan.
Porphyrys was eventually run out of town for his complicity with enemies of the city. Though he lived for many years after the tragic events that lead to his family's shame and ruin, Porphyrys never found an heir to continue his line. He entrusted the family sword to his loyal servant and bodyguard, a tough soldier who called himself "Skullcrusher".
This cold iron blade was crafted with high attention to detail. Its extensive engravings are intricate and ornate, though some of the designs have been blemished by heavy use in battle. One side of the blade contains an illustration of a family history that begins with a weaver's loom and culiminates with a battle against a menacing dragon. The blade's other face contains a family tree for the Cadorna line. A more recent engraving can be found on the hilt, "To Skullcrusher, For All Your Service - P. Cadorna, 1351 DR".
Royalty Guard

Blessed by clerics of Sianamorphe - the Divine Right - these weapons were originally intended to protect royalty. Though whatever noble house they were intended for is probably lost and forgotten, the powers of these weapons persist.
Frigid Chopper
This axe is invested with the freezing breath of Auril the Icemaiden - and the goddess smiles to think her chill sinking into their bones is the last thing this axe's victims will feel.
A thin, ratty-looking eyepatch.
Eyepatch of the Great Sea Corsair
This strip of cloth and leather doesn't look like much, but its enchantments grant the wearer impressive visual acuity.
Supreme Hunter's Garb
Crafted by a servant of Gwaeron Windstrom, this armor incorporates the powers of various beasts, allowing them to be utilized by the user.
Unwieldy Plate

Though the smith who crafted this mail later went on to create superlative works of art, this first piece - while quite useful and effective - doesn't quite fit the user as well as it could, hampering their movements slightly... while still giving them access to the armor's impressive magical abilities.
This is an ornate ivory horn.
Ivory Horn of Valhalla
The Devoted Servant

Created for the most loyal samurai of the Shogun, these katana hail from the far-off land of Wa - an island nation within Kara-Tur. How it managed to find its way to you is somewhat of a mystery, but its powers remain thankfully intact.
Enduring Bow

This bow hearkens back to the days when archers in the north had to remain constantly vigiliant against sudden, violent attacks from orcish hordes, steadfastly holding their positions even as thousands of screaming orcs bore down on them. The magic inherent in this bow ensures that the wielder will never be without the ammo they need, and grants them the strength they need to hold on until more help arrives.
Highwayman
Perfectly designed for bandits, this small crossbow somehow makes its user seem more dangerous and ill-tempered than usual, and its bolts seem to slice dangerously through their targets.
Brainscrambler

A stout and practical looking weapon made from fine oak and high quality steel, Brainscrambler nonetheless bears the marks of a master craftsman. The mercenary Skullcrusher, known as an implacable opponent in the Moonsea and Dragon Reach, had this weapon crafted and enchanted to his unique specifications.
Magmablessed
Forsaking all other enchantments, this morningstar is invested with a tremendous amount of fiery power.
Forgotten Tome
Old Forge
Destroyed Golem
Ruined Contraption
Screaming Needle

Some weapons are crafted to be subtle - the sudden motion of the sap, of the stiletto. This is not one of them - tiny holes in the metal of this rapier make an unearthly shriek as the weapon moves through the air, stunning and unnerving the wielder's foes.
Band of the Forest
Crafted by the elves of the wild, this slender band of green metal has a strange, organic warmth to it - more like a vine than a circle of steel.
Eye of the Spider Queen

This ring is made of blackened metal in the shape of a spider, and its topped with a large design in onyx and amethyst that resembles a beautiful eye, glaring at you balefully. It is no surprise this once belonged to by a devout worshipper of Lolth, the Spider Queen.
Volo's Rejuvenating Ring
A gift to Volo from his old friend Elminster, this ring grants the wearer additional viality, and allows them the gift of healing once a day.

Neverwinter Nights 2: Storm of Zehir Official Campaign
A voyage across the southern seas is cut short by a mysterious storm - your party finds itself shipwrecked on an unfriendly shore. To survive, you and your fellows must accept the aid of a powerful merchant... and unravel a conspiracy that threatens to change the fate of all the Realms.
This bold journey goes to level 15 and beyond. Previous Neverwinter Nights 2 experience is not required.

These creatures resemble green-skinned goblins, but much they're much more muscular and feral.
These creatures are big as an ogres, with a vaguely humanoid shape. Hideous scales sheathe their bodies, and huge wings and a snaking, prehensile tail add to their intimidating appearance.
Like a walking hill, these creatures plod along on two legs of rock and earth. They have clublike arms of jagged stone swinging at its sides, with a featureless head.
These large spiders move with surprising speed - and there is something fearsomely intelligent about their movements.
These large monstrous spider,s unlike its earthly counterparts, have a glint of evil intelligence in their many eyes.
These humanoids are slightly taller than a human, with has gray skin, furry bodies, and a head like a hyena.

These lean, long-legged bipedal creatures have wicked-looking claws on their feet and a brightly colored hide that reminds you of a tropical bird. Each one stands about as tall as a human, and its outstretched tail makes it at least twice as long as it is tall.

Soulsworn batiri are members of a batiri tribe who foolishly swore their souls to a demonic power in exchange for the power to defeat a rival tribe. The power they gained also drove them mad with bloodlust, and what's left of the tribe now roams Chult in scattered warbands - of which this is only one.
