Most of the previous pages have been torn out, leaving only the last few entries. The second to last entry reads: Our research for Zhiir is nearly complete, and not a moment too soon. The djinni is unusually powerful, to put it mildly. He even nearly broke free from the binding circle the other night. Foseth claims it was simply a flaw in the circle, but I have my doubts. As a contingency, I've crafted a ring which will bind the djinni into it should he actually manage to get free. Our experiments have made the djinni quite insane, but it was necessary to complete the research. The latest entry reads: Foseth is screaming. This can't be good, but the wards around my laboratory should be strong enough to keep the djinni out. A hasty postscript follows: I was wrong about the wards.
The cheerful colors of the man's outfit contrast starkly with the worried expression on his face.

This beautiful pendant bears a hauntingly beautiful female voice - you heard it singing through the winding paths of the caverns previously, and now - back in civilized company - it seems content to hum quietly to itself.
| Soldiers dead |So much blood...
This farmer seems the simple sort, guarded but fairly easygoing by Samarachan standards.
Appropriately, most clerics in Samarach's military are followers of Tempus, god of battle - this cleric wears his holy symbol on the crest of his helmet.

The journal is mostly a mix of accounting entries and weather forecasts. The last few entries seem to depict more recent events in the village: I told them all the truth - not only does Oghma will it, they deserved to know. They were suprisingly calm, but then again, we are a resilient people. The latest entry reads: There are soldiers in town, and the people are nervous. Their leader, Akuma, accuses us of yuan-ti collaboration, but we know that there is no truth to his words. Still, he will not leave. I pray that Oghma shows this Akuma that there are no harmful secrets being kept here.
This elf fixes you with an even, intense gaze, as a predator might size up prey.

This powerfully built dwarf is a few inches shy of five feet but walks and talks with the clamor and subtlety of a hill giant. A shield dwarf of the Ironfist clan, Khelgar is a talented warrior who delights in the intimacy of a tavern brawl. Smiling when threatened and downright ecstatic when punched, Khelgar is most at home in a storm of fists and insults. Khelgar's weathered face, long dark beard and massive upper body would likely give him muscular good looks had he not built a collection of cuts, bruises and missing teeth on his face from countless brawls - and a slight limp from his left leg is evidence of his injuries after the battle with the King of Shadows.
Everything about the man screams wealth and privilege. Hardship is a foreign concept to him.
This fell troll is shorter than others of its kind, but a dangerous intelligence is evident in its small, dark eyes - on both heads.

"The Sharrans claim that these rituals will revive our fallen lord. Perhaps, perhaps not. The only certainty is that the Sharrans are using us for their own benefit, and will need to be dealt with eventually. There are only three of us left now, and we will need to rebuild our forces before we're capable of exerting our might once more." "There have also been signs that someone else has begun infiltrating their agents into this region. Their movements are subtle and slow, easily missed, but they are there if you know what to look for. We must find out what they are up to as soon as possible." [The rest of the journal features a rough map of the region showing where the Sharran temple is located, along with a number of battle plans for assaulting the temple.]
This dagger is wickedly sharp and full of tiny serrations - a powerful enchantment on the weapon seems to draw strength to the user from the weapon's victims.
Yes, dear...
It seems as if things are more... cheerful around here, doesn't it?
Have you heard about the bandits raging around this area? This city grows worse all the time!
Yes - I think I begin to see the beauty of this place. A little.
This merchant seems as if he's struggling to recover from hard times.
One of the wealthier citizens of Neverwinter City.
You needn't worry - you'll find no bandits here.

Found only in meteorites and the rarest veins in magical areas, adamantine is an ultra-hard metal that adds to the quality of weapons and armor. These arrows have been tipped with an adamantine head, and delicate etchings of the metal are inscribed in the wooden shaft.

Cold-forged iron is beaten into shape with nothing but raw, brute strength. Popular lore asserts that fey creatures and some fiends are especially vulnerable to cold iron. Though the cold iron heads of these arrows lack elegance, they remain wickedly sharp and capable nonetheless.

Lore holds that shapeshifters and some fiends are especially vulnerable to the bite of silver weaponry. These arrows are tipped with alchemical silver heads, and a hair-thin sheen of the metal coats the rest of the projectile.

Monster Stealth (Global)
Monsters will use stealth if they have any skill ranks in Hide or Move Silently.
Monsters will not use stealth.
Monster Wander (Global)
Monsters will wander around looking for you.
Monsters will not wander around.
Monster Open Doors (Global)
Monsters will open doors when looking for you. Only works if Monster Wander is turned on.
Monsters will not open doors.
Monster Unlock or Bash Doors (Global)
Monsters will unlock or bash open doors looking for you. Only works if Monster Open Doors is turned on.
Monsters will unlock or bash open doors.
Knockdown (Global)
Knockdown use is turned on.
Sometimes
Knockdown use is used sometimes.
Knockdown use is turned off.
Auto Set of Companion Behaviors (Global)
The first time you meet a companion, default behaviors are assigned to them.
No default behaviors are assigned to companions.
Enemies Auto Cast Buffs (Global)
The first time you meet an enemy, they will already have cast long duration buffs on themselves.
The first time you meet an enemy, they will already have cast medium and long duration buffs on themselves.
No enemy pre cast of buffs.
Enemies Create Items (Global)
The first time you meet an enemy, they will create some basic items (healing, buff) for use on themselves.
No enemy creation of items.
Enemies Use Equipped Items (Global)
Enemies are able to use equipped items (not normally possible).
Enemies don't use equipped items.
Warlock One Round Hideous Blow (Global)
Warlocks use hideous blow in one round.
Warlocks use hideous blow in two rounds.
Monster Ally Damage (Global)
Monsters damage allies with area of effect spells based on alignment.
Monsters avoid damaging allies with area of effect spells.

The path from Neverwinter to New Leaf is very dangerous, requiring passage through Neverwinter Wood. However, this route is very profitable, as New Leaf is a major supplier of high quality lumber, and the small logging town desperately needs the ore that is more readily avaiable in Neverwinter.
The trade route between Neverwinter and Highcliff is fairly secure, but also well trafficked, so it is only marginally profitable.

While relatively safe, the roads leading from Neverwinter to Thundertee are less patrolled than the route to Highcliff. As a result, trade with Thundertree is somewhat risky. However Thundertree is a major logging town and, as such, the route is more profitable than that to Highcliff.
A long caravan route that leads through a more perilous section of the High Road, trading between Highcliff and Leilon is both moderately dangerous and fairly profitable.

Travelling through the Mere of Dead Men has always been dangerous - even more so since the War of Shadows. However, residents of the Mere are willing to pay much for Leilon's goods that they can't acquire on their own.

Crossroad Keep to Leilon is a lengthy journey along portions of the High Road that have fallen into disrepair. Though not safe by any means trading between between Crossroad Keep and Leilon is profitable.

Few travel the extremely dangerous route between Conyberry and New Leaf, which passes through the most foreboding parts of Neverwinter Wood. However, residents of New Leaf are quite eager for goods from the Western Heartlands imported through Conyberry.
Phandalin to Conyberry is a fairly safe route that is modestly profitable, considering Phandalin's weak economy.

While less dangerous than the route to New Leaf, caravaning betweeen Conyberry and Thundertree is still quite profitable. Conyberry receives goods from the Western Heartlands that fetch a high price from residents of the neighboring towns.

The tale of how the Knight Captain first travelled from West Harbor to Highcliff is well known in the Sword Coast. The journey is just as dangerous for merchants as it was then, but West Harbor will pay a handsome price for goods to those willing to brave the trip.

It is a short distance via heavily patrolled roads to go between Crossroad Keep and Highcliff. While this much-exploited route can only provide a trickle of income, it is a steady choice for merchants who shy away from riskier trade routes.

While Phandalin is a poor mining town, its ore fetches a good price in Crossroad Keep, which is undergoing rebuilding since the Shadow War. However, the eastern part of the Sword Coast is less well patrolled than the coastline - and the route is somewhat dangerous as a result.

Crossroad Keep to Thundertree is a somewhat dangerous trip that leads across the unpatrolled plains north of Crossroad Keep. This route provides a good profit as the lumber from Thundertree is needed to rebuild Crossroad Keep.

Though Port Llast is a straight journey along the High Road from Neverwinter, most merchants have avoided trade with the coastal town lately. The reasons for this include increased Luskan activity in the region, an undead infestation and freak coastal storms. Though some of these problems have subsided recently, traders remain wary. However, the beleaguered residents of Port Llast are willing to pay a high premium for goods, making the route profitable.
You gain experience from your proximity to One of Many as it consumes the soul of its victim.
Suckling from the stray vapors of One of Many's power, you have gained a barely perceptible aura that makes you stronger and smarter.
Your prolonged exposure to One of Many while it feeds on the souls of its victims has caused your dark aura to grow stronger and more perceptible, granting you a significant increase in power.
Having basked in One of Many's power as it gorged itself on so many of your hapless cohorts, you have gained an overwhelmingly strong aura.
The concealed entrance yields to a large, rough stone stairway, lit by torches with eerie purple flames - your shadow looms large on the walls around you as you descend deeper into the Underdark.
Numerous yuan-ti ruins are present in the jungles of Samarach - not all of them empty.

This cave's entrance speaks of pride - instead of being concealed by the jungle's thick growth, it is marked by totems and well-tended fires. The heads on spikes speak grimly of its inhabitants' success at controlling their territory.

The Mines of Selgol are truly ancient, and they remain among the most productive salt mines in Chult. Hundreds of years ago, miners broke into a section of the Underdark known as the Firelands, unleashing occasional firenewt invasions.

As you enter the mines, the salt-laden dust on the floor makes you cough slighly and stifle a sneeze... but beyond the dry smell of salt, you catch a hint of brimstone and sulfur - two smells that rarely bode well.
The swamp of eastern Samarach is a recent feature, most likely the result of a magical experiment gone awry.

It is apparent from this cave's exterior that the creatures therein aren't thriving - it looks hurriedly excavated, and remnants of broken weapons and tools lie outside the entrance... as if thrown down at the end of a journey.
The haunting song echoes from somewhere within the depths of this damp, lush cavern.
Many herbs found in Samarach are used to create deadly poisons and, despite laws to the contrary, trade in such poisons forms a cornerstone of the economy.
A Samarachan tavern is just about the only place where miners, soldiers, and nobles mingle.

Torich is a small, unassuming town built near the Mines of Selgol - its folk are hardy, used to dealing both with the dangers of mine work and the occasionally aggressive Samarachan troops taking their leave within the town.
Samarachans pride themselves on the quality of their taverns. Even the most rustic of taverns abounds in luxury.

Known as the City of Gilded Pearls, Rassatan is nestled in a bowl-shaped depression at the head of Rassatan Bay - from the oyster beds of these waters come the highest-quality golden pearls in all of the Realms.

Taruin, the City of Seven Spices, is situated near the confluence of creeks and streams that form the River Samar. Home to a large contingent of Samargol's army, the city is frequently used as a staging area for long patrols along the jungle's borders.
As the goddess of trade and commerce, Waukeen is one of the few deities openly tolerated by Samarachans.
Samarachan authorities frown on anyone disturbing the resting place of the dead, but it's a policy that is only loosely enforced.
Lizardfolk are an infrequent sight in Samarach, but small tribes thrive in isolated coves along Samarach's coast.
Kobolds often make their homes along the relative safety of Samarachan's coastline.
Isolated mausoleums and crypts in Samarach's wilderness were often burial sites of heroes or religious figures, many of whom are now long-forgotten.
From time to time, the Samarachans set up watchtowers along the edge of the jungle, but these were inevitably overrun by the jungle's denizens.
The most beautiful locations in the jungles of Samarach also tend to be the most dangerous...
Strange creatures and other terrors often take up residence in abandoned Samarachan mines.
Unlike in Samarach, the yuan-ti rule openly in Chult. All manner of sinister activities take place within their jungle strongholds.

One of the many small villages dotting the landscape of Samarach, Nimbre has little to do with the larger politics of the nation. It lives in near self-suffiency, occasionally serving as a stop-off point for merchants travelling from northeastern mining settlements down to Samargol.
It is rare for any Samarachan person of learning to dwell beyond the safety of a city's walls.
Rassatan soldiers help keep the roads relatively safe for travelers, but the hills around the city are left to the wyverns and ogres.
Rumors persist of an entire firenewt empire lurking beneath the foothills of Torich.
Only the bravest or most foolhardy of Samarachans would live outside the safety of a city's walls.
It is rare for the yuan-ti to tolerate anyone within their territory who isn't either an ally or a slave.
Anyone wishing privacy and isolation would find Chult ideal - assuming they could withstand the horrors of the jungle.
Only the most powerful beings are capable of maintaining a stronghold in the middle of the jungles of Chult.
Burial sites in Chult are rare. It's much more common for the dead to be burned to prevent them from being reanimated as undead.
Chult is rich in rare ore and gems, but acquiring any of it is an undertaking only for the wealthy and well-armed.
Efforts to bring a measure of civilization to Chult usually fail in a matter of months, if not days.
Most portals between Samarach and the lands to the north are non-functional or destroyed, but a handful yet remain.
The Merchant Headquarters is the heart of your trading company on the Sword Coast. Its opulence reflects Sa'Sani's success and prowess as a merchant.
From its worn appearance, the Phoenix Tail Inn has seen better times.
The siege of Crossroad Keep was the greatest battle of the Shadow War - here Graycloaks and undead clashed in massive numbers and unleashed great magical powers.
The strangely beautiful crystal formations in this cave are the result of a misguided magical experiment.
No more than a handful of shadow priests survived the fall of the King of Shadows - the remainder gather in small but deadly cults, hoping for the return of their master.
The presence of a shrine of Waukeeen will bolster Crossroad Keep's prosperity.
With the Knight-Captain missing, Khelgar Ironfist has been granted regency of Crossroad Keep.

Many of the Keep's residents have departed for more prosperous territory, many abandoning their homes outright. This resident - a somewhat mad alchemist - unfortunately left some of his more precarious possessions around as well...
With the presence of unruly children within its walls, Crossroad Keep may face its greatest threat ever.
Comprised of individuals claiming to have been trained by the legendary Knight-Captain, the Adventurer's Guild offers teamwork training.

Much has changed in Neverwinter since the Shadow War - the Blacklake District has seen the destruction of some buildings and the construction of others - including a large temple complex to the goddess Waukeen and a Thayan Enclave.
This temple is lavishly decorated and well-occupied, housing all three of Neverwinter's major trading organizations - the Circle of Friends, the Forgotten Lords, and the Fated Winds.

Founded to bring learning and Thayan magical goods to Neverwinter city, the Red Wizards are tolerated within the borders of the City of Skilled Hands - but it is doubtful that any large number of people really welcome their presence.
Rowdy, busy, and well-trafficked, the Wailing Wench Inn remains one of the most popular taverns in Neverwinter - if not the whole of the northern Sword Coast.
Well-organized and efficient, this trading post works hard to bring a profit to your merchant company.
The dank, twisting tunnels of this cave system bear guttering torches on the walls... and what sound like sinister whispers echoing from within.
The houses in this small city look weatherbeaten and sagging - that same tiredness seems to show on the faces of the town's inhabitants.
The interior of the garrison contains a desk - meant for the First Captain of the town - and a jail. There is little else - the area is meant for utility and practicality, not for show.

The cold seawater laps hungrily at your arms as you swim towards the Priory of the Depths, as if seeking to pull you into the belly of the ocean before reaching your goal. Arriving at last on the chill stone landing, you rid yourself of the worst of the damp before venturing forth...

Somewhere nearby, a wrought iron gate squeaks harshly as a sharp wind catches it, and your breath catches as a flock of crows erupts from a nearby tree, cawing restlessly. This is a place that rejects the living and your presence has been very clearly noted.
This old inn is sparsely decorated and even more sparsely inhabited - though the innkeeper seems plenty happy to see a new face enter the room.

This is West Harbor, where the Knight-Captain is said to have spent their childhood. It may have been a happier place in times past - now, having faced war and loss, its people seem harder, more solemn.

A winding path through the Mere of Dead Men has led you onto this small tussock of dry land - the cult seems to have set up camp here, striking primitive tents and lean-tos up amongst chunks of ancient Illefarn stonework.

The air here is thick with the smells of mildew, decay, and reptile rot. Judging from the partially collapsed walls and floors, this once was a sturdy manor that collapsed into the Mere of Dead Men long ago.

Slowly, you come into consciousness, groggy and waterlogged. Wet sand sticks to your skin and cold rain lashes your face. Somewhere close - and growing nearer - you hear shouting as you stagger, dazed, to your feet...

Known as the City of Veils, Samargol is home to over a hundred thousand citizens... although powerful illusions make the city appear to onlookers as little more than a handful of shacks and a tiny keep.

Named for the most honest gesture in Samarach - the open hand, signifiying no concealed weapons, poisons, or the motions of a spell - the Openpalm Bazaar is the only place in Samargol where foreigners are allowed to do business - or even reside.

Created by the gnomes of Lantan to provide the raw lumber that their island nation requires, the Lantanese Lumber Camp is linked through a portal to a large lumberyard at the Lantanese city of Sundrah.

Named for the dead goddess Leira - patron of illusionists and liars - Leira's Trick remains the only place in Samargol that is truly welcoming to outsiders. The tavern bears strange and beautiful decorations and its rooms are warded against scrying spells.

The Snout of Omgar - the southwestern peninsula of Samarach - is named after the massive sea monster said to live just off the coast. The beast imposes outrageous tolls on passing ships, which pay to avoid foundering or destruction.
The Batiri are relentless trackers, skilled in jungle lore and the use of the bow and spear. Rumors that the goblins devour their captives are absolutely true.
As the goddess of trade and commerce, Waukeen is one of the few deities openly tolerated by Samarachans.
The Viper Temple is the gateway to Chult and under yuan-ti control - a fact that fills the rulers of Samarach with dread.
The largest yuan-ti temples often possess large troves of magical weapons and armor that are stored away in the rare event that the temple is attacked.
Snaketongue cultists believe that devotion to Zehir will one day lead to their transformation into yuan-ti, a false belief the yuan-ti themselves do nothing to discourage.
For all their cruelty and bloodthirst, the yuan-ti value knowledge as much as any Realms sage.
No one but yuan-ti priests and holy guardians are ever permitted inside the holy sanctum of a yuan-ti. For all others, death is the penalty.
The Throne of the World Serpent is one of the holiest sites in the Realms for the yuan-ti. Only the most powerful are ever permitted an audience with their god.
Yuan-ti purebloods tend to be the most versatile of the yuan-ti, possessing a wide variety of martial and arcane skills.
You can retire from your adventures at any time. However, if you retire early, then Volo's mention of you in his book will be but a brief footnote.

The Sword Coast is home to many of the largest, most prosperous and cosmopolitan cities in Faerun. However, due to recent events, the economy has weakened, the roads are less safe, and a sense of unease pervades among the residents of the region.
Caves along the shore frequently provide effective shelter for creatures - both intelligent and not - and often these denizens are unwelcome and unwanted.
While worgs can often be found in the wilderness, it is rare for them to behave aggressively and make their dens near human settlements.
This cave does not seem particularly hospitable - that anything lives here is surprising.
While Bane, the evil god of Tyranny, was slain by Torm during the Time of Troubles, many have spoken in hushed tones about his return.
Cold Iron is a rare material used to forge weapons particularly effective against fey creatures.
The Neverwinter Wood provides shelter for hermits and other bizarre individuals who wish to establish their domain out from under the eyes of society.
While Luskan is technically ruled by the five High Captains - the Arcane Brotherhood, a society of mages, hold true sway over the city from the Hosttower of the Arcane.
Mining is often an extremely dangerous profession. Cave-ins, gas leaks, and other dangers make it a dangerous profession - if extremely profitable for those who own the mine.
Banditry has become increasingly prevalent since the War of Shadow. The economic backlash caused by conflict has created desperate times for many of the folk along the Sword Coast.
Shar, the dark-tressed deity of secrets and darkness, created the Shadow Weave - a dark distorted version of the true Weave that enhances the magic of shadow, enchantment, illusion, and necromancy.
Taverns and Inns dot the Sword Coast, providing respite for travelers in the form of cold ale, warm bread, and a song.
A sense of unease overwhelms you - after the events at New Leaf, it seems that any small tragedy could reveal corruption or greed underlying it.

As the ages have passed, racial tension has eased somewhat throughout the Realms. However, some members of the longer lived races, such as elves, can have a difficult time in forgetting the ancient wrongs done to their kind.
The workings of most portals are mysterious and unpredictable. Each one is built for a reason, but all too often these reasons are lost when the creator passes into history or obscurity.
The smell of death envelopes you as you descend deeper into this barrow.
Hunting for sport is a serious affront to many creatures of the forest including elves, fey, and druids.
Adamantine is an extremely rare metal. Its ultra hard composition increases the protective properties of armor and weapons crafted from it can more easily pierce defenses.
The ancient elven empire known as Illefarn stretched along the Sword Coast, from the Spine of the World to the River Delimbiyr.
This small cave reeks of wet fur and unwashed flesh.
The excessive dust and cobwebs in this ruin give you the feeling that nothing has been here for a very long time.
The walls of this ruin reverberate with the methodical sound of giant footsteps. Dust and debris cascade down around you causing your eyes to tear.
You can visit your trading post to return goods to storage at Crossroad Keep.
Robbing ancient burial sites can have grave consequences. Many forgotten tombs sites are inhabited by the restless dead or worse.
An ancient circle of druids once inhabited the Mere of Dead Men. Housewives tell tall tales of a forbidden love affair between one such druid and an orphan from West Harbor.
Oftentimes creature parts are vital ingredients for crafting magic items.
This cave looks as if it is a recent addition to the topography of Mt. Hotenow. The smooth cavern walls appear to have been scorched by intense heat and flame.
Some creatures have strong resistance to physical damage. If you are having trouble damaging something, try equipping a single weapon with both hands or using the power attack feat.
Ruins of the collapsed Illefarn Empire can contain artifacts of interest to students of the Arcane.
Hide and Seek is a popular game among children and halflings.
It seems rather odd that a mere goblin should be a such a threat to so many...

Corporeal undead creatures have been known to retain portions of the magic that created them in their bodies, organs, and limbs. These creature parts are highly sought ingredients for creating magic items.
Sleeping in an inn is the only way to guarantee a good night's rest.
The Mere of Dead Men is aptly named. Centuries ago, countless warriors died in this salt marsh beneath the swords of an invading orc army.
The extreme heat emanating from this cave is nearly unbearable. The natural, stone walls occasionally rumble as if the mountain itself objects to your intrusion.
Constructs are typically created by powerful wizards to serve as companions, guardians, and servants. Many such creations are resistant to various magical attacks.

It's been over thirty years since the Heroes of Phlan defeated the Possessing Spirit, Tyranthraxus, and reclaimed the Pool of Radiance. Although the event happened far to the east, the telling of that tale has been ever popular along the Sword Coast.

TIP: At 0 Hit Points, a character falls unconscious. If they go below 0, they enter a "Dying" state, and will begin losing 1 Hit Point every 6 seconds. If they are not healed, eventually they will die.
TIP: Spellcasters - remember to memorize new spells when gaining a level!
TIP: Death is permanent in Storm of Zehir - party members, once killed, will not get back up without a Raise Dead or Resurrect spell cast on them.
TIP: The world of Toril is a dangerous place - be sure to save your gold to stock up on any healing potions or antidotes you're able to find.
TIP: The Coin of Life is a special item distributed by the Church of Waukeen, allowing the dead to return to life. Unlike scrolls, there is no class restriction on Coins of Life.
TIP: Located in inns throughout the land, the guest book allows you to swap out your party members - so you can bring the ideal group into any situation.
TIP: The employee registry book is located within the merchant headquarters, and allows you to swap out your party members just like any tavern guest book.
TIP: Throughout your travels, you may acquire valuable parts from creatures you've slain. You can use some of these to enchant powerful magical items, or sell them to various bounty collectors.
TIP: Cohorts are located throughout Samarach and the Sword Coast, and can be recruited into your party either by payment or favors.
TIP: Usually, respectable merchants will not carry items like traps or poisons - if on the hunt for such items, it's best to search in the less reputable areas.
TIP: Recipes for any armor, weapons, wondrous items, or enchantments will be kept in the corresponding recipe tome.
TIP: You can customize your party's AI options under the Behavior tab of the Character Screen.
LORE: Volothamp Geddarm is one of the most well-traveled individuals in the Realms, and has penned numerous volumes about his travels.
LORE: There are three major castes within yuan-ti society: the purebloods, halfbloods, and abominations. The more snakelike the individual, the higher their status.

LORE: In the last few years, the massive trading power of Zhentil Keep has been threatened by the massive City of Shade, which appeared over the desert of Anauroch and has been cutting off their trade routes.

LORE: After the fall of the King of Shadows, Khelgar Ironfist demanded that Nasher give him help to look for the missing Knight-Captain. However, the war had so depleted Neverwinter's forces that no one could be spared for the search.
LORE: Some deities seem to be unusually active recently - the clerics of Chauntea seem to be gathering, the moon elves whisper the name of Angharradh, and cults of the dark god Cyric seem restless.
LORE: Known as "the Hidden Kingdom," Samarach is a vassal state of the nation of Nimbral, and is governed by an Nimbran archmage known as the High Phantasmage.
LORE: In addition to the High Phantasmage, the few merchants given permission to trade with outsiders must also answer to the Trading Council - a group of appointed nobles.

LORE: As a nation, Samarach is nearly as untrusting of its inhabitants as it is of any outsiders, constantly afraid that traitors and yuan-ti lurk in their mist. Lying is the norm, and trust is rare even among family.
LORE: A neighboring nation of Samarach, Tashalar is a wealthy, cosmopolitan nation known for its excellent wines and skilled craftsmanship.

LORE: Much like the other nations of the Chultan penninsula, the people of Thindol - Samarach's eastern neighbor - hold a great fear of snakes, and hold the divinations of the church of Savras in high regard.

LORE: Though they've been dismissed by many, rumors have made their way from the distant land of Rashemen that speaks of an ancient curse resurfacing, and the spirits of that nation forming some kind of army.
LORE: Khelgar's position as the steward of Crossroad Keep is only temporary - one he grudgingly accepted until the Knight-Captain returned.

LORE: Separated from civilization by the vast swath of jungle known as the Samarlogh, the Narubel Pass once served as a connection between the Samarachan city of Taruin and the now forbidden city-state of Narubel.
LORE: The southeasternmost tip of the Jungles of Chult is known as the Samarlogh, a dark jungle only rarely ventured near by only the most daring and elite Samarachan patrols.

LORE: A small clan of yuan-ti, the Sauringar survived being driven out of their ancestral holdings in the Sanrach Basin by infiltrating a merchant organization known as the Rundeen, and forging an alliance with the Se'Sehen, the largest clan of yuan-ti.
LORE: The largest and most powerful of the yuan-ti clans, House Se'Sehen is currently ruled by the powerful Hierophant N'Safa. Their strength and cunning makes them feared enemies and deadly spies.

LORE: Situated between Chondath and the Pirate Isles, Turmish is known for its peaceful farms and ornate, beautiful armor. The careful fashion of the men of the trading class led to the phrase "square as a Turmian beard," which means anything well or carefully done.

LORE: Divided between the rulership of the Mulhorandi and those fighting for freedom, Unther is a land of opportunity. Three powerful figures - the right hand of the dead god Gilgeam, a slave-turned-bandit leader, and a mysterious and beautiful air genasi - fight for the nation's future.

LORE: Within the wilderness of the High Forest stands a massive oak called Grandfather Tree - held in reverence by nearly all nonevil beings. Though defended by the Tree Ghost Uthgardt tribe, the Grandfather is also protected by its own powerful magic.

LORE: Between two great forests - the Chondalwood and the Winterwood - and two great rivers - the Arran and the Nagaflow - lies Sespech. Aldorn "Foesmasher" Thuragar, a former adventurer, rules the barony with a firm but sage hand.

LORE: The vast grassland known as the Shaar - located in the far South - is a wild place where civilization has hardly gained a foothold. Nomadic humans, centaurs, gnolls, and the leonid creatures known as wemics populate its rolling, grassy reaches.

LORE: Ruled by descendents of the ancient kingdom of Netheril, Halruaa is a nation of magic and wizardry, insular and content to keep their research and arcane secrets safe from the rest of the world.

LORE: Chaotic, rowdy, and only loosely considered a country, the nation of Chessenta is home to a people known for being passionate and riotious, dedicated to living life to its fullest and never doing anything halfway.

LORE: A land of merchants and traders, Sembia sneers at foreigners and welcomes corruption. If an outsider can become successful in Sembia it might be assumed that no challenge is too great for them to conquer.

LORE: Batiri differ from their northern cousins in a number of ways. Organized into a matriarchal society, these jungle goblins typically hunt and travel at night, eschewing armor - except in the cases of high-ranking members of a tribe. Batiri are also more feral than normal goblins, often eating those they capture.

LORE: Ubtao, Chult's patron deity, is said to stand guard over the Peaks of Flame, watching against the day when Dendar the Night Serpent slithers forth - dooming the world. With this duty, the gods granted Ubtao divinity and promised never to extend their dominion into his fiefdom.

LORE: Known also as the Lady of Deception and the Mist Maiden, Leira was the goddess of illusions, and the patron of liars. Slain in 1360 by the god Cyric - wielding the sword Godsbane - it is still doubted by some of her followers that the Lady is actually dead...
LORE: Resembling abominations, yuan-ti holy guardians are rare beings bred specifically to be temple guards. Their temperaments are naturally servile - and fiercely territorial.

LORE: Occasionally, yuan-ti transform slaves into broodguards - administering a strange draught that turns humans into hairless, near-mindless reptilian creatures. These monsters protect the yuan-ti egg chambers, obeying their masters without question.

LORE: Once an aspect of the World Serpent Merrshaulk, Sseth is the primary deity of the yuan-ti. Guiding his people in mysterious ways, Sseth's goal is to lead the yuan-ti to greater power... and eventual supremacy over the world.
LORE: Yuan-ti vocabulary: vrael olo - yuan-ti's name for themselves
LORE: Yuan-ti vocabulary: tsaa olo - potential slaves (or a grave insult to another yuan-ti)
LORE: Yuan-ti vocabulary: ssrath - the "lesser tribe" that a yuan-ti lives or works with
LORE: Yuan-ti vocabulary: ha'srammas - greater tribe
LORE: Yuan-ti vocabulary: t'iss'tess - "dear one," a special term of endearment

Welcome to Neverwinter Nights 2: Storm of Zehir! In Storm of Zehir we have introduced three distinct Play Modes - which you can use to make controlling your characters and camera easier. Each Play Mode features a different camera and control style, and you can customize the styles further to suit your own options. The Play Modes are designed to make it possible to quickly and easily to switch between these different camera and control styles based on the current gameplay situation. The three modes are: Exploration Mode - This mode features a top-down camera that always remains focused on the currently controlled party member. By default, left-click and hold in this mode will cause the currently controlled character to walk in the direction of the mouse cursor. This mode is most useful when you want to be able to see your entire party and all of your surroundings, but want to keep the camera focused on one character. Character Mode - This mode features an over-the shoulder camera that remains focused on the currently controlled party member - and by default, will refocus directly behind that character whenever you begin moving. By default, you can left-click and hold and then move the mouse to turn your character. This mode is fantastic for getting a good look at your surroundings from the point of view of your character - and is also useful for a more immersive role-playing experience. Strategy Mode - This mode features a Top-Down camera that is not focused on the currently controlled character. You can move the mouse to any edge of the screen, or use the Keyboard (Default: Arrow Keys) to scroll the camera in this mode. There is a limit to the amount that the camera can scroll in this mode, based upon your selected options and the visual range of your party. Additionally, you can click and drag in this mode to select multiple characters. This mode is fantastic for controlling your party in difficult combat situations, or any time when you need to rapidly issue commands to your party. The default mode for Storm of Zehir is Exploration Mode, however we encourage you to try out the different modes and find which you prefer - or to switch between them (Default: Numpad * ) depending upon the situation.

The portal from the lumber camp seems to have malfunctioned, causing you to arrive in some sort of crypt instead of your expected destination of Crossroad Keep.
Sa'Sani is one of the most powerful and respected merchants in all of Samarach.
Volothamp Geddarm, or Volo for short, is a famous explorer and author. He has travelled far and wide and written several Volo's Guide books.
Puzzling to many, Sa'Sani's company lacks an actual name and is identified only by her symbol. Some just call it Sa'Sani's Merchant Company.
The ever-frugal Volo was offered a free trip to exotic Samarach in order to deliver an important message to Sa'Sani. He would never admit to being a messenger though...

The Samarachan guards within the Openpalm Bazaar obviously don't enjoy their position much - their constant, focused glares seem to stamp a permanent squint on their features - almost making them look more comical than deadly serious.

Though often shunned by the populace and harassed by followers of Cyric, cults of the "dead" goddess Leira still exist within various Samarachan cities, patiently awaiting the revelation of their deity.
Sa'Sani recently opened a branch of her company far from Samargol, at Crossroad Keep. However, as Volo's message said, her business associates in the Sword Coast have mysteriously gone missing.

Volo has gained infamy of sorts for being too curious for his own good. If his tales can be believed, he has somehow managed to survive through hundreds of perilous misadventures. Some suspect that he is highly favored by the goddess Tymora.

Samarachan officials do not know that the Lantanese gnomes have established a logging camp deep in the Samarlogh jungle. The xenophobic Samarachans would likely react violently if they ever found out...

Luaire's identity as a yuan-ti is a terrifying fact - if any scrying spells were to discover that he had peaceful contact with Sa'Sani or any of her associates, Samarachan officials could legally put everyone involved to death.

Normally the paranoid Samarachan's execute anyone suspected of involvement with the yuan-ti. Sa'Sani's high status with Samarach has spared her life and the lives of her associates, including you and Volo. But she can never return to Samargol again.

There's a ringing sound... and a bunch of incomprehensible noises, as if the planes themselves were trying to invent something that had never been heard before. Then - a bright light - and a sense that you're very likely not at Crossroad Keep after all...
Capable and excitable, Variel - the majordomo at the Keep - seems eager to see Sa'Sani's merchant company begin to grow again, and wears a helpful smile on her face at almost all times.

Khelgar Ironfist was one of the famed companions who defeated the King of Shadows. After the Shadow War, he was made the new Knight Captain of Crossroad Keep, though he refuses to bear the title. In his mind, there is only one Knight Captain.

Khelgar claims that his duties at Crossroad Keep have kept him from resuming his two great loves, fighting and adventuring. In truth, he is held back by the great physical and emotional scars inflicted upon him from the collapse of the King of Shadows' fortress in Merdelain.

Sa'Sani is rather tight-lipped on the issue of her associates - Il'foss and Kizu - going missing, although more from concern than rudeness. She is not able to detail more than that they had been capable traders, and she'd known Il'foss for quite some time prior to his disappearance.
Volo seems quite taken with Sa'Sani. Despite his infamous wanderlust, now he finds any excuse to remain near her.

Since the Shadow War, Sir Nevalle has been a great deal more active in Neverwinter's public sphere, helping to keep the city running smoothly. Since martial law was declared and public opinion of Lord Nasher has dropped, he's assuredly had his work cut out for him.

After the declaration of martial law in the city, Neverwinter's Shadow Thieves have largely gone underground, entrenching themselves in their haunts in the Docks. Some - like Martin Keller - have actually joined organzations like the Fated Winds and gone legitimate... mostly.
The bandits and cult members known as Snaketongues seem to be a great deal more active lately... whispers within towns tell of abductions and robberies, and people seem nervous and upset at the news.

Sa'Sani's associates neglected to explain their sudden disappearance in their message, apparently - or, judging by Sa'Sani's reaction, didn't give a satisfactory reason. Either way, it's obvious that she feels uneasy about their reappearance.

Khelgar was obviously intent on keeping word of Sa'Sani and Nas'Sirin's identity as yuan-ti a secret - no Greycloaks have been allowed to see the scene except his most trusted guard, and it's likely he'll have Nas'Sirin's body cremated to prevent inspection.
Many ancient yuan-ti temples dot the vast wilderness of the Chultan jungle... but very few exist as more than ruins. It's likely wherever Sa'Sani escaped to, it's been kept in pretty good shape...

Avernus Fried Chicken

Though outwardly it resembles a humble chicken - albeit engulfed in flames - sordid are the tales of the dreaded Avernus Fried Chicken. From the writings of the mad scholar Anvandyr in 1028 DR: "Lo, and in the ages past, there lived on Toril great and terrifying birds, who rent flesh and snapped bone. When at last the final member died, Gargauth, God of Cruelty, took notice. Noted he the viciousness of the creature, and in appreciation he took up its soul and dragged it hither to the Nine Hells. "Lo! Hearken and fear! So did the Tenth Lord of Nine - with darkest rites and ancient incantations - use a horrifying mix of eleven cursed herbs and demonic spices to clothe the soul of the beast in a humble frame, forever wreathed in the flames of the Hells! For eternity, until Ao extinguishes the Sun, shall the dread Avernus Fried Chicken peck about at the feat of its master, its dark god! Forever shall the fumes rising from its twisted body tantalize and charm its prey, until its hellish form is upon them, rending their flesh with its talons and charring their eyes in their sockets! "Quake at this revelation... and shudder that the Lost Lord of the Pit may send such a beast to you - that you may hear its hideous squawk tear through the nigh!"

Well... it was somethin' I thought I left behind, but I still got the training... hm. Yeah, you know - I think you'll do. Here...
...so that's all you need to know. Don't tell nobody I taught you that, though - other folks from Amn might not take well to me teachin' their ways to others.
Ah - I am pleased to see you. I wanted to let you know that I'd spoken of you to Lord Nasher recently, and that he was greatly impressed with the results of your hard work and forthrightness.

Type of Feat: Item Creation Prerequisite: Caster level 3rd. Specifics: This feat grants the ability to craft a wide variety of magical items, including amulets ,rings, gloves, bracers, cloaks, belts, helms, and boots. Using this feat to craft magical items requires several things: a magical workbench, a magic item recipe, and the ingredients/skills listed within the recipe. Each recipe is unique and possesses its own requirements, but any party members can supply these - including ingredients, caster level, or skill rank minimums. Once all requirements for crafting the item are met, the player must be in close proximity to a magical workbench, and activate the recipe. If all the ingredients are present, the minimum skill ranks are met, and the crafting player is within 10 meters of a magician's workbench, the item will be crafted. Crafting ingredients can vary widely - gems, creature parts, gold, gear, and trade goods can be included. Gear - such as travelling cloaks or leather boots - can be found at any merchant, while gems are carried in more exclusive stores. Creature parts can be found in the stores of bounty collectors, or dropped off the corpse of the creature in question. More exotic ingredients must be found through adventuring. Many useful recipes can be purchased from merchants that sell magical wares. High powered magic recipes are not as commonplace - as many casters jealously guard their secrets. Anyone wishing to acquire such powerful recipes must search diligently throughout the world. Use: Selected.

Type of Feat: Item Creation Prerequisite: Caster level 5th. Specifics: This feat grants the ability to create magic weapons, armor, and shields. Using this feat to craft magical arms or armor requires several things: a magical workbench, a magic weapon or armor recipe, and the ingredients/skills listed within the recipe. Each recipe is unique and possesses its own requirements, but any party members can supply these - including ingredients, caster level, or skill rank minimums. Once all requirements for crafting the item are met, the player must be in close proximity to a magical workbench, activate the recipe, and apply the enchantment to the weapon or armor of their choice. If all the ingredients are present, the minimum skill ranks are met, and the crafting player is within 10 meters of a magician's workbench, the item will be enchanted. NOTE: A magical weapon, shield, or suit of armor can have a maximum of three enchantments on it. Crafting ingredients can vary widely - gems, creature parts, gold, gear, and trade goods can be included. Gear - such as travelling cloaks or leather boots - can be found at any merchant, while gems are carried in more exclusive stores. Creature parts can be found in the stores of bounty collectors, or dropped off the corpse of the creature in question. More exotic ingredients must be found through adventuring. Many useful recipes can be purchased from merchants that sell magical wares. High powered magic recipes are not as commonplace - as many casters jealously guard their secrets. Anyone wishing to acquire such powerful recipes must search diligently throughout the world. Use: Selected.

Ability: Intelligence Requires Training: No. Classes: All. This skill is used to turn alchemical items into various trap kits. Creating a trap kit requires the appropriate recipe and ingredients. Most trap recipes include various alchemical items, hence the best trap makers are generally alchemists as well. More powerful traps require additional ranks in this skill. To create the trap, the player simply activates the recipe. Trap making recipes are often available for purchase in certain, less than reputable stores. Unlike other crafting professions, crafting traps does not require a workbench of any kind once the ingredients are collected. This makes crafting traps very versatile and accessible in dangerous locations. Use: Selected.

Ability: Intelligence Requires Training: No. Classes: All. This skill allows the character to create a variety of alchemical items: alchemist's fire, acid flasks, choking powder, holy water, tanglefoot bags, and thunderstones. Most trap recipes exclusively use ingredients created with this skill. The Craft Alchemy skill requires an alchemical workbench and the appropriate recipe. Each recipe is unique and possesses its own requirements, but any party members can supply these - including ingredients, caster level, or skill rank minimums. Once all requirements for crafting the item are met, the player must be in close proximity to an alchemist's workbench, and activate the recipe. If all the ingredients are present, the minimum skill ranks are met, and the crafting player is within 10 meters of an alchemist's workbench, the item will be crafted. Alchemical recipes can be found in various stores throughout the game. Skilled alchemists can create more potent versions of alchemical items, which are not generally sold by merchants. Use: Selected.

Ability: Intelligence Requires Training: No. Classes: All. This skill allows the character to craft armor and shields from a variety of materials. The Craft Armor skill requires a blacksmith's workbench and the appropriate recipe. Each recipe is unique and possesses its own requirements, but any party members can supply these - including ingredients, caster level, or skill rank minimums. Once all requirements for crafting the item are met, the player must be in close proximity to a blacksmith's workbench, and activate the recipe. If all the ingredients are present, the minimum skill ranks are met, and the crafting player is within 10 meters of a blacksmith 's workbench, the armor or shield will be crafted. Rare resources (such as adamantine and mithral) are typical ingredient types. Participating in trade quests can open new avenues for various rare resources. Recipes can be purchased from stores throughout the game. Use: Selected.

Ability: Intelligence Requires Training: No. Classes: All. This skill allows the character to create weapons from a variety of materials. The Craft Weapon skill requires a blacksmith's workbench and the appropriate recipe. Each recipe is unique and possesses its own requirements, but any party members can supply these - including ingredients, caster level, or skill rank minimums. Once all requirements for crafting the item are met, the player must be in close proximity to a blacksmith's workbench, and activate the recipe. If all the ingredients are present, the minimum skill ranks are met, and the crafting player is within 10 meters of a blacksmith 's workbench, the weapon will be crafted. Weapons can be crafted from basic materials (iron, wood, or leather), or from more exotic components, such as mithral or zalantar. Exotic materials increase the skill requirements to craft a weapon, but also provide additional benefits. Recipes can be purchased from stores throughout the game. Use: Selected.

Animal Trance Enchantment Level: Brd 2, Drd 2 Components: V, S Casting Time: Instant Range: Close (25 ft. + 5 ft./2 levels) Targets: Animals or magical beasts with Intelligence 1 or 2 Duration: 1 round per class level. Saving Throw: No Spell Resistance: Yes
Your swaying motions and music (or singing, or chanting) compel animals and magical beasts to do nothing but watch you for number of rounds equal to your class level. Only a creature with an Intelligence score of 1 or 2 can be fascinated by this spell. Roll 2d6 to determine the total number of HD worth of creatures that you fascinate. The closest targets are selected first until no more targets within range can be affected. For example, if Vadania affects 7 HD worth of animals and there are several 2 HD wolves within close range, only the three closest wolves are affected.

Ability: Wisdom. Requires Training: No. Classes: All.
Survival skill increases overland movement speed.
Characters with this skill may enter Tracking mode, wherein hostile humanoids, animals, and vermin are made visible on the minimap. Higher Survival skill increases the range of detection.
This skill also determines the range for the Track feat and Swift Tracker ranger ability.

Ability: Intelligence. Requires Training: No. Classes: All.
Search is used to detect traps and hidden locations on the Overland Map.
Check: Detecting a trap is an opposed test, pitting the character's Search check against a DC equal to the Set Trap skill check, plus the strength of the trap. Only rogues may detect traps with a DC greater than 20.
Special: Elves and dwarves receive a +2 bonus to their Search checks, and half-elves gain a +1 bonus. Use: Search is part of the Detect modal action. In Passive Detect mode, checks are made automatically every round. Active Detect mode is a modal action that reduces the character's normal movement rate and perform an Active Search, as well as Spot and Listen checks.

Ability: Dexterity. Requires Training: No. Classes: All.
This skill allows a character to hide from enemies and avoid hostile encounters on the Overland Map.
Check: The character must succeed at an opposed test against a searching creature's Spot check. Success means that the character goes undetected. Special: The Hide and Move Silently skills combine into a single Stealth action. Movement in Stealth mode is slower than the normal rate. Wearing armor or using a torch inhibits this ability, but low light can provide a bonus. A character in Stealth mode is harder to spot if standing still, and if his stature is small. Use: Select the Stealth action on the modal bar. Invisible characters automatically enter Stealth mode. Opposed Spot and Listen rolls are made once per round, where applicable.

Ability: Wisdom. Requires Training: No. Classes: All.
Listen alerts a character to hidden creatures that may be nearby. Listen also helps detect hostile encounters on the Overland Map.
Check: Listen detects hidden creatures by opposing their Move Silently check. A successful check renders the hidden creature visible, and makes it a valid target for the listener. Special: Standing still provides a +5 bonus to a Listen check. A character with the Alertness feat gains a +2 bonus on Listen checks. Rangers gain a bonus when Listening against a favored enemy. Elves, gnomes, and halflings gain a +2 racial bonus to Listen checks. Half-elves receive a +1 racial bonus. Use: Listen is part of the Detect modal action. In Passive Detect mode, checks are made automatically every round. Active Detect mode is a modal action that reduces the normal movement rate and makes the character perform an Active Listen, as well as Spot and Search checks.

Ability: Wisdom. Requires Training: No. Classes: All.
A successful Spot check reveals a hidden creature. Spot also helps detect encounters on the Overland Map.
Check: The DC is determined by the Hide check of the hidden creature. Special: The Alertness feat grants a +2 bonus on Spot checks. Rangers receive a bonus on Spot checks against their favored enemy. Elves gain a +2 bonus on Spot checks, and half-elves gain a +1 bonus. Use: Spot is part of the Detect modal action. In Passive Detect mode, checks are made automatically every round. Active Detect mode is a modal action that reduces the normal movement rate and makes the character perform an Active Spot, as well as Search and Listen checks.

Ability: Dexterity. Requires Training: No. Classes: All.
A character may sneak quietly past an enemy, or a hostile encounter on the Overland Map.
Check: A Move Silently check is opposed by the listening creature's Listen check. If the character is successful, the opposing creature remains unaware as the character moves. Special: Hide and Move Silently are combined into a single Stealth action. Movement in Stealth mode is slower than the normal rate. Wearing armor inhibits this ability, but low light can provide a bonus. Use: Select the Stealth action from the modal bar. Invisible creatures automatically enter Stealth mode.

Shadow Thief of Amn (PRESTIGE CLASS: This class is not available at character creation and must be unlocked by meeting special requirements, listed below.) The organization known as the Shadow Thieves is the largest and most prosperous thieves' guild in all of the region. Its success is derived from its system of interlocking guilds, each dedicated to the twin goals of profit and power. From the organization's stronghold in Amn, this series of guilds controls the lion's share of all criminal operations along the Sword Coast and beyond. As a member of a Shadow Thieves' guild, a shadow thief of Amn knows only her own minions, her coworkers, and her superior. This web of secrecy preserves the organization, because any members who are captured can sell out only a few others. A character can achieve a maximum of 5 levels in the Shadow Thief of Amn prestige class. Requirements: Feats: Stealthy. Skills: Bluff 3 ranks, Hide 8 ranks, Intimidate 3 ranks, Move Silently 3 ranks. Class Features: - Hit Die: d6 - Base Attack Bonus: Medium. - High Saves: Reflex. - Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons. - Armor Proficiencies: Light armor. - Skill Points: 6 + Int Modifier. - Class Skills: Appraise, Bluff, Craft Alchemy, Craft Trap, Craft Weapon, Diplomacy, Disable Device, Intimidate, Listen, Lore, Move Silently, Open Lock, Parry, Search, Set Trap, Sleight of Hand, Spot, Taunt, and Tumble. - Sneak Attack: Starting at 1st level, the shadow thief gets the sneak attack ability at +1d6 damage. This is the same as the Rogue ability of the same name, and its effects stack with that ability. This ability increases by +1d6 at 3rd and 5th level. - Doublespeak: At 1st level, the shadow thief gets a +2 bonus on all Bluff and Diplomacy checks. - Bonus Feat: At 2nd and 4th level the shadow thief gets a bonus feat. This feat can be: Alertness, Blind-Fight, Combat Expertise, Feint, Lightning Reflexes, Nimble Fingers, Skill Focus, Silent Spell, Still Spell, Track, Weapon Finesse, and Weapon Focus. - Uncanny Dodge: At 2nd level the shadow thief retains her Dexterity bonus to AC even when caught flat-footed. - Reputation: At 3rd level, the shadow thief gets a 10% discount from all merchants and an additional +2 bonus on all Bluff, Intimidate, and Diplomacy checks because of her reputation. - Improved Uncanny Dodge: At 5th level the shadow thief can no longer be sneak attacked except by a character with 4 more total levels in classes that grant sneak attack than the shadow thief's level.

You are entering the Overland Map for the first time. You will travel between the various locations in Storm of Zehir on the Overland Map - and can explore to discover hidden secrets, adventures, and encounters along the way. Your movement speed on the Overland Map map varies based upon the type of terrain you are traversing. For instance, you will move much more quickly on the Road than you will in Swamp. You will also see hostile, neutral and special encounters on the Overland Map, indicated by rings underneath their feet (colored red, yellow, and blue, respectively). Hostile encounters will attempt to detect you when you are nearby, and if they find you they will move to attack you. You can use your skills to avoid detection by Random Encounters, or you can choose to run away from them - they will eventually give up trying to chase you. All hostile encounters have an Encounter Level, or EL - this number indicates the difficulty of the encounter. An encounter of a given EL is an appropriate challenge for a party of the corresponding level. For instance, an EL 4 encounter is an appropriate challenge for a party of level 4 characters. Encounters with a higher EL than your party's level may be extremely difficult - however, you will receive a larger experience reward for defeating encounters with a higher EL.
[Visit your Merchant Headquarters.]

Only one of your characters is displayed on the Overland Map. This is the Party Leader. Several of your Party Leader's skills are used as you travel across the map: Hide or Move Silently are used to avoid detection by random encounters; the Skill that the Party Leader has a higher bonus with will be used. Listen or Spot are used to detect encounters. If the Party Leader succeeds at the Spot or Listen check, the encounter will be detected further away from the party. If the Party Leader fails at the check, they will be detected much closer to the party, giving the party less time to avoid or flee from the encounter. The Party Leader will use the skill with which they have the higher bonus to attempt to detect encounters. Search is used to discover hidden locations on the Overland Map. A high Search skill will help your party detect interesting and dangerous areas to explore and loot. Survival is used to mitigate the movement penalties of harsh terrain. A Party Leader with low survival will be greatly slowed by difficult terrain - such as Jungle or Swamp, whereas a Party Leader with a high Survival skill will move significantly faster in that terrain. Survival will not increase the Party's movement speed beyond that of a party on open roads. You can change your Party Leader by clicking on the portrait of the character you would like to promote, or by using the function keys.

In addition, you can use your conversation skills to gain an advantage when approached by Random Encounters. If your skill is high enough to gain an advantage in combat, the relevant options will appear when you chooose to Parley with a hostile Random Encounter: Bluff can be used to throw your enemies off guard, temporarily reducing their AC. The duration and magnitude of the effect is determined by the relative number of ranks that the character has in excess of the DC of the skill check. Intimidate can be used to instill fear in your enemies, causing them to become shaken or terrified. The duration and magnitude of the effect is determined by the relative number of ranks that the character has in excess of the DC of the skill check. Diplomacy can be used with intelligent enemies to reduce the amount that you have to pay to bribe them to leave you alone. You may find other skills useful on the Overland Map as well - feel free to explore and enjoy the surprises you find! Note that you can find this and other help messages in your Journal under the "Completed" quests category.

Sa'sani has tasked you with recovering her cargo - this will be your first interaction with the Trading System. In Storm of Zehir, you can choose not only to be an adventurer, but also a merchant. At this point in the game, you can gather Sa'Sani's Ore and other Rare Resources you discover as you adventure around Samarach. You can then take these resources and use them for crafting or sell them to various towns in the region. When selling these resources, you will recieve Trade Bars. These Trade Bars can then be redeemed for gold - along with other hidden rewards - as you trade. Note that different towns may offer different prices for resources - so it helps to scout out the towns that offer the best prices. The cargo that you collect is measured in Units - Sa'Sani has provided you with enough carrying capacity to hold 10 cargo units. To view the cargo you are currently carrying, open your Inventory Screen ("I" by default) and click the Wagon button. As you progress through the game, you will unlock additional Resources and discover new aspects of the Trading System.

Congratulations - you have discovered your first Rare Resource Node! These nodes, which you can discover along your adventures, enable nearby towns to collect a small amount of the Rare Resource you have discovered each day. Locations that produce a rare resource will sell them at a discounted price - so you can make a healthy profit by purchasing resources where they are produced and selling them elsewhere. Some Rare Resources can also be used for crafting; and you may find additional uses for the various resources you discover as you continue your adventures.

The Sword Coast's economy is significantly more open than Samarach's - and as a result you now have access to Trade Goods while on the Sword Coast. Trade Goods are a type of cargo - similar to Rare Resources - that are available in all of the locations on the Sword Coast. Ore, Lumber and Skins - which you may have already collected - are counted as Trade Goods on the Sword Coast. When you return to Samarach, these goods will again be treated as Rare Resources. The price of Trade Goods varies from town to town - so it is possible to generate a significant profit by travelling between two or more locations while buying low and selling high. Alternately, you can simply gather goods along the way and sell them as you see fit - the choice is up to you!

You can now construct Trading Posts at the various cities and towns along the Sword Coast. Each town will have its own requirements to construct a Trading Post - visit the various towns to discover their requirements. Building a Trading Post will give you access to the following: Caravans - You may construct a caravan between any two locations which both contain Trading Posts. A caravan will travel between the two locations that it visits, generating profit for your merchant company each time it reaches a location. You can return to Crossroad Keep to collect this income at any time. Shipping - You can ship goods from your cargo back to Crossroad Keep at a Trading Post, freeing up cargo space and while saving that Cargo. Shops - Each Trading Post is manned by a Trader who will sell you useful goods. Additionally, many towns will send a special merchant to Crossroad Keep when you construct a Trading Post in their town. Trading Posts also passively increase your merchant company's daily income and unlock other gameplay benefits - explore and discover them for yourself!

A successful Use Magic Device check allows the character to use a magic item as if he had a required class, race, or alignment.
Check: The base DC is determined by the value of the item and can vary depending on the type of item the character is attempting to use. Emulate a Specific Race: This involves using items that are typically restricted to a certain race. (Minimum DC5) Emulate an Alignment: This involves using items that are alignment restricted. (Minimum DC10) Emulate a Class: (Minimum DC 13) Use a Scroll: Level 1(DC13), Level 2(DC15), Level 3(DC17), Level 4(DC19), Level 5(DC21), Level 6(DC23), Level 7(DC25), Level 8(DC27), Level 9(DC29) * Use a Wand: (DC 10) Use a Rod: (DC 12)
*Note: The DCs represented here are based on the minimum caster level for a particular scroll. Scrolls with caster levels higher than the minimum can have increased DCs. For example, a character can use a scroll of fireball (5) with a Use Magic Device skill of 17. This is because fireball is a 3rd level spell with a minimum caster level of 5. If the same character attempted to use a scroll of fireball (9), the DC would be increased.
Use: Automatically applied whenever a character attempts to use or equip an item normally unusable by his class, race, or alignment.

One of the new features in Storm of Zehir is the Party Conversation system. In a Party Conversation you will see the portraits of all party members in the conversation window. You can select the portraits to change the speaker. When a party member that is not the speaker has a response option that is different from the speaker, a speech bubble will appear on their portrait. Your dialogue choices will vary greatly based on many of your party members attributes, such as Skills, Class, Race, Gender, Alignment, Deity, Abilities, and more. Be sure to create a well balanced party to have more choices in conversations. Note that you can find this and other help messages in your Journal (default key: J) under the "Completed" quests category.
Tutorial - Death and Dying

Death and Dying work differently in Storm of Zehir from what you may be accustomed to. When one of your party members reaches zero hit points, they fall unconscious. You cannot use them again unless you heal them with a Healing Kit or a spell such as Cure Light Wounds. When a party member goes below zero hit points they will be Dying, and their hit points will gradually decrease unless they are healed. Healing a Dying party member will Stabilize them, which keeps them from gradually losing hit points. When a Dying character loses half of their total hit points or more, they will be Dead. Dead party members can be brought back to life at a with a Coin of Life, or with a spell such as Raise Dead. If you don't have either of these, then you can go to a Temple of Waukeen, located in most major towns, to purchase healing services and items.

In Storm of Zehir, Crafting items is a great way to customize your party in whatever way you see fit. Your crafting recipes can be found in different Recipe Books in your inventory. Throughout the game you will have opportunities to buy or find Crafting Recipes. Once a recipe is collected, it will automatically be transferred to the appropriate Recipe Book. By double clicking on the recipe book in your Inventory (default: I), you can browse through the individual recipes you have collected. By right clicking on a recipe, you can Examine the requirements needed to craft that item. Any party member can supply a needed crafting requirement. When you are ready to craft, head to the appropriate Crafting Station and click on the recipe you want to create. The item will appear in your inventory and any ingredients will be consumed. Crafting Stations are located throughout the game world. These include the Alchemist's, Blacksmith's and Magician's workbenches. For detailed information on the Crafting system, refer to the game manual or skill/feat descriptions in the Character Screen (default: C).

The Market Screen is the interface through which you can buy and sell cargo at towns as you adventure. Each type of cargo you are carrying is listed in one of the rows on this screen. Beside each type of cargo, there are the following columns, from left to right: Town Stock - This is the amount of this cargo that the town you are visiting currently has in stock. Sell Cargo Buttons - These two buttons, indicated by arrows pointing to the left, are used to sell your cargo. The button with two arrows will sell ten units of cargo, and the button with one arrow will sell one unit of cargo. Price - This is the price, in trade bars, being offered for this cargo at the current town. Note that you buy and sell at the same price - and that the price for goods may differ at the various locations you encounter on your travels. The color of the price text itself will indicate the relative price being offered for the associated good. Blue text indicates a low price, Black a moderate price, and Gold a high price. Remember to buy low and sell high for the greatest profit! BuyCargo Buttons - These two buttons, indicated by arrows pointing to the right, are used to purchase cargo from the town. The button with two arrows will buy ten units of cargo, and the button with one arrow will buy one unit of cargo. Party Stock - This is the amount of this cargo that you are currently carrying. At the bottom of this screen you can see your current amount of Trade Bars and your current cargo capacity.
